name: "Cantrips"
entries: You can call upon your "magic" to cast "Cantrips" in combat. Once on each of your turns when you hit a target with a Strength-based attack, you can use one of the following "Cantrips" of your choice.

entries.name: Mage Hand
entries: You can push the target up to 5 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large size or smaller. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you can push the target up to 10 feet instead.

entries.name: Shocking Grasp
entries: The force of your strike is quite shocking. The target can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} until the end of the current turn. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, it can't make Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: True Strike
entries: You really, truly strike, dealing an extra {@damage 1d6} damage to the target. The damage has the same type as the weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} used for the attack. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you add half your Barbarian level (round down) to the extra damage.

name: "Spells"
entries: Your "magic" is powerful enough to cast every "spell" that exists (and no one can prove otherwise without broken ribs). However, you only prepared the following "spells" today. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you can use each of the following "Spells" once. When you do so, you can't use that "Spell" again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Burning Hands
entries: Your backhand slap is legendary. As an action, you can make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against each creature within your reach. On a hit, this strike deals Bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 1d8} plus your Strength modifier and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack it makes before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Magic Missile
entries: As an action, you can make three ranged attacks using {@item Dart|XPHB|Darts}, {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers}, or other weapons with {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} that use Strength for the attack and damage rolls. Because Magic Missile never misses, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on these attack rolls.

entries.name: Shield
entries: When you are hit by an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to quickly don a {@item Shield|XPHB} to defend yourself. You gain the Shield's AC bonus against the triggering attack, potentially causing it to miss. If the attack hits, the damage dealt to you is reduced by an amount equal to your Barbarian level.

name: 1st Manifestation
entries: Starting at 3rd level, the Corruption within begins to manifest in combat.

Whenever you take damage, you also receive a curse marker; if the damage was from a critical hit, you receive two curse markers instead. These markers will remain active until the end of your next turn, and the maximum number of curse markers you can accumulate at a time is 2. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, all the curse markers you have gained are instantly consumed, dealing an extra {@dice 1d4} necrotic damage to the target for each curse marker consumed.

Alternatively, you can use a bonus action to call upon your Corruption to immediately gain the maximum number of curse markers available to you. When you use this ability, you can't gain more than your maximum number of curse markers.
The number of curse markers you can accumulate at once increases when you reach certain levels in this class: 3 at 5th level, 4 at 11th level, and 5 at 17th level.

name: 2nd Manifestation
entries: At 3rd level, you start to observe peculiar happenings within your own body. At times you notice that your limbs and torso exhibit independent movements, seemingly acting of their own volition.

When you make a Strength or Dexterity check, you can choose to replace the result with a number equal to 10 + your ranger level. You can wait until after you roll the d20 before deciding to use this feature, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. You can use this feature a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded up), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: 3rd Manifestation
entries: Starting at 7th level, when you make a weapon attack against a creature, you can expend one curse marker to roll a {@dice d4} and add it to the attack roll. You can choose to use a curse marker in this way before or after making the attack roll. You can expend a curse marker in this way only once per turn.

Additionally, whenever you take damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage taken by an amount equal to your ranger level. Once you reduce damage in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: 4th Manifestation
entries: At 11th level, your ailment is beginning to have side effects on your body. Gain one of the following ailments of your choice.

name: 5th Manifestation
entries: Starting at 15th level, you gain the ability to call upon the Corruption which greatly alters your natural capabilities. As a bonus action, you can activate this feature, doubling your walking speed, increasing your AC by 2, and allowing you to make two additional attacks when taking the {@action Attack} action. In addition, all attacks are treated as if you have the maximum number of curse markers accumulated. The effects of this feature last until the start of your next turn. You can use this ability without negative effects once per long rest.

If you use this feature a second time before finishing a long rest, in addition to the effects wearing off at the start of your next turn, you also suffer one level of {@condition exhaustion} and immediately drop to 1 hit point if you have more than 1 hit point at the start of your turn.
Once you use this feature a second time, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: A Cure for Weariness
entries: Beginning at 7th level, the healing you impart on others also shakes off their weariness. During a short rest, you can reduce a creature's {@condition exhaustion} level by one. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: A Dangerous Gift
entries: Starting at 7th level, you have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Riddle|TLotRR}) and Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks. In addition, you can reroll a single ability check that you fail during the Interaction stage of a council (see {@book Chapter 5|TLotRR|4|3. Interaction}).

name: Abyssal Strength
entries: You are a creature of darkness able to tap into a fierce wellspring of physical power.

entries.name: Monstrous Might
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 2 Blood Points to increase your Strength score by an amount equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} for 1 minute.

name: Acolyte of the Occult
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Arcana|XPHB} skill.

name: Acquired Taste
entries: Your hunger for monster portions has increased to the point of being insatiable. You can now consume 1 additional portion safely. Additionally, for 1 minute when you consume a portion, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, on attack rolls made as part of a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

name: Adamantine Hide
entries: While in a Wild Shape form, you gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

In addition, when a creature makes an attack roll against you or forces you to make a saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend a use of Wild Shape to shape-shift into one of your Wild Shape forms before the attack hits or the saving throw is made.

name: Adrenal Overload
entries: As an action, you trigger a hidden, internal switch within your companion, triggering a cascade of rapid mutations that lasts for the next minute, with the following results:

items: It immediately grows to Huge size (if it isn't already).
Its weight increases by a factor of 8 per size category increased.
It gains temporary hit points equal to ten times your tamer level.
Its Strength score increases to 22 (if it isn't already higher).
It gains proficiency in the {@skill Athletics} skill.

It sprouts an appendage with which it can make melee weapon attacks with a reach of 5 feet that deal bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (your choice when you take the action), equal to {@damage 3d6} plus its Strength modifier ({@hit +6}) on a hit.
It gains the Multiattack action option: The companion makes three attacks with its appendage.

entries: After the minute elapses, your companion falls {@condition unconscious} for {@damage 1d4} hours and gains 2 levels of {@condition exhaustion}. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Adrenaline Rush
entries: At 15th level, the thrill of battle resonates magically within your body. When you use your Second Wind, you also regain maneuver points equal to half your fighter level.

name: Advanced Enchantments
entries: When you reach 13th level, some of your enchantments become more potent. You now use the alternate enchantments features found below. If you have yet to learn any of the following enchantments, you may learn one as part of this feature.

entries.name: Blooming Light
entries: Starting at 13th level, the effects of blooming light lasts for 8 hours.

entries.name: Burning Delay
entries: Starting at 13th level, you can delay the effects of your candle enchantments by 1 round, 3 rounds, 1 minute, 10 minutes, or 1 hour.

entries.name: Candle Pop
entries: Starting at 13th level, candle pop affects the target and each creature within 5 feet of it.

entries.name: Delicacy
entries: Starting at 13th level, the creature regains {@dice 1d12} hit points, instead of {@dice 1d6}, and you can have up to 4 candles with this enchantment at a time.

entries.name: Maker's Mark
entries: Starting at 13th level, maker's mark has no limit to the number of times you can use it per turn.

entries.name: Shielding Seal
entries: Starting at 13th level, you can have up to three shielding seals active at a time, instead of one.

entries.name: Waxlings
entries: Starting at 13th level, you can spend 3 wicks points as an action, instead of 2, to summon two waxlings simultaneously.

name: Agent of Mercy
entries: You harbor a wellspring of positive magic within yourself. It is represented by your Mercy Dice, which fuel features you have from this subclass. The Mercy Dice table shows the die size and number of these dice you have when you reach certain Fighter levels.
A Mercy Die is expended when you use it. You regain all expended Mercy Dice when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Benevolent Presence
entries: When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check or Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check, you can expend one or more Mercy Dice and add those dice to the roll.

entries.name: Merciless Strike
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend a Mercy Die to deal extra Radiant damage to the target equal to the Mercy Die roll.

entries.name: Peaceful Ward
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a Mercy Die to gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the Mercy Die roll plus your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB|Temporary Hit Point}).

name: Aggressive Defense
entries: You know when to switch from defense to offense. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can lose {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to no more than half your Fighter level (round down) to deal extra damage to the target equal to the number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} lost in this way.

name: Agile Response
entries: You can leap aside to avoid enemies rushing toward you. When a creature makes a melee attack roll against you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on that roll and use your {@classFeature Studied Response|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|2} as part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. Whether the attack hits or misses, you can then move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. This movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

name: Aid Not Given
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to take the {@action Help|XPHB} action or touch a creature and restore a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to a roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier. You can use this feature as though you were in the shade's space.

name: Ain't Big Enough for the Both of Us
entries: Your wandplay is legendary, and your territory is assured. Whenever you expend a use of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|XPHB|1} or when a creature within 60 feet of you adds one of your Bardic Inspiration dice to a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, one creature of your choice that can see you within 60 feet of yourself must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. If the target already has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, it must immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, if available, to move as far as away from you as it can, using the safest route.

name: Air Dash
entries: On your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} until the end of your next turn (no action required). You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next melee attack you make before the end of the current turn.

name: Albedo
entries: You can purify your {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|PHB|Philosophy|CrookedMoon14|2|CrookedMoon14} to amplify your spells. When you cast a spell using a spell slot, you can expend 1 {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|PHB|Philosophy|CrookedMoon14|2|CrookedMoon14} as a material component to increase the level of the spell slot by 1, up to 9th level. The maximum {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|PHB|Philosophy|CrookedMoon14|2|CrookedMoon14} you can expend in this way on a given spell is half of your proficiency bonus (rounded up).

name: Albedo
entries: You can purify your {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|XPHB|Philosopher|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} to amplify your spells. When you cast a spell using a spell slot, you can expend 1 {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|XPHB|Philosopher|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} as a Material component to increase the level of the spell slot by 1, up to level 9. The maximum {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|XPHB|Philosopher|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} you can expend in this way on a given spell is half of your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (rounded up).

name: Alchemical Decoctions
entries: You can spend 1 hour and 20 GP worth of alchemical ingredients (such as special herbs or monster salvage) to use your {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} to convert a monster portion into a decoction. A decoction is a magic potion that grants the benefits of a consumed monster portion. You can have 4 unconsumed decoctions active. You can destroy a decoction as a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action.

A creature other than you can consume 1 decoction without adverse effects. A creature gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level for each decoction it consumes after the first. A creature must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before it regains the ability to safely consume a decoction.

name: Alchemical Experiments
entries: You gain a set of {@item Alchemist's Supplies|PHB}, and you have proficiency with it. Additionally, you can use {@item Alchemist's Supplies|PHB} instead of an {@item Herbalism Kit|PHB} to craft {@item Potion of Healing (*)|DMG}.

name: Alchemical Experiments
entries: You gain a set of {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}, and you have proficiency with it. Additionally, you can use {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} instead of an {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB} to craft {@item Potions of Healing|XDMG}.

name: Alchemical Gastronomy
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} and {@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB}.

name: Alchemical Knowledge
entries: You gain a set of {@item alchemist's supplies|PHB}. You have proficiency with it and can use it as an arcane focus. Additionally, you can use {@item alchemist's supplies|PHB} instead of another tool required to craft a magic item.

name: Alchemical Knowledge
entries: You gain a set of {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}. You have proficiency with it and can use it as an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB}. Additionally, you can use {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} instead of the normal tool to craft a magic item.

name: All Will Be Dust
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to twist a creature's fate. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to choose a creature you can see within 120 feet of yourself. That creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next saving throw it makes against your spells before the end of your next turn.

name: Always Ready
entries: You always have your next spell dancing on the tip of your tongue. You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to Ready a spell as if you had used your {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to do so. If you expend a spell slot when you ready a spell in this way, it does not count against the usual limit of only one spell slot expended to cast a spell per turn.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you spend 4 Sorcery Points (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Ambusher
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you excel at ambushing your enemies. You can add your Wisdom modifier to your initiative rolls, and you have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn. In addition, you gain the {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Treasure Hunter|TLotRR|1|TLotRR} feature. The extra damage is {@dice 1d6}, and it increases to {@dice 2d6} when you reach 7th level in this calling.

name: Ambusher's Advantage
entries: You have become a ferocious ambusher. When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can add your Intelligence modifier to the roll. Additionally, you can't be {@status surprised|XPHB} by enemies that include creature types in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1}.

name: An Arcane Art
entries: At 2nd level, you learn to weave magic into origami, allowing you to create magnificent moving art pieces, which act on your behalf. As a bonus action, you can fold and imbue life into a paper construct that takes a form you choose from the list below. When crafted, an origami construct becomes bound to you or another creature of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of you.

A creature with a bound origami construct gains the unique effects and features listed for that construct. A creature can't have more than one of the same origami construct bound to it at a time, unless stated otherwise. A bound construct occupies the same space as the creature it's bound to.

These constructs stay imbued with life for a number of hours equal to half your wizard level. Origami constructs have an AC equal to your spell save DC, are immune to poison and psychic damage, and are destroyed when they take any damage. You can use this feature to create an origami construct a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: An Artist's Soul
entries: You have in you a spark of talent and inspiration that has only been fanned brighter by your vampiric ascension. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Auspicious Senses
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) and Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks. In addition, the range of your {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} increases to 120 feet.

entries.name: Chosen for Talent
entries: You gain proficiency in two skills and one tool of your choice. If you already have proficiency in the chosen skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

name: Anatomical Expert
entries: Your pursuit of osteomancy has required many hours studying the anatomy of a myriad of creatures. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Medicine|XPHB} skill, and when you make a Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}) check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1). In addition, when these checks concern a creature that possesses a skeleton, you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in that skill, even if you don't have proficiency in the {@skill Survival|XPHB} skill.

name: Ancient Protector
entries: When you awaken your connection to the Elderwood, you now become an incarnation of its ancient might. When you activate your {@subclassFeature Wood Wose|Druid|PHB|Old Ways|CrookedMoon14|2|CrookedMoon14}, you now gain additional benefits for the duration.

entries.name: Old Growth
entries: Your size increases to Large (along with anything you're wearing or carrying) if there is space to accommodate your growth, and your reach increases by 5 feet.

entries.name: Mighty Trunk
entries: You gain resistance to bludgeoning and piercing damage.

entries.name: Vengeance of the Elders
entries: When a creature that is covered in Elderwood Sap and is within your reach makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to make a melee attack against that creature.

name: Ancient Protector
entries: When you awaken your connection to the Elderwood, you now become an incarnation of its ancient might. When you activate your {@subclassFeature Wood Wose|Druid|XPHB|Old Ways|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24}, you now gain additional benefits for the duration.

entries.name: Old Growth
entries: Your size increases to Large (along with anything you're wearing or carrying) if there is space to accommodate your growth, and your reach increases by 5 feet.

entries.name: Mighty Trunk
entries: You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning and Piercing damage.

entries.name: Vengeance of the Elders
entries: When a creature that is covered in Elderwood Sap and is within your reach makes an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a melee attack against that creature.

name: Animate Dead I
entries: You learn how to use your taming magic to temporarily raise new allies and bind them to your will You learn the {@spell animate dead} spell, you always have it prepared, it doesn't count against the number of spells you know, and you can cast it once without using a spell slot. After you do so, you can't cast it in this way again until you finish a long rest.

When you issue a command to your companion using either a bonus action or action, you can issue the same command to any creatures you have created with {@spell animate dead} so long as the creatures are within 100 feet of you.

name: Animate Dead II
entries: Once you reach 18th level, when you cast this spell using this feature, the creature you animate has the statistics of a {@creature ghast} (if Medium or smaller) or a {@creature minotaur skeleton} (if Large or larger).

name: Antagonistic Antics
entries: You know the {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB} cantrip. If you already know it, you learn a different Bard cantrip of your choice. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known. Additionally, you always have the {@spell Dissonant Whispers|XPHB} spell prepared.

In addition, when you take the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Influence|XPHB} action on your turn, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on the same turn to cast {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB}.

name: Apex Predator
entries: Your mastery of mutation has made you an apex predator, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Evolved Attacks
entries: Once per turn, you can deal an extra {@damage 2d10} Force damage to a target you hit with a Wild Shape form's attack.

entries.name: Mutate Beasts
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can touch a Beast and expend a spell slot, causing the target to mutate. You gain Mutation Points equal to the slot's level, which you must immediately spend on Mutations for the Beast. Unspent Mutation Points are lost. Mutations remain until the Beast is targeted by this feature again. A {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB}, {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} or similar magic ends the Mutations.

name: Apocalypse Domain

entries: Some say the world ends in fire. Others, ice. I'm ready for both.

Few gods embrace the Apocalypse Domain, yet in times of war, disease, or social upheaval, its Clerics appear at the head of grim cults that proclaim the world's imminent demise. Devotes of the Apocalypse Domain are usually apostates and heretics cast from religious orders for their fanatical conviction to the end of all things.

The exact origin of their divine power confounds the elders of established religions. Sometimes, these Clerics derive their powers from the gods of fate, doom, or change. More often, though, they seem to draw their power from the collective gloom of a population facing disaster. Perhaps the world's demise is truly imminent, and these visionaries have found some way to tap into the apocalypse as it grows near.
{@b Alignment}

Consider your alignment and how it dictates your attitude toward the apocalypse. Below are some ideas on how your philosophy shapes your attitudes and religious practices. You can also use this table to determine the nature of your cult.

rows: Each of us faces the apocalypse alone. We must find our own path to making peace with the imminent destruction of all we hold dear. In these end times, laws, traditions, and restrictions mean nothing. We are entitled to live as we see fit.

The apocalypse is at hand, but if you obey the dictates and commandments determined by your order, you have the chance to escape. The gods will preserve those who are worthy, and you will know the worthy by their observance to the proper traditions, rites, and sacrifices.

All things die, including the world. By cataloging the end times, perhaps we can preserve a sliver of our reality for whatever world arises from the ashes. But make no mistake—when the world ends, we will end with it.

It isn't enough for the apocalypse to come to the world-we must hasten its appearance by culling those foolish enough to defy it. By doing so, the force behind the coming disaster will welcome us as its instruments and preserve us after we end this world.

The apocalypse is a cleansing event, one that will see the wickedness of the world washed away in favor of a new order. Our task is to spread knowledge of the righteous path. We must be patient and kind, for few wish to hear our message. But those wise enough to embrace our hymn will join us in the paradise to come.

name: Apocalypse Domain Spells
entries: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Apocalypse Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Apocalypse Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Darkness|XPHB}, {@spell Hellish Rebuke|XPHB}, {@spell Phantasmal Force|XPHB}, {@spell Thunderwave|XPHB}

name: Apocalypse Sorcery
entries: {@i Hasten or Stall the End of the World}
Apocalypse Sorcerers have seen the shape of things to come. They may have visions of the Great Beast ushering in the end of Etharis or dreams of Gormadraug waking and devouring the land.

These prophecies besiege Apocalypse Sorcerers, plaguing and empowering in equal measure. Some find relief in putting these revelations into writing, producing texts that read as incoherent but slowly seep into the mind as sensible, even inevitable. When the apocalypse-bringer is freed to travel across Etharis unburdened, undoing the works of gods and men, magic will swell and pool, ripe for the taking. This sign of the end is also their gift.

name: Apocalyptic Revelation
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can reveal the true nature of your enemies for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required). You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Blinding Glory
entries: Enemies that start their turn within 5 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw against the Paladin's spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: See the Truth
entries: You have {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Smite the Heretic
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can choose a creature within 60 feet of yourself and reveal its weaknesses. You and your allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against that creature.

name: Apocalyptic Revelation
entries: At 20th level, as an action you can reveal the true nature of your enemies to all for 1 minute. During this time, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have {@sense truesight} out to a distance of 120 feet.

Creatures who start their turn, or move within, 5 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw against your paladin spell save DC. On a failure, the creature is {@condition blinded} until the start of its next turn.

As a bonus action on each of your turns you can choose a creature within 60 feet and reveal its weaknesses for all to see. Attacks made against the chosen creature have advantage until the start of your next turn.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Apocalyptic Spells
entries: When you reach a sorcerer level specified in the Apocalyptic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Apocalyptic Spells
rows: {@spell Augury|XPHB}, {@spell Comprehend Languages|XPHB}, {@spell Hellish Rebuke|XPHB}, {@spell Ray of Enfeeblement|XPHB}

name: Arachnoid Stalker
entries: {@i Sling Webs and Crawl Walls}

A life-changing event, such as being cursed by a drider or being bitten by a dangerously transmuted arachnid, has imbued you with the abilities of a spider. This transformation might have left you physically unchanged, or you may have developed a half-dozen eyes, lanky and hairy limbs, or a set of inhuman mandibles. Whatever the side effects, you can now produce deadly poison and ropes of silken web from your palms, and even scale walls with your fingertips.

name: Arcane Apocrypha
entries: Your obsessive reflections on the end of existence inspire your writing. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can create one {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} at no cost. It must be a spell of level 5 or lower that you can cast. This {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} disintegrates when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Arcane Artisan
entries: You have dedicated your studies to creation and the magic surrounding it. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Bonus Cantrip
entries: You know the {@spell Mending|XPHB} cantrip. If you already know it, you learn a different Wizard cantrip of your choice. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.

entries.name: Creation Savant
entries: You gain proficiency with three {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace your proficiency with one type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} with a different type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice.

entries.name: Mage Craft
entries: Your exceptional wit and aptitude allow you to do more with less time. While crafting using a set of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} with which you have proficiency, you can subtract your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1) from the number of hours you must work each day, allowing you to complete a full day's work in 7 hours or less (to a minimum of 2 hours).

name: Arcane Battery
entries: Beginning at 6th level, when you use your Arcane Recovery feature, your core wand regains 3 expended core charges.

In addition, you gain a new option to use your wand's core charges. When you cast a spell that targets only one creature and forces it to make a saving throw while you're holding your core wand, you can expend up to 3 core charges to gain a bonus to that spell's save DC equal to the number of core charges spent.

name: Arcane Conduit
entries: At 20th level, as an action, you can emanate a field of crackling magic in a 30-foot radius. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have resistance to damage from spells and have advantage on saving throws against spells.
Whenever a creature hits you with a melee attack, that creature takes force damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1) as magical energy lashes out at them.

When you expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher, friendly creatures in the field regain a number of hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1), while hostile ones take force damage equal to the same amount instead.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Arcane Exemplar
entries: Starting at 18th level, you can use a bonus action and expend a charged rune to become a being of pure magical energy. While in your exemplar form, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have a flying speed of 60 feet.
Creatures have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage} on {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1} against your sorcerer spells.
You have resistance to damage dealt by spells.
Whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher, you regain hit points equal to the spell's level.

entries: Your exemplar form lasts until the end of your turn. However, you can expend a charged rune at the end of your turn (no action required) to extend the duration until the end of your next turn. When your exemplar form ends, you are {@condition stunned} until the end of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you complete a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.

name: Arcane Interference
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells cast by creature types in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1}. Additionally, when a creature you can see within 60 feet of you casts a spell or makes a spell attack, you can use {@classFeature Studied Response|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|2} against that creature before the spell is cast.

name: Arcane Prison
entries: Trapped inside of you is the essence of the First Oni, passed down through its children and stretched across a long and treacherous lineage. As you grow in strength, so does the spirit within you. It desperately wishes to bubble to the surface, and it does so when you're at your weakest. At 1st level, you gain the traits of the oni, which manifest as you expend sorcery points. Each oni trait becomes available to you based on how many sorcery points you're missing from your total, represented by the table below. Regaining sorcery points can cause you to lose one or more oni traits.
Each oni trait has both a physical and an arcane manifestation, which lasts until you finish a long rest.

name: Arcane Prototype
entries: You're always working on new projects, crafting Arcane Prototypes. You determine a prototype's appearance, but its functionality is always similar to that of a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG}—it holds the effect of a spell that can be unleashed at a later time. Only you can use a prototype to cast a spell; they're experimental creations that no one else can truly understand.

Your ability to constantly come up with new ideas is represented by Arcane Charges. You have 1 Arcane Charge, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Arcane Charges level of the Arcane Prototypes table. You can't have more Arcane Charges than the number shown in the table for your level. You regain all expended Arcane Charges when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

You can use your Arcane Charges to imbue spells into your prototypes, up to the level shown in the Max Spell Level of the Arcane Prototypes table. While a prototype is in your possession, you can cast the imbued spell without expending a spell slot, without preparing the spell, and without Material components. Casting the spell in this way requires the spell's normal casting time. Once the spell is cast, the prototype crumbles to dust, unless you choose to preserve it by expending a spell slot equal to the level of the spell.

entries.name: Imbuing Spells into your Prototypes
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can create a prototype if you have {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} in hand. When you reach certain Artificer levels specified in the Artificer Level column of the Arcane Prototypes table, the number of prototypes you can create at the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} increases.

When you create a prototype, choose a spell from the Artificer, Cleric, or Wizard spell list. This expends a number of Arcane Charges equal to the level of the spell, up to the maximum spell level allowed. For example, if you're a level 9 Artificer, you can create up to 3 prototypes, each with a maximum spell level of 3, expending a total of 5 Arcane Charges to do so; you could create two level 1 prototypes and one level 3 prototype; one level 2 prototype and one level 3 prototype, or one level 1 prototype and two level 2 prototypes.

name: Arcane Quirk
entries: As the host of a powerful spirit, the magic within you can be strange and unruly. Though you've learned to control your powers, the arcane energy can still spark to life, often creating strange effects.
Choose one or more of the Arcane Quirks listed below:

items: When activating any of the features from this subclass, First Age technology around you begins to act haywire.
Whenever you make a weapon attack, a radio or cassette player on your person plays a snippet of a song.
Whenever you take damage you cough bubbles.
Spirits find your odor to be incredibly off-putting.
Spirits find your odor to be incredibly attractive.
When you are {@condition unconscious}, your body floats 1 foot off the ground and can be carried by the wind.

When you successfully land a critical hit on a creature, your head randomly transforms into a strange visage such as an anthropomorphic pig head, a crimson-skinned version of yourself with flaming locks, the face of an {@creature Urugama|ObojimaTallGrass}, or a {@item CRT TV & Chicken Timer|ObojimaTallGrass|CRT TV}. This transformation lasts until you transform again or take a long rest.

name: Arcane Refresh
entries: At 14th level, your origami constructs return the magic you lent them when you imbued them with life whenever they are destroyed. When one of your constructs is destroyed, you can regain 10 hit points or regain a spell slot of 2nd level or lower (your choice).
Additionally, when one of your constructs would take damage, you can use your reaction to negate the damage against it. Once you use this ability, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Arcane Response
entries: You have learned to anticipate your enemies well enough to rapidly cast spells in response to their attacks. When you use {@classFeature Studied Response|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|2}, you can cast a spell. The spell must have a casting time of an action and must target only that creature.

name: Architect of Ruin
entries: {@i Architects of Ruin are cool and calculating arcane knights who serve Asmodeus, deploying spells, steel, and subterfuge to win at any cost.}

Asmodeus rules Acheron, the City of Fear. His illriggers scour the timescape, collecting secrets and spells designed to deceive and terrify his opponents. The war he fights against the other archdevils is one of deception and information.

His Architects of Ruin work to make Hell's enemies seem outnumbered and outmaneuvered. These illriggers are skillful spellblades on the battlefield, though some employ tactics such as research, infiltration, and propaganda to play mind games with their quarry. When an Architect of Ruin finally confronts an enemy, the advantage is theirs—they have studied, prepared, and gripped fate within their gauntlet, forcing it to favor them. They hungrily seek the dark arts to arm both themselves and Asmodeus with the impossible.

entries.name: Precepts of Ruin
entries: Architects of Ruin swear an oath to Asmodeus when they join the Order of Desolation. These precepts commit them to destroy Asmodeus's enemies by commanding great magic, causing fear, and sowing distrust.

entries.name: The Battlefield of the Mind
entries: By the time my armies meet yours, you'll be filled with terror and doubt your own strength. I won't have to lift a finger to defeat you.

entries.name: The Proper Secret
entries: Once I know your secrets, I know your weakness.

entries.name: Knowledge Is Power
entries: Lore is as powerful as steel. I learn every detail about my enemy and anticipate their every move, checkmating them before the game even begins.

entries.name: Magic Is Mine to Command
entries: Cunning is also as powerful as steel. I wield the dark arcane arts to manipulate your senses, weaken your resolve, and strengthen my blade. Your soldiers will quake for fear of what dark magics may next cloak my blade.

name: Arctic Predator
entries: Your archetype's wintry history grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Helpless Prey
entries: When you make an attack against a target that has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition while you're more than 5 feet away from it, you don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll as a result of that condition.

entries.name: Ice Walker
entries: {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} composed of ice or snow doesn't cost you extra movement, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks while in icy or snowy terrain.

entries.name: Sure-Footed
entries: You can't have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition unless you also have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

name: Armored Focus
entries: Starting at 15th level, while you are concentrating on a paladin spell, your concentration can't be broken as a result of taking damage.

name: Army of Shadow
entries: At 17th level, you can manipulate multiple shadows simultaneously. When you use Shadow Grasp, you can affect a number of creatures equal to your proficiency bonus.

name: Asmodeus's Blessing
entries: When Asmodeus accepts you as an Architect of Ruin, he grants you access to his infernal knowledge. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}.
In addition, you can also read and write the languages granted by your Forked Tongue, instead of only speaking them.

name: Asmodeus's Interdiction
entries: You learn the following additional interdict boons at the noted illrigger levels. Once you learn an interdict boon granted by this feature, you always know it, and it doesn't count against the number of interdict boons you know.

name: Aspect of Tyranny
entries: The fiendish presence in your demonshard revels in the pain it has wrought. When a creature takes damage from your {@subclassFeature Fiendish Punishment|Barbarian|XPHB|Demonshard|FoEQuickstone|3} or {@subclassFeature Overflowing Malice|Barbarian|XPHB|Demonshard|FoEQuickstone|10} features, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cause one affected creature to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). The creature suffers a -1 penalty to its saving throw for each other creature affected by {@subclassFeature Fiendish Punishment|Barbarian|XPHB|Demonshard|FoEQuickstone|3} or {@subclassFeature Overflowing Malice|Barbarian|XPHB|Demonshard|FoEQuickstone|10} on the same turn. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage and has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature's turns, the creature repeats the save (without a penalty), ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Assemble the Troupe
entries: When you cast {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} using your One Life, Many Roles feature, you can target up to six willing creatures you can see within 30 feet of you with the {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} spell. You choose the appearance each creature takes. While under the effects of the spell cast with this feature, the chosen creatures gain a bonus to Charisma checks equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1).

name: Assertive Attacker
entries: While you are {@condition Bloodied|XPHB}, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} and Monk weapons.

name: Astral Domain
entries: {@i Control the Flow of Space and Planar Magic}

Gods of the Astral Plane are as lost to time and space as the realm they reign over. The Astral Plane fills the gaps between the planes of existence and is an important balancing force in the cosmic ecosystem of the multiverse. Practitioners of this domain see the absence of anything as something and consider the Astral Plane as the ultimate destination of all things. These acolytes follow the ultimate path to their destination, and help shepherd others along their way in a grand mission of entropy. Clerics of the Astral Domain are chaotic by nature, but typically choose to destroy evil where they find it and hasten its inevitable journey to the Astral Plane.

name: Astral Domain Spells
entries: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Astral Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Astral Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Blur|XPHB}, {@spell Guiding Bolt|XPHB}, {@spell Invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell Longstrider|XPHB}, {@spell Starry Wisp|XPHB}

name: Astral Griffon Patron
entries: {@i Control Your Own Extradimensional Space}

You have made a pact with a powerful demigod of the Astral Plane named Criir: a griffon whose control over space, creation, and pocket dimensions extends throughout the multiverse. They aim to expand their eclectic collection of treasures, both magical and mundane. These treasures may be worth very little in the average shop, but to the Astral Griffon, they hold a special place in history or the fabric of existence. Your binding may lead you far and wide in search of foreign Artifacts as quickly as it would a nearby pub for a tarnished locket. Regardless of the task, the Griffon's aims are rarely subject to distinctly good or evil motives.

name: Astral Griffon Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Astral Griffon Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Astral Griffon Spells
rows: {@spell Identify}, {@spell Locate Object}, {@spell Magic Missile}, {@spell Rope Trick}
{@spell Mordenkainen's Private Sanctum}, {@spell Leomund's Secret Chest}

name: Astral Missile
entries: You can cast {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB} without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When you cast it in this way, the darts can target a creature you can't see; if the target isn't within range, the dart flies haphazardly before vanishing through an instantaneous planar tear.

name: At Your Fingertips
entries: When you hit a creature with a Bard cantrip or when a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Bard cantrips, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to deal an extra {@damage 2d6} damage to that creature. You can do so only once per round, on your turn.
The extra damage increases when you reach Bard levels 5 ({@dice 3d6}), 10 ({@dice 5d6}) and 15 ({@dice 8d6}).

name: Augment
entries: You can fiddle with the very essence of your companions, crafting minor improvements and modifications. When you choose this paradigm, you gain 3 splicer points. Each time you gain a level in the tamer class, you gain 1 additional splicer point. You can spend these points to modify your companions with the following augments—features and traits that take effect when you next finish a long rest. Splicer points are shared across all your companions. If a companion is ever released, it loses any augments it had and the splicer points are refunded. Augments can be gained only once unless otherwise stated. See the {@table Splicer Augments|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} table for more details.

entries.name: Surgeon's Tools
entries: You also gain proficiency with surgeon's tools. You can spend 1 hour removing all augments from one companion with your surgeon's tools, causing it to lose all the associated effects. You regain all splicer points spent on that companion and can re-allocate those points as you see fit.

entries.name: Splicer Augments
rows: The creature can breathe only underwater.
The creature can breathe air and water.
The creature gains darkvision out to 60 feet If it already has darkvision, the range is increased by 60 feet up to a maximum of 120 feet.
The creature gains an additional limb, allowing it to have one additional target {@condition grappled} A creature can gain a total of four extra limbs from this augment.
The creature gains a swimming speed of 30 feet If it already has a slower swimming speed, this speed is increased to 30 feet.
The creature sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet.
The creature has advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on hearing.
The creature has advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight
The creature has advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on smell
The creature counts as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift.
The creature gains a climbing speed of 30 feet If it already has a slower climbing speed, this speed is increased to 30 feet.
The creature has advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape a grapple.
The creature has advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws made against effects that would knock it {@condition prone}.
While in contact with a web, the creature knows the exact location of any other creature in contact with the same web The creature ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.
The creature gains a burrowing speed of 15 feet If it already has a slower burrowing speed, this speed is increased to 15 feet It does not leave an opening behind it while burrowing.
When the creature makes a melee attack on its turn, its reach for it is 5 feet greater than normal.

The creature can mimic simple sounds it has heard, such as a person whispering, a baby crying, or an animal chittering A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check The DC equals 8 plus your proficiency bonus.
The creature gains a +1 bonus to its AC It can take this augment a maximum of 3 times, gaining an additional +1 bonus each time.

The first time the creature hits with a weapon attack on its turn, it deals an additional {@damage 1d4} poison damage A creature can take this augment again at 9th level, increasing the bonus to {@damage 2d4} poison damage While a creature has this augment, it can't take the Corrosive Touch or Decaying Touch augments.
The creature can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
The creature has advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks made while not moving.

The first time the creature hits with a weapon attack on its turn, it deals an additional {@damage 1d6} acid damage A creature can take this augment again at 13th level, increasing the bonus to {@damage 2d6} acid damage While a creature has this augment, it can't take the Poisonous Touch or Decaying Touch augments.

The creature gains tremorsense out to 15 feet If it already has tremorsense, the range is increased by 15 feet up to a maximum of 30 feet A creature with tremorsense can detect and pinpoint the origin of vibrations within a specific radius, provided that the monster and the source of the vibrations are in contact with the same ground or substance Tremorsense can't be used to detect flying or incorporeal creatures.
The creature gains a flying speed of 30 feet If it already has a slower flying speed, this speed is increased to 30 feet.

The creature gains blindsight out to 15 feet If it already has blindsight, the range is increased by 15 feet up to a maximum of 30 feet A creature with blindsight can perceive its surroundings without relying on sight, within a specific radius. The creature can't use its blindsight while {@condition deafened}.

The first time the creature hits with a weapon attack on its turn, it deals an additional {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage A creature can take this augment again at 17th level, increasing the bonus to {@damage 2d8} necrotic damage While a creature has this augment, it can't take the Poisonous Touch or Corrosive Touch augments
The creature doesn't provoke opportunity attacks when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

The creature's size is increased by one category In addition, the size of its Hit Dice is increased by 1; add 1 to the creature's maximum hit points for each Hit Dice it has when it gains this augment. Note, this augment can be taken multiple times but can't increase a companion's size beyond that permitted by your tamer level (see {@classFeature Tamer Companion Summary|Tamer|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting|1} table).
footnotes: * Each companion can take this augment 4 times.
** Each companion can take this augment up to 3 times.
*** A companion can benefit from only 1 of these three 'touch' augments, but can take them up to two times (see augment description).

**** This augment can be taken multiple times, but can never cause a companion's size category to increase beyond the maximum size dictated by tamer level (see {@classFeature Tamer Companion Summary|Tamer|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting|1} table)

name: Augmentation Compounds
entries: Through continued experimentation or your natural adaptation to your implants, you can now activate one of the compound options below, in addition to a serum, when you enter your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian||1} or change your chosen serum. The chosen compound lasts for the duration of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian||1}, or until you choose a new compound.

entries.name: Stimulated Senses
entries: You gain {@sense blindsight} out to a range of 30 feet. If you already have {@sense blindsight}, its range increases by 30 feet.

entries.name: Maddening Fumes
entries: Your skin emits aggression-spiking fumes out to 30 feet. While in that area, an enemy's speed is halved, and if it starts its turn there, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and proficiency bonus) or have disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Corrosive Expulsion
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|PHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a spray of caustic chemicals from your implants in a 15-foot cone, or a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide (choose the shape each time). Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and proficiency bonus). Roll a number of d8s equal to your rage damage bonus. On a failed save, a target takes acid damage equal to the total rolled, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Augmentation Compounds
entries: Through continued experimentation or your natural adaptation to your implants, you can now activate one of the compound options below, in addition to a serum, when you enter your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} or change your chosen serum. The chosen compound lasts for the duration of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1}, or until you choose a new compound.

entries.name: Stimulated Senses
entries: You gain {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} out to a range of 30 feet. If you already have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB}, its range increases by 30 feet.

entries.name: Maddening Fumes
entries: Your skin emits aggression-spiking fumes in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. While in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}, an enemy's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved, and if it starts its turn there it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Corrosive Expulsion
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a spray of caustic chemicals from your implants in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}, or a 30-foot {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} that is 5 feet wide (choose the shape each time). Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). Roll a number of d8s equal to your Rage Damage bonus. On a failed save, a target takes Acid damage equal to the total rolled, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Aura Magnification
entries: Starting at 14th level, your manipulation of the light around you becomes masterful. While light-shifted, your Flickering Aura produces sunlight. While dark-shifted, your aura produces magical darkness.

If any of this aura's area overlaps with an area of light or darkness created by a spell equal to or lower than the level of your highest available spell slot, the spell that created the light or darkness is dispelled.

name: Aura of Calm
entries: Starting at 10th level, your presence radiates an aura of soothing natural magic. Whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you receives healing from a spell, that spell restores an additional number of hit points equal to half your druid level. Additionally, all plants that aren't creatures within this aura grow thick and plentiful and are restored to their full vigor. Such plants also become safe to travelers while inside the aura, negating difficult terrain caused by plants, including magical effects such as {@spell entangle} or {@spell spike growth}, and granting advantage on any saving throws made to resist the harmful effects of such spells.

name: Aura of Clarity
entries: You and your allies have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a {@condition Blinded|XPHB} ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there. Additionally, you can see {@condition Invisible|XPHB} creatures within your Aura of Protection.

name: Aura of Clarity
entries: Beginning at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be {@condition blinded} while you are conscious. Additionally, creatures and objects of your choice within this range can't benefit from being {@condition invisible}.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

name: Aura of Disruption
entries: Beginning at 7th level, the arcane energy that hangs around you is volatile to enemy spellcasters. Whenever a hostile creature ends its turn within 10 feet of you while concentrating on a spell, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your paladin spell save DC or lose concentration on the spell. In addition, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be perceived through magical scrying sensors.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

name: Aura of Fraternity
entries: You and your allies deal an extra {@damage 1d4} damage on attacks using Melee weapons or Unarmed Strikes while in your Aura of Protection. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

name: Aura of Liberation (18th Level)
entries: When you reach 18th level in this class, the aura affects creatures within 30 feet of you.

name: Aura of Liberation
entries: Starting at 7th level, you fill nearby creatures with the energy of movement. While you're not {@condition incapacitated}, you and creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you cannot be {@condition grappled} or {@condition restrained}, and {@quickref Underwater Combat|PHB|3|0|ignore penalties on movement and attacks while underwater}. Creatures that are already {@condition grappled} or {@condition restrained} when they enter the aura can spend 5 feet of movement to automatically escape unless they are bound by magic restraints.

name: Aura of Rampant Sickness
entries: You emit an aura of contagion and virulence. When a creature within your Aura of Protection is about to make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on that {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}.

name: Aura of Rejuvenation
entries: You emanate an aura that increases the potency of magical healing and hearty meals Whenever a creature of your choice within 10 feet of you regains hit points from a spell, potion, {@footnote magical effect|A paladin's Lay on Hands is not magical so doesn't trigger this effect.}, or food, it regains an additional {@damage 1d6} hit points*.

When a creature rolls one or more Hit Dice to regain hit points during a short rest, it regains 1 additional hit point for each Hit Dice expended in this way, so long as it spends the majority of the short rest within 10 feet of you.
When you reach 18th level in this class, the range of the aura increases to 30 feet

entries.name: Lay on Hands & Magic
entries: The paladin's Lay on Hands feature is neither a spell nor a magical effect, thus it does not trigger the bonus healing from the Aura of Rejuvenation.

name: Aura of Resilience
entries: When you use your {@classFeature Dig Deep|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|4|Pugilist2024}, you can radiate a protective, unseeable aura in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that originates from you for the next 10 minutes. The aura is inactive while you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. Your allies within the aura gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can use it again.

name: Aura of the River
entries: Starting at 7th level, you emanate an aura that causes the area around you to feel as if wading into a body of water, slowing down your enemies as they approach. The area within 10 feet of you is considered {@quickref difficult terrain||3} for other creatures. You can designate any number of creatures you can see to be unaffected by it (no action required).
In addition, the first time you hit a Large or smaller creature on your turn with a melee attack, you can use your aura to move the target up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you choose.
At 18th level, the area within 30 feet of you, instead of 10 feet, is considered {@quickref difficult terrain||3} for other creatures.

name: Aura of Undeath
entries: As an action, you tap into deep pools of necromantic energy, imbuing your companion with an aura of undeath for the next minute. While imbued with this aura, your companion can, as a bonus action on its turn, force one creature it can see within 15 feet of it to make a Constitution saving throw against your tamer spell save DC. On a failure, the creature takes {@damage 4d8} necrotic damage and your companion gains a number of temporary hit points equal to half the damage dealt.

In addition, for the duration, when your companion would be reduced to 0 hit points, it doesn't fall {@condition unconscious} Instead, it is reduced to 1 hit point and gains one failed death saving throw. If your companion gains three failed death saving throws during the minute, or five failed death saving throws if it has the undead type, it immediately dies. At the end of the minute, your companion drops to 0 hit points, falls {@condition unconscious} and is stable.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Aura of Warmth
entries: You and your allies have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold and Fire damage while in your Aura of Protection.

name: Avalanche Stomp
entries: You become as mighty as an unstoppable glacier. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can stomp the ground to send out a tremor. Each creature of your choice in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, a creature takes Bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 3d6} plus your Strength modifier, and it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

name: Avatar of Nourishment
entries: As a bonus action, you become a wellspring of lifeforce, gaining the following benefits for the next minute:

items: At the start of each of your turns, each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you (including you) regains hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) and gains temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).
As bonus action, you can cast the {@spell revivify} spell without having it prepared and without expending a spell slot (material components are still required).
Whenever a creature within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to grant the creature resistance to that damage.

entries: After you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

name: Avoidance
entries: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

name: Backup Battery
entries: At 15th level, you learn to draw on the spirit energy within you to gain a quick rush of energy. You gain an additional use of your {@classFeature Second Wind|Fighter||1} feature. When your hit points drop below your fighter level while you have a use of {@classFeature Second Wind|Fighter||1}, you can choose to expend a use of {@classFeature Second Wind|Fighter||1} immediately (no action required).

name: Bad Attitude
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} skill if you don't have it already. Additionally, you gain a bonus to checks using this skill equal to your Strength modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

name: Bad Luck Charm
entries: You have the ability to cast a sliver of your curse onto another temporarily. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. The chosen creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} it makes before the start of your next turn.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you spend 1 Sorcery Point (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Bad Medicine
entries: When you craft a potion, you can choose to expend a spell slot without choosing a spell to craft a dose of Bad Medicine. When you create a dose, choose one effect per level of the spell slot expended.

items: The creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.
The creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved.
The creature takes an extra {@damage 1d4} Necrotic damage the first time it takes damage each turn.
The creature takes {@damage 1d6} Poison damage each time it takes an action, {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.
The creature takes Acid damage equal to the level of the spell slot expended at the start of each of its turns.

entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can hurl a dose of Bad Medicine at a point you can see within 30 feet. Creatures within 10 feet of that point must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target suffers one of the chosen effects for 1 minute. On each of its turns, the target can take an action and repeat the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Bang, You're Dead!
entries: You can use magic in place of guns.

entries.name: Finger Guns
entries: You learn the {@spell Finger Guns|ValdaGunslinger} cantrip.

entries.name: Arcane Shot
entries: When you hit a target with a {@spell Finger Guns|ValdaGunslinger} attack, you can expend one {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and add it to the damage roll.

name: Bare Knuckle Boxer
entries: Your attacks with {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} can score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}.

name: Barrow Guard
entries: {@i Command the Might of the Grave}

Barrow Guards are warriors who harness the power of the dead, taking upon themselves spectral energies normally forbidden to the living. Some Barrow Guards are those returned from the dead through magical miracles or the whims of the gods. Others stand at the doors of sacred crypts, ready to push back any who attempt to desecrate the dead. No matter their origin, these stoic sentinels are unconcerned with matters of the living. They are separate, other, and duty-bound to their role as crypt-keepers, ensuring the dead—heroes and villains alike—remain at rest.

name: Barrow Guard
entries: {@i Command the Might of the Grave}

Barrow Guards are warriors who harness the power of the dead, taking upon themselves spectral energies normally forbidden to the living. Some Barrow Guards are those returned from the dead through magical miracles or the whims of the gods. Others stand at the doors of sacred crypts, ready to push back any who attempt to desecrate the dead. No matter their origin, these stoic sentinels are unconcerned with matters of the living. They are separate, other, and duty-bound to their role as crypt-keepers, ensuring the dead—heroes and villains alike—remain at rest.

name: Battle Hymn
entries: You unflaggingly maintain the spirits and discipline of your unit. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can start a Battle Hymn which can be heard by all creatures within 60 feet. The hymn lasts until the start of your next turn. While the hymn is active, whenever an ally within 30 feet who can hear you makes an ability check or a saving throw, they can add {@dice 1d4} to the ability check or save.

name: Battle Ready
entries: Your combat training and your experiments with magic have paid off in two ways:

entries.name: Arcane Empowerment
entries: When you attack with a magic weapon, you can use your Intelligence modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, for the attack and damage rolls.

entries.name: Weapon Knowledge
entries: You gain proficiency with Martial weapons. You can use a weapon with which you have proficiency as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Artificer spells.

name: Battle Sagas
entries: You have learned to channel the power from the Eddas, epic poems of heroes, monsters, and gods ingrained into the hearts and minds of the Northlanders. You can spend 1 minute reciting selected passages from the Eddas. When you do so, each creature your choice (other than you) within 60 feet, that can hear you, gains several benefits for 1 hour.

items: It has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions.
Its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point Maximum} increases by {@dice 2d10}, and it gains the same number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Once per turn, when the creature makes an attack roll or saving throw, it can add {@dice 1d4} to the roll or save.

entries: During the same one-hour period, you gain the following benefit.

When an ally you can see who is under the effect of your Battle Sagas fails a saving throw, attack roll, or ability check, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration. The ally can roll your Bardic Inspiration die and add it to their failed result, possibly making it a success.
Once you use your Battle Sagas feature, you can't use it again until you complete a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Battle-Fury
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can throw aside all concern for defence to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength, a bonus to damage rolls equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down), and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

name: Battlefield Harvester
entries: You augment your companions with a highly adaptive mutagen, allowing them to gain the strengths of foes they defeat and confer it to your other companions through a synchronous quantum biomantic link.

As an action, you can command your companion to consume the corpse of a non-swarm creature that has been dead for less than 1 minute. Choose one of the consumed creature's damage resistances, damage immunities, or condition immunities (except immunity to {@condition exhaustion}. All of your companions gain resistance to one damage type to which the slain creature was resistant or immune, or gain immunity to one condition to which the creature was immune.

After you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. When you use this feature again, your companions lose any benefit they had previously gained from this feature Consuming a corpse in this way prevents it from being harvested for components.

name: Bear Witness
entries: You have prepared your entire life for the end of the world. While your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Apocalyptic Inurement
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Force damage.

entries.name: Recite Scripture
entries: Once per active Innate Sorcery, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you can use a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} that has a spell with a casting time of {@variantrule Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Unflappable
entries: You are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

name: Beastborne
entries: {@i Channel Lycanthropic Fury}

Whether by infected bite or insidious curse, your blood was infected with the magic of lycanthropy. A ferocious, bestial form lies just beneath your skin, awaiting the allure of blood and the thrill of a hunt. Perhaps, if you can avoid the violence or the siren call of moonlight, you can resist the lycanthropic urge. Or perhaps you might embrace the infection as a blessing or wield it as a fearsome weapon.

name: Beat Down
entries: Immediately after you miss a creature under the effect of your Size Up feature with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a melee attack against that creature if it's within range. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the new attack roll against that creature.

name: Become Death
entries: You can transmute your physical form into a spectral one when near death. When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead and gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum. At the start of each of your turns, you lose 10 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} and creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you take 10 Necrotic damage. While you have {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} granted by this feature, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage, a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet, can {@variantrule Hover|XPHB}, and you can move through occupied spaces as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. If you end your turn in such a space, you are shunted to the last unoccupied space you were in.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Belial's Interdiction
entries: You learn the following additional interdict boons at the noted illrigger levels. Once you learn an interdict boon granted by this feature, you always know it, and it doesn't count against the number of interdict boons you know.

name: Belly Concoction
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you learn the hard-earned skill of belly brewing, an arcane technique in which you swallow, mix, and brew magical concoctions inside your gut, creating a number of unique effects.

When you enter your rage, you focus your energy to harness and activate the effects of a belly concoction. Choose combat, utility, or whimsy. You gain the effects of the chosen belly concoction, as detailed below. You can change your belly concoction each time you rage.

entries.name: Combat
entries: Your body undergoes a unique change which magically alters your physical form, giving it the characteristics of rubber. While in this elastic state, you can use your reaction when you are hit by a ranged attack, deflecting it with your belly. When you do so, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by {@dice 1d12} + your Constitution modifier + your barbarian level.

Additionally, immediately before you make a melee weapon attack on your turn, you can use your bonus action to stretch your arms, increasing your reach by 5 feet for the rest of the turn. The first time you hit while your arms are stretched in this way, the attack deals an extra {@dice 1d6} damage of the weapon's type.

entries.name: Utility
entries: The bubbling elixir in your stomach is perfectly mixed to dissolve and absorb anything you can swallow. As a bonus action, you can consume any object you can fit in your mouth. When you do so, you can expend one of your Hit Dice as part of this bonus action to heal yourself.
