Roll the die, add your Constitution modifier, and regain a number of hit points equal to the total (minimum of 1). Swallowing an object in this way destroys it, provided the object isn't magical. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Whimsy
entries: You focus on the magical brew inside you, only to get an array of strange and unruly effects. While in this state, you gain one of the following effects at the start of each of your turns:

items: You teleport to an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you that you can see.
You take {@dice 1d4} necrotic damage; the next ability check you make before the end of your turn gains a bonus equal to the number rolled.
You can immediately take the {@action Help} action as a bonus action.

Additionally, you gain a random visual effect that accompanies the other whimsical features, such as your hair turns to moss, a spectral bird circles above your head, or a tattoo of a dancing man appears on your person and moves about your body.

name: Bend Reality
entries: When an ally you can see within 30 feet of yourself fails a saving throw, you can replace the roll with a 20, potentially changing the outcome. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Bestial Aspect
entries: In the throes of combat, you gradually lose control and slip into a beastlike form. The degree of your transformation is represented by your Bestial Aspect Level, which starts at 0. Your Bestial Aspect Level grants you benefits, as shown on the Bestial Aspect table. You gain all the benefits of your Bestial Aspect Level and lower.

When you deal damage to an enemy, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to increase your Bestial Aspect Level by 1. If you don't deal damage to an enemy for 1 minute, your Bestial Aspect Level resets to 0.

entries.caption: Bestial Aspect
rows: {@b Carnage.} You gain a +2 bonus to your damage rolls with weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}.
{@b Fast Movement.} Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet.
{@b Blood Frenzy.} You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
{@b Thick Hide.} If you aren't wielding a {@item Shield|XPHB}, you gain a +2 bonus to AC.

{@b Retaliation.} When you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of yourself, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make one melee attack against that creature, using a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strike}.

name: Better Half
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead, and you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum. In addition, if your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} ends. If your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} was not active, you immediately activate your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} (even if you have no remaining uses of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1}). If any of these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} remain after 1 minute, they vanish.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Bewitched Effigy
entries: Your primal magic can manifest as a wicker effigy and radiate out from it. As a bonus action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape to create a wicker effigy in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself.

The effigy is a Small object (AC 15; HP equal to five times your druid level; vulnerability to fire damage; immunity to poison and psychic damage). The effigy vanishes after 1 minute, when reduced to 0 hit points, or when you use this feature again. It creates one of the following auras (chosen when you create the effigy) in a 30-foot radius that is filled with {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light}.

entries.name: Sacrifice
entries: When a creature in the aura takes damage, you can use your reaction to deal fire damage to the creature equal to {@dice 1d8} plus your Wisdom modifier.

entries.name: Soothe
entries: When you create the effigy, and as a bonus action on subsequent turns while the effigy remains, one creature that you can see within the aura regains {@dice 1d6} hit points. You can use this effigy to restore hit points a number of times equal to twice your spellcasting ability modifier.

entries.name: Ward
entries: You and your allies within the aura gain a +1 bonus to AC.

name: Bewitched Effigy
entries: Your primal magic can manifest as a wicker effigy and radiate out from it. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape to create a wicker effigy in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself.

The effigy is a Small object (AC 15; HP equal to five times your Druid level; {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire damage; {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage). The effigy vanishes after 1 minute, when reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, or when you use this feature again. It radiates one of the following auras (chosen when you create the effigy) in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that is filled with {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sacrifice
entries: When a creature in the aura takes damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to deal Fire damage to the creature equal to {@dice 1d8} plus your Wisdom modifier.

entries.name: Soothe
entries: When you create the effigy, and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on subsequent turns while the effigy remains, one creature that you can see within the aura regains {@dice 1d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. You can use this effigy to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} a number of times equal to twice your spellcasting ability modifier.

entries.name: Ward
entries: You and your allies within the aura gain a +1 bonus to AC.

name: Beyond Space
entries: The nature of distance and location is revealed for the lie that it is. You add the {@spell Scrying} spell to your spellbook, if it's not there already.
When you cast {@spell Scrying}, you can risk Intrusion to choose one of the following.

entries.name: All Knowing
entries: Treat your connection to a target creature as if you have part of its body.

entries.name: All Seeing
entries: Change the spell's casting time to 1 action. When you cast {@spell Scrying}, during the spell's duration, you can cause an automatic Intrusion (and increase the die's size one step, up to its starting size) to teleport yourself, and any willing creatures within 10 feet of you, to unoccupied spaces you can see through the scrying sensor. Once you teleport in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Beyond Space
entries: The nature of distance and location is revealed for the lie that it is. You always have the {@spell Scrying|XPHB} spell prepared.
When you cast {@spell Scrying|XPHB}, you can risk Intrusion to choose one of the following.

entries.name: All Knowing
entries: Treat your connection to a target creature as if you have part of its body.

entries.name: All Seeing
entries: Cast the spell as an action instead of its normal casting time.

When you cast {@spell Scrying|XPHB}, during the spell's duration, as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action you can cause an automatic Intrusion (and increase the die's size one step, up to its starting size) to teleport yourself, and any willing creatures within 10 feet of you, to unoccupied spaces you can see through the scrying sensor.

name: Bibliomancy

entries: Books are a uniquely portable magic.

A spellbook is a Wizard's prized possession. Even the least experienced apprentice knows that each spell's formula must be carefully recorded, understood, and memorized to cast a spell properly. For the typical Wizard, the symbols, words, and equations in a spellbook are a means to an end.

For Bibliomancers, the language of magic is the key to the building blocks of the universe. This tradition believes that a spell's formula holds more than the gathering and shaping magical energy, that the underlying properties of reality itself are illustrated through a spell. By unlocking the mechanisms that construct spells, these Wizards can slowly unlock the riddle of the universe.

name: Binding Release
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can use a bonus action to move one of your origami constructs to a creature that you can see within 30 feet of it.

name: Biochemical Admixture
entries: Your body focuses and combines the strength of your serums. When you activate an option of your {@subclassFeature Volatile Serum|Barbarian|PHB|Experiment|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14}, you activate two options instead of one. Additionally, when a creature within 5 feet of you damages you with a melee attack while your rage is active, the creature takes {@damage 1d12} acid damage. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

name: Biochemical Admixture
entries: Your body focuses and combines the strength of your serums. When you activate an option of your {@subclassFeature Volatile Serum|Barbarian|XPHB|Experiment|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24}, you activate two options instead of one.

Additionally, when a creature within 5 feet of you damages you with a melee attack while your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, the creature takes {@damage 1d12} Acid damage. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

name: Biomancy Savant
entries: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy a biomancy spell into your spellbook is halved In addition, you gain proficiency with surgeon's tools, and the following spells are considered biomancy spells for you instead of their normal school.

name: Biorhythm
entries: At 6th level, you learn to channel the leyline's energies to augment your body's natural healing. As long as you are attuned to a leyline, whenever you use your {@classFeature Arcane Recovery|Wizard|PHB|1|PHB} feature to regain expended spell slots, you regain {@dice 1d8} hit points for each spell slot you recover.
Additionally, when you complete a short rest in a natural setting, you can attune yourself to a different leyline, following the rules of your Natural Attunement feature.

name: Biostimulation
entries: You learn to channel biomantic magic into your cells, restoring your vitality When you cast a biomancy spell of 1st level or higher, you can simultaneously redirect a strand of the spell's magic to energise and repair you or your target's body You or your target (your choice) regains a number of hit points equal to twice the spell's level.

name: Bird Caller
entries: Also at 3rd level, you learn to identify common birds by their calls, and you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) checks when interacting with any {@filter beast that has an innate flying speed|bestiary|type=beast|speed type=fly}. In addition, you gain the ability to cast the {@spell animal messenger} spell, but only as a ritual and only targeting a beast that has an innate flying speed.

name: Birth Parasite
entries: Over the course of 1 minute, you can extrude an independent piece of your patron, causing it to manifest in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you This parasite acts as a familiar, as if with the {@spell find familiar} spell See this creature's game statistics in the {@creature parasitic ooze|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places.
If you have the Pact of the Chain feature, the parasite counts as a familiar for you for the purpose of applying any benefits from that feature or your invocations.
After you birth a parasite, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest. If you use this feature while you already have a parasite, the previous one dissolves in a puddle of goo.

name: Black Magic
entries: At 13th level, you can draw more power from the shadows bound to you. As a bonus action, you can cast {@spell darkness} without providing material components. Once you use this feature three times, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

Additionally, when you are in an area of dim light or darkness, you can use your action to become {@condition invisible}. You remain invisible until you make an attack, cast a spell, or are in an area of bright light.

name: Black Magic
entries: As a result of your relationship with your dread power, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Two Cantrips
entries: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Warlock spell list. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for your Black Magic spells.

entries.name: Level 1 Spell
entries: Choose a level 1 spell from the Warlock spell list. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.

entries.name: Spell Change
entries: Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose with this feature with a different spell of the same level from the Warlock spell list.

name: Blade Breaker
entries: Fighters who emulate the legends of the Blade Breaker strive to be the embodiment of change. Their blade and warrior's spirit are tools through which they project their will upon the world in the form of martial magic. Many who follow the Saga of the Blade Breaker are stubborn, and would sooner force reality itself to bend before their desires than change their ways. Some are idealists, who have a vision for a better world and would do anything to achieve it. Others are tyrants, and see the world as putty to be molded, and all its inhabitants as mere hindrances to their ultimate glory.

entries.subclassFeature: Stance of the Blade Breaker|Fighter||Blade Breaker|GrimHollowPlayerPack|3

name: Blade Breaker Maneuvers
entries: These maneuvers can be used by anyone who studies the Blade Breaker saga. Tales of the Blade Breaker focus on his relentless determination, which granted him seemingly inexhaustible strength and a mystical ability to shape reality.

name: Blade of Radiance
entries: The Blades of Radiance, also called Steel Saints, are known to be one of the most lethal orders of the Church. In order to become a blade, one must be a devout follower of the faith, as only those who would die for the cause are deemed worthy. Prospective members are trained within the walls of the Church, taking on the clergy as their new kin and discarding whatever familial bonds they might have held onto. Their zealous fervor grants them unrivaled powers on the battlefield, wielding massive weapons as if they were mere toys, infusing their blade with divine powers, and breaking down their foes one by one.

The Blades of Radiance receive an incredibly diverse range of missions. The most brutal of their members handle gruesome matters in a lethal fashion, whereas those of a more empathetic temperament are tasked with protecting their fellows. Despite this sundry in character, they all share one goal: safeguarding the Church and its members, no matter what.

name: Blessed Chosen
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can assert your divine will to protect your allies. When an enemy within 30 feet of you that you can see attacks one of your allies, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll before it hits or misses.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Blessed Chosen
entries: Beginning at 11th level, you are protected by the forces who spur your mission. If you are reduced to 0 hit points, you immediately regain hit points equal to your monk level. Alternatively, you can use an action to touch a fallen creature that has been dead for no longer than 10 minutes, and they return to life with hit points equal to your monk level.
You must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.

name: Blessing of the Hearth
entries: From 1st level, you gain the ability to conjure a small flagstone hearth with a simple iron cooking pot whenever you rest. This hearth helps warm you and your companions, and can be used to prepare hearty and nutritious meals on the road. If you or any friendly creatures you make camp with would regain hit points at the end of a short rest by spending one or more hit dice, each of those creatures may choose to re-roll one of their resting dice, taking the higher roll between the two.
Additionally, you gain proficiency with {@item Cook's Utensils|PHB}.

name: Blessing of the Seasons
entries: You can draw upon the powers of the harvest cycle to potentially avert disaster. When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw of a particular type determined by your current aspect, you can use your reaction to allow it to reroll the {@dice d20} and use the new roll. The type of saving throws you can affect are as follows.

entries.name: Sowing
entries: Dexterity and Charisma

entries.name: Growing
entries: Constitution and Intelligence

entries.name: Reaping
entries: Wisdom and Strength
Additionally, after the saving throw succeeds or fails, roll a number of d4s equal to your proficiency bonus. The target regains hit points equal to the total rolled.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Blessing of the Seasons
entries: You can draw upon the powers of the harvest cycle to potentially avert disaster. When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw of a particular type determined by your current aspect, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to allow it to reroll the {@dice d20} and use the new roll. The type of saving throws you can affect are as follows.

entries.name: Sowing
entries: Dexterity and Charisma

entries.name: Growing
entries: Constitution and Intelligence

entries.name: Reaping
entries: Wisdom and Strength

Additionally, after the saving throw succeeds or fails, roll a number of d4s equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. The target regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the total rolled.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Blighted Shape
entries: Also at 2nd level, your physical form begins to show effects of the corruption you wield, tracing blackened veins across your skin, producing gnarled, bony protrusions, or other eerie phenomena. You gain proficiency in the Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) skill.

Additionally, while you are transformed by your Wild Shape feature, you gain a +2 bonus to AC as gnarled spines protrude from your body. Your beast form also gains {@sense darkvision} with a radius of 60 feet, or an additional 60 feet of {@sense darkvision} if it already has that sense.

name: Blindside
entries: At 10th level, you are truly skilled at exploiting the openings you create in combat, hitting off-guard opponents with precise blows that are swift and deadly. You may use this technique against any creature that hasn't yet taken a turn in combat, or who you have successfully misdirected this turn. You may also apply this technique to any attack roll you make with advantage. On a hit, you exploit an opening in the target's defenses, dealing an extra {@damage 5d6} points of damage. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you have taken a short or long rest.
At 15th level, the damage dealt by your blindside increases to {@damage 7d6}.
At 18th level the damage dealt by your blindside increases to {@damage 9d6}. If you have no uses of this ability at the beginning of combat on your turn, you regain one use of it.

name: Blood Armament
entries: While you are wielding a weapon and do not have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, that weapon is considered blood-coated. Such a weapon can deal your choice of Acid, Necrotic, or Poison damage instead of its normal damage type.

name: Blood Boon
entries: Whenever a creature you can see within 60 feet of you is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to claim the last vestiges of its vitality. You regain 1 spent {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die} and grant a creature you can see within 60 feet of you {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Druid level.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once). You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Blood Channeling
entries: When you choose this arcane tradition at 2nd level, you are able to use your own depleted life essence to channel your magical abilities. Whenever your current hit points are below your hit point maximum, you can use your own body as an {@item arcane focus|PHB}.

In addition, when casting a wizard spell that requires a costly material component, you can forego the component by taking {@damage 1d10} necrotic damage per 50 gp of the cost of the component (minimum {@damage 1d10}). This damage can't be reduced in any way. If this damage reduces you to 0 hit points, the spell fails but the spell slot is not expended.

name: Blood Domain
entries: Developed in {@book Wildemount|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Wildemount} by the {@book Claret Orders|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|Claret Orders}, the Blood Domain centers around the understanding of the natural life force as it exists within the body, and the divine conduit it can become. Those who take up this domain understand that the power of blood is the power of sacrifice, the balance of life and death, and the spirit's anchor within the mortal shell.

Gods who grant the power of the Blood Domain, including {@deity The Ruiner|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} and {@deity The Matron of Ravens|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, direct their followers to tap into the connection between body and soul, exploit the hidden reserves of will within one's own vitality, and corrupt the bodies of others through the secret rites of {@variantrule hemocraft|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}. Clerics of good gods use {@variantrule hemocraft|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} to fill their self-sacrifice with purpose and power, while clerics with fewer morals use the blood of others to achieve their own malevolent ends.

name: Blood Explosion
entries: When you make an attack roll with a blood-coated weapon and miss, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to detonate the blood. The target and each creature other than you in a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes damage as if it were hit by the weapon. On a successful save, a target takes half damage.

name: Blood for Blood
entries: Once on each of your turns when you deal damage to one or more creatures with a Wizard spell you cast, you can spend a {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} or a Sangromancy Die, roll the die, and deal extra damage to one of those creatures equal to the roll. If the creature is {@condition Bloodied|XPHB}, you can roll twice and use the higher of the two rolls.

name: Blood Hound
entries: Blood Hounds are cursed beings that should not exist. Birthed from nightmarish experiments by the Obitus Scholare, these hunters use a cursed method of fighting, weaving their own blood into attacks to produce supernatural effects. Their powers come from tarblood, an amalgamation of hundreds of species' blood that was forcefully injected in the veins of hunters. Those who didn't die or go insane during the procedure became the first Blood Hounds; only they and their descendants can wield this vicious power.

name: Blood Hound Anatomy
entries: Your body adapts to the tarblood within. You are immune to magical contagions, have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage, and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

In addition, once you've fought a creature, you can relentlessly track it, sensing the blood of your prey. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}) check you make to find a creature to which you have dealt damage and that has blood.

name: Blood Knight
entries: Your bloodthirst imbues you with preternatural strength and resilience, allowing you to keep sowing slaughter. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Crimson Armor
entries: When a creature within your Aura of Protection becomes {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} by an enemy, you gain 30 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Seeing Red
entries: When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make one melee attack against that creature, using a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: Wanton Slaughter
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can choose any number of creatures within 5 feet of the original target and within your reach. Each chosen creature takes Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Blood Lust
entries: While your Blood Moon is active, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Improved Violent Strikes
entries: The extra Necrotic damage from your Violent Strikes increases to {@dice 2d6}.

items.name: Red Rage
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

name: Blood Magic
entries: Considered taboo by many societies and magic practitioners, the use of blood magic—also known as {@variantrule hemocraft|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}—is a rare art that harnesses the latent powers of a creature's vitality to fuel and amplify the caster's own capabilities, while manipulating and weakening the bodies of enemies from the inside. Some of the more macabre mages seeking to empower their arcane pursuits turn to {@variantrule hemocraft|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} as a means of bolstering their spells, giving their own life's blood to reach new heights of frightening magical prowess.

The secrets of {@variantrule hemocraft|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} and other forms of blood magic were once the sole purview of the mysterious {@book Claret Orders|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|Claret Orders}. In recent years, however, these secrets have begun to spread beyond the order's members and into the hands of less scrupulous mages. Blood magic has a bad reputation in Tal'Dorei, even though its powers can be used for much more than evil.

name: Blood of Creation
entries: You further your insight into the tarblood within yourself. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you roll the Blood Cost of a Blood Strike you can reroll the result and choose the lower number.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one Blood Strike option you know with a different one.

name: Blood Strike
entries: You learn to unleash the destructive properties of your blood. When you gain this feature, you learn three {@filter Blood Strike|optionalfeatures|feature type=bs} options of your choice.

Once per turn when you make a weapon attack as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can apply one of your Blood Strike options to that attack. You can decide to use the option before or after the attack hits, unless the option doesn't involve an attack roll. When you use a Blood Strike, you take Necrotic damage equal to one roll of its Blood Cost. This damage can't be reduced or prevented in any way. A Blood Strike is considered a magical effect.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to 1 + your Constitution modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

You learn an additional Blood Strike option of your choice when you reach Fighter levels 5, 9, 13, and 17. Each time you learn a new Blood Strike option, you can also replace one Blood Strike you know with a different one.

entries.name: Blood Strike Save DC
entries: If a feature of this subclass requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Blood Strike Options
entries: The Blood Strike feature lets you choose options at certain levels, which are presented here in alphabetical order. These options use your Blood Strike save DC.

name: Blood Symphony
entries: All are unmade by the blood. Whenever you use a Blood Strike, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). In addition, if the target dies within 1 minute of being damaged by a Blood Strike, you regain one expended use of your Blood Strike feature.

name: Blood Ties
entries: Your senses easily attune to the supernatural forces that caused your inherited affliction. You always have the {@spell Detect Evil and Good|XPHB} spell prepared and can cast it without expending a spell slot.

In addition, choose one of the following types of creatures as the being that cursed your ancestor: Fey, Fiend, or Undead. On each of your turns while you maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on {@spell Detect Evil and Good|XPHB}, including the turn when you cast it, creatures of the chosen type have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against you, and you can't be possessed, {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} by such creatures.
Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Blood Well
entries: You hold a reserve of vital energy called your Blood Well, which you can use to empower your magic and fuel other powers from this subclass. When you deal damage or restore hit points to a creature, you can expend your Blood Well to add {@dice 1d8} to the total for one target.
You regain your expended Blood Well when you finish a long rest or when a creature takes 10 or more necrotic damage from you at one time.

name: Blood Well
entries: You hold a reserve of vital energy called your Blood Well, which you can use to empower your magic and fuel other powers from this subclass. When you deal damage or restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to a creature, you can expend your Blood Well to add {@dice 1d8} to the total for one target.
You regain your expended Blood Well when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} or when a creature takes 10 or more Necrotic damage from you at one time.

name: Bloodbound
entries: By 17th level, you can command the blood inside certain creatures. Immediately after you deal Sneak Attack damage to a beast or humanoid, you can force that creature to make a Constitution saving throw. The DC is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier. On a failed save, that creature is under the effect of the {@spell dominate beast} or {@spell dominate person} spell, respectively, for 1 minute or until you choose to end the effect (no action required).
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Blooded Clarity
entries: At 18th level, when you become wounded, your senses heighten and your focus improves. While you have less than half your hit points, you add a {@dice d10} to the first attack roll or saving throw you make each turn.
Additionally, while you have less than half your hit points, maneuvers you use cost 1 less maneuver point to use (minimum 1 point).

name: Bloodhound
entries: {@i Follow your Mark to the Bitter End}

Rangers recognise the primal connections between all living things, and as a Bloodhound you know precisely how to exploit them to track down your chosen prey. The Western Frontier is home to countless fugitives and war criminals, and House Tharashk trains its best bounty hunters to follow these ancient techniques— while on the other side of the Border Road, Znir hunters and worgs of the Great Pack use the skills of the Bloodhound to track enemies of Droaam.

name: Bloodhound Spells
entries: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Bloodhound Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

name: Bloodletting Focus
entries: Starting at 1st level, your divine magic draws the blood from magically inflicted wounds, worsening the agony of your foes. When you cast a damage-dealing spell of 1st level or higher whose duration is instantaneous, any creature with blood that takes damage from the spell takes extra necrotic damage equal to 2 + the spell's level.

name: Bloodstitch
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can spend 3 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} or Sangromancy Dice to fling a wave of needle-like blood shards. When you do so, each creature of your choice in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking {@damage 3d8} Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. You regain 1 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die} or Sangromancy Die (your choice) for each creature reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} by this feature.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Bloodstroke
entries: The magic that shields your allies now also saps their enemies' strength. When an ally who has temporary hit points from your Exsanguinate feature is hit by a melee attack, the attacker takes cold, fire, or necrotic damage (your choice) equal to your illrigger level.

name: Bloodthirst Aura
entries: Your lust for blood infects those around you. When a {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} ally within your Aura of Protection makes an attack with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, it gains a bonus to damage. The bonus equals your Charisma modifier.

Additionally, when a {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} creature within your Aura of Protection makes a saving throw against a {@filter Sangromancy spell|spells|subschool=sangromancy}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the save.

name: Bloodthirsty Fury
entries: You have gained control over your bestial rage, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Bestial Mark
entries: You can cast {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} as a part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to increase your Bestial Aspect Level.

entries.name: Greater Carnage
entries: The damage bonus of your Carnage benefit increases to +3.

name: Bloody Blades
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can spend up to 2 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} or Sangromancy Dice to create a number of Daggers equal to the number of dice spent in this way. Each Dagger counts as an Arcane Focus for your Sanguine Thief spells, and you can cast spells with Somatic components even if you wield these weapons in one or both hands.

Additionally, when you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} with this weapon, you can cause the weapon to deal extra damage to the target. The extra damage is a number of d8s equal to the number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} or Sangromancy Dice spent on this feature. The extra damage is Necrotic.
The Daggers lasts until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Bloody Exit
entries: When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and spend 5 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} or Sangromancy Dice to turn into bloody mist. The attack automatically misses you, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, and you regain your normal form. As part of this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can make an attack with a Melee weapon immediately after you teleport. On a hit, this attack deals an extra {@damage 5d8} Necrotic damage to the target.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Boiling Power
entries: At 14th level, your oni traits grow in strength. The following changes apply to your traits:

entries.name: Eyes
entries: In addition to the benefits you normally have, you learn the {@spell Zone of Truth} spell, which you can cast without expending a spell slot. When you cast it, only one creature of your choice within 60 feet of you is affected by the spell. The target must make its saving throw against the spell at the start of each of its turns, provided it can see your eyes; the spell ends early if the target can no longer see your eyes.

entries.name: Horns
entries: The extra damage dealt by your horns increases to {@dice 1d12}.

entries.name: Skin
entries: Whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher, you now regain a number of hit points equal to twice the spell's level + your Constitution modifier.

entries.name: Tongue
entries: When you activate the Tongue trait using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, in place of the trait's normal effects, you can instead cause the target to tremble in fear, becoming hyper fixated on you. The target's passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score is reduced to 5 and it takes a -5 penalty to its AC against all attacks that aren't made by you. This effect lasts until the start of your next turn.

name: Bolstering Howl
entries: When you or another creature that can hear you takes damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to grant it {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} against that damage. In addition, the target gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage type until the end of the current turn.

name: Bolstering Presence
entries: At the start of your turn, you can bolster your allies (no action required). Creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 2d6} plus half your Fighter level (rounded down). You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Bond of Mutual Suffering (14th Level)
entries: At 14th level, you can use this feature twice between rests.

name: Bond of Mutual Suffering
entries: At 6th level, when a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to bind your vitality to the attacker and force them to share your pain. The attacker takes damage equal to the damage you took.
This feature cannot be used against constructs or undead. You can use this feature once. You must finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest} before you can use it again.

name: Bond of Shelter
entries: Once you reach 14th level, your service to the natural balance is rewarded, and nature itself rises to protect you and your allies from harm. As an action, you can create a 30-foot radius, 20-foot tall cylinder of protective energy, centered on you. This cylinder lasts for 1 hour and does not move from its original location.

As long as you are on the Material Plane or an elemental plane, natural features within the cylinder, including plants, trees, rocks, and water (as well as wind, water, earth, or fire, if on an elemental plane) animate to defend you. If you are in a setting, such as an indoor area, where natural features are not present, then plants, trees, rocks, and other natural elements sprout from the floor before animating.
When you activate this ability, choose any number of creatures you are familiar with and can see to be immune to the cylinder's effect. All other creatures are subject to the following effects:

items: Creatures can't willingly enter the cylinder unless they succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. The cylinder also protects the area against planar travel for the duration, preventing any creature from accessing the area by way of the Astral Plane, Ethereal Plane, Feywild, Shadowfell, or the {@spell plane shift} spell.
Creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls against targets within the cylinder.
Targets of your choice within the cylinder can't be {@condition charmed}, {@condition frightened}, or possessed by creatures inside or outside the cylinder.
When a creature enters the cylinder for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, the creature takes {@damage 5d10} magical bludgeoning damage from the animated nature within.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Bone Puppetry
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you target one creature you can see within 60 feet of you that has a skeleton. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or you take total and precise control of its skeleton. Until the end of the creature's next turn, it takes only the actions you choose and doesn't do anything that you don't allow it to do. In the creature's efforts to resist your command, attack rolls it makes against its allies have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, and its allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws from effects caused by the creature.

You can only have one such creature under your control at a time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Bonus Cantrip
entries: You know one cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|level=0|class=sorcerer} (see the Sorcerer class's section of the Player's Handbook for a list of Sorcerer spells). {@spell Fire Bolt|XPHB} is recommended. The cantrip counts as a Bard cantrip for you, but it doesn't count against the number of Bard cantrips you know.
Additionally, you can use a Wand, Rod, or Orb as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Bard spells.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: Also at 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons. You also gain proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion} skill.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor, martial weapons, {@item brewer's supplies|PHB}, and {@item cook's utensils|PHB}.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency with two {@filter martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} of your choice. You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Animal Handling}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Survival}.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: When you join the College of the Road at 3rd level, you gain a few useful proficiencies picked up from your time on the road. Choose three of the following options (each option can only be selected once):

items: You gain proficiency with a {@item Gaming Set|PHB} of your choice.
You gain proficiency with a {@filter martial weapon|items|type=martial weapon=sand|category=|miscellaneous=mundane;!reprinted} of your choice
You gain proficiency with {@item Herbalism Kit|phb|Herbalism Kits}
You gain proficiency with {@item Thieves' Tools|PHB}
You gain proficiency with a skill of your choice
You learn two languages of your choice

name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: Starting at 1st level, your patron grants you enhanced tracking skills. You gain expertise with the {@skill Survival} skill, and you add double your proficiency bonus to any Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) skill checks you make.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: When you choose this path at 3rd level, you become proficient in two of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Performance}, {@skill Persuasion}, and {@skill Riddle|TLotRR}. If you are already proficient in any one of them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: When you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Medicine} skill and with the {@item herbalism kit|PHB}. If you are already proficient in any one of them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: When you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Old Lore|TLotRR} skill and with {@item calligrapher's supplies|PHB}. If you are already proficient in any one of them, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Arcana} skill.

name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: When you choose this Martial Archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Sleight of Hand}, or {@skill Stealth}. Alternatively, you may learn {@class rogue|phb|Thieves' Cant||phb|Thieves' Cant 1}.

name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: When you choose this way at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Perception} skill. If you are already proficient, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: When you choose this oath at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Stealth} skill. If you are already proficient, or if you are in one of your warded lands, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: When you choose this oath at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Hunting|TLotRR} skill. If you are already proficient, or when tracking your favoured foes, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.

name: Booby Trap
entries: You trap your own body against unexpected demise. When you finish a long rest, you can choose one of the following magical effects with which to augment your body until you finish a long rest. After triggering an effect that activates when you are reduced to 0 hit points, that effect can't trigger again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Defibrillate
entries: Once per turn, when a creature hits you with a melee attack, you can trigger an electrical discharge (no action required). The creature is unable to take reactions until the start of its next turn unless it is immune to lightning damage, and you can immediately move up to {@b 10 feet} without provoking opportunity attacks. After you move using this feature, you can't do so again until the start of your next turn.

When you are reduced to 0 hit points and not killed outright, you can instead drop to 1 hit point and immediately take an extra turn, interrupting the current turn. If you don't regain any hit points before the end of your next turn, you drop to 0 hit points, fall {@condition unconscious}, and begin making death saving throws as normal.

entries.name: Dissolve
entries: Once per turn, when a creature within {@b 5 feet} of you hits you with a melee attack, you can trigger a spurt of acid to coat its weapon or limb (no action required). If the melee attack was a spell attack or made with a natural weapon, the creature takes {@damage 1d6} acid damage. If the result of the attack roll meets your AC and is made with a ferrous, non-magical, non-natural weapon, the acid causes the metal to weaken and the weapon is destroyed.

When you are reduced to 0 hit points, all your concealed acid charges gush outward. Each creature within {@b 10 feet} of you must make a {@b Dexterity saving throw} against your {@b ranger spell save DC}. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 10d4} acid damage and an additional {@damage 5d4} acid damage at the start of each of its turns for the next {@b minute} until it uses an action to wipe itself clean. In addition, on a failure, if the creature rolled a 1 on the {@dice d20} for its saving throw and is wearing nonmagical, ferrous armour, the armour seizes. While wearing the armour, the creature's speed is halved, its AC is reduced by 2, and it has {@b disadvantage} on Dexterity saving throws.

entries.name: Entomb
entries: Once per turn, when a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, you can trigger a burst of cold that ripples along the attacker's limb (no action required). The creature takes {@damage 1d4} cold damage and its speed is reduced by {@b 15 feet} until the end of its next turn unless it is immune to cold damage.

When you are reduced to 0 hit points, you become entombed in a block of clear ice that has AC 15, 100 hit points, {@b immunity} to cold damage, and vulnerability to fire damage. This icy block lasts for {@b 1 minute} or until it is destroyed. While the ice persists, you have total cover against all effects and you don't make death saving throws. If you regain 1 or more hit points, the icy block melts at the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Self-Destruct
entries: Once per turn, when a creature within {@b 5 feet} of you hits you with a melee attack, you can cause a small, shaped charge to detonate (no action required). You take {@damage 1} fire damage and the creature takes {@damage 1d8} fire damage.

When you are reduced to 0 hit points, you erupt in an immense ball of fire and immediately fail one death saving throw. Each creature within {@b 20 feet} of you must make a {@b Dexterity saving throw} against your {@b ranger spell save DC}. A creature takes {@damage 14d6} fire damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Book Learning
entries: You have an arcane connection to all books, be they tablets or tomes, allowing you to unravel their secrets. If you touch an object containing a script for 1 minute, you learn a basic, working knowledge of the script's contents unless that information is hidden by a code or cypher. If the book or script is a magic item or magical object, you learn its properties and how to use it, whether it requires {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, and how many charges it has, if any. You learn whether any ongoing spells are affecting the item and what they are. If the item was created by a spell, you learn that spell's name.

name: Borrowed Luck
entries: When you use {@subclassFeature Hex Slinger|Rogue|PHB|Sinner|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14}, you siphon away a sliver of the target's luck. You gain inspiration if you don't already have it. If you do have it, you can expend your inspiration instead of expending a use of {@subclassFeature Hex Slinger|Rogue|PHB|Sinner|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14}.

name: Borrowed Luck
entries: When you use {@subclassFeature Hex Slinger|Rogue|XPHB|Sinner|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24}, you siphon away a sliver of the target's luck. You gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} if you don't already have it. If you do have it, you can expend your {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} instead of expending a use of {@subclassFeature Hex Slinger|Rogue|XPHB|Sinner|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24}.

name: Borrowed Tongues and Hides
entries: Your ability to siphon power from Celestials and Fiends is enhanced. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Arch Daemon Boon
entries: While you are siphoning power from Arch Daemons, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage. In addition, Fiends that know languages can understand your speech and you can understand theirs, even if you do not share a language.

entries.name: Arch Seraph Boon
entries: While you are siphoning power from Arch Seraphs, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Radiant damage. In addition, Celestials that know languages can understand your speech and you can understand theirs, even if you do not share a language.

entries.name: Switch Sides
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can change which power you are siphoning from. Once you switch, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Bough and Branch
entries: Even the humblest of your weapons channels the might of the old forest. When you cast {@spell Shillelagh}, you can cause a shield made of gnarled wood to grow into your free hand if you have one (no action required to don it), and it vanishes when the spell ends. You can't be forced to drop the affected weapon or shield unless you are {@condition incapacitated}. Additionally, for the duration of the spell, you ignore somatic components of your druid spells, and the weapon enhanced by the spell becomes a {@item druidic focus|XPHB} for you.

name: Bough and Branch
entries: Even the humblest of your weapons channels the might of the old forest. When you cast {@spell Shillelagh|XPHB}, you can cause a {@item Shield|XPHB} made of gnarled wood to grow into your free hand if you have one (no action required to don it), and it vanishes when the spell ends. You can't be forced to drop the affected weapon or Shield unless you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.
Additionally, for the duration of the spell, you ignore Somatic components of your Druid spells, and the weapon enhanced by the spell becomes a {@item Druidic Focus|XPHB} for you.

name: Bountiful Harvest
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you present your {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB} and expend a use of your {@classFeature Channel Divinity|Cleric|XPHB|2} to invoke the spirit of the harvest. Up to six creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}. A creature must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before it can gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} from this feature again.
Additionally, you grant all targets one of the following benefits. If your current harvest aspect is a different one, it changes to match the choice.

entries.name: Sowing
entries: A target gains a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} plus your Wisdom modifier.

entries.name: Growing
entries: Until the end of your next turn, when a target makes an attack roll or ability check, it adds {@dice 1d4} to the total.

entries.name: Reaping
entries: A target deals extra Necrotic damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} the first time it damages a creature before the end of your next turn.

name: Bragi's Rune of Speech
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you may expend a use of Bardic Inspiration to cause one of the following effects:

entries.name: Scorn
entries: Choose one creature within 30 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its attack rolls against you for 1 minute.

entries.name: Eloquence
entries: You may roll your Bardic Inspiration die and add the result to the first Charisma check or saving throw you make in the next hour.

entries.name: Vitality
entries: You may roll your Bardic Inspiration die. You and up to three allies within 30 feet gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the result of the roll.
You may have only one of these effects active at a time. If you use another, it replaces the one that is currently active.

name: Brains and Brawn
entries: While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is not active, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to every damage type except Force and Psychic.

name: Brawler's Best Friend
entries: You summon and form a bond with a wild or stray dog, which draws strength from your bottomless well of resilience using the {@creature Hound|Pugilist2024} stat block.
The hound is {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you and your allies and obeys your commands. It flees if you die.

entries.name: The Hound in Combat
entries: In combat, the hound acts during your turn. It can move and use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} on its own, but the only action it takes is the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action unless you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can also sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action to command the hound to take the Bite action. If you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, the hound acts on its own and isn't limited to the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Restoring or Replacing the Hound
entries: If the hound died within the last hour, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to touch it and expend 2 {@classFeature Moxie|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2|Pugilist2024|Moxie Points}. The hound returns to life after 1 minute with all its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} restored.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can summon and bond with a new dog, which appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. If you already have a hound from this feature, the old one vanishes when the new one appears.

name: Breaker of Minds
entries: At 10th level, your prowess at shattering blades and armor extends to harming the will of your foes. If you are grappling a creature, you can spend a bonus action and up to 3 maneuver points. When you do, the {@condition grappled} creature takes {@damage 1d6} psychic damage for each maneuver point you spent.

name: Breathe It In
entries: Being persistently exposed to the deadliest ailments known has given you some small measure of resistance. After you take Necrotic or Poison damage, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage taken. In addition, you are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

name: Briarheart
entries: Your fusion is complete, and your heart is absorbed, its sacrifice making way for a new heart—one that can fully channel the rage of the natural world. While you are a behemoth of your Wickerbone Behemoth feature, you can use the {@itemMastery Nick} mastery property in addition to the {@itemMastery Slow} mastery property with your arms.

In addition, if you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to cast any {@filter Osteomancy spell|spells|components & miscellaneous=|subschool=osteomancy|cast time=action}{@sup *} that has a casting time of an action.

{@note {@sup *}Osteomancy Spells: {@spell Arm Cannon|SGEHPP}, {@spell Brittle Bone Throw|SGEHPP}, {@spell Calcified Memories|SGEHPP}, {@spell Displacing Maw|SGEHPP}, {@spell Dread Scarecrow|SGEHPP}, {@spell Forest of Dread|SGEHPP}, {@spell Fractured Shell|SGEHPP}, {@spell Maiden of Bones|SGEHPP}, {@spell Marrow Transplant|SGEHPP}, {@spell Osseous Impalement|SGEHPP}, {@spell Phalangeal Shot|SGEHPP}, {@spell Skeletal Tail|SGEHPP}}

name: Bright Blade
entries: Starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can imbue a melee weapon that you are holding with your bravery. For 1 minute, you add your Charisma modifier to attack rolls made with that weapon (with a minimum bonus of +1). For the duration of the effect, when you hit a creature, the next attack roll against the target made by an attacker other than you has advantage if the attack is made before the start of your next turn. If you are no longer holding or carrying this weapon, or if you fall {@condition unconscious}, this effect ends.
You must then finish a short or long rest to use this feature again.

name: Brighter Still
entries: At 14th level, you gain the ability to activate your lantern's {@subclassFeature Illuminating Aura|Warlock||Lantern|ObojimaTallGrass|1} at will. Features such as {@subclassFeature Dangerous Tool|Warlock||Lantern|ObojimaTallGrass|6} and {@subclassFeature Brilliant Illumination|Warlock||Lantern|ObojimaTallGrass|10} that work in conjunction with Illuminating Aura are still limited to the number of uses described in their respective features. Additionally, while holding your lantern, you can use an action to cause it to illuminate with a pale blue light, revealing a glowing arcane path to a location you're familiar with, as if casting the {@spell Find the Path} spell.
Once you use your lantern in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Brilliant Illumination
entries: Starting at 10th level, while your lantern's {@subclassFeature Illuminating Aura|Warlock||Lantern|ObojimaTallGrass|1} is active you can use an action to cause the light to flare with an overwhelmingly brilliant flash. Each creature other than you illuminated by either your lantern's {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} or {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} (your choice) must make a Constitution saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes radiant damage equal to {@dice 2d8} + your warlock level and is {@condition blinded} until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't {@condition blinded}.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Brittle Bone Armor
entries: You learn the basics of osteomancy, using it for protection. As an action, if you're not wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|XPHB}, you can force a frame of bones out of your body to protect you, granting you {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Wizard level that last for 1 hour.
While you have these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Piercing and Slashing damage, and you have a +2 bonus to AC.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend a spell slot of level 2 or higher (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Broad Inspiration
entries: You know how to strengthen the hearts of your troops and stir them to greatness. You learn the {@spell Guidance|XPHB} cantrip, which counts as a Bard spell for you. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.
Additionally, when you confer a Bardic Inspiration die to a creature, you can also confer that Bardic Inspiration die to a second creature within range.

name: Bruised Ego
entries: Your ego strengthens you as you fight to prove your value. When you expend a Focus Point, you can also gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB|Temporary Hit Point}). While you are {@condition Bloodied|XPHB}, you gain twice that amount instead.

name: Brujah
entries: {@i Stand Up, Stand Firm, and Fight for Something}

The Brujah are a clan of freethinkers and revolutionaries who thrive on their own liberty and fight against oppression and stagnation. They find a power in themselves that is reflected as strength, speed, and a force of personality that makes them formidable in the varied conflicts they often find themselves in.

name: Brujah Bane
entries: Your blood simmers with the rage of your vampiric ancestors. If you fail a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} that is affected by your {@classFeature The Beast|Kindred|BoundByBlood|1||Beast} feature and choose to expend Blood Points to ignore the effects of {@classFeature The Beast|Kindred|BoundByBlood|1||Hunger}, you must expend a number of Blood Points equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to ignore the effects, instead of 1.

name: Brutal Brawler
entries: At 3rd level, your tavernside scuffles have honed your ability to deal damage with just about anything that's handy. You have proficiency with improvised weapons, and treat any improvised weapon you handle as if it has the finesse quality.

Additionally, whenever you hit with an improvised weapon, you may spend a bonus action to break it over your opponent. Doing this destroys the weapon, but deals the maximum number each of the weapon's damage dice could deal to the target. Any additional dice added to the attack's damage roll are not affected by this ability.

At 10th level, the improvised weapons you wield become even more lethal in your hands. When you spend your bonus action to break an improvised weapon over your opponent, add an additional {@damage 2d6} to the weapon's base damage dice.
At 18th level, you have advantage on attacks you make with improvised weapons.

name: Bullet Time
entries: Once on each of your turns when you make a ranged attack using a weapon, you can gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll.

name: Bulwark Warrior
entries: {@i Provoke Your Enemies, Protect Your Allies}

Those who learn the fighting prowess of the Bulwark Warrior Warriors protect their allies from certain death. With endurance and strength as their primary skills, these warriors are prepared to take lethal strikes for their companions.

name: Burglar
entries: Yours are the venerable arts of pickpocketing, lock picking, or otherwise getting hold of the possessions of others and accessing protected areas.

name: Burn Cycle
entries: Starting at 9th level, you can ignite your weapons in a flash of hot white flames when you successfully catch an enemy off guard. When you deal Sneak Attack damage on your turn, you can spend wick points to deal extra fire damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is {@dice 1d6} for each wick point spent, to a maximum of {@dice 4d6}.

name: Burning Spirit
entries: You can magically ignite yourself to embody your fiery soul. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Firelight
entries: You shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} that fills your Aura of Protection and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 30 feet.

entries.name: Fleet of Foot
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet. In addition, you can pass through and end a move in a space occupied by another creature as if that space were unoccupied, and ending a turn in a space with another creature doesn't cause you or that creature to have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Vengeful Flame
entries: At the end of each of your turns, each creature of your choice in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you takes Fire damage equal to twice your Charisma modifier (minimum of 2 Fire damage).

name: Burning weapon
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to ignite one Melee weapon that you're holding with fiery energy. For 10 minutes or until you use this feature again, you deal extra Fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1) whenever you hit a target with that weapon, and each time you hit with it, you can cause it to deal its normal damage type or Fire damage.
The weapon also emits {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 20 feet.
You can end this effect early (no action required). This effect also ends if you aren't carrying the weapon.

name: Burning Wrath
entries: You pour all of your intensity and fury into yourself, causing your blood to seemingly boil on your skin. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 2 Blood Points to empower your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. For 1 minute or until you fail to make an attack roll against an enemy on your turn, whichever comes first, you can deal an extra {@damage 2d8} Necrotic damage to a target you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

name: Call of the Northlands
entries: You are used to facing the harsh conditions and vicious monsters of the Northlands. At the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you may choose one of these benefits. The one you choose replaces your choice from the previous day.

entries.name: Dragonslayer
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls you make against Dragons, such as red dragons and wyverns.

entries.name: Hardy Swimmer
entries: You have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Inured to Cold
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage.

entries.name: Trollslayer
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls you make against Giants, such as frost giants and trolls.

name: Call of the Shadowseeds
entries: At 6th level, you learn to summon the feral children of the forest from the life force of your enemies. When a creature that is not undead or a construct takes damage within the area of your {@subclassFeature Defile Ground|Druid|PHB|Blighted|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2} feature, you can use your reaction to summon a {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the creature. You can direct the {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|sapling} to make an attack against any creature within 5 feet of it as a part of this reaction. The {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|sapling} then acts on your initiative, obeying your verbal commands.

The {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} remains in your service until it's reduced to 0 hit points, until the end of your next {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}, or until you summon another {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|sapling}, at which point it crumbles into foul-smelling mulch. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.
The {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|sapling} uses the statistics below. Its features scale based on your level and proficiency bonus (PB).

name: Calm Mind
entries: Whenever you successfully persuade a creature to stand down or deescalate an otherwise violent situation, you regain one expended Mercy Die. If multiple creatures are persuaded in this way, you regain one expended Mercy Die for each affected creature.
In addition, you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions.

name: Carrion Raven Maneuvers
entries: The Saga of the Carrion Raven speaks of a talking raven with the power to transform into any animal he had eaten to wield their powers. His tale intersects with Kentigern and his companions on their journey to slay the Great Prismatic Wyrm Gormadraug, where the raven appeared, offering to help in exchange for the chance to eat the Prismatic Wyrm's heart. As the story goes, the raven taught the heroes how to fight with the ferocity of the north's fiercest predators and fly with the speed of their fastest birds.

Warriors who practice the Saga of the Carrion Raven trust in their instincts, and embody the cunning, resilience, and power of the natural world. Masters of this saga learn to knit their flesh, take flight, and even adopt the shape of the beasts they've so long emulated.
These maneuvers can be used by anyone who studies the Carrion Raven saga.

name: Carver Guild
entries: {@i Slay Monsters Fearlessly and Recklessly}

Since the beginning of time, the brave glared into danger's ferocious eyes and fought monsters. Those who survived were the ones smart enough to arm themselves properly and know precisely where to strike—or those who knew when to flee and return with a new plan.

Members of the Carver Guild are the Monster Hunters typically called upon when immediate danger threatens a settlement and there is no army or militia available. Carvers stride unflinchingly toward death, armed with years of training and the knowledge passed down from those before them.

name: Castigate
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend one use of your {@classFeature Channel Divinity|Paladin|XPHB|3} to clap those you would bring to justice in fiery shackles. Choose a number of creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 creature) you can see within 30 feet of yourself. Each creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be wrapped in fiery shackles and have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduced to 0. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can cause the shackles to flare. Each creature bound by the shackles takes {@damage 2d6} Fire damage. A shackled creature repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

name: Catastrophic Power
entries: You have mastered talents, both magical and martial, in your pursuit of the inevitable destruction of mortals and their works. When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you gain one of the following benefits until you finish your next {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Elemental Cataclysm
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend a spell slot to cause elemental energy to burst in a 10-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point within 60 feet of yourself. Choose a damage type: Acid, Cold, Fire, or Lightning.

Each creature in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 1d6} damage of the chosen type per level of the spell slot expended, and then has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to that damage type for 1 minute. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} on a success.

entries.name: Ruinous Smite
entries: Once per turn when you deal damage with an attack with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can choose to expend a spell slot to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage, plus another {@dice 1d8} per level of the spell slot.

entries.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your supernatural connection to destruction allows you to use the mastery property of one kind of weapon of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as {@item Shortbow|XPHB|Shortbows} or {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB|Quarterstaffs}.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change the kind of weapon you choose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery property of {@item Sling|XPHB|Slings} or {@item Greatclub|XPHB|Greatclubs}.

name: Celestial Connection
entries: You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. You don't need to share a language with the creature for it to understand your telepathic communications, but the creature must be able to understand at least one language. Your communication doesn't give the creature the ability to respond to you telepathically.

name: Celestial Emissary
entries: Your connection to Celestials can be used to expand your mind's reach. You always have the {@spell Dream|XPHB} and {@spell Scrying|XPHB} spells prepared. Your spellcasting ability for them is Wisdom, and with this feature, you can cast them without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. Whenever you use this feature to cast {@spell Dream|XPHB} without expending a spell slot, only you can act as the dream messenger. Once you cast a spell with this feature, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

In addition, when you make an attack roll with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} and hit, you can cause the target to take extra Radiant damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die. You can deal this extra damage a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Challenge
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can issue a challenge to a creature you can see within 10 feet of you as a bonus action. You gain advantage on melee attack rolls against the creature for 1 minute or until it drops to 0 hit points or falls {@condition unconscious}. In addition, the creature must make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier). On a failed check, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you for the duration, until you attack another creature, if a creature friendly to you attacks the target, or if you end your turn more than 30 feet away from the target.
You must then finish a short or long rest to use this feature again.

name: Channel Divinity
entries: You gain the following Channel Divinity options. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how Channel Divinity works.

entries.name: Castigate
entries: As an action, you can use your Channel Divinity to clap those you would bring to justice in fiery shackles. Choose a number of creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 creature) you can see within 30 feet of yourself. Each creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be wrapped in fiery shackles and have its speed reduced to 0 for 1 minute. As a bonus action, you can cause the shackles to flare. Each creature bound by the shackles takes {@damage 2d6} fire damage. A shackled creature repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Incite
entries: As an action, you can use your Channel Divinity to better seek out wickedness and corruption. For the next 10 minutes, you have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) and Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks.

During that time, you can take a bonus action to choose a creature you can see within 10 feet of you. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be {@condition frightened} for 1 minute. While the target is {@condition frightened} in this way, it can't speak a deliberate lie. The condition ends early if the target takes damage or if you use this bonus action again.

name: Channel Divinity
entries: When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

entries.name: Absorb Magic
