entries: Your game statistics are replaced by the Beast's stat block, but you retain your creature type; {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}; {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. You also retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies and use your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} for them, in addition to gaining the proficiencies of the creature. If a skill or saving throw modifier in the Beast's stat block is higher than yours, use the one in the stat block. While in Beast form, you retain your personality and memories, and you can understand languages you know, but you can't speak.

entries.name: Objects
entries: Your ability to handle objects is determined by the form's limbs rather than your own. In addition, your equipment merges into your new form. Nonmagical equipment that merges with the form has no effect while you're in that form.

name: Corrosive Haze
entries: At 14th level, your Shadow Smoke is more potent. Any hostile creature that enters the smoke or starts its turn in the smoke must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be {@condition blinded} until the beginning of its next turn. The DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier. Creatures that don't rely on eyesight are immune to this effect.

name: Corrupted Ranger
entries: You have become afflicted by the mysterious illness that haunts the island known as the Corruption. This same foul magic, which has stained the coastlines black, now resides within your body. It curses your skin and seeps from your pores, and in time it will even become difficult to distinguish you from it.

How this has happened is your story to tell. You may have been one of the first responders to the Corruption when it came to the shores of Obojima leaving you to possibly be the only survivor of that brave band of rangers. Perhaps you were an explorer, who stumbled on a pocket of Corruption and became infected, or maybe you were inflicted with this Corruption by an evil witch.

name: Cosmic Restoration
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can touch a willing creature (which could be yourself) and choose one of the following options.

entries.name: Dispelling Touch
entries: You end all spells of your choice currently affecting the target.

entries.name: Purging Touch
entries: You remove one of the following conditions from the target: {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} (decreases by 1), {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, or {@condition Stunned|XPHB}.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending 4 Focus Points (no action required).

name: Couatl Herald
entries: {@i Show Mercy to Enemies and Support Allies as a Paragon of Civility and Restraint}

The Couatl Heralds were, or are, martial warriors whose intention was to neutralize threats without always resorting to deadly force. These combatants were a beloved symbol of peace in the once great city of Hearth, whose terrible destruction has been all but entirely lost to history. Perhaps you come from a long line of sequestered heralds who had escaped the city before its collapse, or maybe you found the age-old journals of one of the city's training officers. Regardless of how you come across this knowledge, training, and virtue, a true Couatl Herald defends the lives of all, regardless of their transgressions.

name: Counsellor
entries: Wise counsel is rare to come by in the Twilight of the Third Age, as words can be distorted and put to crooked uses by the servants of the Enemy. This notwithstanding, you have chosen to oppose the Shadow by bringing your advice to all who need it.

name: Counter-Mage
entries: Your experience in combating spellcasters grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Abjuration-Breaker
entries: Whenever you make a ranged attack roll, you temporarily disrupt protective magic affecting the target. For the duration of the attack, the effects of spells targeting the creature, such as {@spell Mage Armor|XPHB}, as well as the properties and powers of magic items worn or carried by the creature, are suppressed and don't function. The target of the attack can't take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cast spells such as {@spell Shield|XPHB} in response to the attack or damage.

entries.name: Antimagic Shot
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} and the target is affected by your {@classFeature Gut Shot|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|5} feature, it also impedes the target's ability to cast spells. While the projectile is lodged in the target, it can't cast spells or take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action. Additionally, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws it makes to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

entries.name: Inured to Magic
entries: When you fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to roll {@dice 1d6} and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.

name: Coven Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Coven Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Coven Spells
rows: {@spell Hold Person|XPHB}, {@spell Identify|XPHB}, {@spell Locate Object|XPHB}, {@spell Ray of Sickness|XPHB}

name: Cover of Night
entries: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Stealth} skill and {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet. In addition, when you are in dim light or darkness, you can use a bonus action to {@action Hide}.

name: Create Ice
entries: While touching a solid surface (such as the ground or a wall), you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to magically create icy terrain on up to five 5-foot squares, starting with the surface you're touching. Each square covers a solid surface and must be contiguous with at least one other square. The ice-covered squares are {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} and last until the end of your next turn.
You can spend 1 or more Sorcery Points when you take this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to freeze an additional five contiguous squares for each Sorcery Point spent.

name: Create Void
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to open a planar tear at a point you can see within 60 feet of you, creating a powerful vacuum in a 15-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes Force damage equal to {@dice 1d8} plus your Cleric level and is pulled up to 15 feet toward the point. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much Force damage only. The tear then vanishes.

name: Creative Trajectory
entries: You can make your projectiles travel in unexpected ways. Your ranged attacks with weapons ignore {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} and {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover}.

name: Creature of the Night
entries: You always have the {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} spell prepared. With this feature, you can cast it only on yourself without expending a spell slot and without Material components to transform into a {@creature Bat|XMM}, {@creature Rat|XMM}, or {@creature Wolf|XMM}.

Your game statistics are replaced by the Beast's stat block, but you retain your creature type; {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}; {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. You also retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies and use your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} for them, in addition to gaining the proficiencies of the creature. If a skill or saving throw modifier in the Beast's stat block is higher than yours, use the one in the stat block.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Creature of the Night
entries: Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to activate a supernatural aura of deep night. It lasts for 1 minute, or until you dismiss it using another action. You emit heavily obscuring darkness in a 30-foot radius and lightly obscuring shadows 50 feet beyond that. The darkness and shadows overlap and smother existing sources of light. Only light produced by a 9th level spell or similarly powerful effect can negate the darkness and shadows.

Enemies within the shadows constantly feel the presence of hungry predators watching them, and become {@condition frightened} as long as they remain inside the affected area. Enemies in the darkness are both {@condition blinded} and {@condition frightened} for as long as they remain within its area.

name: Creeping Fog
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can burst into a mist of raw shadow and then reassemble yourself somewhere else. As an action, you magically teleport, along with any equipment you are wearing or carrying, up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Before or after teleporting, you can make one melee attack.

name: Crimson Dynasty
entries: {@i Control the Vital Power of Your Lifeblood}

Crimson Sorcerers harness the ancient magic of blood and life essence. They twist and guide the flow of this quintessential energy as a hunger grows deep within them. They manipulate their power to infuse the vitality of others, or they can rip it away and steal it for themselves.

Crimson Dynasty can be acquired in a variety of ways. Some with this power were born with it. Others were infused with it through a dark ritual or grim event. There are those who discover it through lost secrets.
Consult the Crimson Origins table for a possible origin of your power.

There are a variety of ways you might have received the ability to harness your Crimson Dynasty to manipulate vitality and life essence. The Crimson Origins table offers suggestions of where your power comes from.

entries.caption: Crimson Origins
rows: One of your parents was a vampire. Though you aren't one yourself, you inherited their hunger, and it drives your magic.
You studied blood rites at a monastery that infused your own blood with power.
You survived a vampire's bite, though it left you forever changed and awakened your sorcery.
Your family suffers under a generational curse that has reared its head with you, driving you to drain vital energy.
You studied the secrets of life and death, perhaps to save yourself or a loved one. In so doing, you unlocked the crimson power in your blood.
You died, and a cunning entity offered you a second chance at life. You accepted and awoke with Crimson Dynasty coursing through your veins.

name: Crimson Sorcery
entries: {@i Control the Vital Power of Your Lifeblood}

Crimson Sorcerers harness the ancient magic of blood and life essence. They twist and guide the flow of this quintessential energy as a hunger grows deep within them. They manipulate their power to infuse the vitality of others, or they can rip it away and steal it for themselves.

Crimson sorcery can be acquired in a variety of ways. Some with this power were born with it. Others were infused with it through a dark ritual or grim event. There are those who discover it through lost secrets.
Consult the Crimson Origins table for a possible origin of your power.

There are a variety of ways you might have received the ability to harness your Crimson Sorcery to manipulate vitality and life essence. The Crimson Origins table offers suggestions of where your power comes from.

entries.caption: Crimson Origins
rows: One of your parents was a vampire. Though you aren't one yourself, you inherited their hunger, and it drives your magic.
You studied blood rites at a monastery that infused your own blood with power.
You survived a vampire's bite, though it left you forever changed and awakened your sorcery.
Your family suffers under a generational curse that has reared its head with you, driving you to drain vital energy.
You studied the secrets of life and death, perhaps to save yourself or a loved one. In so doing, you unlocked the crimson power in your blood.
You died, and a cunning entity offered you a second chance at life. You accepted and awoke with crimson sorcery coursing through your veins.

name: Crimson Spells
entries: You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Crimson Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be a necromancy or a transmutation spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list.

entries.caption: Crimson Spells
rows: {@spell Blood Bolt|CrookedMoon14}, {@spell Cure Wounds|PHB}, {@spell Inflict Wounds|PHB}
{@spell Field of Reaping|CrookedMoon14}, {@spell Mass Cure Wounds|PHB}

name: Crimson Spells
entries: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Crimson Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Crimson Spells
rows: {@spell Aid|XPHB}, {@spell Blood Bolt|CrookedMoon24}, {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB}, {@spell Inflict Wounds|XPHB}, {@spell Blood Sacrifice|CrookedMoon24}
{@spell Field of Reaping|CrookedMoon24}, {@spell Mass Cure Wounds|XPHB}

name: Cross Counter
entries: You can block the brunt of an attack and launch one of your own in the same fluid motion. When you take damage from a melee attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 1 {@classFeature Moxie|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2|Pugilist2024|Moxie Point} to reduce the damage dealt to you by that attack by {@dice 1d10} plus your Strength modifier and Pugilist level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, you can make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or attack with a Pugilist weapon against a creature within your reach as part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

name: Crown of Horns
entries: As a bonus action, you can manifest the majestic might of the Horned King for 1 minute. For the duration, a visible mark appears on you—such as a crown made of horns surmounting your head, or you grow great antlers—and you gain the benefits listed below. Once you use this bonus action, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest unless you expend a warlock spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

entries.name: Dark Heart
entries: Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage.

entries.name: King of All
entries: You radiate an aura of power out to 20 feet from you. When you activate this feature, and at the start of each of your turns, you can choose a creature you can see in the aura. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer one of the following effects of your choice until the start of your next turn:

items.name: Enticement
entries: The target is {@condition charmed|PHB} by you.

items.name: Wickedness
entries: The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

items.name: Terror
entries: The target is {@condition frightened|PHB} of you and must move away from you by the safest route during its turn unless there is nowhere to move.

name: Crown of Horns
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can manifest the majestic might of the Horned King for 1 minute. For the duration, a visible mark appears on you—such as a crown made of horns surmounting your head, or you grow great antlers—and you gain the benefits listed below. Once you use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

entries.name: Dark Heart
entries: Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage.

entries.name: King of All
entries: You radiate an aura of power in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that originates from you. When you activate this feature, and at the start of each of your turns, you can choose a creature you can see in the aura. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer one of the following effects of your choice until the start of your next turn:

items.name: Enticement
entries: The target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Wickedness
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and ability checks.

items.name: Terror
entries: The target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition and must move away from you by the safest route during its turn unless there is nowhere to move.

name: Cruel Jest
entries: When a creature that you can see or hear within 30 feet of yourself fails a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration; roll your Bardic Inspiration die and deal Psychic damage equal to the number rolled plus your Charisma modifier. In addition, the creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} it makes before the end of its next turn.

name: Crush Weakness
entries: You abhor failure and weakness in all its forms, and you relish punishing those who succumb to it. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Dark Judgment
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails an ability check or saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend 2 Blood Points to deal {@damage 4d8} Psychic damage to that creature.

entries.name: Obliviate
entries: When a creature that you can see within 10 feet of you misses an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 2 Blood Points to deal {@damage 2d8} Bludgeoning damage and {@damage 2d8} Cold damage to that creature.

name: Crushing Guilt
entries: You can expend 3 Focus Points to release your pent-up guilt in a crushing wave that drops your foes to their knees. Creatures of your choice in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you or your shade must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Focus Point save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Psychic damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

name: Crushing Steps
entries: As part of your movement, you can move through the space of any creature with a size smaller than you. An enemy whose space you move through must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and lose the ability to take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of its next turn.

name: Culinary Exploration
entries: Years spent adapting recipes allows you to try unheard-of combinations of ingredients. You gain proficiency with cook's utensils, which you can use as a spellcasting focus, and your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability checks you make that uses these utensils to prepare food. In addition, whenever you craft a food, you can add one additional ingredient to the recipe, conferring the benefits of that ingredient to the dish on a successful Cooking check.

name: Culinary Specialisation
entries: You pursue a particular style of cuisine, choosing from the list below and gaining its feature.

items.name: Slow Cooking
items.entry: You gain proficiency with {@filter medium armour|items|type=medium armor}, {@filter heavy armour|items|type=heavy armor}, {@item shield|phb|shields}, and {@filter martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon}. At the start of each of your turns, you gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

items.name: Fast Food
items.entry: You gain proficiency with {@filter medium armour|items|type=medium armor} and you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

items.name: Patissier
entries: You learn two spells of your choice from any spell list. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. These don't count against the number of bard spells you know.

In addition, when you finish a short rest, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration, rolling the die and recovering a number of levels of spell slots with a combined value equal to or less than the value rolled, and none of the spell slots can be 6th level or higher. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Cunning and Brutal
entries: While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is not active, you can take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} or {@action Help|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, your attack rolls with {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}.

name: Cunning Eye
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to your Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) and Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks. In addition, you can use the bonus action granted by your {@classFeature Cunning Action|Treasure Hunter|TLotRR|2|TLotRR} to take the {@action Search} action.

name: Curse Caster
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and spend 3 Jinx Points to cast {@spell Bestow Curse|XPHB}.

name: Curse Caster
entries: At 13th level, you can use an action and spend 3 jinx points to cast the {@spell bestow curse} spell. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

name: Customized Spell
entries: You can alter the structure of a spell to incorporate a creature's name. Pick a spell in your spell book that has a Verbal component, requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}, and is level 1+. When you prepare that spell, you can name a specific, willing creature other than yourself. If that creature is the only target of the spell, you can cast the spell on it without needing to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

name: Daemonologist
entries: {@i Steal Scraps of Divine and Infernal Power}

Through theological study, or perhaps an induction into a secretive cabal, Daemonologists have learned to cast divine magic without the need for faith or bargains. Their spellbooks are scribed with prayer fragments and blasphemous hymns, enabling them to siphon scraps of power from both Arch Seraphs and Arch Daemons. From their heretical research, they've come to believe such otherworldly beings are two sides of the same divine kin.
Daemonology is rarely practiced. If the nature of their abilities is discovered, they risk being persecuted not only by superstitious folk but also by celestial and infernal powers.

name: Dance of the Dead
entries: Starting at 14th level, when you cast a necromancy spell that targets only one creature, you can have it target a second creature within range. This does not consume additional components.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

name: Dancing Shadows
entries: When you join the College of Shadow at 3rd level, you gain the ability to weave a pocket of protective shadows.

As a bonus action, you can expend a Bardic Inspiration to create a 20-foot-radius sphere of shifting shadows centered on you. The sphere moves with you, spreads around corners, and lasts for 1 minute or until you are {@condition incapacitated} or die.

Allied creatures (including you) standing in the sphere have {@book half cover|PHB|9|Cover}, and creatures outside the sphere have disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks made to perceive anything inside the sphere. {@sense Darkvision} does not nullify this effect. Creatures that don't rely on eyesight are immune to this effect.
If any of this effect's area overlaps with an area of light created by a spell of 2nd level or lower, the spell that created the light is dispelled.

name: Dangerous Tool
entries: Starting at 6th level, your {@subclassFeature Illuminating Aura|Warlock||Lantern|ObojimaTallGrass|1} no longer ends if you let go of your lantern. While you aren't holding your lantern, you can magically take control of it for 1 minute (no action required), using it as if it were a {@spell Spiritual Weapon} cast as a 2nd-level spell. Your lantern continues to act as your spellcasting focus while using this feature, even though you are no longer holding the lantern.
The level at which Spiritual Weapon is cast increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to a 4th-level spell at 10th level and a 6th-level spell at 15th level.
Once you take control of your lantern in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a warlock spell slot to take control of it again.

name: Dare Not Falter
entries: You effortlessly shrug off harm to your body and mind. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Toughened
entries: Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by an amount equal to your Kindred level when you gain this feature. Whenever you gain a Kindred level thereafter, your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by an additional 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}.

entries.name: Unswayable Mind
entries: If you fail a saving throw to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, or {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition, you can reroll it. You must use the new roll.

name: Dark Doom Revisited
entries: Once per active {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1}, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to channel a traumatic death. When you do, choose one of the following options.

entries.name: Contamination
entries: At the start of their turn, each creature of your choice in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take Poison damage and gain the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute.

To determine the Poison damage, roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and add them together. An affected creature can use an action to end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on itself.

entries.name: Hypothermia
entries: At the start of their turn, each creature of your choice in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take Cold damage and have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} halved for 1 minute.
To determine the Cold damage, roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and add them together. A creature can use an action to end this effect on itself.

entries.name: Immolation
entries: At the start of their turn, each creature of your choice in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take Fire damage.

To determine the Fire damage, roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and add them together. As an action, a creature can extinguish the fire on itself by giving itself the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and rolling on the ground. The fire also goes out if it is doused, submerged, or suffocated.

name: Dark Inoculation
entries: Starting at 10th level, your poisonous magic has infused your body. You are immune to disease, poison damage, and the {@condition poisoned} condition.

name: Dark Servant
entries: At 6th level, you gain the ability to awaken shadows to do your bidding. As a bonus action, you can target a creature that you can see within 30 feet. That creature's shadow comes to life as a separate creature under your command, using the {@creature shadow} stat block.

The shadow appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target and can act immediately. The shadow acts on your initiative, it must spend its turn moving toward the target by the most direct route, and it can use its action only to attack the target (and no action is required by you to command the shadow). If the shadow hits with an attack, instead of doing any damage, the target instead has disadvantage on the first attack or saving throw it makes before the start of the shadow's next turn.
The shadow disappears if it is reduced to 0 hit points, if its target is reduced to 0 hit points, or after 5 minutes.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Dark Transfusion
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can feed energy to your symbiote to transform it. As a bonus action, you can expend two spell slots to recover one spell slot equal to or less than the total combined value of the expended spell slots. For example, you could expend a 1st-level spell slot and a 2nd-level spell slot to recover one 3rd-level spell slot.

name: Darkness Falls
entries: At 14th level, you can use an action to emit a 15-foot-radius sphere of magical darkness centered on yourself. The sphere moves with you, and its darkness spreads around corners. When you create the sphere, you can designate any number of creatures that can see through the darkness, but otherwise, a creature with {@sense darkvision} can't see through it, and nonmagical light can't illuminate it.

The sphere lasts for 1 minute, until you are {@condition incapacitated}, or until it comes into contact with sunlight. If any of this effect's area overlaps with an area of light created by a spell of 7th level or lower, the spell that created the light is dispelled.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Deadeye
entries: {@i Shoot with Bullseye Precision}

A well-placed bullet is more powerful than a sword, arrow, or spell. Indeed, you believe that every violent conflict should sound like a single loud crack followed by a long silence. Such shots demand perfection, even at range, for when they are done right, they are as deadly for the target as they are stupendous for the audience.

name: Deadly Redirect
entries: Your strikes have become even deadlier. The extra damage of your Close Quarters increases to {@dice 3d6}. In addition, if you deal damage to a creature with Close Quarters, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all attack rolls until the end of your next turn.

name: Deal with the Devil
entries: You gain one of the following options of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change your choice.

entries.name: Cloak of Shadows
entries: You can cast {@spell Invisibility|XPHB} once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Mask of Many Faces
entries: You can cast {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.

entries.name: Otherworldly Walk
entries: You can cast {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Death Is but a Door
entries: Your familiarity with death has left you resistant to its call. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Hard to Kill
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws}. In addition, you must fail four {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws} to die instead of three as normal.

entries.name: Return the Spirit
entries: You can call the spirits of the deceased to restore life essence to a nearby creature. You can cast the {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB}, {@spell Raise Dead|XPHB}, or {@spell Revivify|XPHB} spell without providing Material components. When you do, you gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level for {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB}, 2 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels for {@spell Revivify|XPHB}, and 3 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels for {@spell Raise Dead|XPHB}. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for this feature.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend two uses of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Death Knight
entries: You house within you the lingering remnants of souls long-departed, and their knowledge and experience imbue you with necromantic energy. It is represented by Draugr Dice, which fuel powers you have from this subclass. The Barrow Guard Draugr Dice table shows the die size and number of these dice you have when you reach certain fighter levels.
Some of your powers expend a Draugr Die, as specified in a feature's description, and you can't use a power if it requires you to use a die when all your Draugr Dice are expended.
You regain one expended Draugr Die when you finish a short rest, and you regain all of them when you finish a long rest.
The save DC for any of your powers is 8 plus your Constitution modifier and proficiency bonus.

entries.name: Dark Rider
entries: As a bonus action, you manifest a ghostly steed that only you can mount. The steed uses the Warhorse stat block, but its creature type is Undead, it has resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and it can only take the {@action Dash}, {@action Disengage}, and {@action Dodge} actions. When the steed takes the {@action Dash} action, you can expend and roll a Draugr Die. During the movement from that action, the steed's speed increases by a number of feet equal to 5 times the number rolled. The steed vanishes after 1 hour, if reduced to 0 hit points, if you are {@condition incapacitated}, or if you die.
Once you take this bonus action, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest, unless you expend a Draugr Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

entries.name: Grave Guard
entries: When you take damage, you can use your reaction to expend and roll a Draugr Die. Reduce the damage you take by the number rolled plus your Constitution modifier.

entries.name: Soul Reaper
entries: When you take the {@action Attack} action, you can forego one of your attacks to magically call forth ghostly hands around a creature within 60 feet of yourself. Expend and roll a Draugr Die. The target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it takes necrotic damage equal to the number rolled on the Draugr Die plus your Constitution modifier, and it has the {@condition grappled} condition (escape DC = your Death Knight power save DC) for 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

name: Death Knight
entries: You house within you the lingering remnants of souls long-departed, and their knowledge and experience imbue you with necromantic energy. It is represented by Draugr Dice, which fuel powers you have from this subclass. The Barrow Guard Draugr Dice table shows the die size and number of these dice you have when you reach certain Fighter levels.
Some of your powers expend a Draugr Die, as specified in a feature's description, and you can't use a power if it requires you to use a die when all your Draugr Dice are expended.
You regain one expended Draugr Die when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all of them when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
The save DC for any of your powers is 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Dark Rider
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you manifest a ghostly steed that only you can mount. The steed uses the {@creature Warhorse|XMM} stat block, but its creature type is Undead, it has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, and it can only take the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, and {@action Dodge|XPHB} actions. When the steed takes the {@action Dash|XPHB} action, you can expend and roll a Draugr Die. During the movement from that action, the steed's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by a number of feet equal to 5 times the number rolled. The steed vanishes after 1 hour, if reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or if you die.

Once you take this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you expend a Draugr Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

entries.name: Grave Guard
entries: When you take damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend and roll a Draugr Die. Reduce the damage you take by the number rolled plus your Constitution modifier.

entries.name: Soul Reaper
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can forego one of your attacks to magically call forth ghostly hands around a creature within 60 feet of yourself. Expend and roll a Draugr Die. The target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it takes Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled on the Draugr Die plus your Constitution modifier, and it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape DC = your Death Knight power save DC) for 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

name: Deathly Pallor
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage, and when you cast a Sorcerer spell that deals damage, it can deal your choice of Necrotic damage or its normal damage type.

name: Deathstrike
entries: When you hit an interdicted creature with a melee weapon attack, you can use your reaction to burn one of the seals on them to turn the hit into a critical hit. When you do, you also double the damage dice you roll for the burned seal.
You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Debilitating Barrage
entries: Upon reaching 17th level, you've gained the knowledge to manipulate a creature's ki to undermine their fortitude. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 ki points to cause the creature to gain vulnerability to one damage type of your choice for 1 minute, or until the end of a turn in which it has taken damage of that type.

If a creature has resistance to the damage type you choose, this resistance is suppressed for 1 minute, rather than gaining vulnerability. A creature that is immune to the damage type you choose is unaffected. A creature who is affected by this feature cannot be affected by it again for 24 hours.

name: Debilitating Fever
entries: You can inflict disease upon a creature. When you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to give that creature the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} in this way, the target also has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. At the end of each of its turns, the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} target makes a Constitution save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Deep Sleep
entries: You can choose to enter a deep state of hibernation when you take a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. While resting in this way, you're cold to the touch and appear dead to all outward inspection and to spells or other magical effects used to determine your status. Noise and other distractions fail to wake you.

You awaken from this rest after 6 hours, when you take damage, or when a creature uses its action to slap you awake. If you finish a continuous 6 hours of sleep in this way, you gain the benefits of finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, and you gain a special pool of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, which lasts until the end of your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} and can be used as normal. This pool has a number of Barbarian {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} in it equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die}).

name: Deepwood Elder
entries: Your connection to the Elderwood grows stronger. When you activate your {@subclassFeature Wood Wose|Druid|PHB|Old Ways|CrookedMoon14|2|CrookedMoon14}, you now gain additional benefits for the duration.

entries.name: Primeval Wrath
entries: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can force the target to succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be knocked {@condition prone}.

entries.name: Bramblebark
entries: When a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, the attacker takes {@damage 1d8} piercing damage. A creature takes this damage only once per turn.

entries.name: Rampant Growth
entries: When you activate {@subclassFeature Wood Wose|Druid|PHB|Old Ways|CrookedMoon14|2|CrookedMoon14} and at the start of each of your subsequent turns, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier plus your proficiency bonus.

name: Deepwood Elder
entries: Your connection to the Elderwood grows stronger. When you activate your {@subclassFeature Wood Wose|Druid|XPHB|Old Ways|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24}, you now gain additional benefits for the duration.

entries.name: Primeval Wrath
entries: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can force the target to succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Bramblebark
entries: When a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, the attacker takes {@damage 1d8} Piercing damage. A creature takes this damage only once per turn.

entries.name: Rampant Growth
entries: When you activate {@subclassFeature Wood Wose|Druid|XPHB|Old Ways|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} and at the start of each of your subsequent turns, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Wisdom modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Defend the Pack
entries: Whenever a creature attacks an ally within 30 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and spend a use of your Wild Shape to conjure a giant phantom wolf to maul that creature. There is no attack roll required, and the creature is not entitled to a saving throw. The target takes {@damage 4d8} Force damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
At 14th level, the damage increases to {@damage 6d8} Force damage.

name: Defensive Intervention
entries: When a creature you can see hits another creature within 30 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend one use of your Channel Divinity to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space within range of the triggering attack and become the target of the attack.

name: Defensive Tactics
entries: At 7th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.

entries.name: Multiattack Defence:
entries: When a creature hits or misses you with an attack, you add your proficiency bonus to your AC against all subsequent attacks made by that creature for the rest of the turn.

entries.name: Stout Resistance:
entries: You gain proficiency in a saving throw of your choice.

entries.name: Swift to Fly:
entries: You can use the {@action Disengage} action as a bonus action on your turn.

name: Defile Ground (10th Level)
entries: Starting at 10th level, the area of your defiled ground increases to a 20-foot radius. Additionally, the extra damage dealt by your defiled ground increases to {@damage 1d6} when you reach 10th level in this class.

name: Defile Ground (14th Level)
entries: The extra damage dealt by your defiled ground increases to {@damage 1d8} when you reach 14th level in this class.

name: Defile Ground
entries: Starting at 2nd level when you choose this circle, you can use a bonus action to corrupt a patch of land or an area of water in a 10-foot radius centered on a point within 60 feet of you. This corruption lasts for 1 minute. The corrupted area is {@quickref difficult terrain||3} for creatures that are hostile to you. Additionally, when a creature in the area takes damage from an attack or spell for the first time on a turn, it takes an extra {@damage 1d4} necrotic damage. You can move this patch of corruption up to 30 feet as a bonus action. Flying creatures are unaffected by the corruption.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}.

name: Deft Deflection [Maneuver]
entries: You can shoot projectiles out of the air. When an ally within 30 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend one {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die} to grant that ally the benefit of the {@optfeature Skin of Your Teeth|ValdaGunslinger} maneuver against that attack. You must be holding a Ranged weapon to use this maneuver.

name: Dematerialize
entries: Your spells deal double damage to objects and structures, and whenever you deal damage to a Construct, it takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Force damage.

name: Demolishing Might
entries: Starting at 6th level, your melee weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d8} damage to constructs, and deal double damage to objects and structures.

name: Demontongue
entries: Your demonshard grants you innate understanding of the languages of fiends. You can speak and understand your choice of either Abyssal or Infernal.

name: Depraved Mind
entries: You've seen the worst depravities that plague this world and have committed most of them. You are immune to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition and gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage.

In addition, if a creature attempts to read your mind or telepathically talk to you against your will, it must first make a Wisdom saving throw against your Technique save DC. On a failed save, it witnesses the horrors within your mind. It takes Psychic damage equal to your level and fails to communicate with you. On a successful save, it can interact with you in this way for 1 minute without making the saving throw.

name: Depth of Feelings
entries: You can see aspects of the world that others can't, including emotions. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Aura Sight
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 2 Blood Points to see a creature's aura for 1 minute. You can ask the GM up to two questions that can be answered with yes or no. You must ask your questions before the effect ends. You receive a correct answer for each question. The following are example questions.

items: Is the creature's creature type X? (Where X is a creature type specified by the player character, such as Monstrosity or Undead)
Can the creature cast spells?
Is the creature {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} toward me?
Does the creature believe what it is saying?

entries: The GM has final say as to whether the question can be answered, but the answers must be truthful.

entries.name: Entrancement
entries: You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the {@spell Calm Emotions|XPHB}, {@spell Charm Monster|XPHB}, or {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} spell.

name: Desert Nomad
entries: Beginning at 14th level, you have the ability to step into the heart of the twisters you create. Immediately after a creature is pushed by your Sandstorm feature, you can spend 2 sorcery points to teleport to the storm's space. You can also teleport in this way if you create the storm in a space that is unoccupied. When you teleport in this way, you and any equipment you are wearing or carrying are {@condition invisible} until the end of your turn.

name: Desert Soul
entries: Your power comes from the relentless and punishing magic that lies at the heart of the world's most unforgiving deserts. Most sorcerers with this power were born to nomads or traveling pilgrims in the H'rethi desert, but perhaps yours came to you in the chaos of a raging sandstorm or the springs of a magical oasis. Regardless of its origin, this blistering magic spirals around inside of you in an ever-present storm that can reduce even the sturdiest enemies to rubble.

name: Desperado
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can use your Hair Trigger feature immediately before you fall {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}.

name: Devastator
entries: As an action, you invoke the authority of Dispater. You make a weapon attack and choose a number of willing creatures up to your proficiency bonus who you can see within 30 feet of you. Each creature you choose can use a reaction to make a weapon attack or cast a damage-dealing cantrip with a casting time of 1 action.
Once you use this action, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Devourer Guild
entries: {@i Gain Power by Consuming Monster Flesh}

Folk in Etharis don't always speak highly of Monster Hunters, and many consider them to be just as depraved and inhuman as the evils they vanquish. Many of the appalling tales about Monster Hunters can be attributed, directly or indirectly, to the Devourer Guild, who are accused of being monstrous cannibals.

The truth is barely any better. Devourers have spent their days consuming the flesh and blood of the monsters they slay, and, over time, their metabolism has changed to tolerate this disgusting practice. Devourers adopt mutations shortly after consuming their prey.

name: Dimensional Duel
entries: You always have the {@spell Banishment|XPHB} spell prepared. When you activate your Rage or as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while your Rage is active, you can cast {@spell Banishment|XPHB} without a spell slot or components and while your Rage is active, and your spellcasting ability for it is Strength. You can maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} while your Rage is active. You can target up to three creatures when you cast {@spell Banishment|XPHB} this way. In addition, you can choose to pursue the creatures you banish. If you do so, the targets you banished don't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition for the spell's duration, and you travel with them to a demiplane. The demiplane is an empty room 30 to 200 feet in each dimension (you choose when you cast the spell) and made of wood or stone (your choice). You must create enough space for you and the targets, or the spell ends. The room is filled with {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}. When the spell ends, if you traveled with any targets, you and any dropped objects reappear in the space you left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Strength modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Dirtier Tricks
entries: You gain the following additional Dirty Tricks. You can use one Dirty Trick each turn, and once you use a dirty trick, you can't use that trick again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Rabbit Punch
entries: When you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or a Pugilist weapon, you strike its head. Until the end of your next turn, the creature loses {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage if it has it and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saving throws.

entries.name: Sucker Punch
entries: When you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or Pugilist weapon, you can turn the hit into a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. For this {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, you roll the attack's damage dice three times and add them together, instead of twice as normal.

name: Dirty Tricks
entries: You have a few tricks up your sleeve to even the odds when the going gets tough. You can use one of the following Dirty Tricks. You can use one Dirty Trick each turn, and once you use a dirty trick, you can't use that trick again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Heelstomper
entries: When you deal damage to a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or Pugilist weapon, the creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 for one minute. An affected creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Low Blow
entries: When you deal damage to a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or Pugilist weapon, you can hit the creature below the belt. When you do, the creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or attacks against the creature have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Pocket Sand
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you toss detritus into the eyes of a creature within 10 feet. The creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

name: Disarm
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} and trigger your {@classFeature Gut Shot|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|5} feature against a creature, you can disarm the target instead of lodging a projectile in it. The target drops one object of your choice that it's holding, with the object landing in a space of your choice up to 15 feet away from the target.

name: Disgusting Resilience
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can spend any number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice}, roll them, and reduce the damage taken by the total rolled on those dice.

In addition, if you are killed, your corpse explodes in a shower of pus and gore. Each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you makes Constitution saving throw gainst the Paladin's spell save DC, taking {@damage 8d6} Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Dispater's Blessing
entries: When Dispater accepts you as his illrigger, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

name: Dispater's Interdiction
entries: You learn the following additional interdict boons at the noted illrigger levels. Once you learn an interdict boon granted by this feature, you always know it, and it doesn't count against the number of interdict boons you know.

name: Distant Switch
entries: When you use your Context Switch class feature, you can choose a creature within 30 feet of you (rather than within 5 feet of you). If you do not choose to do this, you can instead choose for the creature you swap with to have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its save. If your target (regardless of its distance from you) fails its save, you can choose to have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn or until immediately after you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell (whichever comes first).

name: Divine Bargain
entries: Transactions are at the heart of your belief system, and you have learned to buy and sell metaphysical boons with your divine wealth. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can magically conduct a metaphysical trade with one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. Choose either Buy or Sell.

entries.name: Buy
entries: Give one of your divine coins to the target. It can spend the divine coin as if it had your {@subclassFeature Divine Wealth|Cleric|XPHB|Commerce|FoEQuickstone|3} feature. The target takes {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage, and you or one creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage taken.

entries.name: Sell
entries: Gain a divine coin. You take {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage, and the target regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage taken. The damage cannot be reduced by any means.

name: Divine Blessings
entries: Your devotion to eradicating enemies of the Church manifests as righteous power. You have a pool of Divine Points equal to 1 + your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 point). You regain all expended points when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. In addition, whenever you kill an Aberration, Beast, Fiend, or Undead of CR 1/2 or higher with your sanctified blade, you regain 1 expended Divine Point.

entries.name: Radiance Save DC
entries: If a feature of this subclass requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
You can expend Divine Points to use the following features.

items.name: Armor of the Faithful
items.entry: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when a creature targets you with an attack, you can expend 1 Divine Point to force that creature to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the attacker must choose a new target or the attack has no effect. In addition, the attacker can't target you with an attack until the start of your next turn. This feature doesn't protect you from areas of effect, such as the explosion of a {@spell Fireball|XPHB} spell.

items.name: Divine Inspiration
items.entry: When you make an Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Religion|XPHB}) or a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check, you can expend 1 Divine Point to reroll the {@dice d20}, and you must use the new result. You can choose to use this feature after you roll the die, but before the outcome is determined. You gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

items.name: Rend the Blasphemous
items.entry: On your turn after you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action with your sanctified blade, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 Divine Point to let the divine hand guide you. Make a weapon attack with it against a creature within your reach. You gain a bonus to your attack roll equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

name: Divine Strike (14th Level)
entries: When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@dice 1d8} acid or poison damage (your choice) to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@dice 2d8}.

name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with the power of celestial order. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} force damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@dice 2d8}.

name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon with the power to punish wrongdoing. Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} psychic damage to the target. Visions of the evil they have wrought upon others flash before their eyes. You choose whether any foe reduced to 0 hit points by this attack remains stable or dies. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to cause the physical wounds you deal out to bleed profusely. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage to the target.

name: Divine Wealth
entries: Your spiritual savvy manifests as material wealth. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you conjure two divine coins and lose any previously unspent divine coins. Whenever you make a saving throw against a magical effect caused by a hostile creature, you can choose to spend a divine coin or gain a divine coin. You must choose whether or not to spend a coin before you roll your save.

entries.name: Spend a Coin
entries: Roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled tothe saving throw.

entries.name: Gain a Coin
entries: Roll a {@dice d4} and subtract the number rolledfrom the saving throw.

The number of divine coins you conjure when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} changes when you reach certain Cleric levels. You conjure three at level 5, four at level 9, five at level 13, and six at level 17.

name: Dog and Hound
entries: {@i Fight Side by Side with a Brawler's Best Friend}

Pugilists know what it's like to be an underdog, so it's no surprise some form a battleforged bond with a canine companion. They're used to being disappointed by friends that walk on two legs but a friend on four is as loyal as they come. When a fight breaks out, this duo's bite is even worse than its bark.

name: Domain Spells
entries: Whenever you finish a short or long rest, choose an aspect of the harvest cycle: Sowing, Growing, or Reaping. You gain domain spells listed in the Harvest Domain Spells table for your cycle. See the Divine Domain class feature for how domain spells work.

name: Domain Spells
entries: You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Hunt Domain Spells table. See the Divine Domain class feature for how domain spells work.

entries.caption: Hunt Domain Spells
rows: {@spell locate animals or plants}, {@spell pass without trace}

name: Domain Spells
entries: Your connection to the threads of Fate allows you to always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Nornbound Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

name: Domain Spells
entries: You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Blood Domain Spells table.

name: Domain Spells
entries: You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Moon Domain Spells table.

name: Domineering Control
entries: With a glance, you can steer the emotions and thoughts of intelligent creatures.

entries.name: Befuddle
entries: You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the {@spell Hypnotic Pattern|XPHB} spell. When you cast the spell in this way, a creature with an Intelligence of 3 or lower automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the spell while a creature with an Intelligence of 4 or higher has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw.

entries.name: Entrance
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check and expend 2 Blood Points to choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to the result of your {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} check. On a failed save, the creature has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. At the end of each of the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} creature's turns, the creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature with an Intelligence of 3 or lower automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the effect.

entries.name: Persuade
entries: You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the {@spell Charm Monster|XPHB} spell.

entries.name: Terrify
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check and expend 1 Blood Point to choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to the result of your {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} check. On a failed save, the creature has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature's turns, the creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature with an Intelligence of 3 or lower automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the effect.

name: Doom Song
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to hasten a creature's doom. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use your Channel Divinity to choose a creature you can see within 120 feet of yourself. For 10 minutes, attack rolls against the creature can score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}.

name: Doomed to the Shadows
entries: You have perfected your assassin's strike. The extra damage from your Strike from the Dark feature increases to a number of d8s equal to your proficiency bonus (instead of that number of d4s), and you deal an extra {@damage 2d8} damage if the target is in dim light or darkness (instead of an extra {@damage 1d4} damage).

In addition, when you deal damage using Strike from the Dark, you can use your reaction to burn a seal on the creature, causing them to be {@condition blinded} for 1 minute instead of dealing the seal's damage.

name: Double or Nothing
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} using a Ranged weapon, you can gamble for a higher result. Roll a {@dice d20}. If the roll is a 10 or higher, roll all of the attack's damage dice four times and add them together, instead of only two times as normal for a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. If you roll a 9 or lower on the {@dice d20}, the {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} becomes a normal hit.

name: Draconic Lore
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can speak, read, and write {@language Draconic}. Additionally, whenever you make an Intelligence ({@skill History}) check related to draconic history or lore, you can add your proficiency bonus to the check. If you are already proficient in the {@skill History} skill, you can add double your proficiency bonus to the check instead.

name: Draconic Magic
entries: Starting at 10th level, you're able to cast certain druid spells while in your dragon shape. To cast a spell while in this form, it must use a druid spell slot level of 3rd or lower, and it can't require any material components.
In addition, your scales continue to toughen and your wings have become strong enough to carry you. You gain the following benefits while in your dragon shape:

items: Your AC is equal to 15 + your Dexterity modifier (maximum 2).
You have resistance to the damage type associated with your dragon shape.
You have a flying speed of 30 feet.

name: Draconic Majesty
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can present your {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB} and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to manifest an aura of draconic authority around yourself in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. Choose the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition. Each creature of your choice in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the chosen condition for 1 minute. A creature {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} by this feature makes another Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.

name: Dragon Domain
entries: {@i Channel the Might of Dragon Gods}

While dragons are the foremost worshipers of the Dragon Domain, the draconic deities accept the worship of any who crave wealth or power. Clerics of the Dragon Domain, often considered cultists, can channel the power and aspect of dragons, unleashing fearsome elemental magic and manifesting the awe-inspiring presence of an ancient wyrm.
The principal gods of the Dragon Domain include Tiamat, the five-headed mother of chromatic dragons, and Bahamut, the just and wise god of metallic dragons.

name: Dragon Domain Spells
entries: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Dragon Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Dragon Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Chromatic Orb|XPHB}, {@spell Command|XPHB}, {@spell Darkvision|XPHB}, {@spell Dragon's Breath|XPHB}

name: Dragon Shape
entries: At 2nd level, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature as a bonus action to transform into a unique form: your dragon shape. You become a Medium dragon while in this form, standing on all fours, but retain your normal character statistics and senses. Your dragon shape's AC is equal to 13 + your Dexterity modifier (maximum 2) and has a walking speed and climbing speed of 30 feet. In addition, when you take this form, you gain temporary hit points equal to your hit point maximum. When you return to your normal form, you lose any remaining temporary hit points.

You can remain in this form for a number of hours equal to half your druid level, rounded down. You can revert to your normal form earlier by using a bonus action on your turn. You automatically revert if you fall {@condition unconscious}, drop to 0 hit points, or die.

When you use your dragon shape, you determine what type of dragon to transform into. The type of dragon determines your scale color and breath weapon's damage type, as shown in the table below, but your appearance is otherwise up to you. Your wings aren't yet fully formed at 2nd level, but grow stronger as you gain levels in this class.
You can't cast spells while in this form, but gain a different set of actions you can use on each of your turns:

entries.name: Bite
entries: When you take the {@action Attack} action, you can use your dagger-like teeth to make an unarmed strike. You can use your Wisdom modifier, instead of Strength, for the attack and damage rolls with your bite. If you hit with it, you deal piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d12} + your Strength or Wisdom modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

entries.name: Breath Weapon
entries: You can use an action to exhale a plume of powerful energy from inside of you. Each creature in a 15-foot cone must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature takes {@dice 2d6} damage of your dragon's damage type on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Once you use this feature, it can't be used again for 1 minute.

Your breath weapon improves at certain levels. At 6th level, your breath weapon deals {@dice 3d6} damage and extends in a 20-foot cone. At 10th level, it deals {@dice 4d6} damage and extends in a 25-foot cone, and at 14th level it deals {@dice 5d6} damage and extends in a 30-foot cone.

name: Drain Life
entries: You gain an innate power to drain life from the living. After you take the Attack or {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. On a hit, the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} deals Necrotic damage equal to {@dice 1d6} plus your Charisma modifier instead of its normal damage.

When you hit a creature with Drain Life, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage to the target, plus another {@dice 1d8} per level of the spell slot. When you expend a spell slot in this way, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the amount of damage dealt.

name: Dread Hand
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can manifest the evidence of your foul pledge to otherworldly powers. When you do, one of your limbs transmogrifies into a monstrous appearance reminiscent of your dread power and you gain the benefits below for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Revenging Strike
entries: When you are hit by a melee attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against the creature that attacked you if it is within reach.

entries.name: Unslakeable Bloodlust
entries: When you hit a target with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can roll the attack's damage dice twice and use either roll against the target.

entries.name: Whirlwind of Violence
entries: The first time you miss with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} each turn, you can reroll the attack and must use the new result.

entries.name: Dread Powers
entries: A dread power can be any powerful malevolent entity capable of bestowing a portion of its power onto a mortal. Archdemons, Fey royalty, ancient liches, and unfathomable intelligences from beyond space and time are all possibilities.

name: Dual Death
entries: When you cast a Necromancy spell that targets only one creature, you can have it target a second creature within range.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending one use of your Bardic Inspiration dice (no action required).

name: Dunetreader
entries: Starting when you choose this origin at 1st level, you ignore {@quickref difficult terrain||3} created by sand, and you can tolerate temperatures as high as 150 degrees Fahrenheit without any additional protection.

name: Dungeon Precautions
entries: You can cast any of the following spells without a spell slot: {@spell Alarm|XPHB}, {@spell Comprehend Languages|XPHB}, {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB}, {@spell Detect Poison and Disease|XPHB}, {@spell Find Traps|XPHB}, {@spell Identify|XPHB}, and {@spell Purify Food and Drink|XPHB}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this feature (choose the ability when you cast the spell).
You can use this feature five times and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Dungeoneer
entries: {@i Survive the Dungeon}

Only fools would dive headfirst into an abandoned crypt filled with monsters and deathtraps, but it seems only fools emerge from such crypts laden with as much loot as they can carry. The archetypal dungeon delver is a veteran of such suicidal dungeon delves, and has become intimately familiar with the hazards therein. In the course of their adventures, such a Dungeoneer will have adopted countless best practices, along with a litany of unproven superstitions which they believe keeps them alive. Principles from "always be the first one to hit the monster" to "never be the first one to touch a treasure chest" line a Dungeoneer's journal. However, it's probably better to be paranoid and superstitious than lying at the bottom of a pit trap, incinerated by a Fireball, or digested by a mimic.

name: Durable Presence
entries: You now regain all expended uses of your Bolstering Presence feature when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Duty Over Death
entries: Starting at 17th level, you can exert your power to call companions back from the brink of death. When an ally you can see within 60 feet of you is reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, they instead remain conscious and regain hit points equal to half their maximum hit points. You can use this feature only if you aren't {@condition incapacitated}. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Eagle Eye
entries: Beginning at 10th level, your attack made immediately after or during your Launch scores a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20. If you hit a flying creature with this attack, it must also make a Strength saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failed save, its speed is reduced to 0 feet until the start of its next turn.

In addition, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Perception} skill if you don't already have it, and your proficiency bonus is doubled for any Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check you make that relies on sight.

name: Eagle Eye [Maneuver]
entries: Once per turn when you miss with a ranged attack roll, you can expend one {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die} and add it to the attack roll, potentially causing the attack to hit.

name: Eclipse of Ill Omen
entries: At 17th level, you can call upon the vermillion moon Ruidus to flare in the sky above you, eclipsing all other light. Its power surrounds you even where the sky can't be seen, and even on other planes. As a bonus action, you can manifest an area of reddish, dim light in a 60-foot radius around you. In addition to the normal effects of dim light, creatures in the area make {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1} with {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage}. When you create this eclipse, you can choose any number of creatures that are unaffected by it.

This eclipse lasts while you concentrate (as if concentrating on a spell) for up to 1 minute. Concentrating on this feature counts as concentrating on a Moon Domain spell for the purpose of your {@subclassFeature Channel Divinity: Mind of Two Moons|Cleric|PHB|Moon|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|6|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Mind of Two Moons} feature.

Additionally, once per turn when you deal radiant damage to any creatures in this area of dim light, you can curse one of those creatures until the eclipse ends (no action required). A creature cursed in this way has its speed halved and can't regain hit points.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.

name: Edit Spell
entries: Choose a spell in your spellbook that is level 1 or higher. When you prepare that spell, you can give it one or more of the following benefits:

items: The spell save DC of the chosen spell, if any, increases by 1.
If that spell deals damage, you can change that damage's type to a different one of your choice.
If that spell requires a saving throw, you can change that saving throw to Intelligence.

entries: You can prepare the chosen spell multiple times, choosing different benefits for each preparation. Each modified version of the spell counts against your prepared spells.
When you make these changes, you can alter the spell's name. For example, {@spell Burning Hands|XPHB} changed to deal Cold damage and require an Intelligence saving throw might be named Mind Freeze.

When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change your chosen spell. When you change the chosen spell, the benefits to the previous chosen spell end and you no longer have the altered versions prepared.

name: Egotistical
entries: Injuries to your pride enrage you. You are considered {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} if your current {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are below your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum.

name: Eldritch Appetite
entries: When you reduce an enemy to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} with your Drain Life feature, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to consume the last of its fleeting mortality. When you do so, you regain one of your expended Pact Magic spell slots.
