Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Eldritch Contagion
entries: You've been gifted with the ability to impart a fleeting taste of the unknowable on others. When you take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast a spell using a spell slot that targets one or more creatures, you can force one target of the original spell to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, roll on the Eldritch Effects table, and the target creature suffers that effect for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. This effect ends early if you use this feature again.

entries.caption: Eldritch Effects
rows: The creature can't speak or cast spells that have Verbal components.
The creature takes {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage at the start of each of its turns.
The creature is disoriented. If it uses more than 5 feet of its movement to do anything other than stand, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
The creature is distracted by visions and voices and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks.

The creature is unsure of itself. On its turns, it can take either an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, not both, and it can make only one attack if it takes the {@action Attack|XPHB} action.
The creature is reckless. It has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls, but attack rolls against it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.
The creature has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition and can't see anything more than 30 feet away.
The creature has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

name: Eldritch Domain
entries: {@i Wield the Power that Killed the Gods}

Even the most benevolent divine beings operate outside the bounds of mortal comprehension. These eldritch forces sing a siren song that calls to mortal worshippers through lucid dreams and terrible whispers. The Eldritch Domain empowers the followers of the unknown and distant forces of chaos, divine entities of eldritch oblivion, and dead gods.

name: Eldritch Domain Spells
entries: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Eldritch Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Eldritch Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB}, {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|XPHB|Hideous Laughter}, {@spell See Invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell Sleep|XPHB}

name: Eldritch Frenzy
entries: Starting at 14th level, you can use an action to revive your expended eldritch heads in a frenzied burst, during which time they become visible to everyone. When you do, you regain all expended heads, which releases a thunderous roar audible out to 300 feet as they tear into existence. Choose a number of creatures within 60 feet of you up to the number of heads you regain in this way. Each target must make an Intelligence saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 4d8} psychic damage and is {@condition incapacitated} until the end of your next turn as its mind is flooded with otherworldly energy. On a successful save, a target takes half as much psychic damage and isn't {@condition incapacitated}.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Eldritch Heads
entries: At 1st level, you gain a number of eldritch heads equal to your proficiency bonus. Only you and creatures with {@sense truesight} can see these heads, which sprout from your shoulders as representations of your patron. You can choose to ignore the heads and cause them to vanish from your vision.
These eldritch heads provide you with motes of power from your patron that can be expended to grant you the following benefits:

items: Once per turn, you can expend one head when you hit a creature with an attack to cause that creature to take extra psychic damage equal to 1 + your proficiency bonus.
When you make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check, you can expend one head to gain advantage on the roll. When you do, your eldritch heads become briefly visible to everyone.
When you fail a death saving throw, you can expend one head to succeed instead.

entries: When a head is expended, its appearance becomes wispy and gaseous, but its glowing eyes remain. You regain all expended heads when you finish a long rest.
In addition, you can use a bonus action to beseech your patron to restore two of your expended heads. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Electric Beast
entries: You are one with the lightning that flows through you. You can add your Constitution modifier to your Vessel Damage, and the options of your Unbound Storm improve in the following ways.

items.name: Electrified Chains
items.entry: An ensnared creature must make the Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check if it attempts to move 5 feet, and on a failure, it can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Fulgurant Strike
items.entry: The size of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} increases to 20 feet, and you can choose a number of creatures equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum one) that automatically succeed on the saving throw.

items.name: Lightning Step
items.entry: When you rush, you can move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and you can choose to merge with the lightning, teleporting the distance moved instead.

name: Elemental Arrows
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can imbue a {@item Longbow|XPHB} or {@item Shortbow|XPHB} with elemental energy for 1 minute. Choose one of the following damage types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. For the duration, the imbued weapon deals damage of the selected type instead of its normal type and deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of the chosen type when it hits. At the start of each of your turns, you can change this choice.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Elemental Discharge I
entries: Your companions gain the ability to unleash a torrent of elemental energy in a devastating blow. When you infuse a companion at the end of a long rest, it gains an action option corresponding to the chosen element The DC for the saving throw equals your tamer spell save DC.

entries.name: Acid: Caustic Mist
entries: Your companion disperses an acidic vapour into a 20-foot cube originating from it that lasts for 1 minute, or until dispersed by a wind of moderate or greater speed (at least 10 miles per hour). Each other creature that starts its turn in the area must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 4d4} acid damage on a failure, or half as much damage on a success.

entries.name: Cold: Snap Freeze
entries: Your companion absorbs the heat in a 10-foot-radius sphere around it. Each other creature in the area must make a Constitution saving throw On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d8} cold damage and its speed is halved until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and its speed isn't affected.

entries.name: Fire: Flametongue
entries: Your companion unleashes a raging inferno in a 25-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 6d6} fire damage on a failure, or half as much damage on a success. The fire ignites any flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried.

entries.name: Lightning: Sparkstep
entries: Your companion discharges lightning in a 10-foot-radius sphere. Each other creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} lightning damage and it can't take reactions until the start of its next turn On a success, it takes half as much damage and can take reactions as normal. After the saving throws are resolved, your companion can immediately fly up to 30 feet as part of this action.
Once a companion uses one of these actions, it can't use any action granted by this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Elemental Discharge II
entries: Starting at 18th level, a companion can use this action twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.

name: Elementally Imbued
entries: While in a Wild Shape form, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Elemental Strikes
entries: Each of your attacks in a Wild Shape form can deal its normal damage type, Acid damage, Cold damage, Fire damage, or Lightning damage. You make this choice each time you hit with those attacks.

entries.name: Elemental Cascade
entries: Choose one of the following damage types: Acid, Cold, Fire, or Lightning. Once per turn when you hit with a Wild Shape form's attack, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to deal extra damage of the chosen type equal to {@dice 1d6} per level of the spell slot, to a maximum of {@dice 5d6}. The target must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target suffers an effect based on the chosen damage type for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Acid
entries: The target suffers a penalty to AC equal to half your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

entries.name: Cold
entries: The target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0 and they have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength and Dexterity checks.

entries.name: Fire
entries: At the start of each of its turns, the target takes Fire damage equal to your Wisdom modifier.

entries.name: Lightning
entries: The target can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, and the first attack it makes on each of its turns has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

name: Embolden Allies
entries: As a bonus action, you restore a total number of hit points equal to five times your illrigger level, divided however you choose between yourself and other creatures within 30 feet of you.

name: Empowered Cantrips
entries: Starting at 8th level, your cleric cantrips deal extra damage equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1).

name: Encouraging Smite
entries: Immediately after you cast Divine Smite, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and select creatures of your choice within 30 feet of yourself. Until the start of your next turn, these creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on their attack rolls and saving throws against the target of your Divine Smite, and their attacks against the target deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Thunder damage.

name: Endless Dance
entries: Your dance has become so invigorating that it can inspire an ally to attack. When a creature would gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} from your Inspirational Dance feature, it can instead choose to take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make one attack using a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

In addition, your endless dancing allows you to more easily avoid being hit. You can take the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, and whenever you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to expend a Bardic Inspiration die, you can take the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action as part of that {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

name: Endless Evolution
entries: When you gain Mutation Points, you gain an additional number of Mutation Points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). In addition, you can now spend your Mutation Points on the following Mutations.

name: Endocrine Overload
entries: Over the course of 1 hour (which can be done during a rest), you can craft a capsule of potent stimulants, choosing from either the Brutish or Swift archetypes, and embed it within your adrenal gland With a slight tensing of your brain muscles, you can crack this capsule as a bonus action, stimulating your body For the next minute, you gain the following benefits based on the archetype you chose:

entries.name: Brutish
items: If you are smaller than Large, you become Large, and your weight increases proportionately If you lack the room to become Large, your size doesn't change.
Your Strength score increases to match your Intelligence score if it isn't already higher.
You have advantage on Strength and Constitution checks and Strength and Constitution saving throws.

You grow an appendage with which you can make melee weapon attacks When you grow the weapon, you decide whether it deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage You are proficient with this weapon and use your Strength modifier for attack and damage rolls. The weapon deals {@damage 2d10} damage.

You can attack twice, instead of once, when you take the Attack action on your turn You ignore this benefit if you already have a feature, like Extra Attack, that lets you attack more than once when you take the Attack action on your turn.
You gain temporary hit points equal to twice your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 2) at the start of each of your turns.

entries.name: Swift
items: Your Dexterity score increases to match your Intelligence score if it isn't already higher.
You have advantage on Dexterity checks and saving throws.
Your cantrips with a casting time of 1 action have a casting time of 1 action or 1 bonus action

entries: You gain the benefits of the {@spell haste} spell, which can't be dispelled:

items: Your speed is doubled.
You gain a +2 bonus to AC.
You can take one additional action on each of your turns, which can be used only to take the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action.

entries.name: Relapse
entries: When the minute elapses, you gain one level of {@condition exhaustion}, and you can't move or take actions until after your next turn, as a wave of lethargy sweeps over you. You must craft another capsule before you can use this feature again.

name: Enervate
entries: You learn to channel life force between you and your companions. As an action while your summoned companion is within 100 feet of you, you can deal necrotic damage to your companion up to a value equal to twice your tamer level. This damage can't be reduced in any way. You then regain hit points equal to the damage dealt. Alternatively, you can deal the necrotic damage to yourself and restore hit points to your summoned companion equal to the damage you took.

name: Enervating Spell
entries: When you deal damage to a creature with an illrigger spell of 1st level or higher, you can expend a seal (no action required) and imbue the spell with weakening magic. The target has vulnerability to that spell's damage. If they normally have resistance or immunity to the spell's damage, that resistance or immunity is suppressed for this spell, and the target has vulnerability to the damage instead.

name: Entrancing Movement
entries: Your movements become so graceful that even the most cold-hearted enemies are filled with remorse for having stopped your dance. Whenever a creature hits you with an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} or hits you with an attack roll while you're benefiting from the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action, that creature takes Psychic damage equal to your Charisma modifier plus half your Bard level (round down).

In addition, you always have the {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it without a Verbal component. With this feature, you can cast it without expending a spell slot; when you do, it is cast as a level 3 spell, and the targets don't make their saving throws with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} as a result of you or your allies fighting them. Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Entropic Infection
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and select a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. For 1 minute, if you deal damage to the target, the target takes an extra {@damage 2d6} Necrotic damage. In addition, the target loses {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Necrotic damage. The target can make a Constitution save against the Paladin's spell save DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Entropy's Apex
entries: You have mastered the ability to hasten the inevitable slide toward entropy. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Enhanced Ruinous Smite
entries: Until the end of your next turn, any creature affected by your Ruinous Smite suffers a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19-20 on the {@dice d20}.

entries.name: Improved Inexorable Onslaught
entries: While your Ruin Incarnate feature is active, you can attack with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} three times instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

entries.name: World Breaker
entries: You regain your use of your Shake the Earth feature when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Envenomed Attack
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can apply a poison dose to a weapon or up to 20 pieces of ammunition. Once applied, the poison retains its potency for 1 minute. Your attacks with the {@condition poisoned} item deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Poison damage on a hit.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
At Ranger level 11, the extra Poison damage increases to {@dice 2d4}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Epidemic
entries: Your plague has reached the height of its potency and its symptoms rapidly afflict your foes. Your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|PHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14|Miasmic Plague} ignores a target's immunity to the {@condition poisoned} condition. Additionally, when you deal necrotic damage to a target cursed by your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|PHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14|Miasmic Plague}, it takes extra necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die.

name: Epidemic
entries: Your plague has reached the height of its potency and its symptoms rapidly afflict your foes. Your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|XPHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24|Miasmic Plague} ignores a target's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. Additionally, when you deal Necrotic damage to a target cursed by your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|XPHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24|Miasmic Plague}, it takes extra Necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die.

name: Equipped for Battle
entries: You gain training with Heavy armor.

name: Escape Artist
entries: You become slippery and evasive, capable of worming out of even the tightest holds. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks and saving throws made to avoid or end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions. When you have one of those conditions, you can attempt to escape as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} if doing so would normally require an action.

In addition, while you're within 5 feet of a solid surface (such as the ground or a wall), you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and spend 1 Rune Point to magically create a rune on that surface. When you do, you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition for 10 minutes. The condition ends early immediately after you make an attack roll, deal damage, cast a spell, or leave the space where you created the rune.

name: Essence Runes
entries: At 1st level, your body begins to express your innate magic as runes traced out across your skin. You start with 1 essence rune, and gain an additional rune whenever you gain a level in this class. These runes can manifest anywhere on your body, though the first usually manifests on the forehead. Your essence runes remain invisible when inert.

At the end of a turn during which you spent one or more sorcery points, a number of your essence runes equal to the number of sorcery points you spent begin to glow with stored energy, becoming charged runes. You use these charged runes to power your Runechild subclass features. Also, as a bonus action, you may spend a sorcery point to convert two essence runes into two charged runes.
If you have no sorcery points and no charged runes, you can convert a single essence rune into a charged rune as an action.
If you have 5 or more charged runes, you emit bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet.

If you expend a charged rune to use one of your Runechild features, it returns to being an inert essence rune. Any charged runes also revert to inert essence runes after you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.

name: Eternal Night
entries: Your vampire patron grants you a taste of true immortality. You no longer age, and you gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: At the start of each of your turns, you regain {@dice 1d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} if you have at least 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} and you aren't in direct sunlight or running water. If you take Radiant damage, you don't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} from this feature at the start of your next turn.
When you use your Drain Life feature, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage without expending a spell slot.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Eternal War Eruption
entries: You use the powers at your command to call forth warring celestials and infernals. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you summon a manifestation of the war between Arch Daemons and Arch Seraphs in a 30-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point within 120 feet of yourself.

Each creature in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} must make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d10} Necrotic damage, {@damage 4d10} Radiant damage, and has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.
As part of the same action, you can change the power you are siphoning from, and you also regain 1 Wizard spell slot of your choice of 5th level or lower.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Eternal Wheel
entries: When you use your {@subclassFeature Channel Divinity: Bountiful Harvest|Cleric|PHB|Harvest|CrookedMoon14|2|CrookedMoon14}, you can invoke the endless cycle of life, death, and rebirth to grant yourself and the creatures affected by your {@classFeature Channel Divinity|Cleric|PHB|2} an additional benefit based on your current aspect:

entries.name: Sowing
entries: Targets gain the effects of the {@spell Regenerate} spell for 1 minute, or until you lose {@status concentration}.

entries.name: Growing
entries: Targets gain advantage on saving throws and ability checks for up to 1 hour, or until you lose {@status concentration} (as if {@status concentration||concentrating} on a spell).

entries.name: Reaping
entries: Targets gain resistance to necrotic, psychic, and poison damage for 1 hour.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest unless you expend a spell slot of 7th level or higher (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Eternal Wheel
entries: When you use your {@subclassFeature Bountiful Harvest|Cleric|XPHB|Harvest|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24}, you can invoke the endless cycle of life, death, and rebirth to grant yourself and the creatures affected by your {@classFeature Channel Divinity|Cleric|XPHB|2} an additional benefit based on your current aspect:

entries.name: Sowing
entries: Targets gain the effects of the {@spell Regenerate|XPHB} spell for 1 minute, or until you lose {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

entries.name: Growing
entries: Targets gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws and ability checks for up to 1 hour, or until you lose {@status Concentration|XPHB} (as if {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} on a spell).

entries.name: Reaping
entries: Targets gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic, Psychic, and Poison damage for 1 hour.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend a spell slot of level 7+ (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Eternity in Stone
entries: When you reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can cause it to turn to stone. If you do so, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 1d10} + your Warlock level. A creature turned to stone in this way has the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Ever Prideful
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can expend 1 Focus Point to enter a trance. While in this trance, you have the following effects:

items: You are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition.
You can't speak.
You can't cast or concentrate on spells.
You suffer 1 {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} failure from damage from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} instead of 2.

entries: Whenever you start your turn with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}, you must expend 1 Focus Point to maintain a trance, and you make {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws} as normal.

name: Ever Vigilant
entries: Your long nights of vigilance have left your senses attuned to signs of danger, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You gain {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet. If you already have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} when you gain this feature, its range increases by 60 feet.

entries.name: Keen Senses
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls and Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Warning Shout
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to warn creatures of your choice within 30 feet of yourself that can see or hear you. Each creature can then take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on its {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll and move up to half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Evil Eye
entries: You can place a minor curse with a glance. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself to be cursed by your Evil Eye. While a creature is cursed by your Evil Eye, you can deal Sneak Attack damage to the creature if you don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll.
The creature remains cursed by your Evil Eye for 1 minute or until you curse a different creature with your Evil Eye, whichever comes first.

name: Evil Eye
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain the ability to place a minor curse on others with a glance. As a bonus action on your turn, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet. The chosen creature must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your misfortune save DC or be marked by your evil eye. While a creature is marked by your evil eye, you can use your Sneak Attack against the creature even if you don't have advantage on the attack roll, but not if you have disadvantage on it.
The creature remains marked by your evil eye for 1 minute or until you mark a different creature with your evil eye, whichever comes first.

name: Exalted Assembly of the Feline Court

entries: If man could be crossed with a cat, it would improve man but deteriorate the cat.

The entities of the Cthulhu Mythos have many enemies. Not all who learn of these terrible creatures fall victim to their promises of forbidden power. Across the cosmos, a grand conspiracy consisting of the most unlikely of creatures.

A court of intelligent house cats seek to protect the world from the Mythos. Hailing from across planes, worlds, and planets, they use magic and manipulation to ensure that their centuries of work domesticating humans remains uninterrupted. For all their skill at providing food, warmth, and shelter, humans are all too prone to corruption, meddling in powers far beyond their grasp. All it takes is one fool with a forbidden book and generations of work crumbles as yet another human civilization falls to dust.
The Exalted Assembly of the Feline Court coordinates efforts to sustain and protect their servants. They forge magical pact with those who show the right mix of cunning, bravery, and etiquette.

name: Executive Chef
entries: Your confidence and authority in the kitchen translates to battlefield command. When a creature that can hear you rolls one of your Bardic Inspiration dice or eats one of your Petit Fours, you can shout authoritative, verbal encouragement (no action required). The creature can immediately use its reaction to either make one weapon attack or move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. A creature that eats a Petit Fours can attack or move as described as part of the same action or reaction used to eat the Petit Fours.

name: Exit Strategy
entries: When you take damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to evade further harm. You have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn, and you can immediately move up to 10 feet.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending one {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die} (no action required).

name: Expanded Spell List
entries: You learn the {@spell Vicious Mockery} cantrip, and The Great Fool lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Great Fool Expanded Spells
rows: {@spell Disguise Self|PHB}, {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|PHB}, {@spell Vicious Mockery|PHB}

name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Horned King Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Horned King Expanded Spells
rows: {@spell Animal Friendship|PHB}, {@spell Bane|PHB}, {@spell Spike Growth|PHB}, {@spell Suggestion|PHB}

name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Many lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

rows: {@spell arcane eye}, {@spell evard's black tentacles|PHB|black tentacles}

name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Parasite lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Parasite Expanded Spells
rows: {@spell Evard's black tentacles}, {@spell freedom of movement}

entries.name: Flavouring Spells
entries: Some of the spells in the Parasite Expanded Spells table have a divine flavour to them. Feel free to corrupt these to fit your parasitic patron! For example, {@spell sanctuary} might be represented as part of your parasitic symbiont warding the target of your spell from damaging blows. {@spell Spirit guardians} probably deals necrotic damage, even if you're not evil, and could manifest as viscous threads of corrupting ichor that whirl around you with a mind of their own. If you're especially into horror, you could even express {@spell dominate person} as a part of your patron physically invading your target's cranium through a nostril!

name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Predator lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

name: Expect an Ambush
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage on the first round of combat.

name: Exsanguinate
entries: When you use your Blood Boon, you regain spent {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} equal to half your Druid level and give {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Druid level to a number of creatures up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one creature) that you can see within 60 feet of yourself.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Exsanguinate
entries: You can drain enemies to embolden your allies. Whenever you burn one or more seals on a creature who isn't a Construct or Undead, you can choose an ally you can see within 30 feet of you. That ally gains temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt by the seals to the interdicted creature.

name: Extort Truth
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can precisely strike a hidden cluster of nerves on a creature, temporarily preventing it from masking its true thoughts and intent. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 1 ki point to force it to make a Charisma {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw}. On a failed save, the creature is unable to speak a deliberate lie, and all Charisma checks directed at the creature are made with {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|advantage} for up to 10 minutes. You know if it succeeded or failed on its {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw}.

An affected creature is aware of the effect and can thus avoid answering questions to which it would normally respond with a lie. Such a creature can be evasive in its answers as long as the effect lasts.
If you wish to impose this effect on a creature without injuring it, you can attack the creature to simply touch it, dealing no damage on a hit.

name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your cantrips in place of one of those attacks.

name: Extra Attack
entries: Starting at 7th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your Sorcerer cantrips that has a casting time of an action in place of one of those attacks.

name: Extract Aspects
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can strike pressure points to intuit crucial information about a foe. When you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can analyze it. Whenever an analyzed creature misses you with an attack, you can immediately use your reaction to make an unarmed strike against that creature if it's within your reach. This benefit lasts until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}.
Additionally, when you analyze a creature, you learn all of its damage vulnerabilities, damage resistances, damage immunities, and condition immunities.

name: Extradimensional Acuity
entries: Your patron grants you the ability to maintain a small pocket dimension. This extradimensional space is always accessible to you and can hold up to 50 pounds of inanimate material, not exceeding a volume of 1 cubic foot. You can access and interact with this space using your hands the same way you would with a normal container. Your hands disappear within the space while they're accessing it.

Placing a {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG}, {@item Heward's Handy Haversack|XDMG}, {@item Portable Hole|XDMG}, or similar item inside your pocket dimension instantly destroys that item, and the contents of the two extradimensional spaces are scattered in the Astral Plane. When this happens, you are unable to access your pocket dimension again until 7 days have passed.
In addition, you can sense whether extradimensional spaces (other than the one given to you by your patron) are present within 60 feet of you. This feature doesn't reveal their location or number.

name: Extradimensional Mastery
entries: The fabric of existence is clear to you. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Astral Clarity
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to enhance your perception of reality. For 10 minutes, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on sight, and you have {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Magical Snoop
entries: While you're within 10 feet of a magic item that contains an extradimensional space, you can sense what objects are stored within it.

entries.name: Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Force damage.

name: Eye of Twilight
entries: Beginning at 1st level, a divine blessing grants you the ability to see more clearly in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in magical or nonmagical darkness as if it were only dim light. You can't discern color in the darkness, only shades of gray.

When you reach 6th level, you can see in dim light within 120 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in magical or nonmagical darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in the darkness, only shades of gray.
At 8th level, you can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical within 120 feet.

Finally, at 17th level, your eyes are able to see the truth hiding within darkness. You gain the ability to call upon the powers of your deity to grant yourself {@sense truesight} within 120 feet of you for a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of 1 minute). Your {@sense truesight} only functions while in conditions of magical or nonmagical darkness. Once you have used this feature, you cannot use it again until you have completed a long rest.

name: Eyes In the Dark
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, your experience with the raw magic of shadow affects your senses. You gain {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 120 feet.

name: Eyes on the Prize
entries: You focus everything on bringing your chosen target down. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action and target only one creature with all your attacks, you can make an additional attack against that creature. If the additional attack is a melee attack and it hits, the target has either the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} or {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition (your choice). If the additional attack is a ranged attack and it hits, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

name: Face of Rage
entries: When you activate your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1}, your countenance distorts and your body swells. Creatures that haven't witnessed your transformation, now or previously, don't recognize you. In addition, while your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: You can roll {@dice 1d8} in place of the normal damage of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, and whenever you deal damage with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

When you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can push it 10 feet or force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, the creature has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
You count as one size larger when determining the success or failure of a Grapple, and when you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, your reach is 5 feet greater than normal.

name: Fade to Black
entries: At 6th level, you can conceal yourself in shadow. As a bonus action when you are in dim light or darkness, you can magically become {@condition invisible} for 1 minute. This effect ends early if you attack or cast a spell. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Fair and Foul
entries: The spells listed below can be added to your spellbook for no cost when you reach the associated level.

Each time you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose whether you are siphoning power from Arch Daemons or Arch Seraphs. You can prepare the spells listed for your Wizard level and lower, but not those from the opposite faction.

name: Fan the Hammer [Maneuver]
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action with a Ranged weapon that doesn't have {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed}, you can expend one Risk Die as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make two additional ranged attacks with that weapon. These additional attacks always have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, regardless of circumstance. You can't use the {@itemMastery Automatic|ValdaGunslinger} mastery property with these attacks, and you must have a free hand to use this maneuver.

name: Fancy Gunplay
entries: Your flashy weapon tricks grant you the following benefits.

entries.name: Gun Spinning
entries: Once per turn when you make a Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check or a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check using one of your Ranged weapons, you can roll a {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die} and add it to the ability check without expending it.

entries.name: Speed Loader
entries: On your turn, you can reload a weapon with {@itemProperty GC:VSS-Re|ValdaGunslinger|Reload} without taking an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

name: Fast Movement
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet. It increases by another 5 feet when you reach Bard levels 6 (total increase of 15 feet) and 14 (total increase of 20 feet).

name: Favorite Trick
entries: At 6th level, you have gained enough mastery over one of your Traveler's Tricks that you can use it whenever it's needed. You may choose one Traveler's Trick that you know and designate it as your favorite trick. If you roll initiative and have no uses of Bardic Inspiration remaining, you regain one use of it. Any Bardic Inspiration gained in this way can only be used to perform your favorite trick.

name: Favorite Trick
entries: At 14th level you can select a second favorite trick from among Traveler's Tricks you know.

name: Fear of the Dark
entries: Also at 3rd level, your intimate knowledge of darkness allows you to harness its frightful properties to the fullest and keep your allies grounded. While in dim light or darkness, you and any allies that can see you have advantage against {@condition frightened|phb|fear} effects. Additionally, any hostile creatures that can see you roll with disadvantage against fear effects.

name: Fearsome
entries: Your vampiric presence exudes menace from the rise of your inner Beast.

entries.name: Dread Gaze
entries: You bare your fangs, your eyes flash with predatory hunger, and you let out a hiss that strikes terror in the hearts of others. You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the {@spell Fear|XPHB} spell.

entries.name: Predatory Aura
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks.

name: Fearsome Presence
entries: At 10th level, you learn how to channel the presence of a frightful beast, even when not transformed. You can use your action to cause each hostile creature you can see within a 30-foot radius to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the target becomes {@condition frightened} of you for 1 minute, and it is {@condition restrained} until the end of your next turn. A {@condition frightened} creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Feline Affinity
entries: You gain the ability to speak with the world's true nobility. You can cast {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB} without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell this way, the only Beasts you can verbally communicate with are cats, though most cats are reluctant to converse with a creature as simple as you.

name: Feline Form
entries: Your patron takes pity on you and gives you the ability to adopt a superior, more pleasing form. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you shape-shift into a Cat, a Tiny Beast. You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Warlock level (rounded down) or until you use this feature again, have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or die. You can also leave the form early as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. While in this form, you retain your personality, memories, and ability to speak, and the following rules apply:

entries.name: Game Statistics
entries: Your game statistics are replaced by the Beast's stat block, but you retain your creature type; {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}; {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. You also retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies and use your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} for them, in addition to gaining the proficiencies of the creature. If a skill or saving throw modifier in the Beast's stat block is higher than yours, use the one in the stat block.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries: While in your cat form, you can only casts spells that are on your Feline Spells feature. You can cast these spells without needing Material components. In addition, if you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition from the {@action Hide|XPHB} action and cast a spell that doesn't target a {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} creature, you retain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. Shapeshifting doesn't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB} or otherwise interfere with a spell you've already cast.

entries.name: Equipment
entries: You choose whether your equipment falls in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the DM decides whether it's practical for your Tiny Beast form to wear a piece of equipment. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with the form. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect while you're in that form.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Feline Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Feline Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Feline Spells
rows: {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB}, {@spell Cat's Spring|CthulhuTorchlight}, {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB}, {@spell Feline Grace|CthulhuTorchlight}, {@spell Misty Step|XPHB}, {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB}

name: Feral Celerity
entries: Your rage grants you animalistic speed of action. As part of the bonus action to enter a rage, you can make one weapon attack. Additionally, you gain the ability to concentrate on maneuvers, even while you are raging. You still cannot concentrate on spells while raging.

name: Feral Howl
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can roll a {@dice d4} and increase your Bestial Aspect Level to the number rolled.

name: Feral Spirit
entries: Your connection to your wild self forges a spiritual bridge with Beasts.

entries.name: Beastmind
entries: While you look in the eyes of a Beast within 30 feet of yourself, you can speak telepathically with it, and you can use any of the {@action Influence|XPHB} action's skill options with it.

entries.name: Like Minds
entries: You can cast the {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot. And when you cast the spell in this way, it is cast as if you had used a spell slot level equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Wild Hunger
entries: When you are affected by the {@classFeature The Beast|Kindred|BoundByBlood|1||Hunger} of your Beast feature, you can deal {@damage 1d6} extra Slashing damage when you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, and you also count as one size larger when determining what you can grapple.

name: Ferocious Rage
entries: When you enter your rage, creatures of your choice within 10 feet that can see you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Martial Maneuvers save DC. On a failed saving throw, the creature is {@condition frightened} of you until the end of its next turn.

name: Fervent Inquisitor
entries: Whenever a creature damages you or one of your allies within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to gain advantage on your next attack roll against the creature that dealt the damage. Additionally, whenever you deal fire or radiant damage to a creature with half its hit points or fewer, you become aware of any lies the creature has willingly and knowingly spoken to you in the past 24 hours.

name: Fervent Inquisitor
entries: Whenever a creature damages you or one of your allies within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your next attack roll against the creature that dealt the damage. Additionally, whenever you deal Fire or Radiant damage to a {@status Bloodied|XPHB} creature, you become aware of any lies the creature has willingly and knowingly spoken to you in the past 24 hours.

name: Festus Domain
entries: Gods of eating and drinking, such as Daghdha or Dionysus, promote the value of a good meal as much as they do the joy of sharing it with friends. As a follower of this domain, you believe that a good feast can be enough to settle most wars. You may know this first-hand: perhaps your life has been marred by poverty and survival with spoiled scraps, or maybe you've been blessed with lovingly-cooked meals and the joy of a full stomach. Regardless of your origins, you recognize the magic of a good meal and the power it has on a person's spirit and well-being.

Through your passion and devotion, you see mealtime as a joyous way to worship the magic of food and your chosen deity. You are a capable chef with an appreciation of all food, both good and bad. You know that a foul meal can turn even the most veteran of stomachs against themselves, and have learned to harness this power for yourself. Like food, most people will like you at your best, but everyone will fear you at your worst.

name: Festus Domain Spells
entries: You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Festus Domain Spells table. See the Divine Domain class feature for how domain spells work.

rows: {@spell create food and water}, {@spell stinking cloud}

name: Field Surgeon
entries: By 9th level, your medical expertise and blood magic allow you to painlessly mend an ally's wounds using surgical techniques. You decide to use this feature at the start of a short rest, choosing a willing creature within your reach when you do. Roll your Sneak Attack dice and record the result. At the end of the short rest, that creature regains a number of hit points equal to the total of your Sneak Attack dice roll. Once a creature regains hit points from this feature, it can't do so again until it finishes a long rest.

name: Fieldcraft
entries: Your experience in the field grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Quick Change
entries: Using a {@item Disguise Kit|XPHB}, you can create a Costume and don it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Slick Talker
entries: Whenever you make a Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) or Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

name: Fiendish Punishment
entries: The fiendish presence in your demonshard can punish your enemies. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, if you take damage from a creature that you can see within 60 feet of yourself, the creature takes {@damage 1d4} Fire or Necrotic damage (your choice). You can use this feature only once per turn.

In addition, if an allied creature within 10 feet of you takes damage from a creature that you can see within 60 feet of yourself, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cause the damaging creature to take {@damage 1d4} Fire or Necrotic damage (your choice). The damage increases when you reach Barbarian levels 6 ({@dice 1d6}), 10 ({@dice 1d8}), 14 ({@dice 1d10}) and 20 ({@dice 1d12}).

name: Fighting Fury
entries: You can channel the rage simmering below the surface, funneling it into your physical strength and speed. You can expend 1 Blood Point to gain the following benefits for 1 minute.

entries.name: Brawn
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the first attack roll you make with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} on your turn.

entries.name: Swiftness
entries: You can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Dodge|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Weapon Training
entries: You gain proficiency with Martial weapons, and your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice.

name: Fighting Pit
entries: At 6th level, you gain the ability to shore up your allies' reserves. As a reaction, when you or an ally that you can see within 30 feet of you is {@condition charmed}, {@condition frightened}, {@condition paralyzed}, or {@condition stunned}, you can remove that condition.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Fighting Style
entries: Also at 3rd level, you adopt a style of fighting as your speciality. Choose one of the following options. You cannot take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

name: Filth and Fortitude
entries: The time you've spent with plague-bearing rodents has rendered you {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions. Additionally, you gain proficiency in Constitution saving throws.

name: Final Breakthrough
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can swap a spell contained in your Prototype for another spell of the same level, chosen from the Artificer, Cleric, or Wizard spell list.
In addition, you ignore all class, species, spell, and level requirements on attuning to or using a magic item.

name: Final Judgement
entries: Your sanctified blade becomes imbued with holy power, granting you the following benefits.

items.name: Divine Spirits
items.entry: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action while wielding the blade, you can cast {@spell Spirit Guardians|XPHB} without a spell slot or components. Creatures within the area of the spell, for the purpose of your Sneak Attack, are considered within 5 feet of an ally of yours. Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend 3 Divine Points (no action required) to restore your use of it.

items.name: Radiant Blade
items.entry: You can speak a command word (no action required) to cause your blade to emit {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 30-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 30 feet. The light lasts until you speak the command word again or you stow your weapon. While emitting light in this way, the weapon is considered a magic weapon, and attacks made with it deal an extra {@damage 2d4} Radiant damage on a hit.

name: Final Night Catharsis
entries: You are overcome by an emotion a nearby spirit experienced at its death. You gain one of the following options of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change your choice.

entries.name: Hate
entries: When you miss with an attack roll against a creature, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll you make against it before the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Jealousy
entries: When a creature you have {@condition Grappled|XPHB} is about to make an ability check to end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition on itself, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on that roll.

entries.name: Terror
entries: While you are {@condition Bloodied|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to take the {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Disengage|XPHB} action.

name: Fine Tuning
entries: Whenever you cast an Artificer spell while you have {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} in your possession, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of the spell.

name: Fire and Brimstone
entries: As a bonus action, you embody cleansing flame and gain the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a 5th-level spell slot (no action required).

items: You gain immunity to fire damage.
Lashes of divine flame increase your reach by 10 feet, and your melee attacks ignore half and {@quickref Cover||3||three-quarters cover}.

When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, or when a hostile creature ends its turn within your reach, it must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone} and have its speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.

name: Fire and Brimstone
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you embody cleansing flame and gain the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Blazing Ardor
entries: You gain {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Fire damage.

entries.name: Relentless Judgment
entries: Lashes of divine flame increase your reach by 10 feet, and your melee attacks ignore Half and {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover}.

entries.name: Punish the Wicked
entries: When you hit a creature with an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB}, or when a {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} creature ends its turn within your reach, it must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.

name: First Vampire Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the First Vampire Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: First Vampire Spells
rows: {@spell Bane|XPHB}, {@spell Command|XPHB}, {@spell False Life|XPHB}, {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB}
{@spell Conjure Animals|XPHB} (bats, rats, or wolves only), {@spell Gaseous Form|XPHB}

name: Flash Freeze
entries: You're most confident on the ice. Your movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} while you're moving on icy terrain.

In addition, when a creature you can see within 5 feet of yourself hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to deal Cold damage to the attacker equal to your Charisma modifier plus half your Sorcerer level (round down). When you do, you can use your Create Ice feature as part of that {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

name: Fleetness
entries: Your celerity grants you bursts of incredible speed.

entries.name: Dizzying Speed
entries: You can expend 3 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Haste|XPHB} spell on yourself. When you cast the spell in this way, when the spell ends, you aren't {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} and your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} isn't reduced to 0.

name: Flickering Aura
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can choose whether your magic is light-shifted or dark-shifted. You can change your choice at the end of a long rest.

While light-shifted you can use an action to emit an aura of bright light in a 15-foot-radius sphere centered on yourself. While the aura persists, you can use a bonus action to expand or reduce its radius of bright light by 5 feet, to a maximum of 30 feet each or a minimum of 10 feet.
While dark-shifted you gain the same ability, but you project an aura of nonmagical darkness.

name: Focused Shot
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can choose to make only one ranged attack roll using a weapon to make a Focused Shot. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this attack roll and, on a hit, score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}.

name: Follow Through
entries: When a creature in your Aura of Protection becomes {@condition Bloodied|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and make an attack with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. This movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll

name: Forayer
entries: You patrol the land ceaselessly seeking to ambush the servants of the Enemy, for they are found in many places, not in Mordor only.

name: Forbidden Knowledge
entries: In your study of proscribed power, you learn {@language Deep Speech|PHB} or another language of your choice.
In addition, choose a 1st-level spell from the warlock spell list. You add it to your spellbook if it's not there already, and it is a wizard spell for you.

name: Forbidden Knowledge
entries: In your study of proscribed power, you learn {@language Deep Speech|XPHB} or another language of your choice.
In addition, choose a level 1 spell from the Warlock spell list. You always have it prepared. You can change your chosen spell when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Forbidden Magic
entries: The end of Etharis is a time when magic is unbound and magical powers long hidden are unearthed. When you cast a Sorcerer spell using a spell slot, you can choose one option below.

entries.name: Excessive
entries: If the spell requires a Material component with a cost, you can cast the spell without the Material component. You take Force damage equal to four times the level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}

entries.name: Inexorable
entries: Taking damage can't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB} on the spell. When the spell ends, you gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level.

entries.name: Pyrrhic
entries: If the spell requires an attack roll, the spell automatically hits and the attack roll is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by an amount equal to four times the level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum returns to normal.

name: Force of Personality
entries: Whenever any creature tries to attack you for the first time on a turn, you can use your reaction to roll a Charisma ({@skill Performance} or {@skill Persuasion}) ability check. If your check is higher than the creature's Wisdom ability score, it can't attack you on this turn, and it must choose a new target for its attack, or the attack is wasted.

name: Force of Will
entries: You can focus your will upon others in a mental vise of your supernatural dominance.

entries.name: Mesmerize
entries: You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} spell.

entries.name: Shhh ...
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 1 Blood Point to mentally lull a creature that you can see within 15 feet of yourself to sleep. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or gain the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition for 10 minutes. The effect ends if it takes damage or someone within 5 feet takes an action to shake it out of the effect. Creatures that don't sleep, such as elves, or that have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} condition automatically succeed on saves against this effect.

name: Forge Adept
entries: {@i Craft a Mighty Weapon out of Your Soul}

The daashor artificers of the Dhakaani Empire were the finest weaponsmiths in Khorvaire's history, as discussed in Uncharted Domains. As a Forge Adept, you carry on these ancient traditions, creating mystical weapons and armor, strengthening allies on the battlefield, and bringing down enemies with weapons imbued with your own soul energy. If you're dar, you learned these techniques from the masters of your clan. Are you content to follow ancient traditions, or do you want to add your own innovations? If you're not Dhakaani, did you learn these techniques from a daashor mentor? Did you steal this knowledge? Or are you replicating these traditions on your own?

name: Forge Adept Spells
entries: When you reach an Artificer level specified in the Forge Adept Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Forge Adept Spells
rows: {@spell Armor of Agathys|XPHB}, {@spell Shield of Faith|XPHB}

name: Form of Stone
entries: Stone is no prison to you. Whenever you have the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition, you are aware of your surroundings and you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Additionally, you have learned to take on a stone form to protect yourself from injury. As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when you take damage, you can give yourself the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. The {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition applies before you take the triggering damage, possibly granting {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to that damage. When the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition ends, you can choose to emerge from a stone surface into an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Form of the Beast
entries: At 1st level, you can use your bonus action to channel the ferocity and guile of your patron, transforming into a beastly figure. For 10 minutes, you gain the following abilities:

items: You are flooded with adrenaline, feeling nothing besides the thrill of the hunt. You gain temporary hit points equal to two times your warlock level, up to a maximum of 20 temporary hit points at 10th level. These temporary hit points last until the end of your transformation.
Your senses become supernaturally keen. You have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}), Wisdom ({@skill Perception}), and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks you make to track or stalk your prey.

You sprout a set of pointed teeth and razor-sharp claws, which are natural weapons you can use to make unarmed strikes against creatures within 5 feet of you. You have proficiency with these weapons and can use your Charisma modifier for the attack and damage rolls made using these natural weapons. On a hit, your bite deals {@damage 1d6} piercing damage, and your claws deal {@damage 1d4} slashing damage. If you already had a bite or claw attack (talon attacks count as claw attacks), its damage increases by one step (a {@dice d4} becomes a {@dice d6}, a {@dice d6} becomes a {@dice d8}, etc.). As a bonus action, after making a bite attack, you can make a claw attack.

Starting at 5th level, your muscles strengthen, and your movements quicken. You can now make two claw attacks using your bonus action after you have made a bite attack with your action. Additionally, at 5th level, you can take the {@action Dash} or {@action Hide} action as a bonus action while you are in your Form of the Beast.

entries: You can use this feature twice per short or long rest. At 6th level, your transformation lasts for 1 hour instead of 10 minutes.

name: Form of the River
entries: Starting at 20th level, you can manifest the powerful visage of a river spirit around your body. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You gain a swimming speed of 60 feet, and your walking speed increases by 15 feet.
You have advantage on all saving throws.
Whenever you successfully move a creature with your aura you can choose to deal {@damage 2d8} bludgeoning damage to it.

entries: Once you use this bonus action, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

name: Forth to Battle
entries: When you choose this path at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armour, shields, and martial weapons. In addition, you can give yourself a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Charisma modifier.

name: Foul Conjuration
entries: Starting at 10th level, the creatures you conjure are malformed and bloated with toxins. Any beast, fey, or plant (including your {@creature blighted sapling|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}) summoned or created by your spells or class features gains the following traits:

entries.name: Blighted Resilience
entries: The creature has immunity to necrotic and poison damage and to the {@condition poisoned} condition.

entries.name: Toxic Demise
entries: When the creature is reduced to 0 hit points, it explodes in a burst of toxic mulch or fetid viscera. Each creature within 5 feet of the exploding creature must succeed on a Constitution {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} against your spell save DC or take necrotic damage based on the creature's challenge rating (see the table below). As an action, you can also cause a summoned creature to explode, immediately killing it.

entries.caption: Toxic Demise Damage
rows: {@damage (#$prompt_number:min=1,title=Enter the creature's CR!,default=1$#)d8|A number of d8s of necrotic damage equal to the creature's challenge rating}
{@damage (#$prompt_number:min=1,title=Enter your Proficiency Bonus!,default=1$#)d6|A number of d6s of necrotic damage equal to your proficiency bonus}

name: Fountain of Viscera
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and expend 6 {@classFeature Moxie|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2|Pugilist2024|Moxie Points} to attempt to execute a creature of your choice within reach by magically burrowing your hand into its body and extracting its innards. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failure, the creature takes 100 Piercing damage. On a success, the creature takes 50 Piercing damage instead.

If this damage reduces the target to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it immediately dies as you rip a hole through it, creating a stomach-turning fountain of viscera. When this happens, each creature of your choice within a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. A creature that fails the saving throw can repeat the Wisdom saving throw again at the end of each of its turns, ending the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition on itself on a success.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can use it again.

name: Frenzied Slaughter
entries: You can harness the rush of battle to drive you to even greater acts of violence. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to enter a battle frenzy. You gain the following benefits while this feature is active.

entries.name: Reflexive Attack
entries: When you miss with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make another attack with the same weapon.

entries.name: Condition Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, and {@condition Stunned|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Duration
entries: Frenzied Slaughter lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. If your Frenzied Slaughter is still active on your next turn, you can extend it for another round by doing one of the following:

items: Make an attack roll against an enemy.
Force an enemy to make a saving throw.
You are {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} at the end of your turn.

entries: Each time Frenzied Slaughter is extended, it lasts until the end of your next turn. You can maintain it for up to 1 minute.

name: Friends to Darkness
entries: When you cast any spell from your Innate Darkness feaure, you can choose a number creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). A chosen creature can see through any magical {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB} you create for 1 minute.

name: From the Shadows
entries: Starting at 10th level, your shadow symbiote camouflages you, allowing you to get the drop on your enemies. Whenever you roll initiative while in dim light or darkness, you are automatically {@action hide||hidden} from all creatures at least 10 feet away from you. You are no longer hidden if you move, attack, or cast a spell.

name: Frost Sorcery
entries: {@i Summon Storms and Sheets of Slick Ice to Control the Battlefield}

Your magic is created by pieces of the Everheart, the center and driving force behind the expanding Everglacier wastelands. This power within you might be passed down through ancestors who protected the glacier's magical core, or it might have been forced upon you through a chance encounter with the enchanted ice itself. Regardless of the source of your power, you are a creature of cold incarnate.

name: Frost Spells
entries: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Frost Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Frost Spells
rows: {@spell Blindness/Deafness|XPHB}, {@spell Ice Knife|XPHB}, {@spell Misty Step|XPHB}, {@spell Sleep|XPHB}
{@spell Cone of Cold|XPHB}, {@spell Conjure Elemental|XPHB} (Cold damage only)

name: Frostbite
entries: You can unleash the unforgiving cold inside of you with your attacks. Once on each of your turns while your Rage is active, you can choose to release a burst of sheer cold when you hit a target with a Strength-based attack. When you do, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Cold damage from the attack. This extra damage increases by {@dice 1d6} when you reach Barbarian levels 9 ({@dice 2d6}) and 16 ({@dice 3d6}).
When a creature takes Cold damage in this way, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

name: Frozen Body
entries: Your skin takes on a faintly ice-like, crystalline glow. Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by 3, and it increases by 1 whenever you gain another Sorcerer level.
In addition, {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} composed of ice or snow doesn't cost you extra movement, and when you walk on ice, you only spend 1 foot of movement for every 2 feet you move.

name: Frozen Soul
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage.

In addition, you always have the {@spell Wall of Ice|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it without a Material component. You can also cast it once without a spell slot; if you choose for its form to be flat when cast in this way, the panels of ice don't need to be contiguous with one another. Once you use this feature to cast the spell without a spell slot, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Full-Blooded
entries: You draw magic from blood. It is represented by your Sangromancy Dice, which fuel powers you have from this subclass. You have a pool of d12s that you can expend instead of a {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die} when you cast {@filter Sangromancy spells|spells|subschool=sangromancy}. The number of dice in the pool equals 1 plus your Wizard level. You regain one expended Sangromancy Die when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended Sangromancy Dice when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Fury of the Tides
entries: As a bonus action, you channel the powerful might of the waves to bolster your attacks for 1 minute. Once per turn for the duration, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can choose to push the target 10 feet away from you. If pushed into an obstacle or another creature, the target takes bludgeoning damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

name: Future You Patron
entries: {@i Manipulate Time with Help from the Future}

Your patron is you in a decades-distant future. Perhaps your future self found an artifact of great power connecting them to the past, which they must now lead you to discover, or perhaps they were taught the mystic arts by their future self long ago, a cycle you will have to continue someday. Your future self has forgotten the fine details of some things and outright refuses to tell you about things you "can't know yet," but nevertheless offers compelling insight and guidance. You're not quite sure what your future self is planning for your future (and for their past), but one thing is certain—they need you alive.

name: Future You Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Future You Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. New spells are marked with an asterisk (*).

entries.caption: Future You Spells
