rows: {@spell Accelerate/Decelerate|ValdaPlayerPack}, {@spell Delay|ValdaPlayerPack}, {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB}, {@spell Moment to Think|ValdaPlayerPack}, {@spell Recall|ValdaPlayerPack}
{@spell Legend Lore|XPHB}, {@spell Rary's Telepathic Bond|XPHB|Telepathic Bond}

entries: In addition, strange effects linger after communicating with your future self. You gain one of the traits from the Future You Quirks table.

entries.caption: Future You Quirks
rows: You often speak in the wrong tense or refer to yourself in a plural.
You sometimes refer to a person by name before they've introduced themselves.
You are unreasonably calm in dire circumstances.
In certain lighting, you look much older than you are.
Seeing certain people alive instantly reduces you to tears.
Your future fashion sense clashes completely with that of today.

name: Gallows Humor
entries: When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or killed outright, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to regain an expended use of your Bardic Inspiration. When you do so, choose a creature within 30 feet of you that can hear and understand you. That creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or gain the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn. If the creature succeeds on the Wisdom saving throw, you regain the use of this ability. Otherwise, once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Galvanic Heart
entries: Lightning is part of you. It flows through your veins and awaits release. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning damage. If you already have this {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}, you can reduce the Lightning damage further. To determine the amount reduced, roll a number of {@dice d6}s equal to your Rage Damage bonus and add them together (after the {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} applies).

entries.name: Vessel Save DC
entries: If a feature of this subclass requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Vessel Damage
entries: Some of your features use Vessel Damage. To determine that extra damage, roll a number of {@dice d4}s equal to your Rage Damage bonus and add them together. Your Vessel Damage is always Lightning damage.

name: Gangrel
entries: {@i Let the Beast Inside in Order to Control It}

The Gangrel have made peace with their Beast long ago, choosing to harness the wild power it promises and wield it rather than trying to stifle it. They are attuned to its feral nature, embodying the predator.

name: Gangrel Bane
entries: The Beast reveals itself in you as animalistic features and behaviors. If you are affected by the {@classFeature The Beast|Kindred|BoundByBlood|1||Hunger} of your Beast feature, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} and {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Gather the Coven
entries: You can now share the Horned King's power with those you deem worthy. You perform a 1-hour ritual, which can be done during a rest, forming a bond with up to six willing creatures that must remain within 10 feet of you during the ritual. You can end the bond for any number of the creatures (no action required), and the bond ends when you die. The bond grants the following benefits.

entries.name: Witchcraft
entries: Choose one of the curses from your {@subclassFeature Malediction|Warlock|PHB|Horned King|CrookedMoon14|1|CrookedMoon14} feature. The bonded creatures can now each use that reaction option once, and they regain the ability to do so when they finish a long rest.

entries.name: Fly By Night
entries: As a bonus action, choose one of the bonded creatures. If you and the target are on the same plane of existence, you magically teleport to the nearest unoccupied space next to the creature. You can use this benefit once, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a short or long rest. If your Crown of Horns feature is active when you use this bonus action, the use isn't expended.

entries.name: Hand of the King
entries: While your Crown of Horns feature is active, the first time a bonded creature damages another creature during its turn, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} necrotic damage.

name: Gather the Coven
entries: You can now share the Horned King's power with those you deem worthy. You perform a 1-hour ritual, which can be done during a rest, forming a bond with up to six willing creatures that must remain within 10 feet of you during the ritual. You can end the bond for any number of the creatures (no action required), and the bond ends when you die. The bond grants the following benefits.

entries.name: Witchcraft
entries: Choose one of the curses from your {@subclassFeature Malediction|Warlock|XPHB|Horned King|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} feature. The bonded creatures can now each use that {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} option once, and they regain the ability to do so when they finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Fly By Night
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose one of the bonded creatures. If you and the target are on the same plane of existence, you magically teleport to the nearest unoccupied space next to the creature. You can use this benefit once, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. If your Crown of Horns feature is active when you use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, the use isn't expended.

entries.name: Hand of the King
entries: While your Crown of Horns feature is active, the first time a bonded creature damages another creature during its turn, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage.

name: Gestalt Anchor
entries: Your mental power increases, allowing you to project a sense of calm in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that originates from you. The projection is inactive if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.
You and your allies in the projection gain a +2 bonus to Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.
If another Mind Domain Cleric is present, a creature can only benefit from one Gestalt Anchor at a time.

name: Get Jinxed
entries: You have learned the secret art of Jinxcrafting—drawing magical power from the dark deeds and deals of sin. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cards and Bones
entries: You gain proficiency with two gaming sets of your choice ({@item playing cards|XPHB} and {@item dice set|PHB|dice} recommended).

entries.name: Jinx Weapon
entries: As a 1-hour ritual using a {@item gaming set|PHB}, you magically create a jinx weapon that channels your Jinxcraft. This weapon takes the form of a pistol or a {@item gaming set|PHB}. For you, the jinx weapon is a simple ranged weapon with a normal range of 30 feet and a long range of 90 feet, and it deals {@damage 1d8} force damage on a hit. As a {@item gaming set|PHB}, you throw cards, dice, or other {@item gaming set|PHB} pieces, or you use them to unleash bolts of hex magic. Alternatively, you can imbue Jinxcraft into a simple or martial weapon you have proficiency with, turning it into your jinx weapon. The infused jinx weapon deals force damage instead of its normal type. If you create a second jinx weapon, the first vanishes or its Jinxcraft ends.

entries.name: Parlor Trick
entries: You learn one of the following cantrips of your choice: {@spell Dancing Lights|PHB}, {@spell Mage Hand|PHB}, {@spell Minor Illusion|PHB}, {@spell Mysterious Presence|CrookedMoon24}, or {@spell Prestidigitation|PHB}. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it.

name: Get Jinxed
entries: You have learned the secret art of Jinxcrafting—drawing magical power from the dark deeds and deals of sin. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cards and Bones
entries: You gain proficiency with two {@item Gaming Set|XPHB|Gaming Sets} of your choice ({@item playing cards|XPHB} and {@item dice set|XPHB|dice} recommended).

entries.name: Jinx Weapon
entries: As a 1-hour ritual using a {@item Gaming Set|XPHB}, you magically create a jinx weapon that channels your Jinxcraft. This weapon takes the form of a {@item Pistol|XPHB} or a {@item Gaming Set|XPHB} (which uses {@item Pistol|XPHB} game statistics). For you, the jinx weapon ignores {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading} and creates its own ammunition that deals Force damage. In {@item Gaming Set|XPHB} form, you throw cards, dice, or other {@item Gaming Set|XPHB} pieces, or you use them to unleash bolts of hex magic. Alternatively, you can imbue Jinxcraft into a Simple or Martial weapon you have proficiency with, turning it into your jinx weapon. The infused jinx weapon deals Force damage instead of its normal type. If you create a second jinx weapon, the first vanishes or its Jinxcraft ends.

entries.name: Parlor Trick
entries: You learn one of the following cantrips of your choice: {@spell Dancing Lights|XPHB}, {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB}, {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB}, {@spell Mysterious Presence|CrookedMoon24}, or {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB}. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it.

name: Ghaal'Shaarat
entries: You can imbue a weapon with a fraction of your spirit, creating what the Dhakaani daashors call a ghaal'shaarat, Goblin for "mighty blade." As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action while you have {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} in hand, you can turn a Simple or Martial Melee weapon into a Ghaal'Shaarat. The weapon continues to be a Ghaal'Shaarat until you imbue a different weapon or you die.
The weapon gains the following benefits while you wield it.

entries.name: Mighty Blade
entries: A nonmagical weapon becomes a magic weapon. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with the weapon, unless it already had this bonus or a better one.

entries.name: Returning Weapon
entries: The weapon has the {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} property with a normal range of 30 feet and a long range of 120 feet. It returns to your hand immediately after it is used to make a ranged attack roll.

name: Ghost Walker
entries: Beginning at 11th level, you are familiar with how ghosts and creatures of the Border Ethereal meld into the Material Plane. You can choose to partially slip into the Ethereal Plane, granting you the following benefits:

entries.name: Etherstep
entries: You can spend 1 ki point as a bonus action to turn {@condition invisible} until the end of your next turn, or until you make an attack or cast a spell.

Alternatively, you can spend an extra ki point as part of your Step of the Wind to gain this benefit. When you do, you can also move through hostile creatures and solid objects no more than 4 inches thick for as long as you remain {@condition invisible}.

entries.name: Phase
entries: When you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the attack's damage against you by an amount equal to your monk level as you partially slip into the Border Ethereal. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Gift of Pestilence
entries: Through your observation and meditation, you are attuned to the nature of pestilence and the creatures believed to carry it. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Inoculation
entries: You have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition poisoned} condition or diseases, and you have resistance to poison and necrotic damage.

entries.name: Vermin Kinship
entries: Through chittering sounds and hand gestures, you can communicate simple concepts to vermin, such as rats, pigeons, and insects, and you gain the ability to decipher their noises and motions. Vermin lack the intelligence to convey or understand sophisticated concepts, but friendly vermin could relay what they have seen or heard in the recent past. Additionally, you can cast {@spell Animal Messenger} using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability targeting a Tiny Beast that is considered vermin and thought to spread plague and disease. Once you cast the spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Gift of Pestilence
entries: Through your observation and meditation, you are attuned to the nature of pestilence and the creatures believed to carry it. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Inoculation
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition or magical contagions, and you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison and Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Vermin Kinship
entries: Through chittering sounds and hand gestures, you can communicate simple concepts to vermin, such as rats, pigeons, and insects, and you gain the ability to decipher their noises and motions. Vermin lack the intelligence to convey or understand sophisticated concepts, but {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} vermin could relay what they have seen or heard in the recent past. Additionally, you can cast {@spell Animal Messenger|XPHB} using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability targeting a Tiny Beast that is considered vermin and thought to spread plague and disease. Once you cast the spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Gift of Theatre
entries: At 14th level, you gain the ability to give one of your theater masks to an ally within 5 feet of you. As an action, you temporarily release the incantation that binds your theater mask to you, allowing one of your allies to use it. The mask can be used in this way for 1 minute and only one other creature can be designated to use it.
Once you've given an ally a theater mask, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Gifts of Survival
entries: Your body is built to survive whatever the world sets before you.

entries.name: Feral Fortitude
entries: When you take damage except Fire and Radiant, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage taken by your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} plus your Constitution modifier (minimum reduction of 1).

entries.name: Meld with Earth
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the {@spell Meld into Stone|XPHB} spell, except the surface must be dirt, sand, or clay instead of stone. Additionally, while the spell is active, you gain {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet. The spell lasts until you end it (no action required) or when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Gifts of the Beast
entries: Your body reflects the protean gifts of your animalistic Beast. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Eyes of the Beast
entries: The range of your {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} increases to 240 feet.

entries.name: Feral Weapons
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 1 Blood Point to grow rending claws for 1 minute. Your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal {@damage 2d6} Slashing damage, and you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}.

name: Giga-Missile
entries: When you cast {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, you can enhance the damage of the spell. You deal extra Force damage with each dart equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).

name: Glyph of Aegis (6th Level)
entries: When you reach 6th level, you can touch a creature as an action and expend up to 3 charged runes to transfer your protective power to it for up to 1 hour. The next time that creature takes damage within the next hour, it rolls {@dice 1d6} per charged rune spent and reduces the damage by the total. You can't transfer this power to a creature already under the effect of Glyph of Aegis.

name: Glyph of Aegis (14th Level)
entries: Your Glyph of Aegis die becomes a {@dice d8} at 14th level.

name: Glyph of Aegis
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can release the stored arcane power within your runes to absorb or deflect threatening attacks. Whenever you take damage, you can expend any number of charged runes as a reaction. Roll a number of {@dice d6|d6s} equal to the number of runes you expended, and reduce the damage by the total.

name: Glyph of Hemorrhaging
entries: Starting at 10th level, when you damage a creature with a spell, you can choose to curse that creature for 1 minute. While cursed in this way, whenever the creature is hit by an attack, it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage. At the end of each of the creature's turns, it can make a Constitution {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} against your spell save DC, ending the curse on a success.
This feature cannot be used against creatures that are undead or constructs. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}.

name: Gnawing Hunger
entries: Your hunger for your enemy allows you to partake of its essence during battle. When you deal damage to a creature with a melee attack using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the damage dealt. If the target is a creature type in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1}, you instead gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage dealt instead.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Gold Star Hero
entries: Though gunslinging heroism, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Improved Aura
entries: The range of your {@subclassFeature Steely-Eyed Aura|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|White Hat|ValdaGunslinger|3} feature increases to 30 feet.

entries.name: Iron-Clad Law
entries: When you use your {@subclassFeature Lay Down the Law [Maneuver]|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|White Hat|ValdaGunslinger|3|ValdaGunslinger|Lay Down the Law} maneuver, the ally has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Stunned Surrender
entries: When a creature fails its saving throw against your {@subclassFeature Reach for the Skies|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|White Hat|ValdaGunslinger|6} feature, it has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition instead of the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

name: Good Medicine
entries: When you craft a potion, you can choose to expend a spell slot without choosing a spell to craft a dose of Good Medicine. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can drink the dose or administer it to another creature within 5 feet of yourself. When Good Medicine is consumed, roll a number of d8s equal to the level of the spell slot expended, and the target regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the roll's total. If you expended a level 3+ spell slot on this feature, Good Medicine also removes the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

name: Got Your Back
entries: You know how to cast with style, and your allies can take heart from your displays of grit or showmanship. If you expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration to improve the damage of a cantrip with your {@subclassFeature At Your Fingertips|Bard|XPHB|Wands|FoEQuickstone|3} feature, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on the same turn to grant a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next saving throw it makes for 1 minute.

name: Grafted Powers
entries: The multiple aspects of Nature that you forcefully implanted within you manifest themselves in other aspects of your life. You gain one of the following options of your choice.

items.name: Bear Back
items.entry: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and whether you can grapple a creature. In addition, you can add your Wisdom modifier to any Strength check that you make.

items.name: Deer Head
items.entry: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks.

items.name: Goat Hooves
items.entry: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries: These elements can be visible or not, or they can be represented by other natural aspects. Choose at your discretion when you gain this feature.

name: Grand Finale
entries: You gain the ability to deliver a stirring performance that spurs your companions to mighty deeds. As a Magic action, choose up to two other creatures within 60 feet that can see or hear you. Each of the chosen creatures can immediately take an action this turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Grand Strategist
entries: You can order your allies to follow your formation (no action required). Choose one or more creatures within 60 feet of you who can hear you, up to a number of creatures equal to your proficiency bonus. Each target can immediately move up to half their speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

name: Grandfather Paradox
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can goad a creature within 60 feet of you that can see or hear you into causing a paradox. The creature must make an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 10d6} Psychic damage and has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute as it is locked between opposing timelines. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only. The {@condition Stunned|XPHB} creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Grave Bond
entries: You draw deeper strength from the grave. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Ghastly Hound
entries: The Grim gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

entries.name: Grave Fortitude
entries: You gain resistance to necrotic damage.

entries.name: Inescapable Fate
entries: When the target of your {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|PHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14} succeeds on a saving throw, you can use your reaction to force it to reroll the save with disadvantage and use the new roll. Once you cause a save to fail with this benefit, you can't use it again until the current {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|PHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14} ends.

name: Grave Bond
entries: You draw deeper strength from the grave. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Ghastly Hound
entries: The grim gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

entries.name: Grave Fortitude
entries: You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Inescapable Fate
entries: When the target of your {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} succeeds on a saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force it to reroll the save with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} and use the new roll. Once you cause a save to fail with this benefit, you can't use it again until the current {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} ends.

name: Grave Lord
entries: You are no longer a mere vessel for spectral energy, but a lord of it. Your powers improve in the following ways.

entries.name: On A Pale Horse
entries: When you use your Dark Rider power, you can allow one creature of your choice to mount the steed in addition to you. Additionally, when you expend a Draugr Die during the steed's {@action Dash} action, it can move through solid objects and creatures as if they were {@quickref difficult terrain||3} (along with any riders). If the steed ends its turn inside a solid object, it and any riders take {@damage 1d10} force damage and are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space.

entries.name: Sepulchral Shield
entries: When you use your Grave Guard power, choose one of the triggering damage types. You have resistance to that damage type (including the triggering damage) until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Death Grip
entries: A creature {@condition grappled} by your Soul Reaper power is {@condition restrained} until the grapple ends.

name: Grave Lord
entries: You are no longer a mere vessel for spectral energy, but a lord of it. Your powers improve in the following ways.

entries.name: On A Pale Horse
entries: When you use your Dark Rider power, you can allow one creature of your choice to mount the steed in addition to you.

Additionally, when you expend a Draugr Die during the steed's {@action Dash|XPHB} action, it can move through solid objects and creatures as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} (along with any riders). If the steed ends its turn inside a solid object, it and any riders take {@damage 1d10} Force damage and are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space.

entries.name: Sepulchral Shield
entries: When you use your Grave Guard power, choose one of the triggering damage types. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage type (including the triggering damage) until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Death Grip
entries: A creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by your Soul Reaper power has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the grapple ends.

name: Great Fool Patron
entries: {@i Laugh in the Face of Danger with Foolish Antics}

What horrors and sorrows can't be remedied by maniacal laughter? Warlocks that have made a pact with the Great Fool draw their enigmatic power from a powerful, otherworldly being of jolly revelry, whose twisted sense of humor is lost on mortal understanding. They are a mocking mirror to bring low the arrogant and mighty, though the Great Fool's ultimate designs are often nonsensical and incomprehensible.

Many Warlocks of the Great Fool adopt a signature aesthetic and performance style that best represents their folly. The Foolish Personas table offers archetypes of fools with suggestions for corresponding outfits and routines.

entries.caption: Foolish Personas
rows: {@b The Harlequin.} An elegant outfit of diamond motley with a painted mask—performs dances, gives eloquent speeches, and plays tricks
{@b The Jester.} A two-toned, checkered motley outfit with cap and bells—favors feats of acrobatics, tumbling, and juggling
{@b The Joker.} A vibrant, colorful suit with wild hair and bowler hat—favors silly jokes, slapstick comedy, and clumsy self-deprecation
{@b The Mime.} A striped, black-and-white shirt with a flat cap and red suspenders—pantomimes comical scenarios without speaking
{@b The Sad Clown.} A monochromatic, one-piece outfit with pointed hat and puffball buttons—utilizes melodramatic melancholy and song
{@b The Tramp.} A patch-covered coat, tattered scarf, scuffed shoes, and cigar—leverages sardonic wit, insults, and mocking observations

name: Great Fool Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Great Fool Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Great Fool Spells
rows: {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB}, {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|XPHB}, {@spell Rope Trick|XPHB}, {@spell Spiritual Weapon|XPHB}, {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB}

name: Greater Monstrous Gifts
entries: Your physical monstrousness has evolved. You can choose one benefit from the following list.

entries.name: Call the Wretched
entries: You can expend 2 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Blight|XPHB} or {@spell Insect Plague|XPHB} spell.

entries.name: Distending Jaws
entries: You can roll one additional Feed Die when you feed. In addition, you can use your jaws to make {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. When you hit with your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and deal damage, you can deal Piercing damage equal to {@damage 2d6} plus your Strength modifier instead of the normal damage of an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: One with the Night
entries: Your {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} is increased to 90 feet, and you can see normally in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} and {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}—both magical and nonmagical—within 120 feet of yourself.

entries.name: Skin of the Chameleon
entries: You can expend 2 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Greater Invisibility|XPHB} spell. In addition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Stony Flesh
entries: In response to taking damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend 1 Blood Point to gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} for 1 minute to two damage types, other than Fire, Psychic, and Radiant, including against the triggering damage.

entries.name: Wings of the Gargoyle
entries: While you aren't wearing Heavy armor, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet, and you gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

name: Green Reaper
entries: {@i Slay with Nature's Venom}

Green Reapers are assassins who specialize in harnessing the toxic elements of flora and fauna. These Rangers often work as killers for hire utilizing their extensive knowledge to end lives discreetly or with gory panache, depending on the poison used and the client's wishes. Green Reapers exhibit a morbid curiosity when encountering a toxin they're unfamiliar with, typically followed by an enthusiastic application of the substance on their next foe.

name: Green Reaper Spells
entries: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Green Reaper Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

name: Grim Harbinger
entries: {@i Seal Fate as an Omen of Doom}

Grim harbingers wander places touched by death, serving as both a watcher of the dead and the herald of doom for those whose lives are running out. At their side is a guardian spirit and omen of death known as a grim, a constant companion that aids in performing their shared, grave duty.

name: Grim Harbinger
entries: {@i Seal Fate as an Omen of Doom}

Grim harbingers wander places touched by death, serving as both a watcher of the dead and the herald of doom for those whose lives are running out. At their side is a guardian spirit and omen of death known as a grim, a constant companion that aids in performing their shared, grave duty.

name: Grim Harbinger Spells
entries: You learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Grim Harbinger Spells table. Each spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.

name: Grim Harbinger Spells
entries: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Grim Harbinger Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

name: Grim Surgeon
entries: You've developed a unique familiarity with knives, bodies, and blood in your line of work. Like a tinkerer's knowledge of clockwork and gears, you've come to an understanding of how bodies are put together instead. Medical experts in rough or war-torn cities and villages may follow this archetype, but so do rogues who take a particular interest in either clerical or necromantic magic. A grim surgeon uses medical knowledge and strange blood magic to dismantle foes, restore allies, and control bodies like puppets.

name: Grotesque Growth
entries: When you use your {@subclassFeature Dread Hand|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|Hand of Dread|Pugilist2024|3} feature, you gain the benefits of the Enlarge effect of the {@spell Enlarge/Reduce|XPHB} spell and have a 10-foot reach.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you take a level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} (no action required by you) to restore your use of it.

name: Groundwork
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Compression Lock
entries: When you start your turn with one or more creatures {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, you can deal Bludgeoning damage to each creature you have {@condition Grappled|XPHB} (no action required). The damage equals one roll of your Fisticuffs die plus your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Inescapable
entries: When a creature makes a saving throw or ability check against your grapple or shove DC, you can expend 1 {@classFeature Moxie|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2|Pugilist2024|Moxie Point} to give that roll {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Stop and Drop
entries: When you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and don't use a mastery property as part of the attack, you can use both the Grapple and Shove option.

name: Group Assault
entries: You coordinate your allies in their attacks against a powerful foe. If you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action and each attack you make is against the same target, you can choose other creatures within 60 feet of yourself. Each of the chosen creatures gains a bonus to one attack roll and damage roll equal to the number rolled on your Teamwork Die against the same target.

name: Groupthink
entries: Starting at 10th level, your eldritch heads are always there to support your mortal mind and body. You gain a bonus to Intelligence checks, Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks, and Intelligence saving throws equal to half your proficiency bonus.

name: Guarded
entries: Also at 1st level, while you have at least one eldritch head remaining, you can't be surprised, and if a creature would gain advantage on an attack roll against you due to having its ally within 5 feet of you, it makes the attack roll without advantage.

name: Guardian Angel
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you become a living bastion of defense, granting the benefits below for 1 minute or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Walking Bastion
entries: Your Guarding Presence becomes a 100-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. Creatures of your choice within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} can use your AC.

entries.name: Endless Divinity
entries: On each of your turns, if you have no uses of Channel Divinity left, you can give yourself one use.

entries.name: Supreme Punishment
entries: You can use Ward of the Guardian without taking a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} once each round. When you do so, you can't use it this way again until the start of your next turn.

name: Guardian of the Dead
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to better protect the dead under your watch. For 1 hour, whenever you are within 10 feet of a creature reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your attack rolls and on saving throws against spells and effects that inflict the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition. After you gain your Aura of Courage class feature, you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition when using this feature.

During this 1-hour period, when a creature you can see casts a spell to create Undead, or restore a creature to life, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and attack the creature that cast the spell.

name: Guardian of the Way Technique
entries: You have studied alien creatures and learned to disrupt the foul energies that course through them. Once per turn when you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} with Flurry of Blows and deal damage, you can cause one of the following effects:

items.name: Anchoring Strike
entries: Until the end of your next turn, the target can't teleport or use planar travel, including, entering an extradimensional space or demiplane.

items.name: Banishing Strike
entries: The target teleports up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

name: Guarding Presence
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can choose creatures within 5 feet of yourself, up to a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). Each of the chosen creatures can use your AC instead of its own AC as long as it remains within 5 feet of you or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

name: Guide to the Herd
entries: At 17th level, your vigilant watch of your companions while in the midst of combat allows you to give them cues as to when they should raise their defenses. Whenever you use your Patient Defense to gain the benefits of the {@action Dodge} action, you can spend 1 additional ki point to share that benefit with your allies. Each friendly creature that can see or hear you and is within 30 feet of you can immediately use its reaction to also gain the benefits of the {@action Dodge} action until the start of your next turn.

name: Guiding Wind
entries: Starting at 3rd level, when you make an attack, you can whisper to the wind to have it aid your strikes. Once on each of your turns, you can choose to gain one of the following benefits:

items: When you hit with a weapon attack, the target takes an extra {@dice 1d4} damage of the weapon's type. When you reach 11th level in this class, the extra damage increases to {@dice 1d8}.

When you miss with a weapon attack, you can change its trajectory to attack a different target up to 5 feet away from the original one and within range of your weapon. When you do, your attack roll against the new target is equal to the original attack roll plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +0). When you reach 11th level in this class, the new target can be up to 15 feet away as long as it's still within range of your weapon.

name: Haemal Exchange
entries: You have mastered the ability to enervate enemies and endow allies. When an interdicted creature within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll or saving throw, you can use your reaction to burn one of the seals on them and transfer their power. The target must roll a {@dice d8} and subtract the number rolled from the triggering attack roll or saving throw.
You then empower an ally within 30 feet of you. The next time that ally makes an attack roll or saving throw, they roll a {@dice d8} and add the number rolled to the attack roll or saving throw.

name: Hag's Craft
entries: The Hag imparts the knowledge to craft two magic items. You can temporarily turn a normal vessel into a Hag's Cauldron by expending a spell slot. This magical cauldron lasts for 10 minutes. During that time, you can take the {@action Magic|XPHB} to pour out three Common, two Uncommon, or one Rare potion. The potions lose efficacy at the end of your next {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You regain this ability at the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

Additionally, when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can expend a spell slot and imbue a gemstone worth at least 10 GP with magic, turning it into a Minor Heartstone. This magic item grants the bearer {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and the ability to cast {@spell Blink|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot. The magic within the gemstone fades after 24 hours and the gem crumbles into dust.

name: Hag's Eye
entries: As an agent of a Hag, you have been gifted with a magical item known as a Hag's Eye. Crafted from a real eye and fitted into a ring, pendant, or other accessory, this item can be used as an Arcane Focus for your Warlock spells. The Hag can see through the eye, and the destruction of the item can cause the Hag actual pain, so any pawn who loses this talisman often invokes the Hag's ire.

While you possess the eye, you can cast {@spell Hex|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once) without expending a spell slot, and you regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. In addition, when you reach Warlock level 10, you can use the eye to cast {@spell Bestow Curse|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so once you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Hag's Guile
entries: Hags delight in deceiving and manipulating others, and you gain some of their skill in doing so. You know the {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB} cantrip. If you already know it, you learn a different Warlock cantrip of your choice. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.

Additionally, if a creature takes a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine an illusion you have created, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the check.

Also, the first time a creature takes a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine an illusion spell you have cast and succeeds on the Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check, you can cause the illusion to deal Psychic damage. The damage equals {@dice 1d6 plus 1d6} for each spell slot used to cast the spell.

You can do damage a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Hag's Visage
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you twist your face into a horrifying mask resembling your Hag patron. It lasts for 1 minute, but it ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. While this effect lasts, you gain the benefits listed below.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Horrifying Gaze
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose one Humanoid that you can see and that can see you within 30 feet of you. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. The {@condition Frightened|XPHB} target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that can see you has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on this save.

entries.name: Paralyzing Gaze
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, choose one Humanoid that you can see and that can see you within 30 feet of you that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition.

On a successful save, the creature takes Necrotic damage equal to your Warlock level, it is no longer {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, and it can't be targeted by your Hag's Visage again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Death Gaze
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, choose one Humanoid that you can see and that can see you within 30 feet of you that has the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} against your spell save DC or be reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

On a successful save, the creature takes Necrotic damage equal to twice your Warlock level, it is no longer {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, and it can't be targeted by your Hag's Visage again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Hair Trigger
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Blackpowder Pistol|GrimHollowPG24|Blackpowder Pistols}. In addition, when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on that roll, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} for one of the following options:

items: Make one attack with a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.
Move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.
A controlled mount moves up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.
Take the {@action Dodge|XPHB} or {@action Utilize|XPHB} action.

name: Hallowed Hands
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or Pugilist weapon, you can expend a number of points from your {@subclassFeature Lay On Hands|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|Street Saint|Pugilist2024|3} healing pool to deal extra Radiant damage to the target, to a maximum of your Pugilist level. The damage equals the number of points expended, or twice as much if the target is a Fiend or Undead.

name: Halt the Assault
entries: When another creature you can see within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to change the target to yourself. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage against that attack.

name: Hand of Dread
entries: {@i Dabble With Dread Powers}

In your darkest hour, you pleaded for the strength to take what you wanted from the world and a dread power took notice. At first, you may have relished the cathartic rush that came with channeling your eldritch might to claim what you felt you deserved, but this pact came with strings attached. In times of distress you hear the entity whispering in the back of your mind, urging you to indulge your most base impulses.

name: Handy Haints
entries: You can call forth haints—vagabond spirits. When you inspire a creature with {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1}, you can summon a ghostly apparition that drifts around the inspired target.

The haint creates an aura extending 15 feet from the target. The haint vanishes after 1 minute, when you summon a new haint, when you use the reaction it grants you, or if you are {@condition incapacitated} or die. When you summon a haint, choose its form: Grump, Sad Sack, or Scamp.

entries.name: Grump
entries: This red-tinged, elderly spirit dressed in threadbare rags threatens your foes and harangues your allies to do better. The inspired creature and its allies within the aura have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks and Strength saving throws. In addition, when a creature inside the aura deals damage, you can use your reaction to increase the damage dealt to one target by a roll of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} die plus your Charisma modifier.

entries.name: Sad Sack
entries: The blueish, melancholic spirit saps the fervor from your foes. The inspired creature and its allies within the aura have {@quickref Cover||3||half cover} against ranged attacks. In addition, when a creature inside the aura takes damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage taken by an amount equal to a roll of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} die plus your Charisma modifier.

entries.name: Scamp
entries: The gold-hued, childlike spirit delights and invigorates your allies. When the inspired creature or its allies starts a turn in the aura, that creature's speed increases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn. In addition, when a creature inside the aura fails a saving throw, you can use your reaction to let the creature reroll the {@dice d20}.

name: Handy Haints
entries: You can call forth haints—vagabond spirits. When you inspire a creature with {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|XPHB|1}, you can summon a ghostly apparition that drifts around the inspired target.

The haint creates an aura in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} from the target. The haint vanishes after 1 minute, when you summon a new haint, when you use the {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} it grants you, or if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition or die. When you summon a haint, choose its form: Grump, Sad Sack, or Scamp.

In addition, when a creature inside the aura takes damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage taken by an amount equal to a roll of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|XPHB|1} die plus your Charisma modifier.

When the inspired creature or its allies starts a turn in the aura, that creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn. In addition, when a creature inside the aura fails a saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to let the creature reroll the {@dice d20}.

name: Harbinger of Chaos
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you announce changes to the reality of your surroundings. Each enemy that can see and hear you must make an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC. An enemy that fails its save believes the changes you announced to be true. It has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all d20 checks until the end of its next turn, and you and your allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all attack rolls and d20 checks you make against it.
You can use this effect once, and you regain it when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

name: Harbinger of Doom
entries: Your control over doom grows stronger, granting the following benefits.

entries.name: Graveyard Hunter
entries: The {@creature Grim|CrookedMoon24|Grim's} Ominous Rend action deals an extra {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage on a hit.

entries.name: Mortal Reminder
entries: When you deal damage to a creature doomed by your {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|PHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14}, you can change the damage type to necrotic.

entries.name: Mounting Dread
entries: Necrotic damage dealt by you or the Grim ignores resistance.

name: Harbinger of Doom
entries: Your control over doom grows stronger, granting the following benefits.

entries.name: Graveyard Hunter
entries: The {@creature Grim|CrookedMoon24|Grim's} Ominous Rend action deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage on a hit.

entries.name: Mortal Reminder
entries: When you deal damage to a creature doomed by your {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24}, you can change the damage type to Necrotic.

entries.name: Mounting Dread
entries: Necrotic damage dealt by you or the grim ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}.

name: Harrier
entries: Starting at 7th level, you can use the {@action Hide} action as a bonus action on your turn.

name: Harvest Domain
entries: {@i Sow, Grow, and Reap in the Harvest Cycle}

The Harvest Domain draws from the cycle beginning with creation, reaching abundance, and ending in culling before repeating endlessly. Deities of farming and crops can focus on one of the harvest's aspects, but most draw from each phase of the cycle. Clerics of this domain are drawn to the cyclical nature of existence, and they often take on roles as shepherds of different cycles.
Use the Harvest Rites table for inspiration on observances based on each aspect of the harvest cycle.

entries.caption: Harvest Rites
rows: Bury a sacrificial offering into a newly ploughed field, such as dried corn husks, dead fish, robin's egg, or hare's foot
Brew blessed mixtures and concoctions for consumption or irrigation that increase the fertility of crops, livestock, or people
Gift a pouch of seeds to travelers at the start of a journey to ensure they arrive at their destination
Tend to the sick or injured with natural remedies that utilize pure water, fertile soil, rich ash, or fruit poultice to speed up healing
Bless crops or livestock to usher in favorable weather and a growing season that produces a strong and healthy bounty
Oversee marriages, binding the betrothed with woven grain stalks or linen cords
Give funeral rites that return the deceased's body or ashes to the fields, mixing in earth from their home and decaying crops to enrich the soil
Sharpen blades blessed by the harvest gods ahead of a battle or before a harvest to ensure that all that is reaped is offered to the divine
Slaughter adult livestock or reap ripe crops for a feast to celebrate nature's bounty
