You can also restore one use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Rend
entries: You move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and cast a Cleric cantrip that has a casting time of an action or make one melee attack using a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. The attack uses your Wisdom for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity.

entries.name: Tail Swipe
entries: Each Large or smaller creature you choose within 10 feet of you gains the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Wingbeat
entries: You immediately move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. During this movement, you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and don't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

name: Lengthen Shadow
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can manipulate your own shadow to extend your reach. When you cast a cleric spell with a range of touch, your shadow can deliver the spell as if you had cast the spell. Your target must be within 15 feet of you, and you must be able to see the target. You can use this feature even if you are in an area where you cast no shadow.
When you reach 10th level in this class, your shadow can affect any target you can see within 30 feet of you.

name: Let's Make a Deal
entries: You can offer your allies a deal—at a price, of course. As a bonus action, you choose one willing ally within 60 feet of you who can hear you.

Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can choose to gain advantage on one attack roll or saving throw they make and can add a bonus equal to your proficiency bonus to the same roll. If this attack hits or this saving throw succeeds, the creature gains temporary hit points equal to your illrigger level. If this attack misses or this saving throw fails, the creature has disadvantage on the next attack roll or saving throw they make. This disadvantage can't be canceled out with advantage in any way. A creature can strike only one deal with you at a time.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Ley Line Tracker
entries: Given your knowledge of the landscape, you can use ley lines as conduits to stretch your magic over vast distances when tracking a target, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Mark Bounty
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can single out one creature as your bounty. To mark a creature as your bounty, you must have seen that creature or possess an object that has been in their possession for at least 24 hours. Once on each of your turns you can change your bounty to one creature you can see (no action required).

entries.name: Masterful Tracking
entries: Your Ranger spells of the Divination school can target your bounty at any distance, even if you cannot see them, unless your bounty is protected from Divination spells (as with {@spell Nondetection|XPHB}) or is on another plane of existence.

name: Leyline Magic
entries: The primal forces of nature have their own magical energy, one which can be harnessed by wizards with proper training. By drawing on this power, leyline wizards can tap into primordial reservoirs of magic to gain access to new spells, empower their own spellcasting, or disrupt opposing forces that attempt to take root in their domain. The most powerful wizards of this tradition can set new leylines, transforming unnatural or inhospitable places into paradises with time. These wizards work closely with druids, and they can gradually heal environments that have been blighted or corrupted.

name: Leyline Weaving
entries: At 14th level, you have learned how to tap into the interconnected network of distant leylines, temporarily infusing even unnatural or hostile environments with their power. By spending 1 hour in meditation, you can draw on the power of a distant leyline to temporarily create a new one in your location. When you do this, you may choose any one terrain from the {@table Leyline Spells|HumblewoodTales} tables and attune yourself to its leyline. The terrain of this leyline does not need to match the terrain you are currently in. Your new leyline affects a 1-mile radius area from the spot you meditated upon, which counts as the terrain of the leyline you attuned to for the purposes of using your leyline abilities. It is hard for a leyline to take root in unfamiliar spaces, and after 24 hours, this effect dissipates. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

By using this ability to create the same type of leyline on the same spot each day for a full year, you can cause the effect to become permanent. This will forever alter the natural landscape within the zone you created, and you can choose whether the environment within this zone matches your new leyline or combines the features of its terrain with those naturally present.

name: Liar's Dice [Maneuver]
entries: When you make a damage roll with a Ranged weapon, you can expend one {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and declare it to be a hidden roll. Roll the damage in secret and declare any total you wish. The GM has the option to call your bluff, in which case you reveal the damage dice you rolled. This has different consequences based on whether or not you lied.

entries.name: The GM Calls Your Bluff; You Lied
entries: The damage you deal is halved.

entries.name: The GM Calls Your Bluff; You Told the Truth
entries: The damage you deal is doubled.

entries.name: The GM Doesn't Call Your Bluff
entries: Use the total damage you declared, even if you rolled a different total.

name: License to Kill
entries: Whenever you deal damage with a Ranged weapon, you can expend either one or two {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Dice} and add them to the damage roll. If you roll the highest number on a {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die}, you can roll the die again and add it to the damage without expending it, rolling again if it is the highest number again, and so on. The maximum number of {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Dice} you can add to the damage equals your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Life Beyond Death
entries: When you or an ally within 120 feet of you is about to make a {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to heal the target a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to ten times the level of the spell slot expended.

name: Life Hack
entries: Your command of necromantic magic and affinity for the no-longer-living allows you to drain your companions' life force, converting it into a temporary boon. Once per turn, when your companion hits a creature with an attack, you can mentally command the companion to shed some of its life force (no action required). Your companion takes {@damage 1d4} necrotic damage that can't be reduced in any way, gains an equal number of temporary hit points, and deals an equal amount of necrotic damage to its target. This damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class: {@damage 1d6} at 6th level, {@damage 1d8} at 10th level, and {@damage 1d10} at 14th level.

name: Light Weaver Sorcerous Origin
entries: Your powers are drawn from the spark of light kindled within you. In places of great darkness, there are always those born with the affinity for light, and every shadow must have a shining source. The magic within you represents cosmic balance, and like the light, your magic flickers from radiance to darkness moment to moment.

entries.name: Illumination Magic
entries: If you have access to {@i Deep Magic}, consider granting light weaver sorcerers spells from the school of Illumination. These are spells dealing with light, stars, and darkness and fit the character type perfectly from a story and theme perspective.

name: Lightning Reflexes
entries: The lightning you wield enhances your reflexes past what your body could normally handle. As a result, whenever you make a Dexterity check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of +1).
In addition, while your Rage is active, you can use your Lightning Step once on each of your turns without taking a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

name: Lingering Effects
entries: When you finish a long rest, choose one of the following conditions: {@condition blinded}, {@condition charmed}, {@condition exhaustion}, {@condition frightened}, {@condition paralyzed}, {@condition petrified}, {@condition poisoned}, {@condition prone}, {@condition restrained}, or {@condition stunned}. You have advantage on saving throws against that condition until you choose a different one with this feature.

name: Liquefied Body
entries: As a bonus action, you can transform your body into a viscous, liquid form for 10 minutes You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space or merges into your new form For the duration, you can squeeze through a space as narrow as 6 inches wide, and moving through difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. After you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Magical Weapons
entries: Starting at 6th level, your attacks with your parasitic weapon count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

name: Live Fast, Be a Good Looking Corpse
entries: You experience the world, in all its wonders, with vampiric speed. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Your Dexterity score increases by 2, to a maximum of 25.

entries.name: Rapidity
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 1 Blood Point to gain an additional action on your turns. That action can be used to take only the {@action Attack|XPHB} (one attack only), {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, {@action Hide|XPHB}, or {@action Utilize|XPHB} action. This effects lasts for a number of turns equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Living Catalyst
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one compound you know with another one.

name: Living Cauldron
entries: The number of compounds you can safely consume increases to three plus your Constitution modifier (minimum one).
At Fighter level 18, the number of compounds you can safely consume increases to five plus your Constitution modifier (minimum one).

name: Living Crucible
entries: {@i Enhance Your Martial Prowess with Alchemy}

Fighters who become Living Crucibles have discovered an external means of power. While most Fighters train in martial traditions or study the art of war, Living Crucibles hone their craft of alchemy to endure compounds poisonous to others. In exchange for this rigorous physical and mental preparation, these Fighters are able to temporarily push their bodies past their natural limits. Under the influence of their alchemical compounds, these warriors can see in darkness, enhance their speed, inure themselves to magical attacks, and more.

name: Long Arm of the Law
entries: Once per turn when you hit a Large or smaller creature with a ranged attack using a weapon, you can hobble the target. The creature can't move on its next turn unless it first takes the {@action Disengage|XPHB} action.

name: Lordly Power
entries: Your will over others becomes ironclad and staggeringly powerful. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Imposing Aura
entries: When a creature within 15 feet of you targets you with an attack roll or a damaging spell, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or either choose a new target or lose the attack or spell. On a successful save, the target isn't affected, and it's immune to Imposing Aura for 24 hours.

entries.name: Penetrating Dominance
entries: Creatures you can see within 60 feet of yourself have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Summon
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 3 Blood Points to urge a Beast, Humanoid, or Undead you have touched and is on the same plane of existence as you to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, the creature is compelled to come to you. The creature must use as much of its movement as possible to move in your direction on its turns, taking the safest route, and stopping only to eat and rest. A compelled creature repeats the save at the end of each day at dusk, ending the effect on itself on a success. You know if the compulsion ends early. You can't have more than one creature under this effect at a time. If you use this feature again, the effect on another creature ends.

When the creature appears, it is under no compulsion to behave a particular way. You can ask it to perform a service in exchange for payment, but it isn't obliged to do so. The requested task could range from simple (fly us across the chasm, or help us fight a battle) to complex (spy on our enemies, or protect us during our foray into the dungeon). You must be able to communicate with the creature to bargain for its services. Payment can take a variety of forms.

The GM can adjust these payments based on the circumstances under which you called upon it. If the task is aligned with the creature's ethos, the payment might be halved or even waived. Nonhazardous tasks typically require only half the payment, while especially dangerous tasks might require a greater gift. Creatures rarely accept tasks that seem suicidal.
A {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB}, {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB}, or {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell ends this effect.

name: Lore
entries: Some say that lore-masters risk accumulating knowledge at the expense of wisdom. You are determined to prove them wrong.

name: Lore-Master
entries: Also at 3rd level, when a creature rolls a Lore die it gained from you, the creature can reroll the Lore die and use either total.

name: Lycanthrope
entries: Your true form is a bestial hybrid, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Claws
entries: You have a set of vicious claws that you can use to make {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. When you deal damage with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can deal Slashing damage equal to {@dice 1d6} plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier instead of the strike's normal damage.

entries.name: Climb Speed
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You gain {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet. If you already have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, its range increases by 60 feet.

name: Mage Hunter
entries: You consider Humanoids that can cast spells as being a creature type in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1}.

Additionally, when you damage a creature type in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1} that is {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating}, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw it makes to maintain its {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

name: Magic Bullet [Maneuver]
entries: When you make a spell attack roll, you can expend one {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to substitute the spell attack with a ranged attack using a weapon. Add the {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die} to the attack roll. On a hit, the attack deals the weapon's normal damage, in addition to the effects of the spell attack roll.

name: Magic Coin
entries: Also at 3rd level, you know that coins can be just as powerful as the most enthralling rhetoric. Whereas other bards may use words and song as their means for conjuring spells, you instead use a simple coin. You can use any coin worth at least 1 cp as a spellcasting focus for your bard spells.

In addition, you can use an action to magically fling a coin from your hand at a target within 60 feet of you. Make a ranged spell attack with the coin, using your Charisma modifier for the attack roll. On a hit, the target takes 1 bludgeoning damage plus {@dice 1d12} thunder damage. Immediately after the attack, the coin returns to your hand. If you roll a 20 on the attack roll against a hostile creature using a nonmagical copper, silver, electrum, or gold piece, the coin is magically duplicated when it returns to your hand. The new coin can appear in your hand, at your feet, or in a coin pouch on your person (your choice).
The coin's thunder damage increases by {@dice 1d12} when you reach 6th level ({@dice 2d12}) and 14th level ({@dice 3d12}).

name: Magic Missile Mage
entries: {@i Cast Magic Missile Better Than Anyone}

{@spell Magic Missile|XPHB} is a staple wizard spell, beloved for its versatility and unerring accuracy. As a Missile Mage, however, your fondness for the spell borders on obsession. Your studies focus entirely on this spell, exploring every aspect of its casting, resulting in new augmentations and greater power.

name: Magic Missile Savant
entries: Add the {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB} spell to your spellbook for free. Your expertise in this spell grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Extra Darts
entries: When you cast {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, you create an extra dart of magical force. You create two extra darts at Wizard level 6, three extra darts at Wizard level 10, and four extra darts at Wizard level 14.

entries.name: Free Casting
entries: You can cast {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB} without a spell slot. You can do so a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Penetrating Darts
entries: Your {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB} darts bypass any effect, such as the {@spell Shield|XPHB} spell, that specifically blocks the {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB} spell.

name: Magic Resistance
entries: You're such an amazing wizard that other wizards can't even touch you. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

name: Magic Snare
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can imperceptibly create a magical trap in the ground at your feet. The first Large or smaller creature other than you that enters that space in the next minute springs the trap and must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC; the trap can't be sprung by you or creatures you designate when you create it. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d8} Piercing damage, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

A creature that can see {@condition Invisible|XPHB} objects (such as one benefiting from {@spell See Invisibility|XPHB} or {@sense Truesight|XPHB}) can see these traps. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Magical Aegis
entries: You gain the ability to extend a protective charm. You radiate an unseeable aura in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that originates from you. The aura is inactive while you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. You and allies in your aura have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells cast by creature types in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1}.

Additionally, you always have the {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} spell prepared. You can cast {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot. Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Magnum Opus
entries: You have mastered what it means to be one of the greatest vampiric artisans, which defines you as much as you define it. Choose two of the following benefits.

entries.name: Flicker
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 3 Blood Points to dance between the beats of a mortal's heart. Until the start of your next turn, you have a +3 bonus to AC, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled, your movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls.

entries.name: Clairvoyance
entries: You can expend 2 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Clairvoyance|XPHB} or {@spell Scrying|XPHB} spell. When you cast the spell in this way, the sensor can't be perceived.

entries.name: Open Mind
entries: You can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to expend 1 Blood point to choose any number of creatures you know within 5 miles of yourself or any number of creatures you can see within 120 feet of yourself. You and the chosen creatures can communicate telepathically with each other while the creatures and you are within 5 miles of each other for 8 hours. You and the targets can instantly share words, images, sounds, and other sensory messages with each other through the link, and the targets recognize you as the creature they are communicating with. This effect enables creatures to understand the meaning of your words and any sensory messages you send to them.

entries.name: Star Magnetism
entries: You can expend 3 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Mass Suggestion|XPHB} spell. When you cast the spell in this way, you can target any creature you can communicate with, you don't need line of sight, the range becomes 1 mile, and you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@condition Concentration|XPHB}.

name: Malediction
entries: You can call upon the Horned King's malice to manipulate luck and fate. As an action, you can magically curse a creature you can see within 60 feet of you until the end of its next turn. Alternatively, when a creature within range targets you with an attack roll or a spell, you can use your reaction to curse the creature with your choice of one of the curses below. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Agony
entries: The target has disadvantage on its next attack roll or Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status concentration|PHB} (your choice).

entries.name: Hate
entries: The target has disadvantage on its next Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw (your choice).

entries.name: Rot
entries: The next time the target takes damage, it takes an extra {@damage 1d10} necrotic damage, and it can't regain hit points until the end of its next turn.

name: Malediction
entries: You can call upon the Horned King's malice to manipulate luck and fate. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can curse a creature you can see within 60 feet of you until the end of its next turn. Alternatively, when a creature within range targets you with an attack roll or a spell, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to curse the creature with your choice of one of the curses below. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Agony
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its next attack roll or Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} (your choice).

entries.name: Hate
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its next Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw (your choice).

entries.name: Rot
entries: The next time the target takes damage, it takes an extra {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage, and it can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until the end of its next turn.

name: Malleable Visage
entries: Years spent mending, shaping, and adapting flesh have given you a preternatural ability to modify your own body. You are proficient with surgeon's tools, which you can use as a spellcasting focus, and you know the alter self spell, which counts as a bard spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of bard spells you know. Over the course of 1 minute, you can cast the spell without expending a spell slot, choosing only the Change Appearance option. When you cast the spell in this way, it doesn't require concentration.

In addition, over the course of 10 minutes, you can use your surgeon's tools to change the appearance of a willing creature. It magically gains the benefits of the Change Appearance effect of the {@spell alter self} spell, which lasts until it finishes a long rest. After you use your surgeon's tools in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Manifest Blow
entries: You gain one of the following options of your choice.

entries.name: Forged Heart
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can deal extra damage of the same type equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die.

entries.name: Nightmare Shroud
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 2 Focus Points to cause psychic energy to erupt from you. When you do so, each creature of your choice in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes Psychic damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die, and has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Traveler's Blade
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can use both the {@variantrule Damage|XPHB} and the Grapple option. You are always considered to have a free hand when determining whether you can Grapple another creature.

entries.name: Weretouched
entries: When you hit the same creature twice on your turn with {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} you can expend up to 3 Focus Points to deal extra damage on your second hit. The damage equals a number of rolls of your Martial Arts die equal to the Focus Points expended, and is the same type as your triggering {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

name: Manifest Charges
entries: When you reach 14th level, you can convert the core charges within your wand into raw, arcane energy. By manipulating this energy, you can use the wand's core charges in the following new ways:

items: As a bonus action, you can expend 1 or more of the wand's core charges to create a number of motes of magical force equal to the core charges spent. Each mote streaks toward a different target that you can see within 60 feet of you, dealing force damage to each target equal to {@dice 1d4} + your Intelligence modifier.

When you or another creature that you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to expend 1 or more of the wand's core charges to create a magical barrier, reducing the damage taken by an amount equal to three times the number of core charges spent.

entries: In addition, you have gained a supreme mastery and understanding of wands. If you expend the last charge of a staff or wand, you needn't roll a {@dice d20}, even if it says to. Further, the gold and time you must spend to craft a magic wand is halved.

name: Manifest Inscriptions
entries: Also at 6th level, you can reveal hidden glyphs and enchantments that surround you. As an action, you expend one charged rune to reveal hidden or invisible arcane traps, marks, runes, wards, sensors, or glyphs within 60 feet of you. They glow with dim light in a 5-foot radius for 1 minute.

You have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|advantage} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks to discern the nature of any magic revealed in this way for the duration. If the glyphs you reveal mean something in a language you can't read, you can understand them while they are glowing as if you knew that language.

name: Mantle of The Wolf
entries: You can manifest a tiny portion of Fenris's power within you. As an action, you can expend a single use of your Wild Shape to cause an ephemeral wolf's head, blazing with primal power, to appear above your own for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), manifest it again, or have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

While this mantle surrounds your body, you are filled with fierce primordial rage. You gain a bonus to your Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) checks and Strength saving throws equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). Additionally, you can replace one of your melee attacks with a special bite attack using the spectral head. This bite uses your Wisdom modifier instead of Strength for the attack rolls, and it deals {@damage 1d8} + your Wisdom modifier Force damage on a successful hit.

name: Many Roads to Ruin
entries: Your mystic connection to catastrophe and destruction grows stronger. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Elemental Assault
entries: While your Ruin Incarnate feature is active, whenever you hit with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can cause it to deal your choice of Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Necrotic damage rather than its normal damage type.

entries.name: Increased Might
entries: While your Ruin Incarnate feature is active, you can add your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1) to your Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

name: Many-Masked Performance
entries: At 6th level, you gain the ability to enthrall an audience with a dramatic performance. Over the course of 1 minute, you can engage in a captivating performance and attempt to cause nearby creatures to become {@condition charmed}, {@condition frightened}, or fall {@condition unconscious} (your choice). Choose a number of creatures up to your bard level within 60 feet of you that can hear you. When the performance ends, each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be subjected to the chosen condition.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Marauder's Reprisal
entries: When you become {@status Bloodied|XPHB} or if a creature scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an attack against an enemy within your reach, if there is one. If the attack hits, you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, and you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your level.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all uses once you've finished a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Marine Layer
entries: As an action, you channel the sea to create a thick cloud of fog that surrounds you for 20 feet in all directions. The fog moves with you, remaining centered on you and making its area heavily obscured. You and each creature within 5 feet of you instead treat the area as lightly obscured. This fog lasts for 10 minutes, spreads around corners, and cannot be dispersed unless you choose to end this effect (no action required).

name: Mark of the Heretic
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to mark a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself as a heretic.

For 1 minute, your weapon attacks and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} against the chosen creature can score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}. In addition, whenever the target starts its turn, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a melee attack against that creature if it's within reach.

name: Mark of the Heretic
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to mark a creature as a heretic. As a bonus action, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet and a weeping symbol appears on it. For the next minute, your weapon attacks against the chosen creature score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20, and each time the creature's turn starts you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against it.

name: Mark Prey
entries: As a bonus action, you choose a creature you can see within 90 feet and mystically mark it as your quarry for the next hour. For the duration, you deal an extra {@damage 1d6} damage to the target whenever you hit it with a weapon attack, and you have advantage on any Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check you make to find it. If you use this feature to mark a new creature, any previous marks disappear.

name: Marked for Death
entries: You are particularly skilled against foes you mark for death. You have advantage on your first attack against an interdicted creature on each of your turns.

name: Marking Strike
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can forgo using that weapon's mastery property to mark the target until the end of your next turn. This effect ends early if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition or if someone else marks the creature. A marked creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against targets other than you, and it must spend 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves when moving away from you.

name: Martial Form
entries: At the start of your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to manifest your martial form. The form lasts for 10 minutes, until you use this feature again, or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. Choose one of the following options when you adopt the form.

entries.name: Forged Heart
entries: Whenever you hit an object with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, the hit is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. In addition, whenever you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} granted by Flurry of Blows, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 15 feet directly away from you.

entries.name: Nightmare Shroud
entries: When you use Deflect Attacks, the attacking creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Traveler's Blade
entries: Your reach increases by 10 feet.

entries.name: Weretouched
entries: When you reduce an enemy within 5 feet of you to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Monk Level.

name: Martial Maneuvers
entries: You have trained in the manner of heroes from the old sagas, and now you can perform certain martial maneuvers. A maneuver requires you to spend maneuver points to use it.

You know three maneuvers of your choice from the list below. You learn an additional maneuver at 6th, 10th, and 14th level. Each time you learn a maneuver, you can also replace one maneuver you know with a different one you can learn.

entries.name: Maneuver Points
entries: Channeling the heroes from the old sagas is no easy task, and your pool of maneuver points represents the limit of your abilities to do so. Your barbarian class level determines the number of maneuver points you have, as shown in the Maneuver Points column in the Path of the Carrion Raven table below. You regain all spent maneuver points at the end of a long rest.

entries.name: Using Maneuvers
entries: You can use one maneuver during each turn. Some maneuvers require {@status concentration}, as if {@status concentration||concentrating} on a spell, or certain conditions to use. Some maneuvers will require your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver's effects.

name: Martial Maneuvers
entries: You have trained in the manner of heroes from the old sagas, and now you can perform certain martial maneuvers. A maneuver requires you to spend maneuver points to use it.

You know three maneuvers of your choice from the list below. You learn additional maneuvers at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. Each time you learn a maneuver, you can also replace one maneuver you know with a different one you can learn.

entries.name: Maneuver Points
entries: Channeling the heroes from the old sagas is no easy task, and your pool of maneuver points represents the limit of your abilities to do so. Your class level determines the number of maneuver points you have, as shown in the Maneuver Points column in the Blade Breaker Chart below. You regain all spent maneuver points at the end of a long rest.

entries.name: Using Maneuvers
entries: You can use one maneuver during each turn. Some maneuvers require {@status concentration}, as if {@status concentration||concentrating} on a spell, or certain conditions to use. Some maneuvers will require your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver's effects.

name: Martial Sorcery
entries: Your past heroic life grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Heroic Soul
entries: At the start of each of your turns, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to gain {@dice 1d6} plus your Sorcerer level in {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} (no action required).

entries.name: Innate Bladework
entries: Whenever you attack with a weapon with which you have proficiency while your {@classFeature Innate Sorcery|Sorcerer|XPHB|1} feature is active, you can use your Charisma modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity.

entries.name: Martial Training
entries: You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Light armor, Medium armor, and {@item Shield|XPHB|Shields}.

name: Martial Training
entries: You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor and Shields. In addition, you can use a Simple or Martial weapon as a Spellcasting Focus to cast spells from the Bard spell list.

In addition, your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of one Simple or Martial weapon of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can practice weapon drills and change your weapon choice.

name: Mask of Civility
entries: You are proficient in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill History|XPHB}, {@skill Investigation|XPHB}, {@skill Medicine|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}, or {@skill Religion|XPHB}. In addition, you gain proficiency with one type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice or you know one language of your choice.

name: Mass Manipulation
entries: Your ability to command and sway others grows to encompass multiple minds at once. You can expend 3 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Mass Suggestion|XPHB} spell. At level 15, you can expend 4 Blood Points to cast the spell as its level 7 version; at level 18, you can expend 5 Blood Points to cast it as its level 8 version; and at level 20, you can expend 6 Blood Points to cast it as its level 9 version.

name: Master of Disguise
entries: As an action, you can cast the {@spell disguise self} spell without expending a spell slot.

name: Master of Many Faces
entries: You can wear two masks simultaneously, gaining the benefits of both.

name: Master of Words
entries: When you prepare spells, pick two spells from levels 1 to 5 to weave into a linked, powerful spell you can prepare as a single spell. The level of the linked spell is equal to the combined level of the two spells chosen and can't exceed 6.
The chosen spells must have a Verbal component and must have a casting time of one action.
As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can cast the linked spell, and the effects of both spells occur at the same time.

name: Material Enhancement
entries: Your attention to both magic and mundane detail gives you a heightened understanding and control over them. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can touch a weapon, suit of armor, or other object. Until the end of your next {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the object becomes magical if it isn't already, and gains your choice of up to two of the following benefits:

items: (Weapon Only) The wielder of the weapon gains a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it; this bonus increases to +2 when you reach Wizard level 10 and +3 when you reach Wizard level 14. If the weapon already granted a bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls, the wielder must choose whether to use that bonus or the one granted by this feature when attacking with it.

(Armor Only) The wearer of the armor gains a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}; this bonus increases to +2 when you reach Wizard level 10 and +3 when you reach Wizard level 14. If the armor already granted a bonus to AC, the wearer must choose whether to use that bonus or the one granted by this feature when calculating its {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}.
(Armor Only) The armor doesn't impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks if it normally would.

The object sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 20 feet. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, a creature holding the object can cause it to stop or resume shedding this light.

The object's weight is halved. If the object is a suit of armor, it doesn't have a Strength requirement if it normally would. If it's a weapon with the {@itemProperty H|XPHB|Heavy} property, it doesn't impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the wielder's attack rolls as a result of that property.
When a creature throws the object, it flies back to the creature's hand immediately after hitting or missing its target.
You change any of the object's colors, smells, and textures.

entries: You can use this feature twice, expending one use for each benefit you give an object. You regain all expended uses of this feature when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Once you give an object a benefit in this way, you can't give that benefit to an object again until you regain your expended uses of this feature.

name: Materializer
entries: {@i Easily Create and Destroy Matter as a Master Artisan and Arcanist}

Some Wizards abandon the limitations set by magic schools and instead focus on the binding force that holds everything together. These mages spend their efforts weaving and recreating matter from thin air to create art as well as utility. They value the craftsmanship taught by artisans around the world and consider their skills and creations to be a form of magic all its own.

Some arcanists focus on altering the living, whereas Materializers focus on creating and enhancing the inanimate. These mages see beauty in the possibility presented by raw materials and are found as readily studying ancient lore as they are in the center of a bustling forge. Many followers of this tradition take great care and pride in their Component Pouches and find great kinship among Bards, artists, and other craftsmen.

name: Maverick
entries: {@i Craft the Tool You Need in the Moment}

A Maverick Artificer is always tinkering, forever chasing a new idea. Where other Artificers focus on a single path of arcane science, the strength of the Maverick is flexibility. They may lack the discipline or credentials of their scholarly colleagues, but Mavericks have a talent for cobbling together exactly what's needed to solve any problem.

name: Maverick Spells
entries: You learn one cantrip of your choice from the Artificer, Cleric, or Wizard spell list. The chosen cantrip counts as an Artificer spell for you, and Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it.

In addition, any time you prepare Artificer spells, you can prepare an additional number of spells equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. These additional spells can be chosen from the Artificer, Cleric, and Wizard spells lists, and the chosen spells count as Artificer spells for you.

name: Mean Old Cuss
entries: You can offend every creature in the room with the flick of a wrist and a few curt words. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can choose a number of targets within 30 feet of yourself that can see or hear you up to your level in this class. Each chosen creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take Psychic damage equal to a roll of your Fisticuffs die plus your Constitution modifier and have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls it makes against creatures other than you until the start of your next turn.

Once you use this feature, you must finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you use it again. You can also restore your use of it by expending 3 {@classFeature Moxie|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2|Pugilist2024|Moxie Points} (no action required).

name: Meat Shield
entries: While you have a creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, you gain {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} against attacks made by creatures you aren't {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB}. When a creature you aren't {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB} misses you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 1 {@classFeature Moxie|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2|Pugilist2024|Moxie Point} to force that creature make the same attack with a new attack roll against a creature you are {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB}.

name: Medic
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Medicine} skill if you don't already have it. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses this skill.

In addition, your familiarity with blood has become magical, giving you some degree of control over it. As a result, you can use a bonus action to magically stabilize an {@condition unconscious} creature within 5 feet of you.

You can use this same magic when you apply traditional healing techniques. You can use a bonus action to expend one use of a {@item healer's kit|PHB} on a creature. When you do, that creature regains hit points equal {@dice 1d4} + your proficiency bonus. The creature can't regain hit points from this feature again until it finishes a short or long rest.

name: Medicinal Master
entries: When Good Medicine restores {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to a creature, that creature regains {@dice 2d8} additional {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
When Bad Medicine deals Acid damage to a creature, that creature takes {@dice 2d8} extra Acid damage. Additionally, target creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on their saving throw.

name: Mental Agony
entries: You know how to cause pain to your quarry both physically and mentally. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that failed a saving throw against one of your torturer techniques since the start of your last turn makes an Intelligence, a Wisdom, or a Charisma saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to flourish your blades, smile, or perform a similar terrifying display. The target subtracts {@dice 1d10} from its saving throw. Creatures that are immune to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition are immune to this effect.

name: Merrymaker
entries: When you or an ally within 30 feet of yourself that can see or hear you makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to give that creature {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. If the creature still fails the {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, this use of Merrymaker isn't expended.

name: Miasmic Contagion
entries: The strength of your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|PHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14|Miasmic Plague} has increased, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Choking Miasma
entries: Constitution saving throws against your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|PHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14|Miasmic Plague} have disadvantage.

entries.name: Scurrying Spread
entries: When you use your Step of the Wind, until the end of the turn, when you enter a space within 5 feet of any creature of your choice, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be cursed by your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|PHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14|Miasmic Plague}. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

name: Miasmic Contagion
entries: The strength of your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|XPHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24|Miasmic Plague} has increased, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Choking Miasma
entries: Constitution saving throws against your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|XPHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24|Miasmic Plague} have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Scurrying Spread
entries: When you expend 1 Focus Point to use your Step of the Wind, until the end of the turn, when you enter a space within 5 feet of any creature of your choice, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be cursed by your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|XPHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24|Miasmic Plague}. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

name: Might of the Necropolis
entries: Your command of the secrets imparted to you is absolute. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Eternal Vigil
entries: You no longer suffer the effects of aging, you can't be magically aged, and you don't die of old age. In addition, you no longer require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Restless Dead
entries: When you roll initiative, if you have fewer than 3 Draugr Dice, you regain expended dice until you have 3.

name: Might of the Necropolis
entries: Your command of the secrets imparted to you is absolute. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Eternal Vigil
entries: You no longer suffer the effects of aging, you can't be magically aged, and you don't die of old age. In addition, you no longer require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Restless Dead
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, if you have fewer than 3 Draugr Dice, you regain expended dice until you have 3.

name: Mighty Effort
entries: When you use your Heroic Effort feature, you can now target up to two additional creatures, instead of only one.

name: Mighty Quick Brew
entries: Starting at 14th level, you learn an additional {@filter common potion|items|source=ObojimaTallGrass|type=potion|rarity=common} as well as an {@filter uncommon potion|items|source=ObojimaTallGrass|type=potion|rarity=uncommon}, using your Quick Brew feature.
Each time you gain a level in this class, you can swap one of your chosen potions with a different one.

name: Mighty Shot
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you have learned to put all your might into your shots. Before you make an attack with a ranged weapon, you can choose to roll the weapon's damage die and subtract the number rolled from the attack roll. If the attack hits, you roll two additional weapon damage dice on the damage roll. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

name: Mind Domain
entries: {@i Channel Divine Devotion into Psychic Power}

The Mind Domain celebrates the power of the mortal mind, channeling psychic energy to protect the faithful and smite your enemies. While this is most often associated with the Path of Light or the Riedran Path of Inspiration, followers of the daelkyr can also master this power. Visions of Xoriat can drive a priest to madness, but they can also reveal deadly secrets of the mind.

name: Mind Domain Spells
entries: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Mind Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Mind Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Command|XPHB}, {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB}, {@spell Dissonant Whispers|XPHB}, {@spell Mind Spike|XPHB}

name: Mind of Mercury
entries: Starting at 11th level, you've honed your awareness and reflexes through mental aptitude and pattern recognition. Once per turn, if you've already taken your reaction, you may spend 1 ki point to take an additional reaction. You can use only one reaction per triggering effect.

name: Mindset of Perfect Prediction
entries: You have learned to enter a focused state of mind. When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can activate this feature to enter your perfected mindset (no action required), gaining the benefits below. At the end of each of your turns, you must make a Charisma saving throw (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, your mindset ends. If you are {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} on multiple spells when your mindset ends, you can choose one spell to maintain. The rest of the spells end as if your {@status Concentration|XPHB} had been broken. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
While your perfected mindset is active, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Quickened Mind
entries: Your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count becomes 31.

entries.name: Expansive Mind
entries: You can concentrate on any number of spells simultaneously. If you are forced to make a saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} while you are {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} on multiple spells, you make only a single Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, your {@status Concentration|XPHB} breaks on all spells.

entries.name: Predictive Mind
entries: You have {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} prepared. You can cast it as a level 6 spell without expending a spell slot.

name: Minor Creation
entries: When you cast a level 1+ spell, you can magically create a {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} of inanimate material of your choice that is no larger than 5 feet on a side. The {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} appears in an unoccupied space you can see on the ground within 30 feet of you, or it appears magically connected to another {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} within that range that you created with this feature. Once you reach Wizard level 10, the range increases to 60 feet. A {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} created in this way weighs a number of pounds equal to 5 times its length on a side, regardless of its material. The {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes} can support up to 10 times their weight, potentially serving as a bridge, and they can provide cover for creatures behind them.

You can have a total number of these {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes} in existence at a time equal to your Wizard level. You can dismiss any number of the {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes} of your choice as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. Otherwise, a {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} disappears after 1 hour or if it takes any damage. The {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes} are objects that have an AC equal to 10 + your Intelligence modifier, 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Force damage.

entries.name: Cube Detonation
entries: When you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to dismiss one or more of the {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes}, you can choose to detonate any of them instead, destroying them. Each creature within 10 feet of a detonated {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature takes Force damage equal to {@dice 1d6} + half your Wizard level (round down) on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. You can detonate a total number of {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes}—all at once or with multiple separate {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB|Bonus Actions}—equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1), and you regain all expended uses of doing so when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore uses of it by expending a level 1+ spell slot (no action required), regaining a number of uses equal to the slot's level.

name: Mirage
entries: At 6th level, you learn the {@spell mirror image} spell. If you already know this spell, you learn a different sorcerer spell of your choice. The spell doesn't count against your number of spells known. You can cast it by spending 2 sorcery points or by expending a spell slot. If you cast it with sorcery points, any creature within 10 feet of you that destroys one of the spell's illusions takes fire damage equal to half your sorcerer level, as the illusion bursts into a wave of scalding air and sand.

name: Misdirection
entries: At 7th level, you are adept at using words and gestures to taunt or fake-out your opponent, turning their lack of composure against them. This allows you to goad your foe into swinging in ways that can cause them to strike their allies, or which leave them open to a counterattack. As a bonus action you can misdirect an opponent within 5 feet of you. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw against a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier. On a failure, they must spend their reaction to attack a creature of your choice within 5 feet of them. If no other creatures are present within 5 feet of them, they waste their reaction attacking the air where you once were.
In order for you to misdirect a creature in this way they must be able to see, hear, or otherwise be able to understand you.

name: Misfortune Bringer
entries: {@i Curse Those You're About to Strike}

You've matched your penchant for illicit activities with the ability to mark your enemies for mishap and misfortune. Whether you were imbued with magic by spending time among the Fey or you learned the art of cursing from a long line of hedge Wizards, you are a Misfortune Bringer. Although not universal, many Misfortune Bringers possess heterochromia iridum—eyes of two different colors—and they use only one when glaring at targets they intend to curse.

name: Misfortune Bringer
entries: You've matched your penchant for illicit activities with the ability to mark your enemies for mishaps and misfortune. Whether your mother was a hag, you were imbued with magical powers by spending time among the fey, or you learned the art of cursing from a long line of hedge wizards before you, you are a Misfortune Bringer. Although not universal, many Misfortune Bringers have eyes of two different colors, using only one when glaring at the targets they intend to curse.

name: Misfortunes
entries: The misfortunes are presented in alphabetical order.

name: Misfortunist
entries: You learn Misfortunes that you can inflict on those cursed by your Evil Eye.

entries.name: Misfortunes
entries: You learn two Misfortunes of your choice, which are detailed under {@filter "Misfortunes"|optionalfeatures|source=GrimHollowPG24|feature type=mb:m} below.

You learn an additional Misfortune of your choice when you reach Rogue levels 9, 13, and 17. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one Misfortune you know with a different one.

entries.name: Jinx Points
entries: You have 4 Jinx Points. You gain 2 additional Jinx Points at Rogue level 13. To use a Misfortune option, you must spend the number of Jinx Points that it costs.
You regain all expended Jinx Points when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: If a Misfortune requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your Charisma or Intelligence modifier (your choice) + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Misfortunist
entries: Also at 3rd level, you learn misfortunes that you can inflict on those marked by your evil eye.

entries.name: Misfortunes
entries: You learn two misfortunes of your choice, which are detailed under "Misfortunes" below. You learn an additional misfortune of your choice at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. Each time you finish a long rest, you can replace one misfortune you know with a different one.

entries.name: Jinx Points
entries: You have four jinx points. When you spend a jinx point, it is no longer available to you until you regain it. You regain all spent jinx points when you finish a short or long rest.
You gain two additional jinx points at 13th level.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: Your evil eye, and some of your misfortunes, require your target to make a saving throw to resist their effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:

name: Mocking Banter
entries: Your witty and insulting japes become biting to the point of needling your foes' very psyche. When a creature damages you, you can use your reaction to force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes psychic damage equal to the triggering damage you took, or half as much damage on a successful one.
Once you use this reaction, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Mocking Banter
entries: Your witty and insulting japes become biting to the point of needling your foes' very psyche. When a creature damages you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes Psychic damage equal to the triggering damage you took, or half as much damage on a successful one.
Once you use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Modular Upgrades I
entries: You can upgrade each of your companions with exotic organs and appendages. At the start of a long rest, you can choose one of the following upgrades for each of your companions. At the end of the long rest, the biomantic meld completes, and your companion gains the associated action optional. The DC for the saving throw equals your tamer spell save DC.

entries.name: Compelling Plumage
entries: Each creature in a 25–foot cone that can see your companion must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition charmed} by your companion's dazzling display of colour for the next minute. While {@condition charmed} in this way, the creature is {@condition incapacitated} and has a speed of 0. The effect ends for an affected creature if it takes any damage, if someone else uses an action to shake the creature out of its stupor, or if the companion moves out of the creature's line of sight or is ever more than 25 feet away from the creature.

entries.name: Phosphoburst
entries: Each other creature in a 10-foot-radius sphere centred on your companion must make a Constitution saving throw against the dizzying burst of light your companion emits On a failure, a creature takes {@damage 2d10} radiant damage and is {@condition blinded} until the end of its next turn On a success, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't {@condition blinded}.

entries.name: Poison Web
entries: Your companion launches an unfurling web of sticky silk in a 20-foot cube originating from it. All surfaces in the area become lined with webbing for the next minute. Each creature that touches one of these surfaces for the first time on its turn or starts its turn doing so must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become {@condition restrained} for the duration, or until it breaks free. A creature {@condition restrained} by the webs takes {@damage 2d4} poison damage when it becomes {@condition restrained} and at the start of each of its turns. A creature can use its action to make a Strength check against your tamer spell save DC, freeing itself or another creature {@condition restrained} by this web on a success.

entries.name: Sirenshriek
entries: Each other creature in a 15-foot-radius sphere centred on your companion must make an Intelligence saving throw as your companion lets forth a brain-curdling mental shriek. On a failure, a creature takes {@damage 3d8} psychic damage and, if it is concentrating on a spell, loses its concentration. On a success, a creature takes half as much damage and makes saving throws to maintain its concentration as normal.
Once a companion uses one of these actions, it can't do so again until it finishes a short or long rest.

name: Modular Upgrades II
entries: Starting at 18th level, a companion can use the {@subclassFeature Modular Upgrades I|Tamer|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting|Splicer|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting|7} action twice before a rest.

name: Moloch's Blessing
entries: When Moloch accepts you as his illrigger, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Deception} skill (your choice). If you already have proficiency in the skill of your choice, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with that skill.

In addition, your Forked Tongue feature grants you an additional language (for a total of three at 3rd level and four at 9th level). Whenever you speak in a language gained by this feature, your devilish influence is subconsciously felt by creatures who can hear and understand you, granting you advantage on Charisma checks to influence those creatures.

name: Moloch's Interdiction
entries: You learn the following additional interdict boons at the noted illrigger levels. Once you learn an interdict boon granted by this feature, you always know it, and it doesn't count against the number of interdict boons you know.

name: Money Spinner
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you present your {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB} and expend a use of your {@classFeature Channel Divinity|Cleric|XPHB|2} to gain favor or turn away prying eyes. Choose a number of creatures within 30 feet of yourself equal to one plus one more for each divine coin you expend when you use this feature. For each target, choose either a bribe or a reward.

entries.name: Reward
entries: The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute or until it takes damage. While it has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition, it is {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you and other creatures you designate.

entries.name: Bribe
entries: The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

name: Money Talks
entries: By 6th level, you've learned how to briefly enchant a coin with divination magic. You can enchant a mundane copper, silver, electrum, gold, or platinum piece that you're holding in this way using an action. A creature holding the coin that knows at least one language can understand the meaning of any word you speak, and when it speaks, you understand what it says. In addition, you have advantage on the first Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check you make when negotiating the value of a good or service with a creature that's holding or carrying the enchanted coin.

Alternatively, you can use an action to see and hear through the enchanted coin until the start of your next turn as if you were in the coin's space. During this time, you are {@condition deafened|PHB|deaf} and {@condition blinded|PHB|blind} with regard to your own senses.

The coin remains enchanted for 10 minutes or until you end the effect early (no action required). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Monster Kill
entries: Once per turn when you hit an Aberration, Dragon, Fey, Fiend, Monstrosity, Ooze, or Undead with an attack with a weapon, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d10} damage to the target. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon.

name: Monster-Hide Armor
entries: You have learned to craft a set of Light or Medium armor by using dragon scales, werewolf hide, troll leather, or a similar monster component. The armor takes on the appearance of your choice, reflecting the component it is made from.

The armor has the same properties as Light or Medium armor (your choice when the armor is crafted) and gains two modifications from the {@filter Armor Modifications list|optionalfeatures|source=grimhollowpg24|feature type=tg:am}. Whenever you gain a Monster Hunter level, you can replace one of these modifications with another modification.
Modifications require the armor to be worn to function.

name: Monstrous Gifts
entries: You have become more at peace with your monstrous appearance, unlocking aspects of yourself. You can choose two benefits from the following list.

entries.name: Animalist
entries: You can cast the {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB}, {@spell Animal Messenger|XPHB}, and {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB} spells. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast each spell in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Ears of the Bat
entries: You have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Feral Talons
entries: You have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and when you hit with your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and deal damage, you can deal Slashing damage equal to {@damage 1d8} plus your Strength modifier instead of the normal damage of an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: Leathery Hide
entries: Damage dealt to you except Fire and Radiant is reduced by an amount equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum reduction of 1).

entries.name: Patagia
entries: If you aren't {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} or wearing Heavy armor, you can extend your skin to glide. When you fall, you can move up to 5 feet horizontally for every 1 foot you descend, and when you would take damage from a fall, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the fall's damage to 0.

entries.name: The Terror
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can reveal your monstrous nature to up to three creatures you can see within 30 feet. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or gain the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute, or until you deal damage to it.

name: Monstrous Resilience
entries: Once per turn when you take damage, you can reduce the total damage you take, to a minimum of 0. The reduction equals your Constitution modifier plus your Bestial Aspect Level.

name: Moon Domain
entries: Since the {@book Founding|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|The Founding}, all mortal creatures have looked to the skies and sensed the power and mystery carried by {@book Catha and Ruidus|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|Catha and Ruidus}, the two moons of Exandria. The {@deity The Moonweaver|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} herself is said to guide her worshipers from within the pale glow of Catha, revealing hidden paths and granting inspired dreams to those who pray to that moon. Distant, dark Ruidus is often regarded with awe and apprehension, considered a portent for fell deeds and bad luck.

Clerics of the Moon Domain draw on their divine connection to the moons to wield light and shadow, invoke good fortune and ill favor, and reveal or conceal as they see fit. Most Moon clerics worship the {@deity The Moonweaver|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Moonweaver} herself, but her followers are as varied as the stars in the sky. Some seek to protect the vulnerable and do good in the world, while others meddle with impunity and distort the truth for selfish gain. Other Moon clerics worship not the gods but the moons themselves, especially those with an innate connection to the lunar cycles through {@variantrule Player Characters as Lycanthropes|MM|lycanthropy}.

name: Mother of Sorrows
entries: Universal suffering has given rise to an enigmatic being known as the Mother of Sorrows, and warlocks who bind themselves to her cause seek to spread her poisonous vengeance. The Mother of Sorrows was born from the suffering of parents who have lost children to pestilence, disease, and treachery, and her gifts grant warlocks the power to avenge the thousands of sorrows laid at her feet.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Mother of Sorrows lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Expanded Spell List
rows: {@spell detect poison and disease}, {@spell inflict wounds}

name: Muscle Mass
entries: Choose the {@skill Acrobatics|XPHB} or {@skill Athletics|XPHB} skill. If you lack proficiency with the chosen skill, you gain proficiency in it, and if you already have proficiency in it, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

name: Mutable Strike
entries: You have the power to alter your natural weapons, growing claws or reinforcing your fists. Whenever you deal damage with your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, it can deal your choice of Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage.

name: Mutate Shape
entries: When you assume a Wild Shape form, or as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while your Wild Shape is active, you can expend a spell slot to gain Mutation Points equal to the slot's level. These Mutation Points last until they are spent, you gain additional Mutation Points, or  you leave the form. While you have Mutation Points, you can spend them on your turn (no action required by you) to gain a Mutation from the list below. When you do, your body distends and reconstitutes in a gruesome display.
Mutations last until you leave the form or you expend a spell slot to gain Mutation Points.
{@style Mutation Options|large}
The following options are available to your Mutate Shape feature. The options are presented in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Repeatable
entries: A Mutation can be gained only once for each Wildshape use unless its description states otherwise in a "Repeatable" subsection.

name: Mutt With Moxie
entries: You share everything with your faithful hound: food, shelter, even moxie. When you use abilities granted by your {@classFeature Moxie|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2} feature, your hound gains a benefit as well.

entries.name: Brace Up
entries: When you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} from your Brace Up ability, your hound gains the same number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: One-Two Punch
entries: When you use your One-Two Punch ability, your hound can make one or both attacks instead of you.

entries.name: Stick and Move
entries: When you use your Stick and Move ability, your hound can take your choice of the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Help|XPHB} action.

name: Mystical Erudition (11th Level)
entries: You gain an additional language and an additional skill proficiency from the list: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}—(or you can double the bonus of an existing proficiency from the list) at 11th level.

name: Mystical Erudition (17th Level)
entries: You gain an additional language and an additional skill proficiency from the list: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}—(or you can double the bonus of an existing proficiency from the list) at 17th level.

name: Mystical Erudition
entries: Also by 6th level, you have extensively studied the history and lore within the archives of the {@book Cobalt Soul|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|Library of the Cobalt Soul}. You learn one language of your choice, and you gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}. If you already have proficiency in one of the listed skills, you can instead choose to double your proficiency bonus for any ability check you make that uses the chosen proficiency.

name: Mystical Maneuvers
entries: You can use the following martial maneuvers.

entries.name: Blinding Attack
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend two Sorcery Points as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to attempt to blind the target. Add {@damage 2d8} to the attack's damage roll. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the condition on itself on a success.

entries.name: Ruinous Blow
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend two Sorcery Points as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to sunder its defenses. Add {@damage 2d8} to the attack's damage roll. The target has a -3 penalty to AC until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Wounding Strike
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend two Sorcery Points as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to deal the target a bleeding wound. Add {@dice 2d8} to the attack's damage roll. A creature with a bleeding wound can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and takes Necrotic damage equal to {@dice 1d8} for each of its wounds at the start of each of its turns. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}. A creature can take an action to staunch all of its bleeding wounds.

name: Mythic Swashbuckler
entries: At 20th level, you learn to channel the spirits of historic sea captains to briefly become a paragon of heroic adventure. As an action, you embrace these spirits of the sea to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|advantage} on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks and you gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed. If you already have a climbing speed, it is doubled.
If you are within 5 feet of a creature and no other creatures are within 5 feet of you, you have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|advantage} on attack rolls against that creature.
You can take the {@action Dash} or {@action Disengage} action as a bonus action.
You have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|advantage} on Dexterity checks and Dexterity {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1} against effects you can see.
