entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.

name: Natural Attunement
entries: When you choose this arcane tradition at 2nd level, you learn how to attune yourself to the magic of leylines which course through nature. Each day when you prepare your spells in a natural setting, you may also attune yourself to the energy of a nearby leyline to gain additional spells. When you do, consult the list of spells from the {@table Leyline Spells|HumblewoodTales} table that matches the environment in which you prepared your spells. You can only be attuned to one leyline at a time.

While attuned to a leyline, you gain access to any spells on your current list of leyline spells for which you meet the level requirement. For as long as you are attuned to a leyline, you always have these spells prepared, and they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. Leyline spells are not copied into your spellbook. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the wizard spell list, the spell is nonetheless a wizard spell for you.

name: Natural Disruption
entries: By 10th level, you can channel energy from your leyline to disrupt others' magic. You can cast {@spell counterspell} or {@spell dispel magic} without expending a spell slot at the level of the highest spell slot available to you.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Nature Armor
entries: Your connection to nature helps to shield you from harm. You're always under the effect of the {@spell Barkskin|XPHB} spell.

In addition, at the start of each of your turns, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your Druid level (round down). When you assume a Wild Shape form, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Druid level plus half your Druid level (round down).

name: Nature's Wrath
entries: Your natural grafts succumb to your osteomantic powers and allow you to tap deeper into Nature's fury. You are permanently under the effect of the {@spell Barkskin|XPHB} spell.

In addition, while your Wickerbone Behemoth feature is active, your size is Large, and whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing and Slashing damage until the end of your next turn. You lose those {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} early if you take Fire damage.

name: Necromancer
entries: Whether through the tutelage of a lich, a career as a gravedigger, or an innate affinity for the world beyond, you have learnt to manipulate the very essence of life. You can strip it from those that would do you harm, and imbue it in those that serve your aims. Weaving threads of necromantic magic around bone, flesh, and sinew, you create gruesome facsimiles of life—undead puppets that move to the rhythm of the threads you pull.

name: Necromancer Spells
entries: You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Necromancer Spells table. Each spell counts as a tamer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of tamer spells you know.

name: Nemesis Sorcery
entries: {@i Devastate Foes with Speed and Precision}

While some sorcerers revel in unleashing devastation on dozens of enemies at once, you specialize in the arcane duel. You act with absolute precision, focusing your energy to strike at the perfect moment. You learn to break spells directed against you, whether expending your own power to fully counter them or casually dispersing deadly force. You may have learned the arts of magic on the battlefields of the Last War, but now you're the epitome of the lone wandslinger, always ready for the next duel.

name: Nemesis Spells
entries: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Nemesis Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Nemesis Spells
rows: {@spell Compelled Duel}, {@spell Mirror Image}, {@spell See Invisibility}, {@spell Shield}

name: Night Domain
entries: The night is mysterious, and conceals many unseen dangers. However, the cover of darkness also brings protection from predators and shadows within which one can conceal themselves. The gods of night are varied, encompassing those who would use the cover of darkness to protect others from threats, to those who would use the shadows for wrong doings. The motives of night gods are often shrouded in mystery. Many teach their followers that it is only by peering through the darkness and looking beyond what is hidden that one can attain truth. Clerics of night do their best to keep themselves and their companions safe while journeying through the darkness.

name: Night Music
entries: At 14th level, you can imbue your spellcasting with the full energy and terror of night. When you cast a spell, you can spend your reaction to also choose a number of creatures within 60 feet of you who saw and heard you cast the spell, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). Each target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC or be {@condition frightened} for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Night Stalker
entries: You are adept at tracking down enemies in the dead of night, giving you these benefits.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet for 10 minutes. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Slippery
entries: {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} against you. While entirely within {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, your movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

name: Nightwatcher
entries: {@i Take Back the Night}

Nightwatchers come from humble origins, often toiling as guards or investigators. Undaunted by dangers in the darkness, they stand firm against the growing night. Ever vigilant, they use the darkness to surprise and overwhelm foes much greater than themselves.

name: Nimble Lancer
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you are remarkably light on your feet and capable of counterbalancing even some of the most awkward of equipment. Lances have the versatile property for you while you're not mounted, dealing {@damage 1d8} piercing damage on a hit when held with one hand and {@damage 1d12} piercing damage when wielded with two. When you use your Launch feature and immediately hit with a melee attack using a lance, it counts as if you're wielding it with two hands.

If you hit a creature within 5 feet of you using a lance, you can immediately move up to 5 feet away from it, without provoking an opportunity attack from the target. You must be standing and have movement remaining in order to move in this way.

name: Nimble Trickery
entries: You gain proficiency in {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} if you don't already have it. When you make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check to swap an item with another item that has similar dimensions, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the check.

When you reach 6th level, you can swap an object with an unattended object of similar dimensions up to 30 feet away by succeeding on a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check. When you reach 14th level, you can replace the target object with an illusion rather than exchanging it for a real object. The illusory duplicate lasts for 1 minute. Once you use this aspect of Nimble Trickery, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} or expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Nimbus of Pathos
entries: Upon reaching 14th level, you can touch a willing creature as an action and empower it with tragic heroism. For 1 minute, the creature is surrounded by mournful music and ghostly singing, granting it the following benefits and drawbacks:

items: The creature has a +4 bonus to AC.
It has {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|advantage} on attack rolls and {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1}.
When the creature hits a target with a weapon attack or spell attack, that target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} radiant damage.
Any weapon attack against the creature scores a critical hit on a roll of 18–20.

entries: When this effect ends, the creature immediately drops to 0 hit points and is dying. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.

name: Nine Lives
entries: You are gifted with an almost inexplicable ability to survive dangerous situations. You have Nine Lives, which can be expended in the following ways:

items: If you take damage while you have 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can expend 1 life to not suffer a {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} failure. If the damage is from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, you must expend 2 lives to not suffer {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} failures.
If you are forced to make a {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}, you can expend 1 life to cause yourself to succeed instead.
If you are forced to make a {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}, you can expend 5 lives to turn the roll into a 20.
If you would die from massive damage, you can expend 1 life to be reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} instead of being killed outright.
When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can expend 1 life to drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.
If you are targeted with an effect that causes instant death, such as a {@spell Power Word Kill|XPHB} spell, you can expend 9 lives to ignore the effect.

entries: You regain all expended lives when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: No Escape
entries: As a bonus action, you can call on the shadows to entrap a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must make a Charisma saving throw, made with disadvantage if they are in dim light or darkness. On a failed save, the target's speed is halved and they can't willingly move more than 30 feet away from you. This effect ends for the target if you are {@condition incapacitated} or die or if the target is more than 30 feet away from you.

name: Nocturnal Predator
entries: As a predator of the night, you have been blessed with enhanced vision in darkness. You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet. If you already have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, its range increases by 60 feet.

name: Nornbound
entries: {@i Weaves the Threads of Fate}

The Nornbound Cleric pays homage to the Norns and in return is granted the ability to see and manipulate the threads of mortals' fates. This power, seen as tampering to some, can help or hinder the outcome of actions taken by the Cleric's targets. While Nornbound offer prayers to the other gods, the Norns are the guiding light to whom they have pledged their service.

name: Nosferatu
entries: {@i Hide Yourself from Prying Eyes and Unleash Your Own Monstrous Nature}

Nosferatu undergo a tragic transformation upon becoming Kindred. Their visage is warped to represent the Beast inside, making them into a terror who forges connections only with vermin and monsters. They must overcome this adversity with their gifts, lest they become the monsters they resemble.

name: Nosferatu Bane
entries: Your physical appearance is monstrous and unsettling. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks when interacting with non-Undead that can see your hideous visage.

name: Nowhere to Hide
entries: Illusions and other magical concealments cannot hinder your pursuit. You can cast {@spell True Seeing|XPHB} on yourself without expending a spell slot or material components. If you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

Additionally, when you use your {@subclassFeature Ley Line Tracker|Ranger|XPHB|Bloodhound|FoEQuickstone|3} feature to target your bounty, you are not affected by magic that conceals your bounty from your Divination spells.

name: Oak and Thorn
entries: The wrath of the Elderwoods drives you and punishes your foes. When you activate your {@subclassFeature Wood Wose|Druid|PHB|Old Ways|CrookedMoon14|2|CrookedMoon14}, you gain the following additional benefits for the duration.

entries.name: Oakenfist
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

entries.name: Gnarled Thorns
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using a weapon, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} piercing damage.

name: Oak and Thorn
entries: The wrath of the Elderwoods drives you and punishes your foes. When you activate your {@subclassFeature Wood Wose|Druid|XPHB|Old Ways|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24}, you gain the following additional benefits for the duration.

entries.name: Oakenfist
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

entries.name: Gnarled Thorns
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using a weapon, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage.

name: Oath of Castigation
entries: {@i Seek Out and Burn Wickedness to Ash}

Evil and wickedness are widespread and long-lived, but not infinite. Paladins who swear the Oath of Castigation root evil out to burn it away utterly, giving light to all that is innocent and good. Whether bound by the laws of mortals, their deity, or their own personal code, they relentlessly hunt down evil where it thrives. Paladins of this oath know evil cannot hide in any festering place once it burns.

The Wicked Nemeses table offers examples of malefactors, villains, and other evil beings that you have rooted out and purged in the past, or perhaps one you're still hunting. Facing these nemeses may have put you on the path of purging wickedness wherever it lurks.

entries.caption: Wicked Nemeses
rows: A rotting vampire noble who spreads a deadly plague through the command of countless vermin
A brutal contract killer who sells their services to various cults and shadowy organizations
A charismatic cult leader who lords over a remote island, making seasonal sacrifices of mortals to ensure a bountiful harvest each year
An immensely intelligent flesh golem that killed its creator to pursue its own sinister work with strange science and gruesome experiments
A bitterly envious hag of the woods who corrupts the youth of small villages and manipulates them to commit horrific atrocities
A proud and vain heretic who gathers zealous followers after a bloody schism to initiate a brutal crusade in the name of their twisted beliefs
A once-renowned hunter now cursed with lycanthropy who has gone on bloody rampages
A relentless necromancer who scours ancient ruins for forbidden magic to free their otherworldly master from an eldritch prison
A strange amphibious creature that emerges from the depths to kidnap innocents and drag them below the water's surface for unknown purposes
A brilliant doctor who has perfected a serum that transforms them into a hulking brute to commit a string of murders throughout a city
A bloodthirsty revenant who was once a dark knight and now musters other Undead riders to bring about death and decay
A tortured artist bearing a mask of comedy and tragedy who strives for their masterpiece through the mutilation of their victims' corpses

name: Oath of Castigation
entries: {@i Seek Out and Burn Wickedness to Ash}

Whether bound by the laws of mortals, their deity, or their own personal code, they relentlessly hunt down evil where it thrives. Paladins of this oath know evil cannot hide in any festering place once it burns.
These paladins share the following tenets:

items: Burn away all doubt in pursuit of duty.
Purge the wicked and corrupt; spare the innocent.
Sin is forgiven through suffering equal to the pain it inflicted.

name: Oath of Castigation Spells
entries: You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed in the Oath of Castigation Spells table. See the Sacred Oath class feature for how oath spells work.

name: Oath of Castigation Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Castigation Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

name: Oath of Pestilence
entries: {@i Gain Strength Through Suffering}

Clad in grime-soaked armor and wielding rusting weapons, Oath of Pestilence Paladins spread corruption, disease, and filth. Bound by an oath that infests their bodies with all manner of plagues, these heralds of decay lumber forward with unholy toughness and grim resolve.
These Paladins share the following tenets:

items: Spread plague to foster strength in the survivors.
There is nothing unnatural or immoral about the ending of life.
Might makes right.

name: Oath of Pestilence Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Pestilence Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Oath of Pestilence Spells
rows: {@spell Melf's Acid Arrow|XPHB|Acid Arrow}, {@spell Ray of Enfeeblement|XPHB}

name: Oath of Revelry
entries: {@i Work Hard and Party Harder}

Paladins who swear the Oath of Revelry make a solemn vow to party day and night until their hearts give out. The antithesis of stuffy, lawful crusaders, these emissaries of carousal travel the land, crashing parties and raising hell wherever they raise a glass. Authorities bristle at their arrival, but the youth cheer, for a Party Paladin is always accompanied by a good time.
These paladins share the following tenets:

items: Abide by the doctrines of the Codicus Brodicus.
Celebrate every occasion, inviting friend and foe alike.
When necessary, fight for your right to party.

name: Oath of Revelry Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Revelry Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. New spells are marked with an asterisk (*).

entries.caption: Oath of Revelry Spells
rows: {@spell Charm Person|XPHB}, {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|XPHB|Hideous Laughter}
{@spell Create Food And Water|XPHB}, {@spell Hypnotic Pattern|XPHB}

name: Oath of Slaughter
entries: {@i Revel in Unbridled Violence}

The only truth of war is death. The only virtue is to kill. The only victory is to survive. Heroism, honor, and glory are illusions. This is the creed of Tormach, Arch Daemon of Wrath, but this philosophy rings true for all warriors who devote themselves, body and soul, to the thrill of combat and the delight of bloodshed. Such champions find themselves at the forefront of armies, using the most violent methods at their disposal to bring battles to a swift close... or drawing out the war to sate their own appetites.
Paladins who take the Oath of Slaughter share the following tenets:

items: Violence is the end, not the means.
Break the body to break the spirit.
Revel in bloodshed, whether friend or foe.

name: Oath of Slaughter Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Slaughter Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

name: Oath of the Eldritch Hunt
entries: The Oath of the Eldritch Hunt is sworn to the eradication of the unnatural, the aberrant, and the alien. These hunters tread a fine line, enhancing themselves with their prey's powers whilst trying to maintain their own sanity. Unfortunately, this frenzied hunger drives many to madness, and it is no rare occurrence for these Paladins to have to hunt their own.

This oath is found most frequently among Paladins of the Radiant Order. Erroneously nicknamed grey templars, witch hunters, and knights aberrant, these oft-deformed warriors devote themselves to obliterating the Scourge and its creations.

entries.subclassFeature: Tenets of the Eldritch Hunt|Paladin|XPHB|Eldritch Hunt|SGEHPP|3|SGEHPP
Oath of the Eldritch Hunt Spells|Paladin|XPHB|Eldritch Hunt|SGEHPP|3|SGEHPP

entries.caption: Oath of the Eldritch Hunt Spells
rows: {@spell Evard's Black Tentacles|XPHB}, {@spell Maiden of Bones|SGEHPP}

name: Oath of the Guardian

entries: The first step to killing an eldritch horror: don't die.

These Paladins serve as protectors of the common folk and guards against rampaging monsters. Those who embrace this oath range from itinerant Paladins who single-handedly defend towns on the borderlands to elite groups of knights tasked with protecting the cardinals of a religious order.

entries.name: Tenets of the Guardian
entries: Like any Paladin oath, the ethos embraced by specific Paladins or the order they belong to shapes their beliefs. Listed below are sample tenets for the various alignments. Create your specific tenets by picking up to four ideals that capture your views.
{@b Tenets of Chaos}

items.name: Affinity
entries: You protect and help those you feel meet your personal standards.

items.name: Beauty
entries: Violence is nihilistic; protect the beautiful and precious instead.

items.name: Freedom
entries: Tyrants use violence to oppress. You deny that power.
{@b Tenets of Evil}

items.name: Dominance
entries: Let others believe you protect them so you can rule them.

items.name: Opportunism
entries: Protect others while it profits you. Strike when they weaken.

items.name: Profit
entries: Guard the wealthy as long as they pay. Join the mob when they fall.
{@b Tenets of Good}

items.name: Courage
entries: Stand firm in the face of danger.

items.name: Sacrifice
entries: Suffer for others so they may flourish.

items.name: Service
entries: Use your strength to serve those who need help most.
{@b Tenets of Law}

items.name: Fidelity
entries: Keep your oath above all.

items.name: Protection
entries: Guard civilization to preserve order.

items.name: Service
entries: Follow your code to protect others, even in complex duties.

name: Oath of the Guardian Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of the Guardian Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Oath of the Guardian Spells
rows: {@spell Beacon of Hope|XPHB}, {@spell Protection from Energy|XPHB}

name: Oath of the Harvest
entries: The Oath of the Harvest attracts paladins who wish to nourish and heal the world. Often found on aid missions to war-torn lands, such paladins resort to harm only as a means of preventing further suffering. Paladins who swear this oath are more likely than not to heal, feed, and nuture a wounded foe, provided the defeated creature gives its word of honour that it will cease its nefarious activities. They are no fools, however. Typically versed in religion and medicine, these paladins are unlikely to believe the word of creatures inherently inclined to lie, or those that have previously broken their word.

name: Oath of the Hearth
entries: {@i Protect Your Friends with Your Warmth and Incinerate Those Who Would Harm Them}

The Oath of the Hearth originates from the city of the same name, whose tragic downfall has been all but lost to history over centuries. These Paladins swore an oath to protect this tropical, sunlit city in the name of their celestial guardians. Until the end, they fulfilled their oaths. You may swear this oath because you have an age-old connection to the city through your bloodline, or you may have established a connection to the city's principles through stories or interaction with a related celestial being. Regardless of your reasons for taking it, those who swear this oath adorn their armor with symbols of community, fire, and the sun to reflect their commitment to the city and the lives that were led there.
These Paladins share the following tenets:

items: Light the way to progress and salvation.
Offer guidance and respite to those that need it.
Turn those that would douse the peoples' flames to ash.

name: Oath of the Hearth Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of the Hearth Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

name: Oath of the Open Sea
entries: The Oath of the Open Sea calls to seafaring warriors, swashbuckling sailors, and traveling guardians who seek the thrill of a limitless horizon. Driven to search for adventure and mystery across and beneath every endless oceanic expanse, paladins who swear this oath stand against those who would deny liberty to like-minded travelers, rooting out tyranny and corruption wherever it is found.

Such guardians believe in the natural beauty of the sea, often making offerings and prayers to entities or deities such as the {@deity The Wildmother|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Wildmother} or the {@deity The Stormlord|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Stormlord} who influence safe passage. At the same time, they answer the call to hunt the monstrous creatures that too often bloody the waters with wanton violence and ill intent, and which terrorize the folk of the sea and shore.

entries.subclassFeature: Tenets of the Open Sea|Paladin|PHB|Open Sea|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3

name: Oath of the River

entries.name: Religious Archetypes
entries: In Obojima, there are no deities of any sort, which means characters like clerics and paladins must instead draw their power from some other sources. Alternatively, these heroic characters draw their strength from their devotion to ideals and the natural magic that comes from a person who dedicates their life to their beliefs.

Those who commit themselves to the Oath of the River have found guidance in the shifting waters and the great creatures that live within them. These diverse individuals model their lives and the tenets they follow after the tranquil waters of a blue pool and the rushing rapids that spill over a great waterfall, always striving to flow around obstacles if possible, but ready to crash through them when left with no other option. As the river flows and bends, it seeks the path of least resistance in its travels to the ocean. Like the river, paladins who have sworn this oath remain adaptable but steadfast in their own course.

name: Oath of the Spelldrinker
entries: The Oath of the Spelldrinker is devoted to ridding the world of renegade mages, such as liches or the occult, in order to protect the helpless from the forces of evil magic. The paladins who swear this oath believe in maintaining the balance of power between the ordinary and the extraordinary, including themselves. These paladins are resourceful and quick to remember their own mortality and privilege, often choosing to pursue mundane solutions before magical ones. Despite their caution, these wardens of balance are exemplary arcanists who can feel the weave of magic in the world as keenly as some of the finest sorcerers.

name: Oath of Valhalla
entries: {@i Demonstrate Bravery and Honor the Dead}

Paladins who take the Oath of Valhalla ensure they preserve the spirits of those who have died honorably in battle, even their foes. Of course, these Paladins also strive to prove themselves deserving of entry into Valhalla through their own deeds and words. The thunderous revelry of the heroic dead echoing from the gods' mead hall in Asgard fills these paladins, imbuing them with the might of deceased champions.

These Paladins look askance at those who restore heroes to life, but they assume such heroes have agreed to return from Valhalla to continue to fight as mortals. However, they offer no quarter to blasphemers who animate corpses into a mockery of life.

entries.name: Tenets of Valhalla
entries: These Paladins share the following tenets.

items: Protect the worthy dead.
Inspire courage in battle.
Bring justice to those who make a mockery of the dead.

name: Oath of Valhalla Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Valhalla Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Oath of Valhalla Spells
rows: {@spell Beacon of Hope|XPHB}, {@spell Glyph of Warding|XPHB} (Thunder)
{@spell Aura of Purity|XPHB}, {@spell Guardian of Faith|XPHB}

name: Oath of Zeal
entries: {@i Eliminate Threats to Ideological Purity}

The Oath of Zeal is taken by paladins consumed by hatred for a specific group or ideology. Zealots, as these Paladins are sometimes called, pursue an inquisition against their enemies at all costs. They abandon compassion and honor as impediments to the more important work of ridding the world of those they deem dangerous or heretical.
These Paladins share the following tenets:

items: Reveal heresy and destroy those who practice it.
Show unwavering conviction and unflinching resolve.
Perform any sacrifice necessary to stop wickedness.

name: Oath of Zeal
entries: The Oath of Zeal is taken by paladins consumed by hatred for a specific group or ideology. Zealots, as these paladins are sometimes called, pursue an inquisition against their enemies at all costs. They abandon compassion and honor as impediments to the more important work of ridding the world of those they deem dangerous or heretical.
