If the spell requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}, the creature that consumes the potion Concentrates on it.
Unconsumed potions last until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} or until you use this feature again.

name: Powered by Pathos
entries: Your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is empowered by the overwhelming emotions of the unquiet dead. Your Final Night Catharsis feature grants an additional effect based on the chosen emotion.

entries.name: Hate
entries: While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, your attacks with weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}.

entries.name: Jealousy
entries: Whenever a creature you can see starts its turn within 30 feet of you while your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to summon spectral assailants to Grapple the creature. The creature makes a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failure, the creature has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition until the end of its turn. On a successful save, the creature is not {@condition Grappled|XPHB}; however, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot for that creature until the end of its turn.

entries.name: Terror
entries: Whenever a creature you can see starts its turn within 30 feet of you while your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make that creature terrified until the start of its next turn. A terrified creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved and {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

name: Predatory Instinct
entries: Starting at 15th level, you have advantage on initiative rolls, and when you roll initiative and have no uses of Launch remaining, you regain one use.

name: Primal Companion
entries: You magically summon a primal spirit that adopts the form of a beast and accompanies you on your adventures. Choose its stat block: {@creature Primal Guardian|GrimHollowPG24} or {@creature Primal Striker|GrimHollowPG24}. In addition, choose an environment that will modify the creature's stat block: Land, Sea, or Sky. You also determine the kind of animal it is, choosing a kind appropriate for the stat block. Whatever companion you choose, it bears eldritch markings indicating its otherworldly origin.
The companion is {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you and your allies and obeys your commands. It vanishes if you die.

entries.name: The Beast in Combat
entries: In combat, the companion acts during your turn. It can move and use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} on its own, but the only action it takes is the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action unless you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can also sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action to command the beast to take the Beast's Strike action. If you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, the companion acts on its own and isn't limited to the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Restoring or Replacing the Beast
entries: If the companion has died within the last hour, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to touch it and expend a use of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1}. The companion returns to life immediately with all its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} restored.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can summon a different primal companion, which appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. You choose its stat block and appearance. If you already have a beast from this feature, the old one vanishes when the new one appears.

name: Primal Symbiote
entries: Vines and roots grow across your body, forming a symbiotic network. As it draws physical and magical nourishment from you, the symbiote grants you a number of benefits.

entries.name: Fortifying Presence
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

entries.name: Symbiotic Transformation
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of Wild Shape to allow your symbiote to transform you into a plant-like brute as fibrous plates and vines cover your skin. For 1 minute, you gain a +2 bonus to AC, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to 2 plus half your Druid level (round down) at the start of each of your turns, and you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks.

name: Primordial Archer
entries: {@i Channel the Wrath of the Wilds}

In the areas of Etharis where nature still holds sway, many cling to the ancient customs of woodland hunters and witches. Marking themselves with wild plants and bone needles, theirs is a tradition of cunning, cruelty, and reprisal against all trespassers. Unlike the Druids, these wood witches twist natural magic into hexes, imbuing their weapons with nature's fury.

name: Primordial Archer Spells
entries: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Primordial Archer Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

name: Primordial Magic
entries: Taking damage can't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB} on any Ranger spells you cast.

In addition, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to change the damage type you chose for the Weave the Elements feature to a different damage type in the list. When you do, you can choose a creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself. That creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 6d6} damage of the either damage type (your choice).
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Primordial Shield
entries: Your companion gains resistance to the element with which it is infused When your companion takes damage of that type, you can use your reaction to bolster its defences, granting it immunity to that damage type, including against the triggering damage, until the start of your next turn Once you use this reaction, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Prophecy of Doom
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you expend a use of your Channel Divinity to choose a point within 120 feet of you that you can see and roll on the Eldritch Effects table. Each creature in a 15-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer the rolled effect for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Protean Rewards
entries: Your body can perform greater wonders.

entries.name: Flesh of Marble
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 2 Blood Points to double your {@subclassFeature Gifts of Survival|Kindred|BoundByBlood|Gangrel|BoundByBlood|9} feature's Damage Reduction for 1 minute.

entries.name: Mistform
entries: You can expend 2 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Gaseous Form|XPHB} spell on yourself. When you cast the spell in this way, you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@condition Concentration|XPHB}.

name: Protect the Monarch
entries: Your connection to the arthropods you host becomes deeper; they regard you as a worker bee would its queen, and they gladly sacrifice themselves to protect you. As a reaction when you take damage from a source you can see, you can command your insect symbiotes to swarm in front of you, deflecting some of the incoming energy. You gain a number of temporary hit points equal to your druid level, which take as much of the triggering damage as possible.

You lose any remaining temporary hit points at the end of the current turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once) regaining all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.
Additionally, the poison damage of {@subclassFeature Symbiotic Biosphere|Druid||Hive|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting|2} increases to 1d6.

name: Protective Taunt
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with a melee attack using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can taunt it. Until the start of your next turn or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against targets other than you. A creature can only be affected by one Taunt at a time.

name: Psionic Mastery
entries: After much training, you have mastered the psionic disciplines necessary to defend mortals from planar threats. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can spend 5 Focus Points to cast {@spell Dispel Evil and Good|XPHB}, {@spell Hold Monster|XPHB}, {@spell Telekinesis|XPHB}, or {@spell Wall of Force|XPHB}. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells, and you can cast them without Material components.

name: Psionic Prowess
entries: Your psychic powers have manifested in the ability to cast certain spells. You know the {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB} cantrip. You can cast it without Verbal or Somatic components, and you can make the spectral hand {@condition Invisible|XPHB}.

In addition, you can cast certain spells by expending Focus Points. You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and expend 1 Focus Point to cast {@spell Detect Evil and Good|XPHB} or {@spell Protection from Evil and Good|XPHB}. You can also take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and expend 2 Focus Points to cast {@spell Hold Person|XPHB}, {@spell Levitate|XPHB}, or {@spell Shatter|XPHB}. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells, and you can cast them without Material components.

name: Psychic Crush
entries: Each time you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, it gains a Pressure Point. A creature loses all Pressure Points if you cause a different creature to gain a Pressure Point or after 1 minute, whichever comes first. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 1 Focus Point to telekinetically crush a creature with 1 or more of your Pressure Points. The creature loses all Pressure Points and must make a Strength saving throw against your Focus Point save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 1d8} Force damage per Pressure Point, and it has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only.

name: Psychic Feedback
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself succeeds on a Wisdom saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to seek a mental weakness. The triggering creature must reroll the saving throw and use the lower roll.

name: Psychic Force
entries: You learn to buffet your foes with mental power. When you cast a Cleric spell that deals Radiant damage, you can choose to have it inflict Psychic damage instead. When you cast a spell that deals Psychic damage, you can add your Charisma modifier to that spell's damage against one of the spell's targets.

name: Puissant Might
entries: Your raw, supernatural strength is legendary.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Your Strength score increases by 4, to a maximum of 30.

entries.name: Pulverize
entries: When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, your Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} deals two extra dice of its damage.

name: Punishment
entries: When a creature damages you with an attack, you can use your reaction to force the attacker to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the attacker takes necrotic damage equal to the damage they dealt you with the triggering attack. On a successful save, the attacker takes half as much damage.

name: Pure Darkness
entries: When you cast any spell from your Innate Darkness feature that creates an area of {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} and {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} can't see within the area of the spell.

name: Purification Domain
entries: {@i Purge Sickness with Suffering}

The Purification Domain believes sickness, mutation, and other forms of bodily corruption are signs of a corresponding spiritual malady. Virtue can't exist alongside impurity. The wickedness of humanity and other mortal, sentient creatures is a contagion that manifests plagues such as the Weeping Pox. When there's a risk of such corruption spreading, there's only one surefire way to contain the rot and atone for the sins that led to this point: Burn it out.

name: Purification Domain Spells
entries: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Purification Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Purification Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Detect Poison and Disease|XPHB}, {@spell Flame Blade|XPHB}
{@spell Aura of Purity|XPHB}, {@spell Wall of Fire|XPHB}

name: Pursuer of Foes
entries: Starting at 7th level, creatures provoke {@action opportunity attack||opportunity attacks} from you even if they take the {@action Disengage} action. In addition, when you hit a creature with an {@action opportunity attack}, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn.

name: Quick Brew
entries: Beginning at 6th level, you've learned how to better control the effects your belly concoction produces.

Choose a {@filter common potion|items|source=ObojimaTallGrass|type=potion|rarity=common} that you would normally consume. You can activate the effects of the chosen potion as a bonus action. Once you activate it, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. If the potion's effects require a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier.
Each time you gain a level in this class, you can swap your chosen potion with a different one.

An alternate way of using this feature is to only allow the player to choose from a list of potion recipes that they're aware of. If the belly brewer has yet to learn any potion recipes, then the GM should provide a list of 10 options to choose from.

name: Quid Pro Quo
entries: You can whisper to the legions of Hell, ensnaring enemies and calling allies. As an action, you can attempt to banish a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the target is banished to the wastes of Hell for 1 minute, after which they return to the unoccupied space nearest to the one they left. A target banished in this way can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect early on a success. A creature who succeeds on a saving throw against this effect becomes immune to your Quid Pro Quo for 24 hours.

Additionally, when a target is banished in this way, a {@creature devil jurist|FleeMortals} (from MCDM's {@book Flee, Mortals!|FleeMortals}) or a {@creature horned devil} (from the core rules) appears in their place. This devil acts as an ally to you and follows your commands until the banished creature is no longer banished, at which time the devil disappears.
Once you successfully banish a creature in this way, you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

name: Quiet-Footed
entries: Starting at 7th level, you have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) and Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

name: Quintessence
entries: You have learned the fundamental process of dissolution. You know the {@spell Dissolution|CrookedMoon24} cantrip. A creature or object you reduce to 0 hit points with the cantrip is destroyed. If the target was Small or larger, it dissolves into a measure (about an ounce) of crystalline powder called Quintessence. You can have a maximum amount of Quintessence equal to twice your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 2 measures) at one time. If you create more, the oldest measure vanishes. You can use Quintessence you are touching in the following ways.

entries.name: Material Component
entries: When you cast a spell, you can expend Quintessence to serve as the spell's material components up to a value of 100 gp per Quintessence expended.

entries.name: Reagent
entries: When you scribe a spell into your spellbook, or when you use {@item alchemist's supplies|PHB} to craft a magic item, you can expend Quintessence to serve as 50 gp worth of material for the task per Quintessence expended.

entries.name: Vitriolic Enhancement
entries: When you cast a spell that deals damage, you can expend 1 Quintessence as an additional material component to change one damage type the spell deals to force.

name: Quintessence
entries: You have learned the fundamental process of dissolution. You know the {@spell Dissolution|CrookedMoon24} cantrip. A creature or object you reduce to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} with the cantrip is destroyed. If the target was Small or larger, it dissolves into a measure (1 ounce) of crystalline powder called Quintessence. You can have a maximum amount of Quintessence equal to twice your Intelligence modifier  at one time (mimium of 2 measures). If you create more, the oldest measure vanishes. You can use Quintessence you are touching in the following ways.

entries.name: Material Component
entries: When you cast a spell, you can expend Quintessence to serve as the spell's Material components up to a value of 100 GP per Quintessence expended.

entries.name: Reagent
entries: When you scribe a spell into your spellbook, or when you use {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} to craft a magic item, you can expend Quintessence to serve as 50 GP worth of material for the task per Quintessence expended.

entries.name: Vitriolic Enhancement
entries: When you cast a spell that deals damage, you can expend 1 Quintessence as an additional Material component to change one damage type the spell deals to Force.

name: Rage of the Dead
entries: Your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} taps into the endless fury of the unquiet dead. While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you take on aspects of restless spirits and you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Shadow Form
entries: You ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. In addition, you can move through the space of any creature, but you can't end your move in an occupied space.

entries.name: Shadowy Sidestep
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet, and {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} against you.

entries.name: Spectral Sight
entries: You see creatures and objects within 120 feet that have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition as if they were visible, and you can see into the Ethereal Plane.

name: Rage of the Giants
entries: Your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB} taps into the primal power of giants. Whenever you activate your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB}, if you are smaller than Large, you can choose to become Large. Your equipment grows to match your new size. If there is not enough room for you to become Large, you do not grow.

While you are Large, your carrying capacity doubles, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and your attacks with weapons or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal one additional die of damage (a {@item Greatsword|XPHB} attack deals {@damage 3d6} damage, a {@item Greataxe|XPHB} deals {@damage 2d12}, and so on).

name: Rage of the Titans
entries: Whenever you activate your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB}, if you are smaller than Huge, you can choose to become Huge. Your equipment grows to match your new size. If there is not enough room for you to become Huge, you become Large. If there is not enough room for you to become Large, you do not grow.

While you are Huge, your carrying capacity triples, your reach increases by 5 feet, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and your attacks with weapons or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal two additional dice of damage (a {@item Greatsword|XPHB} attack deals {@damage 4d6} damage, a {@item Greataxe|XPHB} deals {@damage 3d12}, and so on).

name: Rapid Consumption
entries: When you use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to drink a compound, you can drink a second compound.

name: Rapid Tinkerer
entries: You have become capable of crafting trapper tools at a much faster rate. You can spend 1 minute to make a Trapper Gadget without spending GP or components.
You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Ravaged But Resolute
entries: When you use your {@classFeature Bloodied But Unbowed|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2}, you can fully replenish your {@subclassFeature Lay On Hands|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|Street Saint|Pugilist2024|3} healing pool.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Raven's Spirit
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Animal Handling} skill. If you are already proficient in it, you gain proficiency in your choice of one the following skills instead: {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Survival}.
In addition, you can cast {@spell speak with animals} as a ritual.

name: Reach for the Skies
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against a creature, you call for the target to surrender instead of lodging a projectile in it. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Maneuver save DC or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} and {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} conditions for 1 minute. These conditions end early if the creature takes any damage, if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or if you die. The creature can repeat the Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the conditions on itself on a success.

name: Reactive Catalyst
entries: Your implants are now sensitive to your response to danger and flood you with stimulating chemicals. When you take damage, or when you are {@condition blinded}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition poisoned}, or {@condition stunned}, you can use your reaction to enter your rage before the damage or conditions are applied. When you enter your rage, you end any of those conditions on yourself, including any triggering conditions.
Additionally, while your rage is active, you have advantage on Constitution saving throws.

name: Reactive Catalyst
entries: Your implants are now sensitive to your response to danger and flood you with stimulating chemicals. When you take damage, or when you gain the {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, or {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to enter your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} before the damage or conditions are applied. When you enter your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1}, you end any of those conditions on yourself, including any triggering conditions.
Additionally, while your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} is active, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws.

name: Reactive Mutations
entries: Immediately after you take damage, you can use your reaction to spend 1 sorcery point and gain resistance to that damage type for 10 minutes or until you use this feature again If you take multiple types of damage simultaneously, you choose one of the damage types to gain resistance to.
Looking for inspiration to describe how a skinshifter's reactive mutations might physically manifest?
Try adapting the following examples!

items.name: Bludgeoning
items.entry: Spongy growths bloom, cushioning the blows of impact weapons.

items.name: Piercing
items.entry: Layer upon layer of pointy membranes overlap one another, dispersing the penetrating potential of piercing weapons.

items.name: Slashing
items.entry: A hard coating of angled crystal deflects blades.

items.name: Acid
items.entry: Secreted alkaline liquid neutralises acid near the skin.

items.name: Cold & Fire
items.entry: An insulating gel prevents the transfer of heat.

items.name: Force
items.entry: Pockets of antimagic dissipate incoming raw, magical energy.

items.name: Lightning
items.entry: Channels of conductive metals in the skin ground the flow of electricity.

items.name: Necrotic
items.entry: Pus-filled sacs of immunity-enhancing symbionts fortify the skinshifter against decay.

items.name: Radiant
items.entry: The skinshifter takes on a brilliant sheen, reflecting radiation of all descriptions.

items.name: Thunder
items.entry: A membrane expands out from the skinshifter's skin. A low-pressure void between the two membranes inhibits the propagation of sound waves.

items.name: Poison
items.entry: Vesicles rapidly excrete toxins before they can do significant harm.

items.name: Psychic
items.entry: A rush of bright purple hormones causes the skinshifter's psyche to relax, shedding the mental harm that might have been caused.

name: Readied Magic
entries: You have learned to hold back your magical power, prepared to unleash it when the time is just right. If you use an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to Ready a spell, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws and ability checks until the start of your next turn. Additionally, if the trigger for your readied spell occurs, you can cast the readied spell without using your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

If the trigger does not resolve, if you choose not to act on the trigger, or if you lose {@status Concentration|XPHB} on the spell, you gain a number of Sorcery Points equal to the spell's level at the start of your next turn. You still expend the spell slot as normal.

name: Ready for Action
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10. When you roll 18-20 on an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll, you can take one additional action, except the {@action Magic|XPHB} action, on your first turn.

name: Reality Tear
entries: Choose a spell of 3rd level or lower from the warlock spell list. You add the spell to your spellbook if it's not there already, and it is a wizard spell for you. When you cast the spell, you can risk Intrusion to remove the need to {@status Concentration|PHB|Concentrate} on it, and the spell ends after 1 minute or its normal duration, whichever is shorter. Additionally, you can cause an automatic Intrusion (and increase the die's size one step, up to its starting size) to cast the spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

name: Reality Tear
entries: Choose a spell of level 3 or lower from the Warlock spell list. You always have the spell prepared. You can change your chosen spell when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When you cast the spell, you can risk Intrusion to remove the need to {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrate} on it, and the spell ends after 1 minute or its normal duration, whichever is shorter. Additionally, you can cause an automatic Intrusion (and increase the die's size one step, up to its starting size) to cast the spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Rebuke Invoker
entries: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} in response to a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself using a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast a spell, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 1d8} Force damage, plus another {@dice 1d8} per level of the spell slot the creature expended. Cantrips are considered level 1 spells for this ability. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage instead.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once). You regain all expended uses of this feature when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Rebuke Invoker
entries: Starting at 6th level, as a reaction when a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes force damage equal to {@dice 1d8} per level of spell slot expended casting the spell + your Wisdom modifier. Cantrips are considered first-level spells for this ability. On a successful save the creature takes half as much damage instead.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once). You regain all uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Reclamation
entries: Also at 2nd level, you learn the art of siphoning off harmful elemental energy. You can use this to lessen elemental damage being done to your allies by shouldering some of it yourself. When a creature within 30 feet of you takes cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to grant that creature resistance against the damage dealt. You take damage equal to the amount taken by the target creature.

Additionally, you may spend an action to reduce the area of natural or magical effects which deal persistent cold, fire, or lightning damage within 30 feet of you. You may remove up to a 20-foot cube from the area of such effects per use of this feature. However, for each 5-foot space of energy damage removed in this way, you take {@dice 1d4} points of damage of the same type the effect would deal. If the effect is caused by a spell, you instead take {@dice 1d4} points of damage per the spell's level for each 5-foot space removed and, if there are no damage-dealing spaces remaining, the spell is dispelled.

name: Red Renewal
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you regain expended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} and Sangromancy Dice equal to half your Wizard level.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Redoubled Efforts
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} while you are {@condition Bloodied|XPHB}, you can roll one additional damage die when determining the extra damage dealt by the attack.

name: Reflexive Adaptation
entries: When you use Self-Restoration, the following conditions are added to the list of conditions you can remove: {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, and {@condition Grappled|XPHB}.

In addition, when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} you can remove 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} from yourself and when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} you can remove all levels of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} from yourself.

name: Refraction Shield
entries: At 6th level, you can manipulate the light around you for protection. As a bonus action, you can spend 3 sorcery points to magically create a shield of light. While the shield is in place, whenever a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, the shield flashes with searing energy, and the attacker takes {@dice 2d8} radiant damage if you are light-shifted or {@dice 2d8} necrotic damage if you are dark-shifted. The shield disappears if you fall {@condition unconscious} or after 10 minutes.

name: Relentless Pursuit
entries: If your bounty or a creature currently marked by your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} ends its turn more than 5 feet away from you and you can see it, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move your speed towards it. This movement does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

name: Relentless Pursuit
entries: When you hit your marked target with a Melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} immediately after you teleport with the Hunt the Prey feature, you can cast {@classFeature Divine Smite|Paladin|XPHB|2|XPHB} without using a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You expend a spell slot as normal, and you can cast this spell in this way only once per turn.

name: Relive the Past
entries: Your Shade of Regret now lasts for 10 minutes. After using Flurry of Blows, your Shade can make one additional {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} as per Shade Strike. You can also use the Stunning Strike feature through the Shade Strike.

name: Rematerialize
entries: When you see a Large or smaller nonmagical object or structure be destroyed within 60 feet of you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cause its debris to magically vanish. Once within the next 8 hours, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to recreate the item, causing it to reappear intact in an unoccupied space you choose within 60 feet of you.

If the item is recreated in the air, it immediately falls. Any creature below it must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet the item fell before reaching it. The amount of damage dealt is based on the item's size: Small or smaller ({@dice 1d6}), Medium ({@dice 2d6}), or Large ({@dice 3d6}). On a successful save, a creature takes half as much Bludgeoning damage. Unless the object is at least one size smaller than a creature it falls on, that creature is pushed to the nearest unoccupied space.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Reposition
entries: Whenever a creature misses you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to end the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition on yourself and move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

name: Resolute Stance
entries: Also at 6th level, you can temporarily refocus your combat ability to make yourself a bulwark of defense. At the start of your turn (no action required), you can assume a defensive stance that lasts until the start of your next turn. While in this stance, you can't be {@condition grappled}, attack rolls against you have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage}, and your weapon attacks are made with {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage}.

name: Resourceful
entries: Your mastery over the arts is lauded by friends and feared by foes. Whenever you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you regain spent Rune Points until you have two if you have fewer than that. In addition, whenever you deal Sneak Attack damage and add one of your Cunning Strike effects, you can spend 1 or more Rune Points to reduce the number of Sneak Attack damage dice you must forgo by one for each Rune Point spent.

name: Revealing Light
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can use an action to cause your lantern to illuminate with a vibrant maroon light, which sheds {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} in a 10-foot radius and {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} for an additional 10 feet. {@condition Invisible} creatures and objects are visible as long as they are in the lantern's {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light}. The lantern sheds light in this manner for 1 hour or until you snuff it out early as a bonus action.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Ricochet [Maneuver]
entries: When you miss with a ranged attack using a weapon, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend one {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die} to reroll the attack and add the {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die} to the roll. You must use the new roll.

name: Ride the Rails
entries: You can whistle as an action to summon a spectral locomotive into existence. It hurtles forward in a 120-foot-long, 10-foot-wide line from you, and it passes through objects and creatures.

You and up to six willing creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you can hitch a ride on the train. You teleport to an unoccupied space of your choice in the line, and any creatures who accompanied you appear in the closest unoccupied spaces to you.

Each other creature in the line must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be {@condition deafened} until the start of your next turn, be pushed up to 10 feet straight away from the line's point of origin, and take an amount of psychic damage equal to three rolls of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|PHB|1} die.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest unless you expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Ride the Rails
entries: You can whistle as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to summon a spectral locomotive into existence. It hurtles forward in a 120-foot-long, 10-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} from you, and it passes through objects and creatures.

You and up to six willing creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you can hitch a ride on the train. You teleport to an unoccupied space of your choice in the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}, and any creatures who accompanied you appear in the closest unoccupied spaces to you.

Each other creature in the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn, be pushed up to 10 feet straight away from the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}'s point of origin, and takes an amount of Psychic damage equal to three rolls of your {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|XPHB|1} die.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend a spell slot of level 3+ (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Ride Them Down
entries: You don't need {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll to Sneak Attack if you or a controlled mount you ride moves at least 20 feet, and you don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll.

name: Righteous Armament
entries: Your faith gives you the power to rebel against fate itself. You learn the following features that use your Divine Points.

items.name: Chains of Judgement
items.entry: When you hit a creature with your sanctified blade, you can expend 1 Divine Point to create holy chains around the creature. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take Radiant damage equal to your Wisdom modifier and have the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

items.name: Divine Retaliation
items.entry: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when a creature damages you with a melee attack while you are wielding your sanctified blade, you can expend 1 Divine Point to make a melee attack with your blade against the creature. You gain a bonus to the damage roll equal to your Wisdom modifier.

items.name: Erupting Blades
items.entry: When you hit a creature with an attack that could apply your Sneak Attack damage, you can forgo damaging the creature with your Sneak Attack and expend 2 Divine Points to cause radiant blades to fall on the battlefield. The target and each creature in a 45-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} originating from the target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes Radiant damage equal to your Sneak Attack damage. On a successful save, a target takes half damage.

name: Righteous Strike
entries: At 6th level, when you hit a target with an unarmed strike, you can spend 1 ki point to cause the attack to deal either radiant (if you are good-aligned or neutral-aligned) or necrotic (if you are evil-aligned) damage equal to your proficiency bonus. You can use this feature only once on each of your turns.

name: Risk Taker
entries: You can use your {@optfeature Maverick Spirit|ValdaGunslinger} and {@optfeature Skin of Your Teeth|ValdaGunslinger} maneuvers without expending a {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die}. When you do so, roll a {@dice d6} instead of a {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die}.

name: Risky Business
entries: Once per turn when you make an attack roll against an enemy and the roll doesn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, you can choose to make the roll with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. When you do, you regain one expended {@classFeature Risk|Gunslinger|ValdaGunslinger|2|ValdaGunslinger|Risk Die}.

name: Rite of the Blood Moon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape to adopt the violent savagery of the Blood Moon for 10 minutes. During this time, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Red Resilience
entries: You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to three times your Druid level.

items.name: Speed Increased
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet, and you can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Violent Strikes
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage to the target.

name: Rite of the Hunt
entries: At 17th level, you can compel a creature to chase or avoid you. As a bonus action while you can see the target of your Mark Prey feature and it is within 120 feet of you, you can force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw against your cleric spell save DC. On a failure, you choose whether the creature is afflicted by Chase or Avoid for the next minute. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. These effects are suppressed while you can't see the creature, and the effects end early if the creature is no longer affected by your Mark Prey feature. A creature that succeeds on a saving throw against this ability is immune to its effects for the next 24 hours.

items.name: Chase
items.entry: The creature is drawn to you. For the duration, it has disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures other than you, and must make a Wisdom saving throw the first time it attempts to move to a space that is more than 30 feet away from you on its turn. On a failed save, it can't move more than 30 feet away from you that turn. On a success, this effect doesn't restrict the target's movement for that turn.

items.name: Avoid
items.entry: The creature is repelled by you. For the duration, it has disadvantage on attack rolls against you, and must make a Wisdom saving throw the first time it attempts to move to a space within 30 feet of you on its turn. On a failed save, it can't willingly move closer to you that turn. On a success, this effect doesn't restrict the target's movement for that turn.

name: Ritual Reskin
entries: Over the course of 10 minutes, you can perform a surgical ritual on creatures that you can see within 60 feet of you (including yourself), up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). The creatures gain one of the following adaptations for the next hour. You choose one adaptation to affect all creatures:

items.name: Bull's Buns
items.entry: The target has advantage on Strength checks, and counts as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift.

items.name: Cactus Skin
items.entry: The target is covered in razor-sharp spikes. At the end of each of the target's turns, each creature grappling it must make a Constitution saving throw against your bard spell save DC. On a failure, a creature takes piercing damage equal to your Bardic Inspiration die and releases the target from its grapple. On a success, a creature takes half as much damage and doesn't have to release the target.

items.name: Cat's Paws
items.entry: The target has advantage on Dexterity checks. It also doesn't take damage from falling 20 feet or less if it isn't {@condition incapacitated}.

items.name: Fish Form
items.entry: The target can breathe underwater and gains a swimming speed equal to its walking speed.

items.name: Owl's Sight
items.entry: The target has advantage on Wisdom checks and initiative rolls.

items.name: Rhino's Hide
items.entry: The target has advantage on Constitution checks and gains temporary hit points equal to one roll of your Bardic Inspiration die plus you Charisma modifier (minimum 1), which are lost when the effect ends.

entries: After you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher to use this feature again.

name: Roaring Crash
entries: You are ready to leap into battle at a moment's notice, crashing down on your foes like thunder from the heavens. As part of entering your Rage, you can leap into the air and crash down on a space on the ground you can see within 30 feet of yourself that isn't occupied by a Huge or larger creature. Each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the destination space must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking twice your Vessel Damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

If a creature is in the destination space, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw and is pushed 5 feet out of the space to an unoccupied space of their choice. If no unoccupied space is available within that range, the creature instead has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

When you reach Barbarian level 10, the distance you can leap increases to 60 feet, and you can land in spaces occupied by Huge creatures. When you reach Barbarian level 14, the distance increases to 90 feet, and you can land in spaces occupied by any creature.

name: Rocborne
entries: The Rocborne are nomads of the sky who travel the world on the backs of ancestral rocs. These travelers understand that the air and wind aren't just one force but the collective effort of untold numbers of spirits that are carried along by it. By listening to the wind the same way a medium beckons to the dead, a Rocborne can learn more about the weather, their path forward, and even themselves. Many Rocborne grow up and live in this culture for their entire lives, but some have been known to begin their own journeys. Alternatively, your path may have been crossed by a powerful windborne spirit later on in life, allowing you to suddenly feel and heed the guiding wind inside you.

By calling on the spirits of the wind to aid them, rangers of this archetype can exert a degree of control over both wind and weather. These skills were passed down from the rocs to the first Rocborne and continue to live on through the dedicated instruction of Rocborne elders, both living and dead. You may be taught these skills or have them passed on to you through the guidance of Rocborne spirits in whispers, dreams, or in moments of deep meditation.

name: Rocborne Magic
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Rocborne Spells table. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.

name: Rouse Emotions
entries: You can extend your own passionate feelings into others, infecting them with your fervor. You can expend 3 Blood Points to cast one of the following spells.

entries.name: Enthrall
entries: You cast the {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} spell as if with a level 6 spell slot, and the creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw.

entries.name: Incite
entries: You cast the {@spell Confusion|XPHB} spell. A creature that fails its saving throw automatically rolls 7-8 to determine its behavior for each turn.

entries.name: Terrorize
entries: You cast the {@spell Fear|XPHB} spell. When you cast the spell in this way, you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@condition Concentration|XPHB} and creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw.

name: Rubedo
entries: The culmination of your great work, you can now distill your perfected knowledge of existence into a physical form. When you finish a short or long rest, you can expend 10 {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|PHB|Philosophy|CrookedMoon14|2|CrookedMoon14} to create a Philosophy's stone—a translucent red crystal. The stone is a Tiny magical object with an AC of 18, 20 hit points, and immunity to all damage except force. If you create a second Philosophy's stone, the first one vanishes. While you carry the stone, it grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Amplification
entries: When you cast a spell, you can expend up to 2 {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|PHB|Philosophy|CrookedMoon14|2|CrookedMoon14} as an additional material component to increase your spell save DC for that spell by the same amount.

entries.name: Equivalent Exchange
entries: When you fail a saving throw, you can use your reaction to expend 5 {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|PHB|Philosophy|CrookedMoon14|2|CrookedMoon14} to succeed on the save instead.

entries.name: Longevity
entries: You stop aging and don't suffer any effects from old age, including dying from it.

entries.name: Sympathy
entries: The stone counts as part of your body for the purpose of the {@spell Scrying} spell and for spells that restore you to life if you die. The stone itself serves as the material component for the spell (if any) and is destroyed when the spell is cast.

name: Rubedo
entries: The culmination of your great work, you can now distill your perfected knowledge of existence into a physical form. When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can expend 10 {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|XPHB|Philosopher|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} to create a philosopher's stone—a translucent red crystal. The stone is a Tiny magical object with AC 19, HP 20, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all damage except Force. If you create a second philosopher's stone, the first one vanishes. While you carry the stone, it grants you the following benefits.

entries.name: Amplification
entries: When you cast a spell, you can expend up to 2 {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|XPHB|Philosopher|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} as an additional Material component to increase your spell save DC for that spell by the same amount.

entries.name: Equivalent Exchange
entries: When you fail a saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend 5 {@subclassFeature Quintessence|Wizard|XPHB|Philosopher|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} to succeed on the save instead.

entries.name: Longevity
entries: You stop aging and don't suffer any effects from old age, including dying from it.

entries.name: Sympathy
entries: The stone counts as part of your body for the purpose of the {@spell Scrying|XPHB} spell and for spells that restore you to life if you die. The stone itself serves as the Material component for the spell (if any) and is destroyed when the spell is cast.

name: Ruin Incarnate
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape to adopt an aspect of entropy and the inevitable end of all things for 10 minutes. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: All Things Pass
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against {@condition Bloodied|XPHB} creatures.

entries.name: Inexorable Onslaught
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

entries.name: Ironskin Armor
entries: Your base AC becomes 17 plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1) if your AC is lower than that.

name: Runechild
entries: The mysterious weave and flow of magic is feared by many folk across Exandria. But while some spellcasters must study the essence and nature of magic in the hope of learning to harness it, sorcerers possess an innate talent to sculpt and wield the errant strands of power that shape the world. For some sorcerers, the body becomes a conduit for this power, which is collected and stored in the form of natural runes—and which sees a sorcerer named as a Runechild.

The talents of a Runechild are rare, and sorcerers with this origin are sought after for study by mages and scholars alike, driven by a prevalent belief that the secrets of their runes can help understand the mysteries of magic. Others sometimes seek to enslave Runechild sorcerers, using their bodies as tortured spell batteries for diabolic pursuits. Runechild sorcerers were subjugated throughout the {@book Age of Arcanum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|Age of Arcanum}, and many of their contemporaries now search for ways to hide their essence—a task that isn't easy given the revealing nature of their gifts.

name: Runes
entries: You have 4 Rune Points, which fuel various magical effects from this subclass. When you hit a creature with a melee attack using a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can spend 1 Rune Point to mark that creature with a magical rune in a flourish of paint and weaponry. These runes remain on a marked creature for up to 1 minute. A rune vanishes early if its magic fades (as described below) or if a creature takes an action to wipe it off. You regain all spent Rune Points when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
When you mark a creature with this feature, you can choose to leave one of the following runes.

entries.name: Cryos
entries: The marked creature can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of your next turn, at which point the rune's magic fades.

entries.name: Hexxus
entries: When the marked creature succeeds on an ability check or attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to activate the rune; the marked creature must be within 60 feet of you and you must be able to see it. When you activate the rune, the creature subtracts {@dice 1d6} from its roll, potentially turning the success into a failure. Once the rune has been activated, its magic fades.

entries.name: Locus
entries: The next attack roll made against the marked creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, and if that attack hits, it deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Acid damage. The rune's magic fades after the next attack roll against the creature hits or misses.

name: Runes of War
entries: You gain the following benefits while wielding your Ghaal'Shaarat.

entries.name: Improved Mighty Blade
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with the weapon, unless it already had this bonus or a better one.

entries.name: Aura of War
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you begin radiating a bolstering aura in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that originates from you. Choose one of the following damage types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. While in the aura, you and your allies each deal an extra {@damage 1d4} damage of the chosen type when hitting with a weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. The aura lasts for 1 minute, until you use this feature again, or until you end it (no action required). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Runetagger
entries: {@i Use Powerful Runes to Weaken Enemies and Escape from Harm}

You concentrate your efforts on perfecting your art, developing special marks to claim and cripple your targets. Rebel leaders, artists, spies, and other members of the political underworld might belong to this archetype. Originally a tactic for subterfuge and assassination for denizens of the Festerwood, those who employ these powerful works of art are famously difficult to pin down. The magical marks left behind become a calling card for any Runetagger, and as their strength and notoriety grow from the deeds that they commit (both good and evil), so too does the renown for their art.

name: Runic Magic
entries: Beginning at 1st level, you learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Runic Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

When you gain a level in this class, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be {@filter an abjuration or transmutation spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list|spells|school=A;T|class=Sorcerer;Warlock;Wizard}.

entries.caption: Runic Spells
rows: {@spell longstrider}, {@spell protection from evil and good}

name: Runic Torrent
entries: Upon reaching 14th level, you can channel runic energy to overpower even the staunchest defenses. When you cast a spell, you can expend 2 charged runes to cause the spell to deal force damage instead of its usual damage types. Additionally, all creatures targeted by the spell or within the spell's area must succeed on a Strength {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} against your spell save DC or be knocked prone or pushed up to 15 feet away from the spell's point of origin (your choice).
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you complete a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}.

name: Saintly Revelations
entries: You experience revelations, showing you how to channel divine energy to embolden your blade. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Cleric spell|spells|level=0|class=cleric|components & miscellaneous=|subschool=osteomancy} list.

In addition, you always have the {@spell Heroism|XPHB}, {@spell Protection From Evil and Good|XPHB}, and {@spell Shield of Faith|XPHB} spells prepared. With this feature, you can cast these spells at will, targeting only yourself, without a spell slot or components. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

Starting at Rogue level 17, when you cast these spells using this feature, they don't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. However, you can only have one spell cast from this feature active at a time; if you cast a second one, the first spell ends.

name: Salty Salute
entries: You have mastered the art of the enraging insult. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can provoke a creature within 60 feet that can see or hear you. That creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take Psychic damage equal to a roll of your Fisticuffs die plus your Constitution modifier and have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on any attack rolls it makes against creatures other than you until the start of your next turn.
The saving throw DC for this and all other features from this subclass equals 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Sanctified Champion
entries: Your intense training bears fruit. You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can perform a ritual on a melee weapon you are proficient with that deals Piercing or Slashing damage, sanctifying it. It becomes your sanctified blade, and you can only have one such blade at a time. The blade has the {@itemProperty Finesse|XPHB} property for you, and attacks made with it against Aberrations, Fiends, and Undead ignore {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to damage.

name: Sand Form
entries: At 18th level, you can become as intangible as sand. You can spend 5 sorcery points as a bonus action to magically transform yourself into a sand-like form. In this form, you have the following benefits:

items: You can't be {@condition grappled}.
You and any equipment you are wearing or carrying can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.
You can move through the space of any creature, regardless of its size, and {@quickref difficult terrain||3} doesn't cost you extra movement.

entries: In addition, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to turn to sand. Until the end of that turn, you have resistance to all damage, including against the triggering attack.
You remain in this form for 1 minute. It ends early if you are {@condition incapacitated}, if you die, or if you dismiss it as a bonus action.

name: Sandstorm
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can cause the magical sandstorm within you to manifest as a nearby twister. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher on your turn, you can use a bonus action to create this storm in a 5-foot cube in a space you can see within 30 feet of you. A Large or smaller creature in the area must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your sorcerer spell save DC. A creature that fails the saving throw is pushed up to 10 feet in a direction of your choice if it's Medium or smaller, or 5 feet if it's Large.

When you reach 6th level in this class, a creature that fails this saving throw also takes either {@dice 1d8} bludgeoning damage or {@dice 1d8} fire damage (your choice). The damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to {@dice 2d8} at 14th level, and {@dice 3d8} at 18th level.

name: Sangromancer
entries: {@i Spill Blood for Power}

You study an uncommon school of magic known as Sangromancy or blood magic. Despite its dark reputation, there's nothing inherently evil about the practice of Sangromancy, though its demands on its practitioners are gruesome. As a Sangromancer, your chosen magic demands more than knowledge: it demands sacrifice. Other Wizards may view you with skepticism or even outright hostility, but none can deny the potency of your art.

name: Sangromancy Savant
entries: {@filter Sangromancy spells|spells|source=grimhollowpg24|subschool=sangromancy} count as Wizard spells for you. Choose two Sangromancy spells, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Sangromancy spell to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

name: Sanguine Burst
entries: Also at 2nd level, you learn how to weave your life force into a spell you cast, boosting its intensity at the cost of your vitality. Whenever you roll damage for a spell you've cast of 1st level or higher, you can choose to take necrotic damage equal to the spell's level to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum one). This damage can't be reduced in any way, and you must use the new rolls.

name: Sanguine Feast
entries: Your hunger for vital essence is unquenchable. As an action, you can unleash tendrils of blood that lash any creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you. A target must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 5d8} necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If your {@subclassFeature Blood Well|Sorcerer|PHB|Crimson|CrookedMoon14|1|CrookedMoon14} is already expended when you use this action, the targets have disadvantage on the saving throw. If at least one creature takes damage from Sanguine Feast, you regain a number of hit points equal to the damage roll.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 5 sorcery points to use it again.

name: Sanguine Feast
entries: Your hunger for vital essence is unquenchable. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can unleash tendrils of blood that lash any creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you. A target must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 5d8} Necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If your {@subclassFeature Blood Well|Sorcerer|XPHB|Crimson|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} is already expended when you use this action, the targets have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw. If at least one creature takes damage from Sanguine Feast, you regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage roll.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you spend 5 Sorcery Points to use it again.

entries.name: Variant: Bloodless Crimson Sorcerers
entries: If you're playing a character from a species that lacks blood in the traditional sense, you can still take the Crimson Sorcery subclass. The essence of Crimson Sorcery is lifeforce, or animating energy that approximates life.

name: Sanguine Fortification
entries: Your vitae has resilience-enhancing properties. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Draught of Endurance
entries: When a creature within 60 feet of you drinks your vitae, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 2 Blood Points to grant that creature a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Kindred level.

entries.name: Flesh of Marble
entries: When you take damage except Fire and Radiant, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 2 Blood Points to reduce the damage you take by half (round down) or 4 Blood Points to reduce the damage to 0.

name: Sanguine Knight
entries: {@i The blood-knights of Hell, Sanguine Knights serve Sutekh, Lord of Blood. Their sorceries drain their enemies' life force, pouring this stolen vitality into infernal rituals to turn the tide of battle.}

Sutekh rules Naraka, the City of Blood. Recognized as the greatest sorcerer in hell, he carries the title of High Sanguinary and rules from the Temple of Vitality. He is a master of blood magic, and his inner circle of priests and wizards are the Bloodliches, undead spellcasters whose corporeal forms turned to ash centuries ago and whose bodies are crafted from solid blood.

Sutekh's illriggers all belong to a cult known as the Chalice of Vitality. Knights of the Chalice drink deeply of their enemies' essence, draining it to power their magics. Other members of the Order of Desecration fear that the Sanguine Knights seek more than Sutekh's mere ascension to the Throne of Hell; some whisper that the Chalice secretly schemes to make Sutekh a god. This would, of course, be treason.

entries.name: Content Warning
entries: This subclass deals with manipulating another creature's blood. Before choosing this subclass, please ensure everyone at your table is comfortable with this concept. And as always, we encourage the ongoing use of safety tools throughout your game.

entries.name: Precepts of Blood
entries: Sanguine Knights swear an oath to Sutekh when they join the Order of Desolation. These tenets swear them to wield profane blood magic, commanding loyalty and inflicting terror.

entries.name: Their Strength Is Their Weakness
entries: I target the strongest of my foes, for their vitality shall feed my victory.

entries.name: Sin Demands Suffering
entries: Opposing me is heresy. Before my enemies taste defeat, they must pay for their unbelief with agony.

entries.name: Loyalty Rewarded
entries: My boons lead my allies to depend on me—and on the bloodshed that empowers me.

entries.name: Mercy Is Power
entries: In granting succor to my allies, I prove how great my power is. Each time I restore life, it serves as a reminder of how quickly I can strip it away.

name: Sanguine Recall
entries: At 6th level, you can sacrifice a portion of your own vitality to recover expended spell slots as an action. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to or less than half your cleric level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You take {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage for each spell slot level recovered, which can't be reduced in any way. You can't use this feature again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.

For example, if you're an 8th-level cleric, you can recover up to four levels of spell slots—a single 4th-level slot, two 2nd-level slots, a 3rd-level slot and a 1st-level slot, or four 1st-level slots. You then take {@damage 4d8} necrotic damage.

name: Sanguine Thief
entries: {@i Eliminate Your Prey with Blood Magic}

In dark alleyways across Etharis, deals are made in coin and blood, but a few enterprising Rogues have posed the question: "Why not both?" Sanguine Thieves are assassins who harness the power of Sangromancy to fuel their abilities, finding new and innovative ways to utilize the blood they see all too frequently in their line of work.

Sanguine Thieves learn to draw upon the vitae of their victims, extending their ability to use blood magic beyond the limits of their own vitality. When cornered, Sanguine Thieves can unleash this power in a hail of crimson darts or fade before a foe's blade, leaving nothing behind but a red mist.

name: Sanguine Vigor
entries: Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by 6, and it increases by 1 whenever you gain another Wizard level. In addition, whenever you cast a {@filter Sangromancy spell|spells|source=grimhollowpg24|subschool=sangromancy} with a spell slot, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the level of the spell slot.

name: Savage Charge
entries: As an {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and make a single melee attack. If this attack hits, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. With the movement from this {@action Dash|XPHB} action, you can pass through the space of the target and do not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

name: Scarlet Vigor
entries: You have resistance to necrotic damage. In addition, when you finish a short rest, you can expend your {@subclassFeature Blood Well|Sorcerer|PHB|Crimson|CrookedMoon14|1|CrookedMoon14} to reduce your level of {@condition exhaustion}, if any, by 1.

name: Scarlet Vigor
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage. In addition, when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can expend your {@subclassFeature Blood Well|Sorcerer|XPHB|Crimson|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} to reduce your {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level, if any, by 1.

name: School of Biomancy
entries: Practitioners of biomancy tend to have a growth mindset and an endless propensity for self-improvement You likely bear symptoms of this continual desire to improve yourself: patches of scales, manes of peacock feathers, hawk's eyes, adhesive palms, gills... the list is as long as there are ideas to try Biomancers are masters of biomantically-enhanced surgery, transplanting specially-grown (or amputated) appendages onto other creatures.

name: Scofflaw
entries: A fighter who hits hard and fights dirty, the Scofflaw balks at the ideals of honor and tradition, doing what they need to survive. Rules are made to be broken, and the Scofflaw extends this logic to their fighting style. Using every trick at their disposal to gain the upper hand against their foes, the Scofflaw cows their enemy into submission, or overwhelms their defenses with a single cheap shot.

Scofflaws eventually trust their notorious reputation to do much of the work for them, gaining the ability to cause foes to quake with a single threat. Scofflaws are a diverse bunch that run the gamut from graceful yet deadly knaves to bruiser thugs. What ties them together is their belief that there's no such thing as a bad win.

name: Seaborne
entries: You are used to being aboard rocking ships and other vehicles. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Strength and Dexterity saving throws and checks to avoid being pushed, having the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, or otherwise being moved against your will.
In addition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks to pilot or otherwise control a waterborne vehicle, such as a canoe or longboat.

name: Sealed Fate
entries: The strength of your {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|PHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14} reaches its peak, granting the following benefits while it is active.

entries.name: Jaws of Doom
entries: The {@creature Grim|CrookedMoon24|Grim's} Ominous Rend action deals an extra {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage (for a total of {@damage 2d6} extra damage).

entries.name: Marked for Death
entries: When you use {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|PHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14}, you can force the target to make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, until the current {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|PHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14} ends, the target has vulnerability to damage dealt by the grim and to the extra damage you deal with {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|PHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14}. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a spell slot of 4th level or higher (no action required).

name: Sealed Fate
entries: The strength of your {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} reaches its peak, granting the following benefits while it is active.

entries.name: Jaws of Doom
entries: The {@creature Grim|CrookedMoon24|Grim's} Ominous Rend action deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage (for a total of {@damage 2d6} extra damage).

entries.name: Marked for Death
entries: When you use {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24}, you can force the target to make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, until the current {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} ends, the target has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to damage dealt by the grim and to the extra damage you deal with {@subclassFeature Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24}. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 4+ spell slot (no action required).

name: Sear Imperfections
entries: You can cast {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB} and {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} on a willing creature without expending spell slots and without Material components, but the target takes {@damage 1d6} Fire damage for each level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}.

name: Second Skin
entries: Starting at 14th level, your shadow symbiote shares your pain. While in dim light or darkness, you have a +2 to AC and resistance to all bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

name: Secret Agent
entries: {@i Engage in Espionage and Assassination}

Knowledge is power. The best way to defeat your enemies is by stealing what they know and replacing it with misinformation. To that end, you have been trained in the ways of covert warfare, giving you a broad range of abilities to complement your fearsome gunnery skills.

name: Seeker
entries: You always have the {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} and {@spell Comprehend Languages|XPHB} spells prepared. With this feature, you can cast one of the spells without a spell slot or components, and your spellcasting ability for it is Wisdom.

Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend 1 Focus Point (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Selective Shift
entries: As a bonus action, you can spend 1 or more sorcery points to magically transform your body for the next 10 minutes For each sorcery point you spend, you gain one adaptation of your choice from the {@table Skinshift Adaptations|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} table, the effects of which last until the transformation ends The adaptation must have a value in the {@dice d20} column equal to or lower than 20 plus half your sorcerer level If you gain a random skinshift adaptation that replaces one you already had (for example, tumour skin replacing rubber skin), this new adaptation lasts for the duration of the transformation.

name: Self Improvement
entries: You can perform minor surgery on your body, improving yourself in a very literal sense Over the course of 1 hour (which can be done during a rest), you can enhance yourself with one bio-magical improvement, choosing from the following options:

items.name: Amphibisprings
items.entry: With enhanced quads and a ratcheting mechanism in your achilles, your jumping distance is tripled.

items.name: Extra Appendage
items.entry: You gain a prehensile tail or an extra arm, allowing you to hold one more thing and conferring advantage on any ability checks you make to climb.

items.name: Detachable Hand
items.entry: As an action, you can detach your hand and imbue it with biomantic magic The hand follows the rules of the {@spell unseen servant} spell, except it is not {@condition invisible} and waits patiently if ever more than 60 feet away from you If your hand is ever reduced to 0 hit points, it is destroyed, and you grow a new one over the course of a short or long rest.

items.name: Firefly Skin
items.entry: You can cast the {@spell light} cantrip at will with yourself as the target As a bonus action, you can flash brightly for a moment; each creature within 5 feet of you that can see you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your wizard spell save DC or be {@condition blinded} until the end of your next turn. After you use this bonus action, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

items.name: Owl Eyes
items.entry: You gain darkvision out to a range of 120 feet.

items.name: Slime
items.entry: You exude slime; checks made to grapple you have disadvantage.

items.name: Scales
items.entry: Your skin is covered in overlapping scales You gain a +1 bonus to AC when you aren't wearing armour.

items.name: Spidersense
items.entry: You gain a 1d4 bonus to your initiative rolls.

items.name: Talon
items.entry: One of your hands is replaced with a wicked giant hawk's talon, a natural weapon that you can use to make unarmed strikes If you hit with it, you deal slashing damage equal to {@damage 1d8} + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike If you are grappling a creature with this talon, you can automatically deal this damage to the {@condition grappled} creature once on each of your turns as a bonus action.

items.name: Third Leg
items.entry: Your speed increases by 10 feet and you have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made against effects that would knock you {@condition prone}.

items.name: Trimorphism
items.entry: You can cast the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell on yourself at will (no material components or concentration required).
