The number of damage dice in the pool equals the number of damage dice as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue Features table. You can't have more Sangromancy Dice than the number of damage dice shown in the Sneak Attack column for your level, unless you have Sangromancy Dice from a different source.

entries.name: Blood Magic
entries: You can spend Sangromancy Dice instead of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} when you cast {@filter Sangromancy spells|spells|subschool=sangromancy}.
Your pool regains all expended dice when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Stolen Secrets
entries: You have uncovered or stolen secret power from agents of the Arch Daemons and Arch Seraphs. You gain one {@filter Eldritch Invocation|optionalfeatures|feature type=EI} of your choice.

entries.name: Prerequisites
entries: If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. If an invocation has a Warlock level prerequisite, you use your Wizard level instead. For example, if an invocation requires you to be a level 5+ Warlock, you can select the invocation once you reach Wizard level 5.

entries.name: Replacing and Gaining Invocations
entries: Whenever you gain a Wizard level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify. You can't replace an invocation if it's a prerequisite for another invocation that you have.
You gain an additional invocation when you reach Wizard levels 6 and 14.
You can't pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.

entries.name: Intelligent Invocations
entries: You can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Charisma modifier for your invocations.

name: Stone Servant
entries: You gain the ability to control the actions of {@condition Petrified|XPHB} creatures, while bestowing upon them the power of your patron. One creature with the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition that you touch becomes an {@creature Elemental Spirit|XPHB|Earth Elemental Spirit} under your control as if you had cast the {@spell Summon Elemental|XPHB} spell at 6th-level. The creature's size does not change and you do not need to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}. The transformation lasts until a {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} spell is cast on the creature, until the Elemental Spirit is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, or until you use this feature again.

name: Stone Sovereign Patron
entries: {@i Hear the Whispering of the Stones}

You have listened to the will of the stone, and made a pact with one of Eberron's great earthen powers. The whispers of the daelkyr Orlassk corrupt many Warlocks to their cause, but similar magics may be the gifts of the greedy fey King Grayfinger or even the medusa Queen Sheshka of Cazhaak Draal. The gnomes of Lorghalan draw their power from their friendship with the earth elementals of their island; perhaps you have made peace with the earth itself.

name: Stone Sovereign Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Stone Sovereign Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Stone Sovereign Spells
rows: {@spell Absorb Elements|FoEQuickstone}, {@spell Earthbind|FoEQuickstone}, {@spell Earth Tremor|FoEQuickstone}, {@spell Spike Growth}

name: Stone Speaker
entries: Your pact grants you the ability to commune with earth and stone. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you imbue stones in an immobile 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} with limited sentience, giving them the ability to communicate with you. You can question stones about events in the spell's area within the past day, gaining information about creatures that have passed, items that might have been removed from the area, and other circumstances.

If an earth Elemental or a creature with the {@condition Petrified|XPHB} condition is in the area, you can communicate with it as if you shared a language, but you gain no magical ability to influence it.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Stone's Embrace
entries: You always have the {@spell Meld into Stone|XPHB} spell prepared. When you cast {@spell Meld into Stone|XPHB}, you can choose up to five willing creatures within 5 feet of you to also gain the benefits of the spell. Each creature must be touching a stone object or surface large enough to fully contain their body. Affected creatures can end the effect on themselves early by using 5 feet of movement to leave the stone where they entered it.

Creatures who finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} while under the effect of your {@spell Meld into Stone|XPHB} spell gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} against the first instance of damage they take after leaving the stone.

name: Stormy Waters
entries: At 15th level, you can call on the force of crashing waters as a reaction whenever a creature moves into or out of your reach. The creature takes {@damage 1d12} bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a Strength {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} against your spell save DC or be knocked {@condition prone}.

name: Street Saint
entries: {@i Devote Yourself to Prayer and Pummeling}

Pugilists rise above the adversity they face. Those known as Street Saints do so with the aid of their deep and abiding faith in the gods. These Pugilists were tested and came out the other side with their righteous resolve to live in service to the gods strengthened. A resolve their gods have taken note of.

name: Strength of Spirit
entries: Your bond with your phantom companion empowers it. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your familiar's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by four times your Sorcerer level.
You can cast spells as if you were in the familiar's space.
When you use your action to cast a spell, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to command your phantom companion to use its Life Drain attack with its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

name: Strength of the Swarm
entries: You can call on your rodent minions for defense. When you take damage from a creature you can see within 10 feet of yourself, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to direct the damage toward a swarm you control you can see within 5 feet of yourself.

name: Strike from the Dark
entries: You understand the power of striking from the shadows. Once per turn, when you hit an interdicted creature with a melee weapon attack and you have advantage on the attack roll, you can roll a number of d4s equal to your proficiency bonus and deal extra damage equal to the total you rolled. This damage increases by {@dice 1d4} if the target is in dim light or darkness.

name: Strong Stomach
entries: Starting at 6th level, your divinity and magically enhanced constitution have strengthened your natural defenses. You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance to acid and poison damage.

In addition, whenever you cast the {@spell create food and water} spell, the food tastes delicious, and you can choose to replace up to 5 gallons of the water created by the spell with ale or wine. You choose what the food and ale or wine look and taste like.
Finally, if you're drunk or {@condition poisoned}, you can use an action to magically suppress the effect for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Student of Alchemy
entries: Your long nights of vigilance have left your senses attuned to signs of danger, granting you the following benefits.

You gain {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}, and you have proficiency with it. In addition, your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} is doubled for ability checks with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}.

name: Submit
entries: When you cast an illrigger spell you know, you can burn two seals on an interdicted creature (no action required) to impose disadvantage on their saving throw against the spell.

name: Subtle Hand
entries: Your martial arts are enhanced by a capacity for telekinetic strikes. During your turn, your reach is 5 feet greater with {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. In addition, when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can choose to have it deal your choice of Psychic damage or its normal damage type.

name: Summon the Courtiers
entries: Having served the Feline Assembly with grace, tact, and good taste, you have earned their favor. When you take damage from a creature that is within 60 feet of you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to call upon the Assembly's wrath. A horde of hissing, spectral cats emerges from the planar firmament and descends upon the creature that damaged you. That creature takes {@damage 5d10} Force damage and has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} and {@condition Prone|XPHB} conditions until the end of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you spend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: Sunder the Weave
entries: You always have the {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} spell prepared. With this feature, you can cast it without a spell slot or components while your Rage is active, and your spellcasting ability for it is Strength. As part of the {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} you take to cast the spell, you can move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and make one attack with a weapon against the target of the spell.
Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Supernal Safeguard
entries: Spell Shield can target a number of creatures up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one creature).

name: Supernal Safeguard
entries: Starting at 17th level, when you use your Channel Divinity: Spell Shield feature, you can choose a number of creatures up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 2) instead of choosing only one.

name: Supreme Switching
entries: Your Spatial Exchange feature improves in the following ways:

items: Whenever you cast {@spell Misty Step|XPHB}, you can swap places with a willing creature, even if you cast it using a spell slot instead of your Channel Divinity.

When you cast {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} using your Channel Divinity, you can now choose a space within 30 feet of yourself that is occupied by an unwilling creature, swapping places with it as normal. If the creature succeeds on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC, this effect fails and that use of your Channel Divinity is wasted.

Whenever you successfully swap places with another creature using your Channel Divinity, you can cast a level 0-5 spell with a range of Touch as part of that {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. The spell must have a casting time of an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, and it must target the creature you're swapping places with. The spell takes effect as you and the other creature appear in your new spaces.

name: Surge of Sustenance
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend one use of Wild Shape to grant the benefits of finishing a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} to yourself or a creature you touch.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Survival Instinct
entries: While you are in mortal peril, your symbiote can attempt to move you to safety. While you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, you can take the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Dodge|XPHB} action, and you retain the benefits of the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action while you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

name: Sutekh's Blessing
entries: When Sutekh accepts you as his illrigger, he grants you access to his sacrilegious command of blood and life. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Religion} skill.

In addition, as an action, you can expand your awareness of life around you. Until the end of your next turn, you can sense creatures who have blood within 120 feet of you without having to see them. This ability can penetrate most barriers, but is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt. You know the distance and direction of each creature, as well as the creature's type. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Sutekh's Interdiction
entries: You learn the following additional interdict boons at the noted illrigger levels. Once you learn an interdict boon granted by this feature, you always know it, and it doesn't count against the number of interdict boons you know.

name: Suturer
entries: You know the {@spell spiritual weapon} spell, which is a bard spell for you, but doesn't count against the number of spells you know. You can cast this spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a long rest. When you cast it as a bard spell, the weapon takes the form of a giant needle and thread, and deals piercing damage instead of force damage.
You also learn different ways to use this spiritual weapon. You gain the Suture benefit below, and you gain an additional benefit below when you reach 5th level and 10th level in this class.

entries.name: Suture (3rd Level)
entries: As a bonus action or an action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to move the weapon up to 20 feet and grant temporary hit points equal to one roll of your Bardic Inspiration die to one creature within 5 feet of the weapon. If the creature has 0 hit points, you can stabilise it, instead.

name: Suturer II
entries: You learn different ways to use your spiritual weapon. You gain the Unspool benefit below.

entries.name: Unspool
entries: As an action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to move the weapon up to 20 feet and force one creature within 5 feet of the weapon to make a Strength saving throw against your bard spell save DC. On a failure, magical threads wrap around the creature, which is {@condition restrained} for 1 minute. The target can use its action to repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on a success.

name: Suturer III
entries: You learn different ways to use this spiritual weapon. You gain the Acupuncture benefit below.

entries.name: Acupuncture
entries: As an action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to move the weapon up to 20 feet and make a melee spell attack against one creature within 5 feet of it. On a hit, the creature takes piercing damage equal to one roll of your Bardic Inspiration die plus your Charisma modifier, and must make a Constitution saving throw against your bard spell save DC. On a failure, the creature is {@condition paralysed} until the end of its next turn.

name: Swarm Shape
entries: When you use your Wild Shape feature, you can turn into a swarm of creatures, adhering to the normal limitations on CR and speed.

name: Swarming Strikes
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can command all of your swarms to make an {@action Attack|XPHB} action instead of just one. Alternatively, a single swarm can attack twice instead of once when it takes the {@action Attack|XPHB} action.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Swarmsense
entries: Hosting such a variety of tiny beings has permanently altered your personal biosphere. You gain the following benefits:

items: Blindsight and tremorsense out to a range of 10 feet.
Resistance to poison damage.
Immunity to the {@condition poisoned} condition.
Advantage on initiative rolls.

entries: Additionally, the poison damage of {@subclassFeature Symbiotic Biosphere|Druid||Hive|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting|2} increases to 1d10

name: Sweet Science
entries: {@i Float Like a Butterfly, Sting Like a Bee}

Pugilists who practice the Sweet Science hit hard, fast, and often. These Pugilists sometimes battle for the entertainment of the upper classes, but just as often duke it out in back alleys and bars where their next breath depends on a knockout.

name: Symbiotic Biosphere
entries: The symbiotes that inhabit your body flit in and around you, harmless until threatened. As a bonus action, you can release pheromones, stimulating hyper-aggression in your symbiotes for the next minute. The first time you are hit by a melee attack by a creature within 15 feet of you on its turn, the swarm retaliates, forcing the attacker to make a Constitution saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a failure, the attacker takes {@damage 1d4} poison damage. The poison damage increases to {@damage 1d6} at 6th level, {@damage 1d8} at 10th level, and {@damage 1d10} at 14th level.
After you activate this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
In addition, you can communicate with arthropods using pheromones, conveying basic emotions and ideas.

name: Symbiotic Reflexes
entries: Your plant symbiote empowers you. You always have the {@spell Haste|XPHB} spell prepared. Once per active Symbiotic Transformation, you can cast {@spell Haste|XPHB} on yourself without a spell slot or components.

name: Symbiotic Reinforcement
entries: Invested in your survival, your patron manifests in protective ways You can use your Charisma modifier in place of your Strength modifier when making Strength saving throws In addition, as a bonus action, you can cause your patron to manifest as a shield in your free hand, with which you are proficient. This shield disappears if you are incapacitated or if you dismiss it as a bonus action The increase to AC rises to 3 when you reach 10th level in this class.

name: Symbiotic Sentinel
entries: Your patron remains alert to threats to its host at all times. You can't be {@status surprised|XPHB} and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions.

name: Sympathetic Shield
entries: Starting at 6th level, you learn how to channel the energy of your beast shapes into manifestations of nature's protection. As an action, you may expend a use of your {@classFeature Wild Shape|Druid|PHB|2|PHB} feature to shield yourself or an ally within 30 feet of you in the protective armor of a beast spirit. This spirit armor is translucent and doesn't block line of sight. The shield can take the shape of any beast you can transform into using your wild shape. The shielded creature gains {@dice 1d10} temporary hit points for every 3 druid levels you possess and a +1 bonus to its AC. The shield lasts until these temporary hit points are expended or replaced by another ability that grants temporary hit points.

At 14th level, the spirit armor can retaliate against foes who attack it directly. Whenever a shielded creature is dealt damage by a target within 5 feet of it, the spirit armor deals {@damage 1d8} points of magical bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage to that target. This damage type is chosen by the druid when activating Sympathetic Shield. The shield can deal damage to multiple targets in a round, but only once per round for each target.

name: Synchronized Response
entries: Your ingestion of monsters heightens your understanding of them and their behaviour. You gain this additional effect when you consume a monster portion: For 1 minute, when you make an attack as part of a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you deal an extra {@damage 1d6} damage. This damage has the same type as the weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} used for the attack.

name: Table-Turner
entries: At 1st level, you can cause an attacker's own body to turn against itself. When a creature within 5 feet of you that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to cause the creature to make a Constitution saving throw against your cleric spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes {@dice 1d12} poison damage and is {@condition poisoned} until the end of its next turn. On a successful one, it takes half as much poison damage and isn't {@condition poisoned}.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Tactical Assault
entries: Your ability to direct the movement and attacks of your allies improves.
Each ally you choose with your Coordinate Tactics feature that can see or hear you gains one of the following benefits of their choice.

entries.name: Guardian Maneuver
entries: Until the start of your next turn, the first time the ally takes damage, they can reduce the damage taken by the number rolled on your Teamwork Die.

entries.name: Recon Maneuver
entries: When an ally takes a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move, it can take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action as part of that {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. It gains a bonus to the Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check equal to the number rolled on your Teamwork Die.

name: Tailor the Skein
entries: You can see the threads of the celestial skein and manipulate them in service to your faith. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, roll a d6 twice and record the numbers rolled. These numbers are known as Skeins. As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, after learning the result of an attack, damage roll, saving throw, or ability check made by a creature you can see within 60 feet, you may add or subtract one of your Skeins from the result. This can cause the roll to succeed or fail when it otherwise wouldn't have. If you add or subtract a Skein from a damage roll, it could cause a creature to live or die when it otherwise wouldn't have.
Your die increases at higher level. At 7th level it, becomes a {@dice d8}; at 11th level, it becomes a {@dice d10}; and at 15th level it becomes a {@dice d12}.
Each Skein can be used only once. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you regain all Skeins.

name: Take to the Skies
entries: By the time you reach 11th level, you've mastered a unique technique that lets you glide on the wind, just like a majestic sheep dragon. When you use your Step of the Wind, you also gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed. This flying speed lasts until the end of your turn.
Additionally, when you use your Step of the Wind, you simultaneously take both the {@action Disengage} and {@action Dash} action.

name: Tale of Hubris (14th Level)
entries: At 14th level, the critical hit range of this feature increases to 17–20.

name: Tale of Hubris
entries: At 6th level, you learn to weave a magical narrative that draws out the fatal arrogance of your foes. When a creature scores a critical hit against you or an ally within 60 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction and expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to target the attacking creature and evoke the story of their downfall. For 1 minute or until the target suffers a critical hit, any weapon attack against the target scores a critical hit on a roll of 18–20.

name: Talented Adventurer
entries: You learn an adventurer's talent of your choice from the {@filter "Adventurer's Talent Options"|optionalfeatures|feature type=ca:at} section later in this subclass's description. You learn an additional adventurer's talent of your choice when you reach Bard levels 6 and 14.

name: Tall Tales
entries: You have gained a knack for telling embellished tales of your past achievements. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Deception|XPHB}, {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, {@skill Performance|XPHB}, or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}.

name: Taste of Oblivion
entries: You are infused with the essence of darkness itself, gaining the following benefits.

entries.name: Oblivion's Sight
entries: You can see normally in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} and {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}—both magical and nonmagical—within 120 feet of yourself.

entries.name: Shadow Cloak
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks, and you can take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

name: Tenebrous Form
entries: Your body can be wreathed in a whirling, armored skin of tangible darkness. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 5 Blood Points to assume a Tenebrous Form for 1 minute. While in your Tenebrous Form, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Armored by Darkness
entries: You have a +4 bonus to AC.

entries.name: Dark Vigor
entries: You gain {@dice 4d10} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Extend Shadows
entries: You can expend 1 Blood Point to increase the duration of Tenebrous Form by 1 minute.

entries.name: Power of Oblivion
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength and Constitution checks and saving throws.

entries.name: Shadowstep
entries: You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} spell, but the unoccupied space you travel to must be in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}.

entries.name: Umbral Limbs
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, your reach is 5 feet greater than normal, you can deal an extra {@damage 2d10} Cold damage to a target you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, and you can grapple a creature if it is Huge or smaller.

entries.name: Resolve
entries: Through willpower and tenacity, the strain of the hunt is endured; aching limbs and ailing minds are no reason to fall short.

entries.name: Respect
entries: Take life only when doing so protects others. Kill only when necessary, lest the bloodshed enamour your soul and hunter becomes beast.

entries.name: Responsibility
entries: Many rely on your talent to survive the moonlit nights. No matter the circumstances, do not fail them. Sacrifice your own body so that others can retain the sanctity of their own, untainted forms.

name: Tenets of the Harvest
entries: The tenets of the Oath of the Harvest inspire their followers to seek out potential harm and quell it before it blossoms.

entries.name: Share Your Meal
entries: Your powers are a gift to be shared; if someone is in need, you must use your power to meet those needs. To eat your fill while another goes hungry is selfish.

entries.name: Nurture Over Cure
entries: Act in the greatest interest of the many. Find ways to prevent harm before it must be healed.

entries.name: Permit Prosperity
entries: Whether in matters of love, politics, or war, always give your antagonist the opportunity to change and redeem themselves before casting a fatal judgment. A good meal can serve as the backdrop to such events.

name: Tenets of the Open Sea
entries: Freedom can be a selfless virtue or a selfish want. For paladins who swear the Oath of the Open Sea, freedom is the highest calling, and a gift to be granted to all.

entries.name: No Greater Life than a Life Lived Free
entries: One should be free to chart their own path without oppression. Those who would exert their power to dominate others shall be smote.

entries.name: Trust the Skies
entries: The guidance of a strong breeze. The rumbling warnings of a coming storm. Nature is a source of portent and council that should be heeded.

entries.name: Adapt Like the Water
entries: The waters of the ocean can shift around any obstacle—or become the most impassable obstacle of all. They carve away the land to reveal the secrets of the past, or swallow the truth and hide it forever. To embrace this fluidity is to be ready for any challenge.

entries.name: Explore the Uncharted
entries: The world is filled with mystery. Through the pursuit of enigmatic ends, one can uncover those who hide their foul deeds, and find the path to becoming something great.

name: Tenets of the River
entries: The tenets of the Oath of The River vary by paladin, but all of them revolve around embracing the flow and adaptability found in water. Paladins who uphold these tenets must understand when it is best to dispatch justice through violence or through understanding and forgiveness. The core principles of the tenets are:

entries.name: The River Flows On
entries: Forgiveness can be as sharp as any blade.

entries.name: The River Quenches or Drowns
entries: Judgment is reserved for those truly deserving of it.

entries.name: The River Rages
entries: If I must battle, I will fight with all my passion and strength.

entries.name: The River Seeks the Sea...Always
entries: I will not abandon my duty, especially when others are counting on me.

name: Tenets of the Spelldrinker
entries: The tenets of the Oath of the Spelldrinker were written and passed down by cautious guardians set to rid the world of evil mages. They emphasize balance within oneself through the following tenets:

entries.name: Be the Sword
entries: Be a stalwart champion of fairness and equality among all. The sword doesn't cheat fate: it dances with it.

entries.name: Be the Shield
entries: Defend the innocent against the forces of rampant magic. The shield is patient and unwavering in the face of the unknown.

entries.name: Be the Spell
entries: Use your power to provide balance and guidance. The spell can lead to prosperity as easily as it can to ruin: you must always choose the righteous path.

name: Tenets of Zeal
entries: The tenets of the Oath of Zeal are serious and severe, as are those paladins who choose to take them.

items.name: Uncover Corruption
entries: Darkness cannot abide the light of day. Wickedness must be revealed before it can be destroyed.

items.name: Purge the Heretics
entries: Heresy is a tumor that spread through the hearts of the innocent. Cut it out at the source.

items.name: No Mercy
entries: The righteous path requires unwavering conviction and unflinching resolve.

items.name: By Any Means Necessary
entries: There is no sacrifice too great when it comes to defeating the wicked.

name: Terrifying Visage
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can adopt the terrifying visage of the being that cursed your ancestor for 10 minutes. During this time, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cause creatures of your choice you can see you within 30 feet of yourself to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. In addition, while your Terrifying Visage feature is active, you gain the following benefit based on the creature type chosen with your Blood Ties feature.

entries.name: Fey
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

entries.name: Fiend
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold and Fire damage.

entries.name: Undead
entries: When you take damage of any type other than Radiant, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage by half your Sorcerer level.
Once you use Terrifying Visage, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Terrorize the Terrors
entries: Your reputation has become such that monsters preying on the fearful have come to fear you. When you hit a creature with an attack as part of a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. The DC for the saving throw equals 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Thane
entries: You have sworn service to a King and serve as one of their chosen fighters. As long as war must be, you stand ready to protect the innocent and destroy your lord's enemies.

name: The Concealing
entries: Your obfuscation abilities can now extend to objects and creatures in your vicinity.

entries.name: Conceal
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action you can expend 3 Blood Points to touch an object and make it vanish from sight and memory. The object gains the Invisible condition and creatures forgetting it may recover memories by succeeding on the Investigation check described in the source. A {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} or {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} restores true memory.

entries.name: Cloak the Gathering
entries: When you cast {@spell Invisibility|XPHB}, you can expend up to 6 Blood Points to affect additional creatures within 30 feet.

name: The Coven
entries: {@i Curse and Befuddle with Hag Magic}

Hags dwell in the deep places of Etharis, from the primordial forests of Valika to the putrid streets of Liesecht. These creatures, though rarely benevolent, are willing to bargain with mortals in exchange for furthering their own capricious goals.

Warlocks often find themselves with a single Hag as a sponsor. Should this Hag have a coven, it can lead to the peculiar situation of Warlock agents acting against other Hags or their Warlocks within the coven. But such is the politics of the Realm of Faerie.

name: The End is Nigh
entries: You loudly proclaim what will come to pass when the world ends. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you describe the end of days. When you do so, each creature of your choice in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 6d6} Psychic damage and {@damage 6d6} Force damage and has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only. A {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition on a successful save. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the creature can be revived only by a {@spell True Resurrection|XPHB} or a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you spend 6 Sorcery Points (no action required) to restore your use of it.

name: The First Vampire Patron
entries: {@i Wield the Power of Undeath}

You have made a pact with a powerful vampire cursed by the gods or born as a creature of the night. Hundreds of haunted beings serve this vampire, so why enter a pact with you? Because you can act in the light of day unhindered? To cull weaker vampires?

name: The Great Fool
entries: {@i Laugh in the Face of Danger with Foolish Antics}

What horrors and sorrows can't be remedied by maniacal laughter? Warlocks that have made a pact with the Great Fool draw their enigmatic power from a powerful, otherworldly being of jolly revelry, whose twisted sense of humor is lost on mortal understanding. They are a mocking mirror to bring low the arrogant and mighty, though the Great Fool's ultimate designs are often nonsensical and incomprehensible.

Many Warlocks of the Great Fool adopt a signature aesthetic and performance style that best represents their folly. The Foolish Personas table offers archetypes of fools with suggestions for corresponding outfits and routines.

entries.caption: Foolish Personas
rows: {@b The Harlequin.} An elegant outfit of diamond motley with a painted mask—performs dances, gives eloquent speeches, and plays tricks
{@b The Jester.} A two-toned, checkered motley outfit with cap and bells—favors feats of acrobatics, tumbling, and juggling
{@b The Joker.} A vibrant, colorful suit with wild hair and bowler hat—favors silly jokes, slapstick comedy, and clumsy self-deprecation
{@b The Mime.} A striped, black-and-white shirt with a flat cap and red suspenders—pantomimes comical scenarios without speaking
{@b The Sad Clown.} A monochromatic, one-piece outfit with pointed hat and puffball buttons—utilizes melodramatic melancholy and song
{@b The Tramp.} A patch-covered coat, tattered scarf, scuffed shoes, and cigar—leverages sardonic wit, insults, and mocking observations

name: The Horned King
entries: {@i Live Deliciously with Bewitching Power}

Whether motivated by desperation or cunning, warlocks that have signed their name in the book of the Horned King have chosen to live deliciously in a pact sealed in blood and a corrupted soul. Bestowed the power of witchcraft by the beast that stalks the deepest woods and darkest hearts, they perfect ancient rituals and weave maledictions toward aims only they know. With each victim of their malign spells filled with rot, hate, and agony, they become more like their patron until they effortlessly wield his kingly might.
Warlocks of the Horned King prefer particular implements in working their magic. The Witchcraft Implements table offers options for your favored reagents.

entries.caption: Witchcraft Implements
rows: Candles made from tallow mixed with blood
Dried bundles of herbs or mushrooms
Skulls or long bones carved with glyphs
Crushed berries or roots mixed into a paste
Curved blade for offering animal sacrifices

name: The Lantern
entries: Warlocks who make a pact with a powerful spirit are able to tap into the magic that flows through the Spirit Realm. These warlocks are known by the special lanterns they carry—lanterns that burn with the essence of their patron. The illumination of this vessel carries with it the attributes of the spirit, granting the warlock an array of abilities.

When spirits enter pacts with people, there is often more to it than generosity. Spirits powerful enough to lend out bits of their magic do so for a variety of reasons. Perhaps the spirit is beholden to do so due to a bargain or curse. It could be that the spirit needs allies (though they might not readily admit it). Or maybe they simply see something in you that amuses them. The things that motivate spirits are as varied as they are. And truly powerful spirits can be inscrutable.

name: The Many
entries: Your patron is a powerful entity composed of a multitude of heads. These heads provide unique strengths, such as the regenerative properties of a mighty hydra, or the bewitching gaze of a medusa. Your patron may consider you one of its estranged or forgotten heads, allowing you to do as you please, or compel you to work toward a shared goal as one of its own. Those that make a pact with a patron such as this may find beauty in patterns or matching sets, or become plagued with internal bickering and indecisiveness. Regardless, one thing is for certain: two heads are always better than one.

Entities of this type include extremely powerful or godlike multi-headed or -conscioused beings, swarms, or hiveminds. Example patrons in this book include the Butcher Dray, Three-Headed Ettin; Grihoo, the Superhydra; Lady Feluciana, Legendary Medusa Sorceress; the Thousand Voices, Supreme Soul Vortex; and Vaanor, Primeval Cerberus. Details on these patrons can be found in appendix I on page 378.

name: The Other Side
entries: You can call on your otherworldly friends in low places to change the odds of anything you do in your favor. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Crossroads Devilry
entries: When you miss with an attack roll or fail a saving throw, you can expend and roll any number of your Sneak Attack dice (choose the number before you roll) and add the total rolled to the attack or save, potentially turning a miss into a hit or failure into success. Expended dice return after you next use your Sneak Attack.

entries.name: Lady Luck's Smiling
entries: When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can expend and roll any number of your Sneak Attack dice (choose the number before you roll) and add the total rolled to your AC against that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss. Expended dice return after you next use your Sneak Attack.

name: The Other Side
entries: You can call on your otherworldly friends in low places to change the odds of anything you do in your favor. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Crossroads Devilry
entries: When you miss with an attack roll or fail a saving throw, you can expend and roll any number of your Sneak Attack dice (choose the number before you roll) and add the total rolled to the attack or save, potentially turning a miss into a hit or failure into success. Expended dice return after you next use your Sneak Attack.

entries.name: Lady Luck's Smiling
entries: When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can expend and roll any number of your Sneak Attack dice (choose the number before you roll) and add the total rolled to your AC against that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss. Expended dice return after you next use your Sneak Attack.

name: The Parasite
entries: You have bonded, mind and body, with a rare and enigmatic being that calls your body home, whether you like it or not Its origins are unknown; perhaps it came from a vat of biomantic mut-x, the nightmares of an astral projector, or a subterranean pool of primordial ooze. Survival is its watchword and you are its host.

entries.name: Invocations & Parasitic Weapon
entries: If you are the GM, consider allowing invocations that have thethat have the {@spell eldritch blast} cantrip as a prerequisite to also benefit attacks the warlock makes with their parasitic weapon. For example, {@optfeature Repelling Blast} would permit the parasitic weapon to push targets, while {@optfeature Agonizing Blast} would allow the warlock to add their Charisma modifier to its damage rolls. However, take this with a pinch of salt; {@optfeature Eldritch Spear} extends the weapon's reach by a factor of 2.5 only, not 180 feet!

name: The Parasite Patron
entries: {@i Become One with a Cosmic Being}

Your patron is a cosmic parasite, draining the vitality of entire peoples and worlds. Upon forging a pact with such a patron, you become host to one of its nascent offspring. As you grow in power, the boundary between your identity and the parasitic larva within blurs.

name: The Predator
entries: Your patron is a primal beast, driven by a bloodthirsty need to hunt. These beings tempt creatures to give in to their base instincts and become apex predators. {@creature Ancient White Dragon||Ancient white dragons}, demons with a bestial bent, and the Amaranthine {@deity Kren|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} have all been known to occasionally grant feral powers to those desperate enough to seek their aid. Many who strike a pact with a Predator find themselves forever changed, bearing razor teeth and wicked claws, an aspect of their predatory patron.

name: The Road Not Traveled
entries: When you take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action, instead of moving, you can teleport yourself or an ally within 60 feet of you to the location of your shade.

name: The Spirit-Fused
entries: Even the life of a spirit must come to an end.

Those who take on the moniker of a spirit-fused fighter do not normally do so by choice but rather by circumstance. Because to become a spirit-fused fighter, you must first become the vessel of a dying spirit, a task that can't be accomplished by choice, as no one truly understands how or why this occurs.

All that is known is that the spirit's mind and body have passed on, and its essence now coexists within the fighter, granting them abilities beyond the capability of a normal spirit. Those who can harness this power can channel the latent energy into objects, which produce a magical quirk or powerful attacks. These arcane tricks are how these unconventional warriors fight and are the reason they have garnered so much attention and interest on the island.

name: Thicker than Water
entries: Upon reaching 14th level, the blood that flows through your veins is empowered with arcane vigor that mends wounds and helps preserve your life. Whenever a spell or magical effect causes you to regain hit points, you regain an additional number of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.
In addition, while you are concentrating on a spell, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

name: Threatening Presence
entries: You can provoke your enemies into single-minded hatred of you. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, each creature of your choice that can hear you in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 5d6} Psychic damage and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against targets other than you. When you use this feature, you restore your use of Weather the Storm.
You can use this feature twice. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
When you reach Fighter level 15, you gain another use of this feature.

name: Thrill of the Hunt
entries: At 6th level, you gain the ability to feast on the vitality of your foes while you are in your {@subclassFeature Form of the Beast|Warlock|PHB|Predator|HumblewoodTales|1|HumblewoodTales}. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with your bite attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 3d6} points of necrotic damage. You regain a number of hit points equal to half the total damage dealt with this attack.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you score a critical hit with a bite or claw attack or until you finish a short or long rest.
At 10th level, the extra necrotic damage provided by this feature increases to {@damage 5d6}.

name: Thrum of the Land
entries: Also at 2nd level, you learn how to channel energy from a leyline to supplement your spells, infusing them with power. Whenever you are in an environment that matches a leyline to which you are attuned, you can apply one of the following benefits to any leyline spell you cast (chosen when you cast the spell):

items: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls made with this spell.
You gain a +1 bonus to your spell save DC for this spell.
You have advantage on Constitution saving throws you make to maintain {@status concentration} on this spell, and you can concentrate on this spell for up to twice its normal duration.

entries: At 14th level, you can apply one of these benefits to a single spell of 6th level or higher when you cast it, so long as you are in an environment that matches a leyline to which you are attuned. You can't use this feature again until you have completed a long rest.

name: Thunderous Aura
entries: You and your allies have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Thunder damage while in your Aura of Protection.
Also, when you cast {@spell Find Steed|XPHB}, you can choose your Faithful Steed's attacks to deal Thunder damage instead of its typical damage.

name: Thunderous Blows (10th Level)
entries: Starting at 10th level, you can push a creature up to 10 feet when you hit it with a melee attack while you're raging.

name: Thunderous Blows
entries: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, your rage instills you with the strength to shove and smash your way through your foes, making any battlefield your domain. When you hit a creature with a melee attack while you're raging, you can push that creature up to 5 feet away from you in a direction of your choice. A creature that is Huge or larger makes a Strength {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} with a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier. On a success, the creature is not pushed.

entries.name: Rules Tip: Forced Movement
entries: Usually when one creature moves out of a hostile creature's reach, the hostile creature can use its reaction to make an {@action opportunity attack}. However, forced movement—such as being pushed by a Path of the Juggernaut barbarian's {@subclassFeature Thunderous Blows|Barbarian|PHB|Juggernaut|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3} feature—doesn't provoke {@action opportunity attack|PHB|opportunity attacks}.

Likewise, a juggernaut barbarian's {@subclassFeature Hurricane Strike|Barbarian|PHB|Juggernaut|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|10} feature allows an ally to make a melee weapon attack as a reaction only if the foe ends its forced movement within 5 feet of the ally. If a foe is pushed through other spaces within 5 feet of your allies, those allies can't make normal {@action opportunity attack|PHB|opportunity attacks} against the foe.

name: Tireless Leader
entries: Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you suffer the effects of {@condition exhaustion} as if it was one level lower (no effects at level 1, disadvantage on ability checks at level 2, and so on).

name: Titanic Strikes
entries: When you use your {@classFeature Brutal Strike|Barbarian|XPHB|9|XPHB} feature, the distance the target is pushed by your Forceful Blow is doubled, and the {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of a target struck by your Hamstring Blow is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.

name: Tolling Censer
entries: You can unleash a cloud of miasma upon your enemies. As an action, you can expend 2 ki points to magically unleash a cloud of miasma in a 20-foot radius around you. Each creature of your choice in that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes necrotic damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die and is cursed by your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|PHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon14|3|CrookedMoon14|Miasmic Plague}. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

name: Tolling Censer
entries: You can unleash a cloud of miasma upon your enemies. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 2 Focus Points to unleash a cloud of miasma in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you. Each creature of your choice in that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes Necrotic damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die and is cursed by your {@subclassFeature Contagious Discipline|Monk|XPHB|Pestilent Haze|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24|Miasmic Plague}. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

name: Tomb Castellan
entries: The powers of your Death Knight feature improve in the following ways.

entries.name: Phantom Charger
entries: The ghostly steed of your Dark Rider power now ignores Difficult Terrain. Additionally, when your steed takes the {@action Dash|PHB}, {@action Disengage|PHB}, or {@action Dodge|PHB} action, you can expend and roll a Draugr Die. Your steed magically teleports (with you if you're riding it) to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of the steed. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of the steed when it appears must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, taking Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled on the Draugr Die plus your Constitution modifier on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Death Knell
entries: When you use your Grave Guard power in response to a creature damaging you, the creature takes Psychic damage equal to half the amount of damage the power reduced.

entries.name: Spectral Shrieking
entries: When a creature {@condition Grappled|PHB} by your Soul Reaper power starts its turn, it takes Psychic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. When it does, you can take a Reaction to expend and roll a Draugr Die, adding the number rolled to the damage.

name: Tomb Castellan
entries: The powers of your Death Knight feature improve in the following ways.

entries.name: Phantom Charger
entries: The ghostly steed of your Dark Rider power now ignores {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. Additionally, when your steed takes the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, or {@action Dodge|XPHB} action, you can expend and roll a Draugr Die. Your steed magically teleports (with you if you're riding it) to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of the steed. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of the steed when it appears must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, taking Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled on the Draugr Die plus your Constitution modifier on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Death Knell
entries: When you use your Grave Guard power in response to a creature damaging you, the creature takes Psychic damage equal to half the amount of damage the power reduced.

entries.name: Spectral Shrieking
entries: When a creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by your Soul Reaper power starts its turn, it takes Psychic damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. When it does, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend and roll a Draugr Die, adding the number rolled to the damage.

name: Tool Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB}. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice.
In addition, when you craft an ordinary or magic weapon, the amount of time required to craft it is halved.

name: Tool Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB}. If you already have proficiency with {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB}, you gain proficiency with one other type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice.
In addition, when you craft a magic item, the amount of time required to craft it is halved.

name: Tools of Performance
entries: When you join the College of Masks at 3rd level, you gain the ability to weave arcane boons into theater masks, which grant you abilities while you wear them. You craft two masks of your choice, which are detailed under the "{@filter Masks|optionalfeatures|source=ObojimaTallGrass|feature type=Mask}" section below. You're able to craft one additional mask of your choice when you reach 7th, 11th, and 15th level in this class. Each time you craft a new mask, you can also replace one mask you've already crafted with a different one.

While wearing a mask you gain the abilities granted by it. You can don or swap masks as an action or bonus action. If an ability from a mask requires a saving throw, the DC is equal to your bard spell save DC.

name: Tools of the Trade
entries: You've learned to interrogate and use implements of torture. You gain proficiency with {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP} and the {@skill Insight|XPHB} skill. You also have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} with them.

name: Toreador
entries: {@i See the World Like No One Else Can}

Toreador are steeped in art and beauty. They use their superhuman senses to experience aspects of the world no one else can. They feel everything deeply, and, with a glance or a few words, can instill similar feelings in others. If there is awe to be found, a Toreador can find it.

name: Toreador Bane
entries: You suffer a great malaise in the absence of beauty. When you roll a 9 or lower on the d20 for an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check, you see nothing of immediate beauty and gain the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. At the end of each of your turns, you can make a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw, ending the condition on a success.

name: Torturer Conclave
entries: Enshrouded within the radiance of Luyarnha, a conclave of Rangers lies concealed, their solemn duty vowed to the preservation of peace within the walls, regardless of the means. Ever vigilant against the insidious advance of the Scourge, they have honed their inquisitorial craft, recognizing the importance of early prevention of this plague. They achieve this by finding and interrogating victims—and even potential victims—before signs of sickness manifest themselves.

Although these Rangers have been known to serve the clergy and royalty, since the fall of the House of Commons, they are no longer beholden to the fickle desires of any specific lord or lady. Many are now driven by a loftier purpose, one that necessitates the utmost discipline and commitment, for they recognize that if the Scourge is allowed to propagate, it shall wreak havoc upon all they cherish. Yet, some pursue baser ambitions, offering their expertise to those who desire to bend these Rangers to their malevolent will, extracting confessions or inflicting retribution upon adversaries. After all, torture, a practice as ancient as the very bedrock of the earth, is a dreadful instrument, potent enough to shatter even the most indomitable of spirits.

In the throes of battle, these Rangers bring their torturous expertise with them, employing it with merciless precision to break their enemies and methodically subject them to unspeakable agony. They show no mercy to their foes, for they are well aware that none would be extended to them in kind.

entries.name: Disclaimer
entries: Please be advised that while some may use torture as a plot device or as a means of gathering information, it is a sensitive and disturbing topic. While the use of torture can be integral to the story being told, which is why it is included in this book, it is important to ensure that everyone at the table comes to an agreement regarding its use prior to the session beginning, and if it's included, whether descriptions should fade to black or be more detailed.

name: Torturer Techniques
entries: You learn to use techniques. Unlike others who require patience and careful preparation, you make use of techniques that are fueled by your magic, letting you employ of {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP} in the midst of hunts—no creature too alien or too resolute to escape your methods.

You can use each technique twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can expend one use of your {@classFeature Favored Enemy|Ranger|XPHB|1|XPHB} feature (no action required) to regain one use of a technique.

entries.name: Techniques
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} while you have {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP} in one hand (or a free hand and the presence of {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP} at your disposal, such as strapped around your leg), as part of that attack, you can use a technique to enhance it in some way. You can only use a technique once per turn, though you can use different techniques in the same turn, and you can only use one technique per attack.

entries.name: Empowered Techniques
entries: When you use a technique, you can empower it by expending a spell slot (no action required). When you do so, you inflict extra damage to the target, and the target subtracts a number of {@dice d4}s from the saving throws it makes against the technique. The amount of damage and the number of dice subtracted are determined by the level of the spell slot expended, as shown on the following table. You can expend a spell slot up to a level determined by your Ranger level, also shown on the following table. You can also empower a technique if you expend one use of your Favored Enemy feature, which counts as a level 1 spell slot.

entries.name: Techniques
entries: You learn each of the following techniques. At higher levels, these techniques are improved.

entries.name: Technique Save DC
entries: If a technique requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Combing
entries: You scrape, tear, and flay the victim's body. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} Slashing damage.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if you damage a target two rounds in a row with this technique, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it begins to decompose, taking Necrotic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute. This damage can't be reduced or prevented. The creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Any extra damage from empowering this technique also applies to this Necrotic damage. A creature can't suffer multiple instances of this effect at once.

entries.name: Enucleation
entries: You aim a vicious strike at the target's eye, reducing their vision to a macabre blur. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} of the weapon's damage type, and it must make a Constitution saving throw. Creatures with more than two eyes have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this saving throw. On a failed save, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks and has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition against anything further than 60 feet from it for 1 minute. The target repeats this save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Starting at Ranger level 11, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, it has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for the same duration.

entries.name: Hamstringing
entries: You slash at the creature's tendons. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 0 for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Nerve Scraping
entries: You damage the creature's nerves. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d4} Psychic damage and must make a Constitution saving throw.

On a failed save, until the start of your next turn, the target must use its action before moving to make a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within reach other than itself. If no creature is in reach, it acts normally but randomly determines targets.

Starting at Ranger level 11, if the target fails this save two rounds in a row, it subtracts {@dice 1d4} from its attack rolls and saving throws for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Throat Chop
entries: You deliver a fierce cleave to the target's throat, severely impairing its ability to breathe and speak. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning damage and can't speak or use the Verbal components of spells until the start of your next turn.

Starting at Ranger level 11, if you hit a target two rounds in a row with this technique, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Tympanic Rupture
entries: You slam the target's ears in an attempt to destabilize it. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. A {@condition Deafened|XPHB} creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, it is disoriented for the duration. While disoriented, the target can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}.

name: Touch of Sorrow
entries: Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to infuse the target with your sorrow. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition paralyzed} and {@condition poisoned} for 24 hours. The creature remains paralyzed until it takes damage or is no longer poisoned.
You must finish a short or long rest before you can use this feature again.

name: Toxic Shock
entries: At 13th level, when you gain temporary hit points from your Transfusion feature, the target of the attack is overcome by a wave of sickness. Until the end of its next turn, the target's speed is reduced by 10 feet, and it has disadvantage on the next attack roll or ability check that it makes before the end of its next turn.

name: Toxic Tradecraft
entries: You gain a {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}, and you have proficiency with it. In addition, your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} is doubled for ability checks with a {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}. If you lose the kit, you can harvest toxic flora and venomous fauna for 1 hour to magically create a replacement. This harvest can be performed during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, and it destroys the previous {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}.

Once per turn when you deal Poison damage to a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend a spell slot (no action required). The attack deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Poison damage and the target gains the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. You may also add a Toxin Effect, chosen from the appropriate list below. All Toxin Effects last until the end of your next turn, unless its description states otherwise.

entries.name: Level 1 Spell Slot Effects
entries: When you expend a level 1+ spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

entries.name: Attenuate
entries: While a creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition from this toxin, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

entries.name: Befuddled
entries: While a creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition from this toxin, it can't speak, read, or write and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saving throws made to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on spells.

entries.name: Uncoordinated
entries: While a creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition from this toxin, it can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} or the {@action Disengage|XPHB} or {@action Dodge|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Level 2 Spell Slot Effects
entries: When you expend a level 2+ spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

entries.name: Debilitate
entries: For 1 minute, the creature can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Potent
entries: For 1 minute, the creature loses {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage.

entries.name: Suffer
entries: For 1 minute, the first time on each turn the creature takes Poison damage, it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Poison damage.

entries.name: Level 3 Spell Slot Effects
entries: When you expend a level 3+ spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

entries.name: Lingering
entries: Instead of ending at the end of your next turn, the creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 10 minutes. During this time it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saving throws to end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on itself. At the end of each of the creature's turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw to end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Supernatural
entries: When you deal damage to a creature with a {@condition poisoned} item, the creature loses {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and then has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the creature's turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw to end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and regain its {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Level 4 Spell Slot Effects
entries: When you expend a level 4+ spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

entries.name: Flesh Eating
entries: For 1 minute, the creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. While a creature has the Posioned condition from this toxin, it takes {@damage 2d6} Acid damage at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Insensate
entries: While a creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition from this toxin, it also has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} and {@condition Deafened|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Paraplegia
entries: While a creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition from this toxin, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws.

entries.name: Level 5 Spell Slot Effects
entries: When you expend a level 5 spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

entries.name: Enhanced
entries: Apply one option from the Level 4 Spell Slot Effects list, and an additional option from either the Level 1 or Level 2 Spell Slot Effects list.

entries.name: Stinging Application
entries: For 1 minute, once per turn, when you hit a creature with a {@condition poisoned} item, the attack deals an extra {@damage 5d6} damage. The damage type is your choice of Acid, Necrotic, or Poison.

name: Toxin Transmutation
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage. Also, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on yourself.

When you end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on yourself in this way, you can choose to gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Fighter level. You regain the ability to gain these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} after completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Tracker
entries: You are an expert at detecting and obscuring tracks. When you make an ability check to find or follow tracks, you can add your proficiency bonus to the result of the check, even if you aren't proficient in the relevant skill. If you are already proficient in the relevant skill, your proficiency bonus is doubled for that check.

name: Tradition of Performance
entries: The College of Masks not only describes the bard, but it also refers to an Obojiman theater tradition where a solitary masked actor plays out a story from the island's myths and folktales, which feature a set of archetypal characters such as the Old Man, the Fish, and the Demon, among others. Throughout the show, the actor artfully shifts between masks depicting each character. Each performance is its own special thing, as no two are the same.

name: Tragic Hero
entries: A great performance sometimes comes at a cost to the artist. If you fail a saving throw, choose other creatures you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Each of the chosen creatures gains a bonus to saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) against the same effect that triggered this feature, potentially turning a failure into a success.

name: Trail Warden

entries: Wanting to become a hero is a noble aim, but no one remembers the guy who died of dysentery on his way to the dungeon.

Trail wardens are Rangers who have taken an oath. When they lead others into the wilderness, they swear to bring them back safe and sound, but they aren't mere bodyguards or tour guides. Trail Wardens only lead those they deem capable of providing the skills and abilities needed to endure the horrid monsters and grinding conditions of an expedition. Far from civilization's protective grasp, there is no room for dead weight. A single mistake can cost the lives of an entire party.

Trail Wardens are known for their harsh attitude toward others. Some Trail Wardens believe that they must bring the realities of the wilderness into civilization to prevent the careless from joining their expeditions and endangering the group. But once in the wilds, they become nurturing, protective, and insightful as they guide their charges safely through dangerous territory.

name: Trail Warden Spells
entries: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Trailwarden Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

name: Transformation
entries: Beginning at 18th level, you can fully embody the fabled visage of your demon ancestor without needing to exhaust your sorcerous power. As an action, you can instantly manifest all of your oni traits, regardless of how many sorcery points you're missing. While manifesting your oni traits in this way, you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks, and you can't be {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}.

This effect lasts for 1 minute, after which you lose any trait you haven't gained by normal means in that time. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 5 sorcery points to use it again.

name: Transfusion
entries: Starting at 3rd level, once on each of your turns when you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature that isn't a construct or an undead, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). When you reach 13th level, you gain temporary hit points equal to twice your Wisdom modifier instead. These temporary hit points last until the start of your next turn.

name: Transmit Parasite
entries: At 10th level, you learn new ways to use your parasitic ooze to aid your friends or harm your foes As a bonus action while your parasitic ooze isn't incapacitated, you can command it to immediately use one of the options below.

entries.name: Detonate Ooze
entries: The ooze moves up to its speed and then explodes, causing it to drop to 0 hit points Each creature within 10 feet of the ooze must make a Dexterity saving throw against your warlock spell save DC On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} necrotic damage and is {@condition blinded} until the end of your next turn On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't {@condition blinded}.

entries.name: Symbiote's Ward
entries: The ooze moves up to its speed and attaches to the body of a willing creature within 5 feet of it While attached in this way, the ooze is incapacitated, has a speed of 0, and you can communicate telepathically with the creature it's attached to, whether or not you share a common language Whenever the creature the ooze is attached to takes damage, the ooze takes the damage instead As a bonus action, you can command the parasite to detach from the creature.

name: Transmuting Metabolism
entries: You gain the ability to consume monster remains, which causes your body to adopt powerful and frightening mutations. These appear in the "Mutations" section later in the subclass's description.

entries.name: Salvaging Portions
entries: As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, you can harvest a single portion from the physical remains of a creature. Only one portion can be harvested from each creature. Record the monster's creature type. A harvested portion lasts until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, at which point it loses its potency.

entries.name: Consuming Portions
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can consume a portion. After you consume the portion, you choose a mutation to gain, depending on the creature's type. You can gain the benefits of consumed portions a number of times up to 1 plus your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you regain the ability to safely consume portions.
You can benefit from multiple portions simultaneously, but you can't gain the same mutation more than once at the same time.

entries.name: Mutations
entries: The mutations are presented here in alphabetical order, with required creature types shown in brackets after the mutation's name.

name: Trapped Weapons
entries: When you finish a short or long rest, you can augment one weapon or up to twenty pieces of ammunition that you are holding with a concealed, magical augmentation. You decide whether the augmentation deals acid, cold, fire, or lightning damage. The augmentation lasts until you finish a short or long rest.

Once per turn, when you hit a target with a weapon attack using the augmented weapon or ammunition, you can activate the concealed augment (no action required). The target of your attack takes {@damage 1d8} extra damage of the associated type. At 11th level, you can augment one additional item or up to 20 additional pieces of ammunition when you finish a short or long rest, and the damage increases to {@damage 2d8}

name: Trapper
entries: Through careful preparation, trappers can create both physical and magical traps to ensnare, explode, or enrapture those unlucky enough to find themselves in their vicinity Trappers are found in all terrains where there are creatures to be hunted With tact and guile as their companions, a trapper can lay low even the mightiest of prized beasts.

name: Trapper Gadgets
entries: You learn to create gadgets and mechanisms that help you during the hunt.

As part of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can craft two {@filter Trapper Gadgets|optionalfeatures|source=|feature type=tg:tg} if you have materials and {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} on hand. Also, with 1 hour of work with such a kit and expending 20 GP worth of materials (such as equipment or monster salvage), you can create one Trapper Gadget from the list below.
Some Trapper Gadgets allow your target to make an ability check or saving throw to resist the gadget's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:

name: Trapper Guild
entries: {@i Dispatch Monsters with Cunning Traps}

Legends say that the founding members of the Trapper Guild were game hunters who had grown bored of stalking common elk and dreamed of taking down bigger game. Trappers take pride in their kills and the ingenuity exhibited when a trap works perfectly.

The legacy of the Trapper Guild is a consistent testament to the benefits of lying in wait. The element of surprise is paramount to the trapper, whose kit can flourish before the hunter and monster even meet. Preparation is key, and the resourceful trapper has devices to assist in bringing down even the strongest foes.

name: Trapper's Avoidance
entries: The merest hiss of escaping air, depression of a tile, or scent of ozone is all the warning you need to avoid traps' effects. When you are subjected to a trap's activation effect that allows you to make a saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail. In addition, if a trap makes an attack roll against you, that attack roll has {@b disadvantage}.

This feature doesn't function against a trap's ongoing effects. For example, you can mitigate the effect of a poisonous cloud as it is being released by holding your breath or covering your skin, but on subsequent rounds, the cloud's saving throw would affect you as normal on a success or failure.

name: Trapper's Tools
entries: Having learnt how to create traps, you've gained an understanding of how to thwart the traps of others. You gain proficiency with thieves' tools and you add double your proficiency bonus to any ability check you make using those tools to disarm or manipulate a trap.

name: Traveler's Tricks
entries: At 3rd level you already have several memorable experiences from your life on the road. You learn two Traveler's Tricks of your choice (see Traveler's Trick Options).

These Traveler's Tricks represent skills, techniques, and useful pieces of knowledge picked up along the way. Each one requires you to expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration, and takes a bonus action to use unless otherwise specified.
