At 6th level and at 14th level you learn an additional Traveler's Trick.

entries.name: Traveler's Trick Options
entries: The Traveler's Trick feature lets you choose options for it at certain levels. The options are presented here in alphabetical order. Each one is associated with a different class.

Unlike traditional bard abilities which rely on skill or panache to be properly executed, the greatest asset for picking up tricks along the road is common sense and an openness to learning new ideas. Wisdom affects how powerful your traveler's tricks are, as well as how hard they are to counter. If an option requires a saving throw, your Traveler's Trick save DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier.

name: Traveler's Tricks
entries: At 6th level you learn an additional Traveler's Trick.

name: Traveler's Tricks
entries: At 14th level you learn an additional Traveler's Trick.

name: Tree-Climber
entries: Also at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement.
In addition, you can add your Dexterity modifier to Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks you make to climb or jump, and to the distance you cover (in feet) when you make a running jump.

name: Trick of the Light
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 60 feet.

name: Trick Shot
entries: {@i Ricochet Bullets from Every Angle}

Accuracy means different things to different people. For you, true accuracy isn't necessarily in hitting a target on the first shot, but might include hitting the mark after the bullet bounces around a dozen times. Your attacks are just as dangerous if they miss, or even after hitting their mark, as others' are while they're still in the air.

name: Trickster
entries: {@i Imbue Life with a Touch of Chaos}

From the halls of the fey to the antics of Loki, there are entities who embody the primal nature of chaos. Your pact draws upon one of these powers, perhaps a creature with an aspect of whimsy or a deity relishing in tricks and ploys. Your patron asks you to sow chaos and delight in mischief. If you squint, you can almost make sense of the method behind their seeming madness.

name: Trickster Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Trickster Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Trickster Spells
rows: {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB}, {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB}, {@spell Enlarge/Reduce|XPHB}, {@spell Magic Mouth|XPHB}, {@spell Silent Image|XPHB}

name: Tripped Defenses
entries: You have learned to use a creature's mistakes against them. When a creature you can see within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to attempt to throw it off balance. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition; otherwise, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the end of the current turn unless it has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. Immediately after you do this, you can either make one attack with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against that creature or move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} from that creature.

name: True Grit
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, and you are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition caused by creature types in your {@classFeature Monster Grimoire|Monster Hunter|GrimHollowPG24|1}.

Additionally, when you hit a creature with an attack as part of a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can choose a {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature within 60 feet that can see you (including yourself). The condition ends on that creature.

name: True Grit
entries: You gain proficiency in Constitution saving throws. In addition, when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

name: True Shadow
entries: Your Shadowy Reflection gains the ability to become a deadly clone of you. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, your Shadowy Reflection transforms into an exact duplicate of you.

For 1 hour, your Shadowy Reflection becomes substantial, and you can have it take the {@action Attack|XPHB}, {@action Hide|XPHB}, or {@action Utilize|XPHB} action by controlling it with your Shadowy Reflection feature. Its {@action Attack|XPHB} action uses your game statistics, including class features, feats, and weapons. It vanishes when reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
When you make an attack roll against a creature within 5 feet of the duplicate, the attack roll has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: True Shot
entries: By 7th level, once per turn when you take the {@action Attack} action and attack with a ranged weapon, you can forgo one of your attacks. If you do so, the next hit you score with a ranged weapon before the end of your turn is a critical hit.

name: Truly Majestic
entries: You exude vampiric allure and have learned how to charm others. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Eerily Convincing
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} and {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks. In addition, when you cast a spell with your Entrancement feature, a creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on any saving throw it makes against the spell.

entries.name: Majesty
entries: You can expend 3 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Sanctuary|XPHB} spell on yourself. When you cast the spell in this way, the spell doesn't end if you make an attack roll, cast a spell, or deal damage.

name: Trusty Mount
entries: You always have the {@spell Find Steed|XPHB} spell prepared. With this feature, you can cast it without a spell slot or components, and your spellcasting ability for it is Intelligence.
Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Turncoat
entries: As an action, you wield your manipulative tongue against your enemies. You choose a number of enemy creatures up to your proficiency bonus within 60 feet of you who can hear you. Each target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or use their reaction to make a weapon attack against a single target of your choice. A creature affected by this feature can't attack themself.

name: Two For Flinching
entries: At 18th level, you have perfected the art of exploiting your opponent's weakness. Whenever you take the attack action against an opponent you have successfully misdirected this turn, or an opponent that is afflicted by a {@book condition|PHB|11}, you may make one additional attack against that opponent. You may only use this feature once per round.

name: Umbral Binder
entries: Some rogues are content to steal mere treasures, but umbral binders possess the energies that shape the world. Through secret rites and rituals, these rogues have learned to bind the powers of shadow into themselves and to use its power to fuel their abilities.

name: Umbral Form
entries: Starting at 2nd level, as a bonus action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to take on a shadowy umbral form, rather than transforming into a beast.

While in your umbral form, you retain your statistics, but your body becomes transparent like smoke. The form lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), are {@condition incapacitated}, die, or use this feature again.
While you are in this form, you gain the following features:

items: While in dim light or darkness, you can take the {@action Hide} action as a bonus action.
You can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.
When a creature you can see hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal cold damage equal to your proficiency bonus to that creature.

name: Umbral Killer
entries: Shadows are your companion, aiding you in your exploits. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain {@sense darkvision} out to 60 feet. If you already have {@sense darkvision}, its range increases by 60 feet.
Your movement speed increases by 10 feet.

You have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks made to hide. Whenever you make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage from an effect, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and half damage if you fail.

name: Unarguable Wizardry
entries: Your unquestionable legitimacy (and immense pectoral muscles) give you {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks made to convince others that you are, in fact, a wizard.

Additionally, if someone questions your legitimate magical prowess, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to enter your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1} until the end of your next turn. This Rage can't be extended and doesn't expend a use of your Rage.

name: Unbound Storm
entries: While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB} is active, you can unleash lightning with the following options.

items.name: Electrified Chains
items.entry: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to create chains of lightning that wrap around your weapon. The next time you hit a creature this turn, it takes your Vessel Damage and becomes ensnared by the chains, which anchor to the ground, until the start of your next turn. Each time it attempts to move more than 10 feet while ensnared, it must make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check against your Vessel save DC, freeing itself on a success. On a failure, it takes your Vessel Damage, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Fulgurant Strike
items.entry: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can leave the weapon embedded in their chest for a brief moment and immediately take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to call down lightning from the heavens to strike them, using the weapon as a conduit, before retrieving it. The target takes your Vessel Damage, and each other creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or also take that damage. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this saving throw.

items.name: Lightning Step
items.entry: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. During this rush, your body becomes supercharged; if you end this movement within 5 feet of a creature, it takes your Vessel Damage as the lightning leaps to them. If there are multiple creatures, choose one that takes the damage.

name: Unbroken Circle Spells
entries: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of the Unbroken Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Circle of the Unbroken Spells
rows: {@spell Ensnaring Strike|XPHB}, {@spell Shillelagh|XPHB}, {@spell Shining Smite|XPHB}, {@spell True Strike|XPHB}

name: Uncaged Beast
entries: Upon reaching 14th level, you become even more ferocious when pushed to your limits. When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to immediately transform into your {@subclassFeature Form of the Beast|Warlock|PHB|Predator|HumblewoodTales|1|HumblewoodTales} and then make one bite or claw attack at an enemy within 5 feet of you.

Additionally, while transformed into your {@subclassFeature Form of the Beast|Warlock|PHB|Predator|HumblewoodTales|1|HumblewoodTales}, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a bite or claw attack against that creature.

name: Unclean Brand
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee attack with a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, instead of dealing the strike's normal damage, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to sear a symbol into the creature's flesh, marking it with a glowing brand for 1 minute. During that time, the creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saving throws against your spells. Additionally, the creature gains {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire damage you deal, even if it normally has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Fire damage.

name: Unearthly Countenance
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you adopt an infernal or celestial countenance for 10 minutes. For the duration, your appearance gains aspects of the power you choose. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Commanding Presence
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks.

entries.name: Improved Spells
entries: When you expend a spell slot to cast a spell from the Arch Daemon or Arch Seraph table, the spell is cast as if you had spent a spell slot of one level higher.

entries.name: Unearthly Wings
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 60 feet.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5+ spell slot (no action required).

name: Unflinching Mark
entries: The bonus damage of your Mark Prey feature increases to {@damage 2d6}

name: Unflinching Mark II
entries: The bonus damage of your Mark Prey feature increases to {@damage 3d6}

name: Unhinged Asservations
entries: You are obsessed with documenting your visions. You gain proficiency with {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|XPHB} and you can create {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} in half the time and at half the cost in GP.

In addition, when you create a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG}, you can ensorcell it. When you ensorcell a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG}, you must expend a spell slot equal to or greater than the spell's level and you can spend Sorcery Points to apply one of your Metamagic options. Any creature that knows at least one language can use your ensorcelled {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG}, which casts the spell with the benefit of the Metamagic option you chose. The {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} remains ensorcelled until it is used or you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Unnatural and Unnerving
entries: When you expend a level 2+ spell slot to gain Mutation Points, you regain one expended spell slot. The slot you regain must be of a level lower than the slot you expended and can't be higher than level 5.
In addition, while in Wild Shape form, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Unnatural Attacks
entries: Each of your attacks in Wild Shape form can deal its normal damage type or Force damage. You make this choice each time you hit with those attacks.

entries.name: Unnerving Aura
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} or {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) and Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}) checks.

name: Unstable Fusion
entries: Sometimes, more is better As an action, you can infuse your companion with a second element for 1 minute, choosing from the options in the Infuse feature. Your companion gains the benefits of the Infuse, Elemental Discharge, and Primordial Shield features for both of the elements with which it is infused. If you activate your Primordial Shield feature while Unstable Fusion is active, your companion gains immunity to both damage types Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

name: Unstoppable
entries: At 14th level, your fury in battle makes you unstoppable. While you're raging, your speed cannot be reduced, and you are immune to the {@condition frightened}, {@condition paralyzed}, {@condition prone}, and {@condition stunned} conditions.

If you are {@condition frightened}, {@condition paralyzed}, or {@condition stunned}, you can still use a bonus action to enter a rage (even if you can't otherwise take actions). You aren't affected by any of these conditions while you're raging.

name: Unstoppable Assault
entries: As an action, you spin your weapon in a furious arc, decimating all creatures before you. You can attack a number of times equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} in addition to your normal attacks. If any of these attacks hit, they are {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB|Critical Hits}, and a creature struck by the attack must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier) or be pushed 10 feet away from you.
Once you have used this feature, you cannot use it again until after you've finished a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Unsubtle Strike
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or Monk weapon, you can force it to make a Strength saving throw against your Focus Point save DC. On a failed save, you can move the target up to 10 feet toward or away from you.

name: Unwavering Attention
entries: When you hit your bounty or a creature currently marked by your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}, you deal an extra {@damage 1d6} damage. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn. If you deal this damage as part of an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} again from the start of the next creature's turn (instead of on your next turn).

name: Unyielding Determination
entries: When you reach 7th level, your unshakable will allows you to persevere through any hardship. You have advantage on saving throws made during your turn.

name: Urban Colossus
entries: While shape-shifted into an {@creature Animated Object|XPHB}, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Armor Class
entries: Until you leave the form, your AC equals 18.

entries.name: Limited Damage Threshold
entries: Once per turn when you take less than 10 damage from a single attack or effect, you can reduce that damage to 0.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries: You can use Slam twice when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Unstoppable
entries: You can move through the space of any creature. Moving through its space doesn't cost you extra movement, but you can't stop in the same space. If the creature is your size or smaller, it takes Bludgeoning damage equal to {@damage 2d6} plus your Wisdom modifier and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition when you enter its space. A creature can take this damage once per turn.

name: Urban Druid
entries: Your magic and skills are specialized for city life, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Street Savvy
entries: Choose {@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}, {@skill History|XPHB}, {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, {@skill Investigation|XPHB}, {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}, or {@skill Stealth|XPHB}. You gain a bonus to checks using this skill equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1). You can change your selection when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Urban Magic
entries: Your magic takes on the aesthetic trappings of the urban landscape. Spells like {@spell Entangle|XPHB}, {@spell Grasping Vine|XPHB}, {@spell Spike Growth|XPHB}, and {@spell Wall of Thorns|XPHB} might cause growths of cobblestones, twisting pipes, or broken glass. The spells {@spell Speak with Plants|XPHB}, {@spell Transport via Plants|XPHB}, and {@spell Tree Stride|XPHB} can target structures instead of plants.

name: Valorous Soul
entries: When you reduce a foe to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} with a melee attack, you can choose any number of allies within 60 feet of you. For 1 minute, these allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on their attack rolls and saving throws.

Should you die, your body is treated as if {@spell Gentle Repose|XPHB} had been cast on it, and if you choose, you can refuse to return to life when you are the target of {@spell Raise Dead|XPHB} and similar spells.

name: Variant Capstone: Improved Genius

entries: The {@classFeature Soul of Artifice|Artificer|EFA|20} feature an Artificer gains at 20th level allows them to cheat death—sacrificing their creations to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} when they drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}—and to regain uses of {@classFeature Flash of Genius|Artificer|EFA|7} after completing a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}. While these are useful, they are also passive abilities that don't capture the flavor of a particular subclass. With the DM's permission, an Artificer who reaches level 20 can choose an alternative feature associated with their subclass instead of Soul of Artifice.

You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast any spell of level 8 or lower. This takes the place of the usual casting time of the spell, and you don't need to meet any requirements to cast the spell, including costly components; the spell simply takes effect. Once you cast a spell with this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Variant Capstone: Weapon of Legend

entries: The {@classFeature Soul of Artifice|Artificer|EFA|20} feature an Artificer gains at 20th level allows them to cheat death—sacrificing their creations to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} when they drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}—and to regain uses of {@classFeature Flash of Genius|Artificer|EFA|7} after completing a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}. While these are useful, they are also passive abilities that don't capture the flavor of a particular subclass. With the DM's permission, an Artificer who reaches level 20 can choose an alternative feature associated with their subclass instead of Soul of Artifice.
You are able to connect your spirit to your allies, making them living weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding your Ghaal'Shaarat.

entries.name: Constant Aura
entries: Your Aura of War is always active, and you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to change its damage type.

entries.name: Retributive Aura
entries: Whenever an enemy starts its turn in your Aura of War, that creature takes damage equal to the extra damage provided by the aura.

entries.name: Empower Aura
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can increase the extra damage provided by your Aura of War to {@dice 2d6}. This increase lasts for 1 minute. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Variegated Vexations
entries: Whenever you would deal Poison damage with a weapon attack, you can change that damage to be either Acid or Necrotic instead.

name: Vascular Corruption Aura
entries: At 17th level, you can use your action to emit a deathly aura of necrotic energy that causes the veins of nearby foes to burst and bleed. For 1 minute, any hostile creature with blood that moves within 30 feet of you for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes {@damage 3d6} necrotic damage. If a hostile creature with blood regains hit points while in the aura, it regains only half as many hit points as expected.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.

name: Veil of Dreams
entries: When you reach 8th level, you gain mastery over magical sleep. When you cast the {@spell sleep} spell, add your cleric level to the dice you roll to determine how many hit points of creatures the spell can affect.

You may choose the order in which creatures within the spell's area are affected. If the first target chosen has too many hit points to be affected, the spell will instead target the next creature you have chosen that the spell could affect before affecting other targets.
Additionally, any creature you put to sleep cannot be woken until the start of your next turn. Otherwise, the {@spell sleep} spell acts as normal.

name: Veil of Pain
entries: When you damage a creature with your torturer techniques, you can attempt to rattle its mind with the pain (no action required). The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Technique save DC or start dissociating your presence, its mind refusing to acknowledge the anguish you are causing it, only perceiving you as a flicker. You have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition to the target for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Vengeful Summons
entries: Your magic has become powerful enough that you can call and command a servant of those who cursed you. Choose one of the following creatures based on the choice you made with your Blood Ties feature: {@creature Lamia|XMM} or {@creature Troll|XMM} (Fey only), {@creature Barbed Devil|XMM}, {@creature Incubus|XMM}, or {@creature Succubus|XMM} (Fiend only), {@creature Ghost|XMM} or {@creature Wraith|XMM} (Undead only).

You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and spend 5 Sorcery Points to summon your chosen creature. The creature appears in an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet. It disappears when it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you use this feature to summon another creature, or after 10 minutes have passed.

The creature is an ally to you and your allies. In combat, the creature shares your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don't issue any, it takes the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action and uses its movement to avoid danger.

name: Venomous Mark
entries: Also at 1st level, as a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target is cursed for 1 minute. The curse ends early if the target dies, you die, or you are {@condition incapacitated}. Until the curse ends, you deal an extra {@dice 1d6} poison damage to the target whenever you hit it with a spell attack. (You can only apply this damage once per spell even if there are multiple spell attack instances, such as with {@spell eldritch blast}.)

If the target drops to 0 hit points before the curse ends, you can use a bonus action on a subsequent turn of yours to curse a new creature. Only one creature can be affected with a venomous mark at any given time.

name: Venomous Strike
entries: When you deal {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|XPHB|1} damage to a creature, you can choose for the Sneak Attack to deal {@dice d8}s of Poison damage instead of {@dice d6}s of the same type dealt by the weapon.

name: Ventrue
entries: {@i Control Others with Influence and Guile}

The Ventrue have elevated themselves to be the "Clan of Kings," imposing their will on the clans and standing contemptuously against those who would defy them. After lifetimes of prudent rule, the Ventrue have earned their figurative throne.

name: Ventrue Bane
entries: You have an arguably refined palate for blood. Choose a specific physical aspect (such as natural blondes or the elderly) or a social aspect (such as employees, soldiers, or the willing). It cannot be a wide generalization, such as creature type. When you use your {@classFeature Feed|Kindred|BoundByBlood|1} feature on a creature that doesn't have your preferred aspect, you roll half the number of Feed Dice.

name: Vermin Lord
entries: {@i Grow Powerful from Strength in Numbers}

Vermin Lords cultivate loyal hordes of disease-bearing rodents to help them battle greater evils. For many of these Rangers, that greater evil is some kind of societal ill, but a rare few see their fellow Humanoids as an infestation that threatens the natural world. Regardless of their goal, they make their homes in sewers, slums, and other forgotten places where they are free to plot against their enemies and tend to their verminkin.

name: Vermin Lord Spells
entries: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Vermin Lord Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

name: Verminkin
entries: You can comprehend and verbally communicate with Tiny Beasts.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend a spell slot to summon vermin swarms. You summon a number of swarms equal to the slot's level for 1 hour. Each swarm is summoned to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself. A swarm uses the {@creature Swarm of Vermin|GrimHollowPG24} stat block.

In combat, each swarm acts during your turn. It can move and use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} on its own, but the only action it takes is the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action unless you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can command each swarm with a single {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Versatile Missiles
entries: You can accurately guide your {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB} darts to strike a target wherever you choose. When you cast {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, you can add one of the following Versatile Missile effects to a target struck by the darts. Each effect has a cost, which is the number of darts you must forgo to add the effect to the target. You can add different effects to different targets, paying the cost for each effect separately.

entries.name: Trip Missile (Cost: 1 Dart)
entries: The target must succeed on Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Blinding Missile (Cost: 3 Darts)
entries: The target must succeed on Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Stunning Missile (Cost: 5 Darts)
entries: The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

name: Veteran Hero
entries: Your dungeoneering expertise gives you the following benefits.

entries.name: Peerless Heroism
entries: Once per turn when you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can expend {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} to turn the roll into a 20, instead of rerolling the {@dice d20}.

entries.name: Double Inspiration
entries: You can have two instances of {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} at one time. You can use only one {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} per roll.

name: Vexing Distraction
entries: While in your cat form, you can pass off the most destructive, distracting, and irritating behavior as cute or even adorable.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while in your cat form, choose a creature within 5 feet of you that can see and hear you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom save against your spell save DC or be affected by one of the following effects of your choice:

items.name: Annoy
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} until the end of your next turn.

items.name: Confound
entries: The target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 until the end of your next turn.

items.name: Distract
entries: A creature of your choice has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} against the target until the end of the chosen creature's next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Viking
entries: {@i Dangerous Raider of the Sea}

Vikings are battle-hardened warriors and sailors who ply the seas of the Northlands for glory and plunder. As followers of the Reaver's Way, they have their own sense of honor, yet they can be merciless in times of raiding and war. Vikings are known for their prowess with the spear and axe, and for their belief that they can earn a special place in the halls of the dead through their deeds of valor in battle.

name: Viking Weapon Mastery
entries: If you have {@variantrule Weapon Mastery Properties|XPHB|Weapon Mastery} with a {@item Battleaxe|XPHB}, {@item Longsword|XPHB}, or {@item Spear|XPHB}, once on each of your turns, you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to a damage roll with that weapon.

name: Vile Transmogrification
entries: You uncover two new ways to employ Asmodeus's magic:

entries.name: Regaining Seals
entries: As a bonus action on your turn, you can expend one spell slot to regain a number of seals equal to that slot's level.

entries.name: Regaining Spell Slots
entries: As a bonus action on your turn, you can expend any number of seals to regain a spell slot of a level equal to one-third that number. For example, you can expend six seals to regain a 2nd-level spell slot.
Once you use one of these benefits, you can't use that benefit again until you finish a long rest.

name: Violent Hunger
entries: When you deal damage to a creature with a weapon attack and roll the maximum result of one of the damage dice, you can spend 1 maneuver point to roll another die of the same type and add its result to the damage dealt by the attack. You can do this once per attack.

name: Virtuoso Skill
entries: Once per turn when you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can choose to make it with Charisma if the test doesn't use it already.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Virulent Form
entries: Your patron allows you to unleash a modicum of its true power as it envelops your form As an action, you can gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You grow in size by one category—from Medium to Large, for example If you lack the room to grow, your size doesn't change.
You gain a number of temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) at the start of each of your turns.
The damage dice of your parasitic weapon increases to {@damage 2d8}
Your parasitic weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.
Whenever you take damage from a creature within your parasitic weapon's reach, you can use your reaction to make an attack with the parasitic weapon against that creature.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Visionary
entries: You have honed your skills and your perceptions to a razor's edge. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Practiced Perfection
entries: You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in three of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

entries.name: Spirit's Touch
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 2 Blood Points to touch an object and perceive emotional residues on it for 10 minutes. You can ask the GM a number of questions equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, which must be answered truthfully. You must ask your questions before the effect ends. The following are examples of questions that can be asked.

items: What did the last creature that touched this look like?
What was the emotional state of the last creature that used the object?
Is this object magical?
Is this object cursed?
Is this object trapped?
What are any physical details of the object that aren't readily visible?
How many creatures have touched the object in the last 24 hours?

name: Visions of Annihilation
entries: You gain the ability to foretell a creature's doom. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose a creature you can see within 120 feet of yourself. Until the start of your next turn, attack rolls against that creature have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Vital Siphoning
entries: You can feed on your own life essence to fuel your magic. As a bonus action, you can expend a Hit Die and choose one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Blood Boil
entries: You regain the use of your {@subclassFeature Blood Well|Sorcerer|PHB|Crimson|CrookedMoon14|1|CrookedMoon14}.

entries.name: Crimson Pulse
entries: Expend your {@subclassFeature Blood Well|Sorcerer|PHB|Crimson|CrookedMoon14|1|CrookedMoon14} to make the next Metamagic option you use this turn cost no sorcery point.

name: Vital Siphoning
entries: You can feed on your own life essence to fuel your magic. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Points Die} and choose one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Blood Boil
entries: You regain the use of your {@subclassFeature Blood Well|Sorcerer|XPHB|Crimson|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24}.

entries.name: Crimson Pulse
entries: Expend your {@subclassFeature Blood Well|Sorcerer|XPHB|Crimson|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24} to make the next Metamagic option you use this turn cost no Sorcery Points.

name: Vitalize
entries: You can flood your allies with invigorating vivacity (no action required). For 1 minute, each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you gains a bonus to ability checks equal to your proficiency bonus.

name: Voice of Authority
entries: You can impose control over others while keeping others from imposing control over you. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Do as I Say
entries: You can cast the {@spell Command|XPHB} and {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} spells. You can cast either spell without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Unshakably Confident
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom saving throws.

name: Volatile Serum
entries: You have an implanted series of syringes and reservoirs that hold alchemical serums and deploy them into your body. When you enter your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian||1}, choose one of your serums to inject and gain its benefits.
The chosen serum lasts for the duration of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian||1}, or until you choose a new serum as a bonus action. You have the following serum options.

entries.name: Ferocity
entries: This serum throws you into an energized frenzy. You ignore {@quickref difficult terrain||3}, and when you hit with a Melee weapon or unarmed strike, you can make another attack with it against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

entries.name: Monstrosity
entries: The serum expands your body to monstrous proportions and can change your appearance in cosmetic ways, such as by altering facial features, skin tone, and hair length or color. Your reach increases by 5 feet, and once per turn when you miss with an attack roll that relies on Strength, you can add your rage damage bonus to the total, potentially causing the attack to hit. If you are smaller than Large, you become Large, along with anything you are wearing or carrying. If there isn't enough room to accommodate the size change, your size doesn't change.

entries.name: Reconstruction
entries: The serum dulls pain and forces wounds to rapidly knit. Upon activation and at the start of each of your turns, you can expend and roll a Hit Die. You regain a number of hit points equal to the number rolled plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 hit point). You gain any excess beyond your hit point maximum as temporary hit points. If you take acid or fire damage, this serum doesn't function at the start of your next turn.

name: Volatile Serum
entries: You have an implanted series of syringes and reservoirs that hold alchemical serums and deploy them into your body. When you enter your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1}, choose one of your serums to inject and gain its benefits.
The chosen serum lasts for the duration of your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1}, or until you choose a new serum as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You have the following serum options.

entries.name: Ferocity
entries: This serum throws you into an energized frenzy. You ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}, and when you hit with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can activate the {@itemMastery Cleave} mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you're using.

entries.name: Monstrosity
entries: The serum expands your body to monstrous proportions and can change your appearance in cosmetic ways, such as by altering facial features, skin tone, and hair length or color. Your reach increases by 5 feet, and once per turn when you miss with an attack roll that relies on Strength, you can add your Rage Damage bonus to the total, potentially causing the attack to hit. If you are smaller than Large, you become Large, along with anything you are wearing or carrying. If there isn't enough room to accommodate the size change, your size doesn't change.

entries.name: Reconstruction
entries: The serum dulls pain and forces wounds to rapidly knit. Upon activation and at the start of each of your turns, you can expend and roll a {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Points Die}. You regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the number rolled plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}). You gain any excess beyond your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum as {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.
If you take Acid or Fire damage, this serum doesn't function at the start of your next turn.

name: Wall Crawling
entries: You've become accustomed to moving like a spider, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Climber
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Hiding on Ceilings
entries: If you are on a ceiling and {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|XPHB}, you can take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action as long as any enemy that could see you is below you.

entries.name: Spider Climb
entries: You can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and along ceilings, while leaving your hands free.

name: Wall Warp
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you takes damage from an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cast {@spell Wall of Stone|XPHB} between the target and the attacker. When you cast the spell in this way, you create a single 10-foot-by-10-foot panel that is 1 inch thick (AC 15, 30 HP, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage), which disappears at the end of your next turn. The panel takes the damage of the attack and disappears early if it is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

name: Wand Lore
entries: Some children grow up sword-fighting with sticks and become soldiers, but you've learned how to turn a simple stick into something more powerful than a blade. The study of wand lore delves deeper into old magic, beyond the normal lists of components and incantations, and into the rich history and tradition of wandcraft. As a wizard of wand lore, you know that a mage's true power can be amplified with the right tool: for you, that tool is a wand of your own creation.

name: Wand Savant
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can interpret staves and wands the way other wizards read scrolls and spellbooks. If a staff or wand in your possession can cast a spell that's on the {@filter wizard spell list|spells|class=wizard}, you can copy the spell into your spellbook as if you were copying a spell from a scroll. In addition, when you cast a wizard spell with a range of touch while holding your core wand, you can choose a target that you can see and isn't behind cover up to 10 feet away from you instead. At 14th level, this range increases to 30 feet.

name: Wanderer's Lore
entries: At 3rd level, you can share any useful tidbits of information you have come across in your travels to help others to see problems from a new angle. When a creature has a Bardic Inspiration die granted by you, they may make a single {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion} check with advantage. The creature may choose whether or not to add the Bardic Inspiration die to this roll.

name: Wandslinger's Presence
entries: You know how to talk yourself up and tear your opponents down. If you speak to a creature for at least 1 minute, you can attempt to distract and rattle them when the call to action finally comes. If the creature rolls an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count equal to or higher than your own, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature's {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} is reduced to be equal to yours, and it acts immediately after you in the {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} order.

name: War Druid
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with a casting of one of your Druid cantrips that has a casting time of an action.

name: War-Hardened
entries: By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls, Strength checks, and Strength saving throws, and you cannot be {@status surprised}. To gain this benefit, you cannot be {@condition blinded}, {@condition deafened}, or {@condition incapacitated}.

name: Ward Against Corruption
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end diseases and against any effect that would change your form, such as the {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} spell.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can touch a willing creature to grant this benefit, but the creature takes Fire damage equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}. Once you grant this benefit, it lasts for 1 hour or until you grant this benefit again.

name: Ward of Shadows
entries: At 1st level, you can create a ward of divine shadows to conceal yourself from an attacking enemy. When attacked by a creature you can see within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, as shadows envelop your form. An attacker that can't be {@condition blinded} is immune to this feature.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Ward of the Guardian
entries: When a creature marked by you that you can see reduces an ally to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and doesn't kill the ally outright, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to have the ally drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead. If you do so, the ally can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a melee attack against the marked creature if it's within reach.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Ward the Profane
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend 3 Focus Points to cast {@spell Banishment|XPHB} targeting that creature. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

name: Warden of Harmony
entries: When a creature within 60 feet of you attempts to teleport, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and spend 1 Focus Point to prevent the teleportation.

name: Warrior of Cosmic Balance

entries: When the cosmos spins out of alignment, my job is to kick it back into place. Literally.

Warriors of the Cosmic Balance watch the mystic paths of the world, the dimensional portals and arcane gates. And where eldrtich horrors seek to intrude upon the world, these warriors stand waiting. They are trained to use their inner power to purge even the strongest afflictions, and their merest touch can send the mightiest abominations back to the horrid pits that spawned them.

entries.subclassFeature: Guardian of the Way Technique|Monk|XPHB|Cosmic Balance|CthulhuTorchlight|3

name: Warrior of Pride
entries: {@i Prove Your Superiority}

Monks who become Warriors of Pride value themselves above all. These monks focus on mastering their form, ego, and their destructive power. They display monastic aesthetics publicly with the intention of gaining the respect and admiration of "lesser beings."
The prideful traditions of this order include adorning themselves with jewelry, hiding their scars, and commanding respect from those who would oppose them.

name: Warrior of Regret
entries: {@i Atone for Past Mistakes}
No one is born intent on bringing evil into this world, yet many lives are transformed by the suffering inflicted upon them. Warriors of Regret are haunted by the shadows of evil deeds done.

Through training and reflection, Warriors of Regret accept their past can't be erased. Instead, they focus on forging remorse and grief into a weapon against their foes. Though their misdeeds follow their every step, Warriors of Regret are not powerless to atone for them.

name: Warrior of the Celestial
entries: {@i Divine Answers, Support Allies, and Smite Foes with Holy Energy}

Monks of the Way of the Celestial are peacekeepers and protectors of their chosen kin. These monks meditate to achieve a greater understanding of a divine being, granting them the ability to channel celestial energies into their own. These martial defenders are pensive, patient, and understanding, but they offer little mercy when evil intentions are made clear.

The Way of the Celestial originated from the lost city of Hearth as a tribute to the city's guardian couatl protectors. While these teachings are far from common knowledge, there's no telling what small, protected monasteries may still exist after the city's untimely destruction. Regardless of how you come upon this tradition, the wisdom of the celestials guides its every principle.

name: Warrior of the Leaden Crown
entries: {@i Harness the Will to Resist}

In contrast to the esoteric ideals of other orders, Warriors of the Leaden Crown have practical aims: the self-governance of all people. These Monks see history as a series of clashes between groups of powerful beings where Humanoids are at best collateral damage and at worst disposable pawns. To break this cycle of dependence and destruction, Warriors of the Leaden Crown master mental abilities to fight against the otherworldly powers of the multiverse and protect Humanoid sovereignty.

One component of this plan involves training to do battle with powerful planar foes. The other equally important component is ensuring that Humanoid societies are prepared to overthrow those already dominating them. To that end, these Monks seek political positions that place them in or near decision-making roles where they can influence others to fight back against Arch Seraphs, Arch Daemons, and Primordials.

name: Warrior of the Living Weapon
entries: {@i Reshape Your Body for Battle}

Warriors of the Living Weapon pursue physical perfection, honing their body as a smith sharpens a sword. Their traditions are drawn from cultures of shape-shifters and creatures who fight with tooth and claw.

name: Warrior of the Pestilent Haze
entries: {@i Spread Virulent Plague with a Touch}

Warriors of the Pestilent Haze draw plague into their very beings, folding it into their energy and becoming one with the disease. Monks who follow this tradition wander, often following or even preceding waves of pestilence. Some walk with caution, their touch measured, unleashing sickness only where dense populations must be culled. Others revel in the miasma spreading as far and fast as possible.

Your Miasmic Plague is a unique magical contagion that can take many forms that you weave through your deep connection to the affliction. The Plague Manifestations table offers suggestions for what magical form your signature disease takes as it spreads, as well as its hallmark symptoms.

entries.caption: Plague Manifestations
rows: {@b Bloodbreath.} Bruise-colored miasma, the edges of which form into slithering tentacles—painful bruises and a hoarse, bloody cough
{@b Drone Spew.} Swarm of monstrous, mutated flies that buzz with a horrifying drone—bleeding ears and intense vomiting
{@b Festergut.} Viscous, gray sewer water that leaves a film on surfaces—intense stomach pain, dehydration, and blood loss
{@b Gutterpox.} Globs of toxic, greenish sludge that oozes erratically to the touch—swollen, green papules and oppressive mucus buildup
{@b Knell Fever.} Hot wind that prickles the skin and howls with the sound of a tolling bell—heat blisters and feverish hallucinations
{@b Rotface.} Numerous spiked, fungal spores that float through the air—rapid rotting of flesh, especially around the eyes and mouth
{@b The Unclean.} Undulating mass of pallid flesh, teeth, and tongues—grotesque, mutated growths such as new tentacle-like appendages and gnashing mouths
{@b Toadscale.} Infected rains filled with venomous, spectral toads—hardened, itchy patches of scaly skin that turn vibrantly colorful and fits of agonized croaking
{@b Verminplague.} Scurrying mass of ravenous, spectral plague rats that gnaw and scratch victims—painful boils and pustules and an incessant, squeaking cough
{@b Yellow Death.} Billowing, skull-shaped clouds of foul-smelling fumes with a sickly yellow hue—debilitating fatigue, muscle aches, and sunken, sallow skin

name: Warrior of the Street
entries: {@i Strike with Combos and Special Moves}

"Street fighting" is an urban discipline founded on necessity, whose blindingly fast, unique brand of martial arts has been honed and perfected in back-alley brawls and tournaments alike. Monks who adopt this relatively new technique place comparatively little value on spiritual enlightenment and inner focus; the thrill of split-second timing, rapid combos, and decisive knock-outs drive them to become the best combatants in the world

name: Wax Enchantments
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn wax enchantments, which are fueled by your ability to pull and manipulate magic from the Spirit Realm. These are represented by a number of wick points.

entries.name: Enchantments
entries: You learn three enchantments of your choice, which are detailed under "{@filter Enchantments|optionalfeatures|source=ObojimaTallGrass|feature type=we}" below.
You learn two additional enchantments of your choice at 5th, 10th, and 15th level. Each time you learn new enchantments, you can also replace one enchantment you know with a different one.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: Some of your enchantments require creatures to make a saving throw to resist the enchantment's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:

entries.name: Wick Points
entries: You have 3 wick points, which represent your current ability to harness the magic from the Spirit Realm. Manipulating the magic from another realm and pulling its energy into an object, even one as small and simple as a candle, can be both physically and mentally taxing. When you spend a wick point, it is unavailable until you finish a short or long rest, at the end of which you regain all of your expended wick points.
Whenever you gain a level in this class, you gain 1 additional wick point.

name: Waxwork Rogue
entries: Waxwork rogues have a long history on the island of Obojima in dealing with the dangerous and the arcane. They're known for having an array of tools and tricks to delve into the most perilous of places and almost always coming back with treasures and tales. To a Waxwork rogue, any challenge or danger can be solved with a bit of wax, a pinch of smarts, and a whole lot of magic.

entries.name: In the Beginning
entries: The Courier Brigade was created to carry packages between villages as well as guard merchant wagons through treacherous areas. But there are some areas on Obojima that are rife with the arcane, spirit dangers, and uncanny occurrences.

Legend says that it was Lydia Starwright, Courier Brigade First Class, who, against all advice, sought out the aid of a powerful witch who was rumored to live within a hut of melted wax deep within the Land of Hot Water. It was there in that melted hut where the witch taught Lydia the arcane practices known only to certain spirits of the island, the ability to enchant wax and fire in wondrous ways. It was this knowledge that transformed Lydi into the first Waxwork Rogue.

Lydia brought back this knowledge to the Courier Brigade, and formed the Waxworks Division, a dedicated group of arcane rogues who would volunteer for the most perilous assignments and deliveries of the Courier Brigade.
In the present day, Waxwork rogues have transcended the ranks of the Courier Brigade, and their skill sets are practiced across the island.

name: Way of the Aether
entries: Monks of the Way of the Aether tap into the energy of spirits and the Ethereal Plane. This energy is the fifth element, aether, which is contained by every living—and nonliving—soul. Sometimes called ghostfists, monks of this tradition explore the Material and Ethereal Planes on lifelong missions to give the souls of the dead a final resting place. By aligning the ki and aether within themselves, monks of this tradition treat their spirit as an extension of their physical bodies and move through the world unimpeded by material obstacles like a ghost.

name: Way of the Cobalt Soul
entries: Driven by the pursuit of knowledge and its scholars' worship of {@deity The Knowing Mentor|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, the {@book Library of the Cobalt Soul|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|Library of the Cobalt Soul} is one of the best-respected and most heavily guarded repositories of tomes, history, and information in all Exandria. People from all lands come to the library to seek knowledge, and those particularly dedicated to the virtues of truth often pledge their minds and bodies to the {@book Cobalt Soul's|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|Library of the Cobalt Soul} cause. To become a member of the {@book Cobalt Soul|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|Library of the Cobalt Soul} is to give oneself over to a quest dedicated to unveiling life's mysteries, bringing light to the secrets of concealed evil, and guarding the most powerful and dangerous of truths from those whose unwholesome thirst for knowledge might bring death and suffering to others.

The monks of the {@book Cobalt Soul|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|Library of the Cobalt Soul} are the embodiment of the maxim: "Know your enemy." Through tireless research, they steel themselves against the unrelenting tides of evil. Through rigorous training, they learn to break through their foes' mental and physical defenses. Then, once the fight is done, they record their findings for future generations of monks to study.

name: Way of the Pestilent Haze
entries: {@i Spread Virulent Plague with a Touch}

Warriors of the Pestilent Haze draw plague into their very beings, folding it into their energy and becoming one with the disease. Monks who follow this tradition wander, often following or even preceding waves of pestilence. Some walk with caution, their touch measured, unleashing sickness only where dense populations must be culled. Others revel in the miasma spreading as far and fast as possible.

{@b Festergut.} Viscous, gray sewer water that leaves a film on surfaces—intense stomach pain, dehydration, and blood loss

{@b Yellow Death.} Billowing, skull-shaped clouds of foul-smelling fumes with a sickly yellow hue—debilitating fatigue, muscle aches, and sunken, sallow skin

name: Way of the Prophet
entries: Monks who follow the Way of the Prophet refuse to cloister the wisdom they have learned. They are driven to spread their knowledge to all the peoples of the land. Some are set on this path by divine intervention. Others take up the prophet's mantle out of a sense of personal obligation, and they all share a deep-rooted faith that empowers their actions.

name: Weak Spot
entries: Also at 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check against a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, contested by the target's Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check. If you win the contest, you can use your {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Treasure Hunter|TLotRR|1|TLotRR} against that target even if you don't have advantage on the attack roll, but not if you have disadvantage on it.
This benefit lasts for 1 minute or until you successfully use this feature against a different target.

name: Weather the Storm
entries: You have grown accustomed to being battered and bruised. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you toughen up for 1 minute. At the end of each of your turns, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Fighter level plus your Constitution modifier.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Weave the Elements
entries: With 1 hour of work or when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can use an {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB} to mark yourself with elemental patterns. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one of the following damage types of your choice until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

name: Weaver of Words
entries: You become a master of all words. You learn all languages available to characters in the campaign.

name: Webbing
entries: You can magically produce sticky, silken spider webs from your hands as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. This web dissolves after 1 minute. When you create the webs, you can use them to do one of the following.

entries.name: Pull Yourself
entries: You project a line of web at a point you can see within 30 feet, pulling yourself to that point in a straight line without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. You can use this benefit as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when you fall to pull yourself up to 10 feet in any direction.

entries.name: Manipulate Objects
entries: You can use a line of web to manipulate an object that isn't being worn or carried within 30 feet. For example, you can pull an object to your hand, close a door, or snatch a Small or smaller object weighing less than 10 pounds.

entries.name: Create Rope
entries: You create a 60-foot-long Rope of web and anchor it to a point you choose.

entries.name: Web Spell
entries: You cast {@spell Web|XPHB} without a spell slot as a part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} used for this feature (DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). When you cast it using this feature, the webs fill a 5-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube}, and the spell's duration becomes 1 minute. You can cast this spell using this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Well-Rounded
entries: You gain proficiency with one type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice, you gain proficiency in one skill of your choice, and you know one language of your choice.

name: What Goes Bump in the Night

entries.name: Lord of Vermin
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action expend 3 Blood Points to summon {@dice 1d4 + 1} swarms of bats, insects, or rats for 1 hour. Once used, can't use again until a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Stalk the Shadows
entries: You can cast {@spell Greater Invisibility|XPHB} on yourself without a spell slot a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining uses on a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Whispers of Knowledge
entries: Also at 3rd level, you can seek knowledge through meditation by calling upon the spirits carried on the wind. You can spend 10 minutes communing with these spirits to gain proficiency in one skill or tool of your choice that you don't already have proficiency in, as a traveling spirit shares its knowledge with you. You lose this proficiency the next time you use this feature or finish a short or long rest.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Whistling Wanderer
entries: You've shaped the superstition of whistling to the dead into a potent instrument. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Wanderer's Bindle
entries: When you finish a long rest, you can touch a nonmagical bag, sack, or similar container and turn it into a magical container called a bindle. This container functions as a {@item Heward's Handy Haversack|DMG|Handy Haversack}. If you create a second bindle, if your bindle is more than 1 mile away from you, or when you die, the bindle loses its magic, and anything inside appears in unoccupied spaces closest to the container.

entries.name: Whistled Spells
entries: You can whistle in place of verbal components for your bard spells. Observers unfamiliar with this tradition must succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check to recognize your spellcasting for what it is by whistled verbal components alone.

name: Whistling Wanderer
entries: You've shaped the superstition of whistling to the dead into a potent instrument. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Wanderer's Bindle
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can touch a nonmagical bag, sack, or similar container and turn it into a magical container called a bindle. This container functions as a {@item Heward's Handy Haversack|XDMG|Handy Haversack}. If you create a second bindle, if your bindle is more than 1 mile away from you, or when you die, the bindle loses its magic, and anything inside appears in unoccupied spaces closest to the container.

entries.name: Whistled Spells
entries: You can whistle in place of Verbal components for your Bard spells. Observers unfamiliar with this tradition must succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check to recognize your spellcasting for what it is by whistled Verbal components alone.

name: White Hat
entries: {@i Protect Your Allies and Uphold the Law}

Some Gunslingers live by a code and expect others to do the same. These Gunslingers, known as White Hats, sometimes serve as officers of the law but never hesitate to do what's right when the law says otherwise. Despite their affinity for deadly weapons, White Hats prefer to keep their friends safe and subdue their enemies nonviolently—a preference their enemies don't often oblige.

name: Wicker Rising
entries: The energy you channel through your wicker effigy grows stronger, empowering its benefits.

entries.name: Sacrifice
entries: The fire damage increases to {@dice 2d8} plus your Wisdom modifier.

entries.name: Soothe
entries: The healing of your effigy increases to {@dice 1d8}, and when you target a creature with the effigy, you can expend 5 hit points from the effigy to remove one of the following conditions on the target: {@condition charmed}, {@condition frightened}, {@condition paralyzed}, {@condition poisoned}, {@condition stunned}.

entries.name: Ward
entries: Choose a damage type other than force. You and your allies in the aura have resistance to the chosen type.
